b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Concept 4GL  [1]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake til\n   Lexical Definition\xc2\xa0>                                              kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[2]Neste\n                           Notation                                      side\n\n   [3]How to browse through the Unique 4GL lexical definition\n\n   All terms are written in a fixed width font, descriptions are written in a\n   proportional font.\n\n   Logical terms (non terminal symbols) are shown in normal type. The\n   definition of a logical term is introduced by the name of the term\n   followed by a colon. One or more alternative expansions of the term then\n   follow on succeeding lines. For example, the definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0fieldName:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0applicationField\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0internalField\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   states\xc2\xa0that\xc2\xa0fieldName\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0either\xc2\xa0applicationField\xc2\xa0or\xc2\xa0internalField.\n\n   For convenience, an extra indentation may be used to have a definition\n   spanning several lines. For example, the definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0fieldAttribute:\n\n   \xc2\xa0column-name(\xc2\xa0columnName\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0columnName}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0consists-of(\xc2\xa0applicationField\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0{consistOfSeparator\xc2\xa0applicationField}\xc2\xa0;\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0default-value(\xc2\xa0expression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   contains\xc2\xa0a\xc2\xa0definition\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0consists-of\xc2\xa0spanning\xc2\xa0two\xc2\xa0lines.\n\n   Keywords (terminal symbols) are shown in bold type. For example, the\n   definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0onOff:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0ON\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0OFF\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   states\xc2\xa0that\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0logical\xc2\xa0term\xc2\xa0onOff\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0either\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0keyword\xc2\xa0ON\xc2\xa0or\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0keyword\xc2\xa0OFF.\n\n   The words "one of" following the colon of a logical term definition\n   signifies that each of the keywords or number on the following line or\n   lines is an alternative definition. For example, the definition of onOff\n   above may alternatively be written:\n\n   \xc2\xa0onOff:\xc2\xa0one\xc2\xa0of\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0ON\xc2\xa0OFF\n\n   A term enclosed in square brackets signifies that the term is optional,\n   i.e. it may or may not occur. For example, the definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0integer:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0[sign]\xc2\xa0unsignedInteger\n\n   states that a integer is an unsignedInteger optionally prefixed with a\n   sign.\n\n   A term enclosed in curly brackets signifies that the term may occur zero\n   or more times. For example, the definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0fieldDefinition:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0field=name\xc2\xa0{fieldDecl}\xc2\xa0{fieldFunc}\n\n   states that a fieldDefinition is the keyword field followed by the\n   character = followed by a name followed by zero or more fieldDecl and zero\n   or more fieldFunc.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_la_zoobrowse.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_la_zoobrowse.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Concept 4GL  side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Lexical Definition\xc2\xa0>                                          til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n         How to browse through the lexical definition                    side\n\n   [4]About the notation used within the Concept 4GL lexical definition\n\n   The Concept 4GL lexical definition is organized in a hierarchical\n   structure. On the top level, a definition is given of the application; at\n   the lowest level definitions of e.g. digits can be found.\n\n   All definitions can be accessed by mouse-clicking on the elements of a\n   definition. Normally in a Windows help system, these \xef\xbf\xbdjump\xef\xbf\xbds would appear\n   highlighted in green. But to maintain readability, this highlighting has\n   been turned off. A "jump" will identify itself by changing the cursor to a\n   small hand.\n\n   Almost every word in a definition can be clicked upon. It will bring up\n   the lexical definition of the word, thus moving "deeper" into the\n   hierarchical structure. If a word is preceded with a ?, clicking on the\n   question mark will bring up the same definition, but in a pop-up window.\n   This makes it easier to scan quickly the underlying definitions of the\n   whole definition.\n\n   When clicking on a bold-face word, a link is executed to the Reference\n   Manual. For example, clicking on the bell() word in the definition of\n   fieldfunction will bring up the bell()-topic from the Reference Manual,\n   describing how to use the bell()-function in a 4GL application.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_la_notation.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_la_application.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_la_notation.htm\n'

b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                   Concept 4GL Applications                              side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Concept 4GL applications can be divided into 2 main groups. An application\n   can either be linked to a dialogue-based screen on which interaction with\n   the user takes place, or it can consist of a report, i.e. a systematic\n   printout of several rows in one or several tables.\n\n   Sample online application\n\n   Sample output from an XTRA application\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Screen applications are termed ONLINE, whereas report-based applications\n   are termed XTRA applications. You may combine these application types if\n   you wish.\n\n   Although the functions of ONLINE and XTRA applications are different, most\n   Concept 4GL language keywords (i.e. declarations and functions) can be\n   used both in ONLINE and XTRA applications. However, there are a group of\n   keywords whose functions become unique in relation to ONLINE or XTRA. By\n   studying this reference manual, you will get a further description of\n   these keywords.\n\n   In addition to generating reports, XTRA applications can be used for all\n   types of tasks which require sequential treatment of your data. Typical\n   tasks easily handled by XTRA applications are:\n\n   \xc2\xb7modification/updating of data in database tables,\n\n   \xc2\xb7transferring data from one database to another - independent of the\n   database type,\n\n   \xc2\xb7import/export to other data formats,\n\n   \xc2\xb7etc.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   In most cases, a 4GL application consists of a framework of 7 components\n   as illustrated in the table below:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Component           Component layout\n   [5]Application file <[6]application file declarations>\n                       [8]online=<name> or xtra=<name> or layout=<name>\n\n   [7]Application      <application properties>\n\n                       <application events>\n                       [10]stream=<name>\n\n   [9]Stream           <stream properties>\n\n                       <stream events>\n                       [12]form=<name>\n\n   [11]Form            <form properties>\n\n                       <form events>\n                       [14]element=<name>\n   [13]Element\n                       <element properties>\n                       [16]database=<name>\n   [15]Database\n                       <database properties>\n                       [18]table=<name>\n\n                       <table properties>\n   [17]Table\n                       <table functions>\n\n                       <table events>\n                       [20]field=<name>\n\n                       <field properties>\n   [19]Field\n                       <field functions>\n\n                       <field events>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Application file\n\n   Concept 4GL contains a few declarations that can be defined ahead of the\n   first application component in a Concept 4GL source file. These\n   declarations will apply to every application component (sub application)\n   in the source file.\n\n   Application component\n\n   Every Concept 4GL application has to contain one (and only one)\n   application component. The main purpose of the application component is to\n   indicate whether the application is a screen, i.e. an ONLINE application,\n   or a report, i.e. an XTRA application. The LAYOUT keyword is used to\n   define that the source file only contains Form and Element component\n   declarations which are referred to from within one or more ONLINE or XTRA\n   applications (a file containing the LAYOUT application component is often\n   referred to as an \'external form file\').\n\n   The application properties define permanent properties of an application.\n   Examples of this may be to specify legal illegal user commands on\n   application level in order to modify the functionality of the application.\n\n   Stream component\n\n   If Concept is to know where to send the result of data processing, and in\n   what format, you must specify a stream component. Or, if you want to\n   design a screen dialogue, you need a stream component that then represents\n   a window on a computer screen. Concept is able to handle several output\n   units in the same application at the same time. In XTRA reports you may\n   specify up to 16 different output units. Each of them is responsible for\n   one of the data streams out of the application. In addition, a stream can\n   be used to read data from a file so that its content can be processed in\n   the application. In ONLINE applications, one (and only one) stream\n   component needs to be defined.\n\n   A stream does not physically need to be a unit. It may just as well be a\n   file to which you transmit data (e.g. a file in HTML format that has to be\n   published on the Internet).\n\n   The stream properties define attributes of the stream. Examples of stream\n   properties for XTRA reports may be specification of page width and length,\n   top and bottom margins, etc. In an ONLINE application you may define\n   screen colours, window frames, scroll-bars, etc.\n\n   Form component\n\n   In most applications you need to program either a screen dialogue or a\n   report in order to present your data. To do this in Concept, you must\n   specify a form component. A form is then defined to be an area of a report\n   or screen layout which is always written as one unit. Examples of\n   different form components needed in an XTRA report are page headers, forms\n   for each row found in a table, tails including sums etc. In an ONLINE\n   application, a form groups the visual items (called \'elements\') that are\n   placed on it together, and often visualizes this by drawing a frame around\n   the items. A form can be just a rectangular area in an ONLINE application,\n   but it can also be a tabulated form or a grid-form.\n\n   Form properties define attributes of a form. For example, that the form\n   should be treated as a page heading or that it should always start on a\n   new page. For ONLINE applications, forms can have attributes that relate\n   to tabulation or visual appearance of a form.\n\n   Element component\n\n   Elements are the visual items in a report or on the screen. A push-button\n   is an element, a text string is an element, and so on. Most elements can\n   be used in both ONLINE and XTRA applications, some are only suitable for\n   ONLINE (for example a push-button). Elements are always owned by a form\n   and by one form only.\n\n   Database component\n\n   The database component instructs the application as to which database to\n   use. The database component is a passive definition, and its main purpose\n   is to prepare the database used by the table components and field\n   components in the application.\n\n   An application may handle data from several databases, and you must\n   therefore declare all the databases you wish to use.\n\n   In addition to using the database component in the application, you must\n   be sure that the database(s) exist(s) and is/are properly defined in\n   Concept\'s configuration file uqconfig.\n\n   Table component\n\n   The table component specifies which table(s) to employ in your application\n   and which properties and functions you attach to them. In a 4GL source\n   code file, a table component must be placed after the appropriate database\n   component. Therefore, the table component always belongs to the most\n   recently declared database component.\n\n   An application may access several tables. It is always the most recently\n   used table which the application considers as active. If you use a table\n   from another database, you must remember to declare the related database\n   component first.\n\n   It is possible to extend the table component\'s functionality by adding\n   functions to its declaration.\n\n   Examples of table component properties are access rights, sorting orders,\n   and automatic caching.\n\n   Field component\n\n   Fields are the data items in an application. A field can be a stand-alone\n   variable of type integer (or any of the other data types available), or it\n   can be related to a database table in which case it represents a column in\n   the table. When functions are added to the declaration, the field\n   component can be considered as a procedure definition that can be called\n   using the 4GL function execute().\n\n   Fields (not being declared to be local, static or global) that are defined\n   following a table component declaration, are mapped to those table columns\n   that have the same name as the fields. When a record is retrieved from the\n   database table, these fields will contain the values of the database\n   record.\n\n   Examples of field component properties are storage code, data range,\n   letter type, etc.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [21][IMG]\n\n   Functions\n\n   Functions are services that are called upon to execute specific\n   operations. For example to fetch and display a row from a database table,\n   delete a table row, display a dialogue box, play a video, and so on. A\n   grouped sequence of one or more functions is called a procedure. The\n   Concept 4GL language includes functions for database operations, text\n   manipulation, conditional and iterative execution, calculations, menu\n   construction and a lot more.\n\n   As explained in a previous section, functions can be coupled to a field\n   component. These field functions can be activated by using the 4GL\n   execute() function, but they will also be activated automatically when the\n   field value changes. This means that when the user enters a new value in\n   the field (that is represented in an application by an element), the\n   field-functions will be executed.\n\n   The Concept 4GL language also offers event handling for all kinds of\n   events. 4GL functions can be used inside the event handlers in the same\n   way as functions for a field component. An event handler could also call\n   field functions (and event handlers can be called using the\n   perform-event() function). Events occur as a result of a user action (like\n   moving the elevator in a scroll-bar) or \'automatically\' (like the timer\n   event). The event handler indicates what kind of event it handles in its\n   declaration that starts with the keyword on and ends with endon.\n\n   The component table above shows which components have event handlers\n   defined. For most events, there exists a default event handler - but this\n   event handler can always be overridden by a user-specific handler. The\n   default event-handler can then be called by using the 4GL function\n   perform-event().\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [22][IMG]\n\n   General syntax rules\n\n   This section briefly describes a few general syntax rules to be applied in\n   a Concept 4GL program.\n\n   Comments\n\n   The \'*\' character is used to specify a comment. Everything following \'*\'\n   on the same line will be ignored, except when used inside quotes or inside\n   brackets This is done to allow expressions containing the multiply (*) or\n   the exponent operator (**).\n\n   Empty lines are allowed everywhere in a 4GL program and do not need the\n   comment character.\n\n   Names\n\n   The names of databases, fields, streams, forms etc. may or may not be\n   enclosed by double quotes. If a name contains blanks or non- alphanumeric\n   characters, the name must be enclosed in double quotes.\n\n   Examples:\n\n   \xc2\xa0field=Customer_name\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="Customer\xc2\xa0name"\n\n   If the double quotes are not used, then a name may only consists of\n   letters, digits or the underscore. If the name is enclosed in\n   double-quotes, it may consist of any printable characters except @ and #.\n\n   Abbreviations\n\n   Keywords can be abbreviated as long as they are not ambiguous. We\n   recommend avoiding abbreviations, as they may be ambiguous in future\n   releases when new keywords are introduced.\n\n   Brackets\n\n   Brackets are used in two situations:\n\n   1) To enclose the parameters of a function:\n\n   \xc2\xa0dialogue-box(title(\'Error\'),\xc2\xa0buttons(\'OK/CANCEL\'))\n\n   In expressions to control the order of evaluation:\n\n   \xc2\xa0assign(Amount\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0A\xc2\xa0*\xc2\xa0(B\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0C))\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_la_anyfunction.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/callback_elements.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_application_declaration.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_applfile\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_appldefinition\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_online.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_streamdefinition\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_formdefinition\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_elementdefinition\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_databasedefinition\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_database.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_tabledefinition\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm#idh_ma_application_fielddefinition\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_appldecl_decl.htm\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_appldecl_fct.htm\n'

b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                     Unique Character Set                                side\n\n   Description of the internal character set used in Concept. The\n   abbreviation UCS (Unique Character Set) is used to refer to this\n   definition. The relationship between UCS and external character sets used\n   in file formats and databases is also described.\n\n   Definition\n\n   Each character is identified by a value between 32 and 255. In the table\n   this value is found by adding the number in the top row to the number in\n   the left column.\n\n   Example: uppercase A has value 64+1 = 65.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0  32 48 64 80 96 112 128 144 160 176 192 208 224 240\n   0  \xc2\xa0  0  @  P  `  p   \xef\xbf\xbd   \xc2\xa0   \xc2\xa0   \xc2\xb0   \xc3\x80   \xc2\xa0   \xc3\xa0   \xc2\xa0\n   1  ! O  _  o  \xc2\xa0   \xc2\xa0   \xef\xbf\xbd   \xc2\xaf   \xc2\xbf   \xc3\x8f   \xc3\x9f   \xc3\xaf   \xc3\xbf\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [4]Textual representation.\n\n   Notes:\n\n   \xc2\xb7The range 0 - 31 is reserved for internal use.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Values 127,129,141,143,144 and 157 are undefined.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Value 32 is the space character.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Value 160 is the non-break space character.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Value 173 is the soft hyphen character.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Not all Window fonts is capable of showing the characters in the range\n   between 128 and 159.\n\n   Standards\n\n   UCS is the same as the ANSI Windows CP-1252 character set, which is\n   identical to ISO 8859-1 Latin1 with the exception of the characters in the\n   range between 128 and 159 (these characters are undefined in ISO8859/1).\n\n   Sorting order\n\n   Sorting of UCS character is predefined in Concept and is used in\n   expressions when using the lexical "greater than" and "smaller than"\n   operators.\n\n   This sorting order is also used in the order-by function, but may be\n   overruled by the sort parameter. This parameter refers to a setup file\n   with extension .USO where customized sorting can be defined. Syntax rules\n   for such files are described in Visma Enterprise Concept Operations Guide.\n   The standard installation includes UQNC<lang>.USO files for case\n   insensitive sorting.\n\n   Note that sorting of indexes, as well as order-by done in databases have\n   their own rules for sorting order. Consult your database documentation for\n   details.\n\n   Mapping to external character sets\n\n   When reading from or writing to files used with other products it is often\n   necessary to convert UCS to and from other character sets. The same\n   applies when querying and updating databases.\n\n   This conversion is done by writing a filter file. Filter files describe\n   relationship between characters in UCS and other character sets. The\n   definitions of such files are found in Visma Enterprise Concept Operations\n   Guide. The files are located under the setup directory and have .UCS\n   extension. The file names reflect the character set name.\n\n   Concept standard installation includes filters for some common characters\n   sets:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIIUS7 bit standard US ASCII character set.\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIIDK7 bit national character set, Denmark\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIIEN7 bit national character set, England\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIIGE7 bit national character set, Germany\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIINO7 bit national character set, Norway\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCIISW7 bit national character set, Sweden\n\n   \xc2\xb7ASCII7 bit national character set using the language in the current\n   session. The character set used will be one of the ASCII sets over.\n\n   \xc2\xb7I8859_1ISO 8859/1 Latin1\n\n   \xc2\xb7I8859_15ISO 8859/15 Latin9\n\n   \xc2\xb7DECMCSDEC multinational character set\n\n   \xc2\xb7ROMAN8HP Roman 8 character set\n\n   \xc2\xb7CP850IBM CP 850. Character set used by MS-DOS and OS/2.\n\n   \xc2\xb7MACCharacter set used on MACINTOSH computers.\n\n   Mapping to files\n\n   The character set is only one attribute of a file format. Filter files can\n   only be used as converters for plain 8 bit files. For file formats like\n   Word Perfect, UNIPLEX and Microsoft Word, Concept has more complex\n   converters linked with the program module.\n\n   When writing to files in the internal Editor, the Save As dialogue\n   includes a file format field where the character set can be changed.\n\n   When writing to files through streams, the file-format declaration may be\n   used to specify the file format and the character set.\n\n   When reading files, the more complex file formats are detected\n   automatically by analyzing the file header. In the case of plain files\n   this is not possible and a different method of identification is required\n\n   In Concept the character set is linked to the file extension for\n   identifying the character set used in the file. For instance "FILE1.850"\n   is a code page 850 file and "FILE2.UCS" a UCS file. The relationships\n   between file extensions and character sets are defined in the file\n   uqdio.ini in section PLAIN. This file is explained in Visma Enterprise\n   Concept Operations Guide.\n\n   Mapping to database objects\n\n   The relationship between database character sets and UCS is defined in the\n   file uqconfig under databases using the db-charset definition. db-charset\n   refers to a filter file. All object names (tables, columns etc) and\n   character fields will be converted according to this definition. If this\n   definition is inconsistent with the database itself, the database can very\n   easily be corrupted.\n\n   The uqconfig file is explained in Visma Enterprise Concept Operations\n   Guide.\n\n   Displaying and printing\n\n   Terminals, display screens and printers have different capabilities for\n   presenting characters from UCS. Most of these devices will lack some of\n   the characters in the UCS. On output, a replacement character (like & or )\n   is used instead.\n\n   On input, all characters are possible, but the echo may be a replacement\n   character as described above. The character will be stored correctly, even\n   when not shown as expected.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/callback_elements.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compileroptions.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_textual_ucs.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Compiler Options                                  side\n\n   Compiler options define properties for the Concept 4GL Compiler. The\n   options are stored in the concept.ini file, section 4GLCompiler, and are\n   read by the compiler on startup. The concept.ini file may be edited using\n   any text editor, or the compiler options settings may be changed using the\n   Compiler Options dialogue - invoked through the Compiler Tool menu\n   Options/Compiler. Compiler options may also be set in a system compilation\n   file using the $option command.\n\n   Available options\n\n   The available options as they appear in the concept.ini file are:\n\n   Archive=<ArchiveFile>\n\n   This option can be used in system compilation files. All files compiled\n   after the option is set will be written to the ArchiveFile specified. The\n   archive file will be written to the object path. The default extension for\n   archive files is "UCA".\n\n   ArchiveImageAdd=<ImageFile>\n\n   This option can be used in system compilation files. The image file will\n   be written to the current ArchiveFile specified. The file MUST exist on\n   the current image-path.\n\n   AutoFindOnJoin=ON|OFF\n\n   The option specifies whether the compiler should automatically add the\n   default FIND functionality when a join function is placed on field level.\n\n   BackwardCompatible=ON|4.10\n\n   The BackwardCompatible option is automatically set to ON if\n   start-form/endform syntax is encountered in an application. Thereby old\n   language syntax and semantics and execution rules are forced at both\n   compilation and runtime. The definition of "old" is "as in version\n   4.00.00", unless BackwardCompatible is set to 4.10 whereby "old" is\n   defined "as in version 4.10.00".\n\n   BrowserInfo=OFF|ON|FULL\n\n   The option specifies whether the compiler should write a browse\n   information file for the application. If the option is active, such a file\n   will be written to the object path along with the object file. Browse\n   information files have the extension UBI and contain structural\n   information about the source file which can i.e. be used to produce a\n   system documentation. FULL browse information contains information about\n   functions in the source code in addition to information about object\n   definitions.\n\n   DynamicTextHeight=ON|OFF\n\n   The option specifies whether text labels found inside start-form/end-form\n   should get a dynamic height or not. If set to OFF text labels will be\n   given a height of 1.\n\n   ErrorWarningLevel=-1|0|1|2|3|4\n\n   The option specifies whether warning messages with a certain severity\n   should be reported as errors. When set to -1, no warning messages will be\n   reported as errors. All other values will result in error messages for\n   warnings with that level and higher levels.\n\n   FieldWidthThreshold=<Number>\n\n   When a field with a visible width less or equal to <Number> is found\n   inside start-form/end-form the following width is assigned the connected\n   element:\n\n   Width = FldWidth + 1 + (1 - FldWidth/<Number>)\n\n   The default value is 0.\n\n   ProtectAppl=OFF|ON\n\n   The option specifies whether the application should be protected or not. A\n   protected application may not be "disassembled", that means the source\n   code may not be regenerated from the object file and the debugger may not\n   be used to trace the execution of a protected application.\n\n   SkipApplicationTests=OFF|ON\n\n   The option specifies whether the test application ($TEST_APPLICATION <sub\n   application name>,<Test OK result>) should be called after successful\n   compilation.\n\n   SystemAppl=OFF|ON\n\n   The option specifies whether the application should be marked as system\n   application. A system application can only be run from a Concept tool.\n\n   TextCompatibility=OFF|ON\n\n   The option specifies whether elements should inherit visual attributes\n   from the form owning them.\n\n   WarningLevel=0|1|2|3|4\n\n   The option specifies the severity of compiler warnings written to the\n   compiler output file. When the warning level is set to 0 (the highest\n   warning level), only the most severe warning messages will be produced.\n   When set to 4, all warning messages will be written.\n\n   The $OPTION command\n\n   Compiler options may be temporarily changed in a system compilation file\n   using the $option command. The command takes a compiler option setting as\n   its argument in exactly the same syntax as written in the concept.ini\n   file.\n\n   Example : $option ProtectAppl=on\n\n   The Compiler Options Dialogue\n\n   The compiler options dialogue has corresponding entries for each of the\n   available options.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_characterset.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_cursor_def.htm\n'

[8]?[9]resourceId )\n\n   Remarks\n\n   \xc2\xb7The <fileName> should consist of both path and file extension. b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        Display Codes                                    side\n\n   A general description of display codes, which are used to indicate how\n   field values are to be displayed.\n\n   General Format Codes\n\n   The following codes may be used in any display code definition:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Code Description\n        (Single quote) Indicates that the corresponding positions in the\n   '    display string should be occupied by the text following. At the end\n        of the text string there must be another single quote character (').\n   /    Equivalent to '/'\n   0    Equivalent to '0' (zero)\n   B    Equivalent to ' '\n        Indicates a repetition. It may be used after the following field\n   (n)  format codes: B, 0, comma, - , +, $, *, 9, Z,and X. n must be an\n        integer giving the number of repetitions of the preceding symbol.\n        Indicates left justification.\n\n        Note: Left justified numbers with leading sign should not use the Z\n   <    display code. Instead use the - or + display codes repeated. E.g. use\n        \xef\xbf\xbd<----9\xef\xbf\xbd instead of \xef\xbf\xbd<ZZZZ9\xef\xbf\xbd and \xef\xbf\xbd<++++9\xef\xbf\xbd instead of \xef\xbf\xbd<+ZZZ9\xef\xbf\xbd. Also\n        note that left justified numbers with trailing sign will not justify\n        the sign.\n   >    Indicates right justification. This is default for numeric fields.\n   ><   Indicates center justification.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Numeric Fields\n\n   The following codes may be used in display codes for numeric fields:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Code Description\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the data (which\n        must be a number). A leading zero in this position will be displayed\n        as a blank.\n   Z\n        Note: Left justified numbers with leading sign should normally not\n        use the Z display code. Instead use the - or + display codes\n        repeated. E.g. use \xef\xbf\xbd<----9\xef\xbf\xbd instead of \xef\xbf\xbd<ZZZZ9\xef\xbf\xbd and \xef\xbf\xbd<++++9\xef\xbf\xbd instead\n        of \xef\xbf\xbd<+ZZZ9\xef\xbf\xbd.\n   9    As Z above, but a leading zero in this position will be displayed as\n        a '0' (zero).\n        The sign '+' before or after a number indicates that the position\n   +    gets a minus (-) when the data item is negative or a plus (+)\n        otherwise.\n        The sign '-' before or after a number indicates that the\n        corresponding position in the display string will display a minus\n        sign if the number is negative, or a blank if positive.\n\n        If there is more than one minus, the additional minuses have the same\n   -    meaning as the Z, except that the sign will be moved towards the\n        first non-blank digit.\n\n        It is illegal to use Z, * or $ in the same string when more than one\n        minus is given. Every 9 must be preceded by a minus in the display\n        code.\n        Decimal point specifies the position of the decimal point. Only one\n        occurrence is allowed. Positions for decimals must be indicated when\n        a decimal point is used.\n\n        The character displayed depends of the setting of the decimal-point\n   .    parameter in the system section of the uqconfig. The default value of\n        this parameter depends on the language used for the Concept session.\n        To force Concept to display a certain character instead of the one\n        defined in the uqconfig, use the modifier '\\.' followed by the\n        character to display (e.g. '\\.:' to display a ':' instead of the\n        standard decimal point)\n        Number group separator is used to separate groups of digits within a\n        number.\n\n        The character displayed depends of the setting of the decimal-point\n   ,    parameter in the system section of the uqconfig. The default value of\n        this parameter depends on the language used for the Concept session.\n        To force Concept to display a certain character instead of the one\n        defined in the uqconfig, use the modifier '\\,' followed by the\n        character to display (e.g. '\\,;' to display a ';' instead of the\n        standard group separator)\n        This indicates the same as Z above , but a leading zero in this\n        position will be displayed as a '*', i.e. it is used to fill the\n        empty space with asterixes.\n   *\n        Note: When the result is displayed in an element in a dialogue or\n        printer output, it will only produce the expected result when the\n        element uses a fixed size font and the element size corresponds to\n        the display length.\n        Substituting Z's by $'s moves text before the $ to the right, toward\n        the first significant digit within the number.\n   $\n        Warning: This is functionality is not fully implemented yet and may\n        thus not give the expected result.\n        Is used to split positive and negative numbers into two separate\n        columns. The negative numbers will appear in the right column and the\n        positive in the left. This field format is often used to split debit\n   >>>  and credit sides of an account or balance sheet.\n\n        Warning: This is functionality is not fully implemented yet and may\n        thus not give the expected result.\n        This has the same function as >>> except that negative numbers will\n        appear in the left column and the positive numbers in the right\n        column. \xc2\xa0The display code following >>> or <<< indicates the size of\n   <<<  one column. Concept duplicates this size to make two separate\n        columns.\n\n        Warning: This is functionality is not fully implemented yet and may\n        thus not give the expected result.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Alphanumeric Fields\n\n   The following codes may be used in display codes for text fields:\n\n   Code Description\n   X    Indicates a position to be filled with a character from the data\n        (which must be alphanumeric text).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Date and Time Fields\n\n   The following codes may be used in display codes for date and time fields:\n\n   Code Description\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the day number in\n   D    a date or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the month number\n        in a date or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n\n   M    Note:\n\n        As long as M is used in a display code using only time codes (H, T\n        and S), it is interpreted as minute instead of month for backward\n        compatibility reasons. We recommend to use T whenever the minute is\n        to be displayed.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the year number\n   Y    in a date or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the week number\n   W    in a week value. A leading zero in this position will be displayed as\n        a zero.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the hour in a\n   H    time or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the minute in a\n   T    time or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n        Indicates a position to be filled with a digit from the second in a\n   S    time or datetime value. A leading zero in this position will be\n        displayed as a zero.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The display code is a sequence of field format codes. There has to be one\n   field format code for each position in the field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Normally, if the display code is shorter than the data to be displayed,\n   the data will be truncated.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Each * or Z in the display code must be to the left of every 9 in the\n   display code. Z and * cannot both be used in the same display code.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The position of the sign (- or +) is changed when using the display code\n   in the display [4]field or [5]element declaration. It will not be in the\n   position defined in the display code, but will be aligned with the value\n   displayed. Spaces between the sign and the value will be removed. The\n   position of the sign is preserved when using display codes with the format\n   [6]operator or when field/element values are used in situations where the\n   length of the resulting text is important (i.e. when writing formatted\n   files).\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the date display codes D, M or Y in the [7]field declaration\n   display will make sure that a date value entered in the order 'DDMMYYYY'\n   will be stored in reversed order (YYYYMMDD) for correct comparison and\n   sorting.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the week display codes W or Y in the [8]field declaration display\n   will make sure that a week value entered in the order 'WWYYYY' will be\n   stored in reversed order (YYYYWW) for correct comparison and sorting.\n\n   [9][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_cursor_def.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dio.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorstext\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm#idh_ma_field_display\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm#idh_ma_field_display\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_displaycodes.htm\n"
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                    Document Input/Output                                side\n\n   A set of file-format independent macros that are interpreted on reading\n   and converted when writing to a specific file-format. Some of the macros\n   are replaced by text, while others control the format and layout of a\n   result document. Use these macros to build a set of portable file\n   templates, e.g. initial documents that can be used in the editor command.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   <Lead-In\xc2\xa0Character><Macro\xc2\xa0Name>[,<Parameter>]*;\n\n   Lead-In Character\n\n   A special character that defines the start of a macro. Initially this\n   character is '^'. It can be changed at any time using the LI macro. When\n   used in layouts, the initial lead-in character may be declared in the\n   application header using the lead-in-character command.\n\n   Macro Name\n\n   Most macros have a two letter name. The possible names are defined below.\n   Some of the macros also have a full name as an alias.\n\n   Parameter\n\n   Macro parameter. The parameters depend on the macro in use.\n\n   Text macros\n\n   ^DA[,<DisplayCode>];\n\n   Replaced by today's date in the specified [4]display code. The default\n   display code is language dependent.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^IMG,<FieldName>,<Height>,<Width>[,<Options>];\n\n   Replaced by the [5]image definition in the value of the specified field.\n   The height and width are specified in Points (1 Point = 1/72 Inch =\n   2.56/72 Cm). Additional [6]image options can be specified in the options\n   part.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^LT,<LDTReference>;\n\n   Whenever an [7]LDT reference is used, Concept will try to fetch the text\n   referenced from the file specified in the System Database. When no text\n   with the specified number exists, or the file specified in the LDT\n   definition could not be found, an error message will be returned.\n\n   When the LDT file name used is not defined for the current language,\n   Concept will try to use the definition in the English section\n   (LDT-FILE-EN) by default.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^NPG[,<DisplayCode>];\n\n   Replaced by the total number of pages in the specified [8]display code.\n   The default is '<ZZZZZZ9'. The NPG macro returns zero (formatted) if the\n   total number of pages is not available. The NPG macro is only applicable\n   for streams that are using one of the [9]print-modes DELAYED,CONFIRMED or\n   PREVIEW.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^PN[,<DisplayCode>];\n\n   Replaced by the current page number in the specified [10]display code. The\n   default is '<ZZZZZZ9'.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^TI[,<DisplayCode>];\n\n   Replaced by the current time in the specified [11]display code. The\n   default display code is language dependent.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^UQ,<FieldOrMacro>[,<Length>];\n\n   Replaced by the contents of the field or macro specified. The following\n   values are allowed:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FieldOrMacro                           Result\n   The name of a field in the current     Returns the value of the field.\n   application\n   @GLOBAL(<name of a global alphanumeric Returns the value of the global\n   field>)                                field.\n   @ENVIRONMENT(<environment variable>)   Returns the value of the\n                                          environment variable.\n   @EXPRESSION(<[12]expression>)          Returns the result of the\n                                          expression evaluation.\n                                          Returns the value of the field\n                                          after it's functions have been\n   @COMPUTE(<[13]field name>[{,|=}<new    executed. If a new value is\n   value>])                               specified, the value will be\n                                          assigned before executing the\n                                          field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The optional length parameter specifies the length of the resulting string\n   as follows:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Length Result\n   < 0    Remove trailing spaces.\n   = 0    The storage length of the field. (Default)\n   > 0    The string will be truncated or padded with spaces to the specified\n          length.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^UQHTML,<FieldOrMacro>[,<Length>];\n\n   Replaced by the contents of the field or macro specified converted to an\n   HTML conformant text (see [14]to_html operator). The following values are\n   allowed:\n\n   Replaced by the contents of the field or macro specified. The following\n   values are allowed:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FieldOrMacro                           Result\n   The name of a field in the current     Returns the value of the field.\n   application\n   @GLOBAL(<name of a global alphanumeric Returns the value of the global\n   field>)                                field.\n   @ENVIRONMENT(<environment variable>)   Returns the value of the\n                                          environment variable.\n   @EXPRESSION(<[15]expression>)          Returns the result of the\n                                          expression evaluation.\n                                          Returns the value of the field\n                                          after it's functions have been\n   @COMPUTE(<[16]field name>[{,|=}<new    executed. If a new value is\n   value>])                               specified, the value will be\n                                          assigned before executing the\n                                          field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The optional length parameter specifies the length of the resulting string\n   as follows:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Length Result\n   < 0    Remove trailing spaces.\n   = 0    The storage length of the field. (Default)\n   > 0    The string will be truncated or padded with spaces to the specified\n          length.\n\n   Layout macros\n\n   ^BL,{+|-};\n\n   Turns the 'bold' ('emphasized') text attribute ON or OFF.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^CL,{FIELD|TEXT|INVISIBLE|<ColourCode>};\n\n   Sets the colour of the leading text. For a description of parameters, see\n   the section on [17]colour. Note that colours are not supported for all\n   printers.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^FN,<Font>;\n\n   Sets the character font for all following text up to the next FN macro.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^IT,{+|-};\n\n   Turns the 'italic' text attribute ON or OFF.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^LB,<Width>;\n\n   Sets the border (in element units) from the left side of the paper.\n\n   This macro has no effect on output to a printer.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^RB,<Width>;\n\n   Sets the border (in element units) from the right side of the paper.\n\n   This macro has no effect on output to a printer.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^UL,{+|-};\n\n   Turns the 'underlined' text attribute ON or OFF.\n\n   Other macros\n\n   ^BN,<SourceTrayNumber>;\n\n   Changes the [18]source tray (bin) for the next page to be printed and all\n   following pages. This change is not effective unless a new page is to be\n   printed. If the source tray is changed again before a new page is printed,\n   the last tray specified will be used.\n\n   Please note that only source tray numbers are supported in the macro. Use\n   the [19]change-stream function to change the tray based on it's name.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^LI,<Character>;\n\n   Sets a new Lead-In Character.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^PG;\n\n   Forces a form feed (new page) to be generated.\n\n   This macro has no effect when the layout is specified in the source file\n   (between start-form and endform); you can use the form declarations\n   [20]top-of-page or [21]append-new-page in such situations.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The text macros can also be used inside the [22]text of elements. All\n   other macros may only be used in template files or in layouts specified\n   between the start-form and endform keywords in a [23]form definition.\n\n   \xc2\xb7One or more macros alone on a line will not generate a new line in the\n   result document/layout.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The space taken up by a macro (between the lead-in and lead-out\n   characters) does not take up any space in the result document.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The macros are expanded when:\n\n   othe file being read is the basis of a result document, i.e. during the\n   reading of initial-documents given in the [24]editor function.\n\n   othe file is connected to a form using the [25]file-name or\n   [26]wide-column declaration.\n\n   othe file is read by the compiler (4GL source files)\n\n   \xc2\xb7Note that Concept will convert documents read to an internal format\n   before sending it to a printer driver, which in turn converts the output\n   to a printer specific format. During this process, some formatting\n   information may be lost. The best output is therefore obtained by using\n   the external program that fully supports the file format being used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Note that if you use the [27]stream declaration formatting(DIRECT) (which\n   is the default), documents read will first be converted to PLAIN, and\n   almost all the formatting will be lost. Use formatting(NONE) for best\n   results.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The IMG macro only works if the result [28]file format is RTF.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_documentation_application.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm#idh_ma_images_definition\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm#idh_ma_images_definition\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldt.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_printmode\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_la_filename.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorstext\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_la_filename.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_styles.htm#idh_de_stylecolour\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_streambinin.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changestream.htm#idh_ma_changestream_binin\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_topofpage\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_appendnewpage\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_text\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm\n  24. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_editor.htm\n  25. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_filename\n  26. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_widecolumn\n  27. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm\n  28. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_fileformat\n"
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                  Documentation Application                              side\n\n   Documentation applications can be used in Quick to document single\n   applications (UCO files) or system (SYS files). By default Visma\n   Enterprise Concept Documentation is used for this task, but it is possible\n   to write your own applications to produce the documentation.\n\n   Application Interface\n\n   A documentation application must at least contain two sub-applications:\n   Actions and Main.\n\n   Actions\n\n   This sub-application is called by Quick to build the documentation menu.\n   It returns a list of menu texts and menu actions.\n\n   Export\n\nField   Storage  Description\n                 A list of actions supported by the application. The list must be defined\n                 using the following syntax:\n\n                 <MenuText>,<MenuInfo>,<MenuAction>[;<MenuText>,<MenuInfo>,<MenuAction>]*\n\nActions A(10240) The <MenuText> and <MenuInfo> will be shown in the Documentation menu in\n                 Quick. The <MenuAction> will be passed on the Main application when the\n                 menu entry is selected.\n\n                 The special menu action \'DEFAULT\' is associated with the accelerator key\n                 Ctrl+F7.\n\n   Main\n\n   This sub-application is started by Quick when an entry from the\n   documentation menu is selected. In this case the name of the current file\n   and the action associated with the menu entry are passed on to the\n   application.\n\n   Import\n\n   Field    Storage Description\n   FileName A(260)  Name of the current file in Quick.\n   Action   A(260)  Action text (as defined by the Actions sub-application)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The documentation menu in Quick is only available when a "runnable" file\n   is selected. Which file types (extensions) are "runnable" can be defined\n   in the Quick File Type options. In any case the full file name of the\n   selected file is imported. System compilation files (SYS files) are\n   considered runnable and are automatically generated when a number of files\n   is selected in the Quick Workspace. If a SYS file name is imported, all\n   applications listed in the SYS file should be documented.\n\n                           Application Documentation\n\n   One of the actions performed by the documentation application should be to\n   produce the documentation for the selected file. To perform this task, the\n   system application [4]@UQUDocApp can be used to analyse the code stored in\n   the UCO file. How the documentation is produced and how much information\n   from the tables you want to use is up to you.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n                                 Configuration\n\n   By default Quick uses Visma Enterprise Concept Documentation as the\n   documentation Application. Make Quick use your own application by defining\n   the name of the application in the Applications section of the System\n   Database (uqsystem.ini).\n\n   Example\n\n   [Applications]\n\n   Documentation=mydocapp\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [5][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dio.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_draganddrop.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_uqudocapp.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_example_documentation_application.htm\n'
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                    Drag and drop overview                               side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Concept supports parts of the Microsoft Windows drag and drop\n   functionality. Text values and filenames can be dragged out of or dropped\n   into a Concept application by just adding a few lines to your 4GL code,\n   support for OLE (Object Linking and Embedding) has not been added.\n\n   Adding drop functionality\n\n   In order to support dropping of objects into your application the\n   following things must be done:\n\n   1. Elements that should be able to act as a drop target must be defined as\n   one, either by using the [5]drop-types declaration or by using the\n   change-element function with the [6]drop-types parameter.\n\n   2. The DROP key event must be handled in the ON chain of the fields\n   connected to each of the elements.\n\n   3. Use the [7]drop function to retrieve the type and value of the dropped\n   object.\n\n   Adding drag functionality\n\n   In order to support dragging of objects from your application the\n   following things must be done:\n\n   1. Implement event handlers for the DRAG key. Only elements connected to\n   fields with a DRAG key event handler in it's ON chain can act as a drag\n   source. (This means that if on DRAG is implemented at application level,\n   all elements of a type that allows drag and that are connected to a field\n   will be able to support dragging in that application.)\n\n   2. Use the [8]drag function inside the DRAG event handler to initiate the\n   drag operation.\n\n   Special notes\n\n   \xc2\xb7Concept does not differ between drag operations initiated by the RIGHT or\n   the LEFT mouse button.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When dragging values from a multi-selection list box, use the RIGHT mouse\n   button to avoid the list box from deselecting the list box entry under the\n   mouse pointer.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The following element types can be used as a drag source : INPUT, OUTPUT,\n   LIST-BOX, DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX, TREEVIEW, PUSH-BUTTON, DEFAULT-BUTTON,\n   COOL-BUTTON, POPUP-BUTTON, COMBO-BUTTON, HEADER, MENU-ENTRY, IMAGE and\n   WINDOW.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Concept incorporates the de facto standard keyboard handling for drag and\n   drop operations. SHIFT button down while dragging means MOVE, CTRL button\n   down while moving means COPY, If no key is pressed while dragging and the\n   drag source allows both COPY and MOVE operations, COPY is preferred.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [9][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_documentation_application.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_types.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_drag_and_drop_functions.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_drop_types\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changeelement.htm#idh_ma_changeelement_drop_type\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_draganddrop.htm\n"
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        Element types                                    side\n\n   The following element types are handled in Concept 4GL.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   type(\xc2\xa0[4]APPLICATION\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [5]CALLBACK\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [6]CHECK-BOX\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [7]COMBO-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [8]COOL-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [9]DEFAULT-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [10]DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [11]DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [12]HEADER\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [13]HORIZONTAL-SCROLL-BAR\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [14]IMAGE\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [15]INPUT\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [16]LINE\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [17]LIST-BOX\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [18]MENU-ENTRY\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [19]OUTPUT\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [20]POPUP-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [21]PUSH-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [22]RADIO-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [23]TEXT\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [24]TREEVIEW\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [25]VERTICAL-SCROLL-BAR\xc2\xa0|\n\n   [26]WINDOW\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Image\n\n   An image element is used to show a bitmap [27]image. The following\n   attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       Uses the original size of the image and aligns the image\n                   inside the element boundaries.\n   background      \xc2\xa0\n   connect         If the connected field is alphanumeric, it\'s value is used\n                   as the image specification.\n   cursor          \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types      \xc2\xa0\n   focus-behaviour \xc2\xa0\n   frame           \xc2\xa0\n   image           \xc2\xa0\n   information     \xc2\xa0\n   label           \xc2\xa0\n   position        \xc2\xa0\n   show            \xc2\xa0\n   size            When calculating a dynamic size the size of the image is\n                   used.\n   style           \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index       \xc2\xa0\n\n   Line\n\n   A line is drawn between the points given by position and end-position. The\n   direction of the line is given by the values of position and end-position\n   and is used to select the pens used to draw complex line types as ENGRAVED\n   or EMBOSSED. The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Declaration  Notes\n   colour       The colour of the line. Not used for complex line types.\n   frame        The line type. The colour specification for frames are\n                ignored (use the colour attribute).\n   end-position \xc2\xa0\n   position     \xc2\xa0\n   show         \xc2\xa0\n   style        \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index    \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Cool-Button, Default-Button, Popup-Button, Combo-button,Header and\n   Push-Button\n\n   A button element is used to trigger the execution of functions on the\n   connected field when the button is clicked or when the Space or Enter key\n   are pressed while the button has the input focus.\n\n   Cool-Button, Default-Button, Header and Push-Button elements are nearly\n   equivalent. The differences between them are briefly discussed below.\n\n   A Cool-Button can not receive input focus and does not have a frame unless\n   the mouse pointer hovers over it.\n\n   A Default-Button is activated when pressing the Enter key. Visually it is\n   distinquished from a Push-Button by a surrounding black frame. There can\n   only be one Default-Button in a window.\n\n   A Header element is used as a grid-form column header and can only be used\n   inside forms of type GRID and must have a corresponding element that\n   refers to it by the label attribute. A header element has the same visual\n   appearance as a Push-Button.\n\n   A Popup-Button displays the connected popup menu when clicked, accessed by\n   the accelerator, the blowup command (ALT+DownArrow) or when the Space or\n   Enter key are pressed. Functions on the field connected to a popup-button\n   will never be activated by input in the popup-button directly. Programming\n   on [28]ACTIVATE on the connected field changes the behaviour slightly, the\n   accelerator key will now move focus to the popup-button and not display\n   the popup menu, unless focus is on the popup-button already, pressing\n   ENTER in the popup-button will trigger on ACTIVATE.\n\n   A Combo-Button is a combination of a Push-Button and a Popup-Button. When\n   the mouse is clicked in the rightmost part of the button it acts as a\n   Popup-button. When the mouse is clicked elsewhere or the Space or Enter\n   key is pressed it acts as a Push-Button.\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       \xc2\xa0\n   background      \xc2\xa0\n   colour          \xc2\xa0\n                   If connected to an alphanumeric field, it\'s value is used\n   connect         as the button text. The field connected to a Popup-Button\n                   or Combo-Button should have a popup menu declared.\n   cursor          \xc2\xa0\n   display         \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types      \xc2\xa0\n   focus-behaviour \xc2\xa0\n   font            \xc2\xa0\n   frame           The following frame types are supported : EMBOSSED,\n                   LIGHT-EMBOSSED and NONE.\n   image           See below.\n   information     \xc2\xa0\n   label           \xc2\xa0\n   lock            \xc2\xa0\n   multi-line      \xc2\xa0\n   position        \xc2\xa0\n   show            \xc2\xa0\n   size            \xc2\xa0\n   style           \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index       \xc2\xa0\n   text            See below.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The image specification for these-button types is assumed to include 4\n   images for visualizing the following states: not-pressed, pressed,\n   not-pressed with focus and locked. If only one image is specified it is\n   used for all of the states.\n\n   Multiple images can be specified in the following ways:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the dimension image modifier (e.g\n   image(\'@UQ!ED_EXIT,dimension(1,4)\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a semicolon separated image list (e.g.\n   image(\'buttonUp.bmp;buttonDown.bmp;buttonFocus.bmp;buttonLocked.bmp\'))\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the ? button-image modifier, which substitutes the question mark\n   with the following letters; U for the not pressed state (Up), D for the\n   pressed state (Down), F for the not pressed with focus state (Focus) and L\n   for the locked state (Locked). (E.g image(\'button?.bmp\') which is the same\n   as; image(\'buttonu.bmp;buttond.bmp;buttonf.bmp;buttonl.bmp\')).\n\n   \xc2\xb7\n\n   If the image attribute is used and the text attribute is not used, the\n   image is assumed to include the button frame when used on Default-Button,\n   Push-Button and Header elements (if the image does not include the frame,\n   one might use the @@ image prefix to instruct Concept to draw the button\n   frame).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   When both the image and the text attributes are specified, the appearance\n   of the button is defined by the alignment attribute as explained in the\n   following table:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Vertical  Horizontal Alignment Appearance\n   Alignment\n                                  The image is drawn above the text label.\n                                  Both the image and the text are centered\n             CENTER (other        horizontally and vertically. The size of\n   TOP       settings are         the image is adjusted to the size of the\n             ignored)             button only, thus if the image covers the\n                                  whole button, the text is drawn on top of\n                                  the image.\n                                  The image is drawn below the text label.\n                                  Both the image and the text are centered\n             CENTER (any other    horizontally and vertically. The size of\n   BOTTOM    setting is ignored)  the image is adjusted to the size of the\n                                  button only, thus if the image covers the\n                                  whole button, the text is drawn on top of\n                                  the image.\n                                  The image is drawn to the left of the text.\n   CENTER    CENTER               Both the image and the text are centered\n                                  horizontally and vertically.\n                                  The image is drawn to the left of the text.\n   CENTER    LEFT                 Both the image and the text are centered\n                                  vertically on the left side of the button.\n                                  The image is drawn to the right of the\n   CENTER    RIGHT                text. Both the image and the text are\n                                  centered vertically on the right side of\n                                  the button.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Menu-Entry\n\n   Menu-entries are used in the same way and for the same purpose as\n   push-buttons. However, menu-entries are "slimmer" than push-buttons, and\n   thus suitable for "stacking", i.e. showing multiple selection\n   alternatives. A mouse click in a menu-entry only executes the connected\n   field if the menu-entry already is current (has the input focus),\n   otherwise the menu entry is made current without executing the connected\n   field (a mouse click in a push-button will execute the connected field\n   immediately without making it current).\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       \xc2\xa0\n   background      \xc2\xa0\n   colour          \xc2\xa0\n   connect         If connected to an alphanumeric field, it\'s value is used\n                   as the menu-entry label.\n   cursor          \xc2\xa0\n   display         \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types      \xc2\xa0\n   focus-behaviour \xc2\xa0\n   font            \xc2\xa0\n   frame           \xc2\xa0\n   information     \xc2\xa0\n   label           \xc2\xa0\n   lock            \xc2\xa0\n   position        \xc2\xa0\n   show            \xc2\xa0\n   size            \xc2\xa0\n   style           \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index       \xc2\xa0\n   text            \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Check-Box\n\n   A check-box is used to show and manipulate a Boolean value (a value either\n   being true or false, on or off etc.). The corresponding state of a\n   check-box is checked and not-checked. If the check-box element is\n   connected to a field, a field value of 0 (zero) or \xef\xbf\xbd \xef\xbf\xbd (blank) is\n   interpreted as not-checked whilst any other value is interpreted as\n   checked. If the check-box is toggled, the connected field receives the\n   values 0 (zero) or 1 (one), respectively and the field\'s functions are\n   executed.\n\n   The list of supported attributes is the same as for radio-buttons.\n\n   Radio-Button\n\n   Radio-buttons appear as a set of small circles. When an radio-button is\n   set, a dot appears in the middle of the circle. A radio-button is normally\n   used to represent a single choice within a limited set of mutually\n   exclusive choices- the user can choose only one of a set of options.\n\n   A radio-button should be connected to a field which is part of a\n   radio-group (a group field with a values declaration).\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       Affects only the text position.\n   background      \xc2\xa0\n   colour          \xc2\xa0\n   connect         If connected to an alphanumeric field, it\'s value is used\n                   as the button text.\n   cursor          \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types      \xc2\xa0\n   focus-behaviour \xc2\xa0\n   font            \xc2\xa0\n   frame           The following frame types are supported : EMBOSSED,\n                   ENGRAVED and LINE.\n   image           See below.\n   information     \xc2\xa0\n   label           \xc2\xa0\n   lock            \xc2\xa0\n   multi-line      Enable multi line texts. When set to ON, the vertical\n                   alignment decides the position of the check-mark.\n   position        \xc2\xa0\n   show            \xc2\xa0\n   size            \xc2\xa0\n   style           \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index       \xc2\xa0\n   text            \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The image specification for check-boxes and radio-buttons is assumed to\n   include 5 or 6 images for visualizing the following states: not-selected,\n   selected, not-selected with focus, selected with focus, not selected\n   locked (optional) and selected locked.\n\n   Multiple images can be specified in the following ways:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the dimension image modifier (E.g\n   image(\'myCheckBox.bmp,dimension(1,6)\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a semicolon separated image list (E.g.\n   image(\'checkBoxNS.bmp;checkBoxS.bmp;checkBoxFNS.bmp;checkBoxFS.bmp;checkBoxLS.bmp\')).\n   Please note that only the five state variant is handled when using an\n   image list.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Drop-Down-Combo-Box\n\n   A drop-down combo box combines the characteristics of an input element\n   with a drop-down-list-box. The closed state of a drop-down-combo-box is\n   similar to that of a drop-down-list-box, except that the element accepts\n   normal input. When the user clicks the element\'s menu button, the list is\n   opened. When the user clicks the menu button a second time, chooses an\n   item in the list, or clicks another element, the list is closed.\n\n   When the element has the input focus, the DownArrow/UpArrow keys can be\n   used to select the next/previous value in the list without having to open\n   the list. The list is opened when the user presses Alt+DownArrow. The list\n   is closed when the user makes a selection in the list either by pressing\n   the Enter,Tab or Esc key, clicking the mouse or pressing Alt+DownArrow.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The list of supported attributes is the same as for drop-down-list-box.\n\n   Drop-Down-List-Box\n\n   Like a single-selection list box, a drop-down list box allows the\n   selection of a single item from a list. The difference is that the list is\n   displayed on demand. In its closed state, the control displays the\n   currently selected item in the list. When the user clicks the element\'s\n   menu button, the list is opened. When the user clicks the menu button a\n   second time, chooses an item in the list, or clicks another element, the\n   list is closed.\n\n   When the element has the input focus, the DownArrow/UpArrow or\n   RightArrow/LeftArrow keys can be used to select the next/previous item,\n   the Home/End keys can be used to select the first/last item in the list\n   without having to open the list. The list is displayed when the user\n   presses Alt+DownArrow and the list is closed when the user makes a\n   selection in the list either by pressing the Enter, Tab or Esc key,\n   clicking the mouse or pressing Alt+DownArrow.\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       \xc2\xa0\n   background      \xc2\xa0\n   colour          \xc2\xa0\n   connect         The values in the selection list are defined by the values\n                   declaration of the connected field.\n   cursor          \xc2\xa0\n   display         \xc2\xa0\n   drop-down-lines \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types      \xc2\xa0\n   focus-behaviour \xc2\xa0\n   font            \xc2\xa0\n   frame           \xc2\xa0\n                   The image specification for drop-down-list/combo-boxes\n   image           follows the same rules as for push-buttons, and is applied\n                   to the elements menu button.\n   information     \xc2\xa0\n   label           \xc2\xa0\n   lock            \xc2\xa0\n   multi-select    \xc2\xa0\n   position        \xc2\xa0\n   show            \xc2\xa0\n   size            \xc2\xa0\n   style           \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index       \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please note that the drop-down-lines, multi-select and font attributes\n   only affect the drop-down-list.\n\n   List-Box\n\n   A list box is designed for selecting one or more items from a list.\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute    Notes\n   background   Only colour backgrounds are supported.\n   colour       \xc2\xa0\n   connect      The values in the selection list are defined by the values\n                declaration of the connected field.\n   cursor       \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types   \xc2\xa0\n   font         \xc2\xa0\n   frame        \xc2\xa0\n   information  \xc2\xa0\n   lock         \xc2\xa0\n   multi-select \xc2\xa0\n   position     \xc2\xa0\n   show         \xc2\xa0\n   size         \xc2\xa0\n   style        \xc2\xa0\n   tab-index    \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Input\n\n   An element that shows a field value and allows changing the value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The list of supported attributes is the same as for the output element.\n\n   Output\n\n   An element that shows a field value but does not allow changing the value.\n   The cursor can be moved into an output element (if connected to a field)\n   and the text can be selected and copied to the clipboard.\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute       Notes\n   alignment       \xc2\xa0\n   background      When multi-line is set to ON, only solid colour\n                   backgrounds are supported.\n   colour          \xc2\xa0\n   connect         \xc2\xa0\n   cursor Each item consists of a label and an optional\n   bitmap image, and each item can have a list of sub-items (children)\n   associated with it. By clicking an item, the user can expand and collapse\n   the associated list of sub-items.\n\n   The separate chapter \'[29]Treeview Element\' contains detailed information\n   on treeviews.\n\n   The following attributes are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Attribute    Notes\n   background   Only solid colour backgrounds are supported.\n   branch-lines \xc2\xa0\n   buttons      \xc2\xa0\n   colour       \xc2\xa0\n   connect      \xc2\xa0\n   cursor       \xc2\xa0\n   drop-types   \xc2\xa0\n   edit-labels  \xc2\xa0\n   font         \xc2\xa0\n   frame        \xc2\xa0\n                The image property specifies the default images for\n                non-focused and focused items in the treeview, and must be\n                specified if images are to be shown in the treeview.
