b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         Expressions                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This chapter defines how to build Concept 4GL expressions. Expressions are\n   constructions denoting rules of computations for obtaining values of\n   variables and generating new values by the use of operators. Expressions\n   consist of OPERATORS and OPERANDS. An expression can be one of the\n   following:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [5]?[6]number\n\n   \'[7]?[8]textConstant\'\n\n   [9]?[10]fieldName\n\n   [11]?[12]fieldName( [13]?[14]numberExpression )\n\n   [15]?[16]fieldName( [17]?[18]numberExpression : [19]?[20]numberExpression\n   )\n\n   [21]?[22]operator\n\n   ( [23]?[24]expression )\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Each of these elements is described either in this section or in the\n   sections about variables and operators.\n\n   Operands\n\n   Constants\n\n   There are two types of constants: numeric constants and alphanumeric\n   (text) constants. A numeric constant is a sequence of characters \xef\xbf\xbd0\xef\xbf\xbd -\n   \xef\xbf\xbd9\xef\xbf\xbd, optionally prefixed with a sign character \xef\xbf\xbd-\xef\xbf\xbd or \xef\xbf\xbd+\xef\xbf\xbd and optionally\n   separated by the full stop character \xef\xbf\xbd.\xef\xbf\xbd representing the decimal point.\n\n   An alphanumeric constant is a sequence of characters enclosed by\n   apostrophes (single quotes). An apostrophe is represented inside an\n   alphanumeric constant by two consecutive apostrophes.\n\n   Examples of constants:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Numeric  Alphanumeric\n   12       \'APRIL\'\n   14121963 \'Smith, John\'\n   -24.5    \'John\'\'s car\'\n\n   Fields\n\n   Fields are referred to by field names. If a field name starts with a digit\n   or contains blanks or non-alphanumeric characters (except underscore), it\n   must be enclosed in double quotes, else a field name may or may not be\n   enclosed in double quotes.\n\n   Examples of field names:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Field name\n   RESULT\n   FIELD_B\n   "Current directory"\n   @DIRECTORY\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A complete field reference has the following syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <FieldName>[(<Index1>[,<Index2>])][(<From>:<To>)][#(<RepeatLine>)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <FieldName>\n\n   The name of a field as described above.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <Index1>, <Index2>\n\n   Can only be used on arrays: Indicates a single cell in the array. <Index2>\n   is only used for two dimensional arrays. <Index1> and <Index2> may be\n   expressions.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <From>, <To>\n\n   May only be used on alphanumeric fields: Indicates a range of characters\n   of the field from position <From> up to position <To> included. <From> and\n   <To> may be expressions. If <From> or <To> is a negative number (using \'<\'\n   equals to -1), then this is handled as a backwards offset from the last\n   non-blank character in the value of the field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   #<RepeatLine>\n\n   Integer expression which determines a specific repeat line when the field\n   belongs to a table that is repeated.\n\n   Operator precedence\n\n   The following list shows the operator precedence in descending order, the\n   highest precedence level is at the top Each paragraph denotes operators\n   with the same precedence. Operators that share the same precedence are\n   evaluated from left to right.\n\n   -(unary minus) OLD\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ABS ASCII ATAN CHAR COS DATE DATE_AS_TEXT DATEPART DAY DAYNUMBER\n   ENVIRONMENT FIELD FROM_CRLF FROM_HTML HIGHCHAR HOUR ISNULL ISNUMBER\n   KEYSTROKE LDT LENGTH LISTVALUE LN LOG LOWERCASE MAX_REPEAT MINUTE MONTH\n   MONTH_NAME MONTHNUMBER NAMECASE NUMBER PAGE RAND RECORD_STATE ROUND SECOND\n   SIN SQRT STATUS STATUS_TEXT STRING_COUNT STRING_TO_NUMBER STRING_IS_NUMBER\n   SYSTEM_SETTING TAN TEXTCASE TIME TIMEPART TO_CRLF TO_HTML TO_PLAIN TRIM\n   TRUNCATE UPPERCASE WEEKDAY WEEKNUMBER YEAR YEAR_AND_WEEK\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ** # SUBSTR WORD\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   * / DIV MOD POS STRING_POSITION STRING_VALUE\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   -(subtraction) & && &, + ADD_DAYS ADD_SECONDS DATETIME DAYS_BETWEEN FORMAT\n   INTEREST_DAYS LOCATE_FILE MAX MIN REPEAT SECONDS_BETWEEN\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   % IN JUSTIFY TOKEN TOKEN_VALUE\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   = > < >= <= <> MATCH CONTAINS :(range operator used by SUBSTR and IN)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   NOT\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   AND\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   OR\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Example:\n\n   According to the operator precedence the following expression:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   1+2-3*4/ABS(-2)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   is evaluated in the following sequence:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   -2      -> 2\n   ABS(-2) -> 2\n   3*4     -> 12\n   12/2    -> 6\n   1+2     -> 3\n   3-6     -> -3\n   -3\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [25][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_types.htm\n   2. b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       External layout                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   Keep the application logic separated from the application layout.\n\n   External layout is a method for separating the application logic from the\n   application layout, and leaves the programmer with a library of reusable\n   layout components. The inclusion of an external-defined layout is done\n   dynamically at run-time, and is fetched from a file from the layout-path,\n   defined in the uqconfig configuration file, or defined in the SECURITY\n   system.\n\n   The layout-path defined in the SECURITY system splits the path into a\n   public and a private area. The public area is used for customer default\n   and solution default layout. The private area is used for end user private\n   layout.\n\n   A system supervisor can easily allow an end user to modify an external\n   layout component by copying the layout component file to the users private\n   area, and give the user access to modifying external layout components in\n   the SECURITY system. The end user can then enter the Forms Painter and\n   make changes to the layout. Its equally easy for the system supervisor to\n   make changes to the system default layout, change the company logo,\n   telephone number or other customer specific information contained in the\n   external layout components.\n\n   The Forms Painter effectively lets the programmer reuse layout components,\n   export layout components to an external layout component file (Unique\n   Compiled Forms file, UCF), and define connections between local fields and\n   elements.\n\n   In prior versions of Concept the possibilities for separating the logic\n   from the layout where limited, leading to larger source code files when\n   using the element syntax. The external layout mechanism allows the\n   developer to create reusable layout components, and makes customized\n   layout easy. To take advantages of the new mechanism follow the recipe\n   given here.\n\n   Recipe\n\n   Enter the Forms Painter with an application, identify the forms suitable\n   for reuse or customer modifications, select the form and choose to export\n   the form to an external layout component file. If the application is an\n   XTRA application the form divider will change colour on the label tag, but\n   for an ONLINE application the change does not imply any visual changes.\n   When leaving the Forms Painter the corresponding files are updated. An\n   external layout component file can contain numerous form components\n   restricted by unique names.\n\n   When having a layout component that can be used in an application, just\n   enter the Forms Painter and choose to insert an 'external form'. The form\n   is inserted at the insertion point for ONLINE and as the last form in\n   XTRA. An external layout component is controlled in the same manner as a\n   normal form. In an ONLINE application it is possible to have a hierarchy\n   of forms, and such a hierarchy is also possible to both store and retrieve\n   from an external layout component file.\n\n   An [5]external layout component included into an application can be\n   protected from changes; specifying that the form is [6]read-only does\n   this. For XTRA, the position and connect to the elements are freely\n   adjustable, and for ONLINE the title as well.\n\n   Allowing the programmer to include an external layout component that is\n   dynamically loaded at runtime means that the compiler has no knowledge\n   about the elements in the external layout component. This implies that the\n   element names are not guaranteed to be unique within an application, and\n   this has impact on the dynamic element functions. The dynamic element\n   functions (create-, inquire-, change- and delete-element) are extended\n   with a new parameter to be able to specify in what form the element\n   resides.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_archive_files.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_external_layout.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_externalform\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_readonly\n"
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                 Unique Concept Archive Files                            side\n\n   Concept offers the option to save UCO and Image files into Unique Concept\n   Archive files (UCA). A UCA file is a collection of files zipped into a\n   single file, containing a Concept specific header for fast access to the\n   files inside the UCA.\n\n   Creating UCA files\n\n   The compiler option [4]Archive is used to create an UCA file during a\n   system compilation. The compiler option [5]ArchiveImageAdd can be used to\n   add an image file to the current UCA during a system compilation.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Concept 7.11-00 introduced the new utility applications @UQUCAManager and\n   @UQUCACreator for maintaining and creating UCA files. These applications\n   can be found in the tools menu of Quick.\n\n   Accessing UCA files\n\n   Using UCA files for UCO\'s at runtime is quite simple, just add the full\n   UCA name (including extension) to the application-path in uqConfig, and\n   Concept will use the UCA for retrieving the files.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Using images from UCA files are seemingly easy, \xc2\xa0Add the full UCA name to\n   the image path in uqConfig and Concept will use the UCA for retrieving the\n   files. It is also possible to to use <Full UCA Name>\\<Image Name> for\n   accessing the image. Images that resides in system UCA\'s (UCA files that\n   are located in the uco70 sub directory of the Unique Home Directory) are\n   accessed as @<System UCA Name><Image Name>. Please note that <System UCA\n   Name> is limited to two characters and should be specified without the UCA\n   extension!\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The [6]file-list function can be used to list the contents of an UCA file\n   simply by using the UCA file name instead of a directory name in the path\n   parameter.\n\n   The @UQUCAManager application\n\n   The UCAManager is an application for maintaining existing UCA files. It\n   allows adding, removing and deleting single files in an UCA file. To add a\n   new file to the UCA, simply press the button on the upper left side of the\n   grid and select the file you like to add. To update a single file in the\n   UCA, enter the Modify drop-down-comb-box for the file you like to update\n   and select or write the full path including the filename of the file to\n   replace the existing (must have the same name as the original file). To\n   the delete a file in the UCA, use the DELREC key combination (default\n   CTRL+D). When all changes are applied, press the Recreate button and the\n   UCAManager will unpack the UCA file, remove deleted files, add new and\n   substitute modified files before recreating the UCA file.\n\n   Please note that this will replace the original timestamp (written date)\n   for existing files in the UCA.\n\n   The @UQUCACreator application\n\n   The UCACreator is an application for creating UCA files. A selection of\n   files can also be saved as a "UCA project" that can be reused.\n\n   To add files to a UCA use the Add files combo button and choose to select\n   multiple files from disk or open a previously saved "UCA project". Use the\n   DELREC key combination (default CTRL+D) to remove files from the\n   selection.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout_external.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_externalservers.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compileroptions.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compileroptions.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filelist.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Definitions > External Server          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Drivers\xc2\xa0>                                                     til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n              External Server Driver Application                         side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   General\n\n   An external server is a non-Concept program that provides services to the\n   Concept run-time engine. The driver application is a Concept 4GL program\n   that provides the interface between the stream output produced by the\n   Concept run-time engine and an external server program.\n\n   This mechanism can be activated by the 4GL programmer by specifying the\n   @EXTERNAL macro in the file-name attribute of a stream declaration. It can\n   also be activated by end-users when they are prompted for the report\n   output destination printer/file name.\n\n   On output, this will cause Concept to write the data to a temporary file\n   which, in turn, is read by a special 4GL application, the external server\n   driver application. This 4GL application may then convert the data into\n   appropriate DDE commands which are "poked" to the DDE server specified; or\n   it may simply send the whole file unchanged.\n\n   External server driver applications may also be used to create files in\n   formats not directly supported by Concept. In this case no external server\n   program is needed - the driver application simply converts the interface\n   file to the appropriate file format.\n\n   The external server driver application is a standard 4GL application which\n   must contain the following sub-applications:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Output\n\n   \xc2\xb7Options\n\n   \xc2\xb7Properties\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   To make the driver known to a system it can either be named\n   \'UEX<DriverName>\' and placed in the \'UQ\' system application directory of a\n   Concept installation (\'$UNIQUE_HOME\\uco<ConceptMainVersion>\\uq\') or -\n   preferable - defined in the \'ExternalDrivers\' section of the uqsystem.ini\n   file.\n\n   Output sub-application\n\n   The Output sub-application passes the raw data produced by a standard\n   Concept report to the external server program. It reads and interprets the\n   file supplied as input parameter and feeds the destination server program\n   with data.\n\n   Import\n\n   Name          Storage code       Purpose\n                                    Name of the interface file which contains\n   InterfaceFile alphanumeric(256)  the report output. The file format used\n                                    in this file is determined by the\n                                    Properties sub-application\n                                    Comma separated list of interface\n   Option        alphanumeric(1024) specific options (extracted from the\n                                    @external() file name string)\n\n   Export\n\n   Name       Storage code      Purpose\n   StatusText alphanumeric(256) Status of the operation. Empty if OK, else a\n                                text describing the error\n\n   Options sub-application\n\n   The Options sub-application is called by the Printer Selection Dialogue to\n   aid the user in setting the options for this interface. It uses the same\n   format for the Option string in the Output sub-application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Import\n\n   Name       Storage code       Purpose\n   Parameters alphanumeric(1024) Parameter string as supplied in the\n                                 @external() file name\n\n   Export\n\n   Name       Storage code       Purpose\n   Parameters alphanumeric(1024) Parameter string as supplied in the\n                                 @external() file name\n\n   Properties sub-application\n\n   The Properties sub-application returns information about the server\n   interface application to the Printer Selection Dialogue. When this\n   application is not present, default values will be used. This also applies\n   for fields not exported.\n\n   Export\n\n   Name       Storage code      Purpose\n   Heading    alphanumeric(30)  Descriptive name of the driver to be\n                                presented to end-users.\n   ServerName alphanumeric(30)  Not used.\n                                File-format that Concept Run-Time will use\n                                when generating the interface file\n                                (InterfaceFile in the Output\n   FileFormat alphanumeric(30)  sub-application). Note that this will\n                                override the file-format specified on the\n                                stream. The default value is \'UEF\' (Unique\n                                Element File Format). Other formats supported\n                                are RTF and CSV.\n                                Type of the driver. An arbitrary text that\n                                can be used to group certain types of drivers\n   DriverType alphanumeric(30)  (e.g. WORDPROCESSING or SPREADSHEET). If no\n                                driver type is exported, the default value is\n                                \'UNKNOWN\'.\n                                Icon to be displayed in the list of drivers\n                                shown in the standard [5]Ask Stream Dialogue.\n   Icon       alphanumeric(256) The icon definition must follow the rules for\n                                icon definitions used in [6]listviews. A\n                                standard icon is displayed when the Icon\n                                parameter is empty.\n                                A value different from 0 will cause the\n                                standard Ask Stream Dialogue to exclude the\n   Status     integer2          driver from the list of available drivers.\n                                Such a status value should be returned when\n                                an external application needed by the driver\n                                is not installed on the current system.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_archive_files.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_externalexcel.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_external_server_driver.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_streamfilename.htm#idh_ma_streamfilename_interactive\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_listview.htm#idm_ma_listview_image\n'

The interface file is processed and the data contained in\n   the file is transferred directly to a new or existing spreadsheet. If\n                            the worksheet does not exist, an error message\n                            will be issued. This template worksheet will be\n                            copied to a temporary worksheet file\n   template(<worksheet>)    ($SCRATCH_PATH\\tmpsheet.xls). When this parameter\n                            is not given, the temporary worksheet will be\n                            created instead. An occasionally existing\n                            temporary worksheet file will either be\n                            overwritten by the template worksheet or deleted\n                            before creating a new empty one.\n                            This parameter defines the full file name under\n                            which the result of the output should be stored.\n                            It depends on the definition of the \xef\xbf\xbdSaveAs\xef\xbf\xbd\n   saveas(<worksheet>)      command in the servers.ini file whether the user\n                            will be asked to overwrite a file or not.\n\n                            When this parameter is not present, the file is\n                            not stored at all.\n                            This parameter sets the upper leftmost cell\n                            position in the worksheet to put the data in.\n                            Each element on an output line will be written in\n                            a new cell in the current spreadsheet row. New\n   position(<Row>,<Column>) lines in the report output will result in a new\n                            row in the spreadsheet. Page breaks in the report\n                            output will be ignored.\n\n                            When this parameter is not given, the output will\n                            begin in row 1, column 1.\n                            This parameter specifies whether the Excel\n                            application window should be maximized or not\n                            when the output process is finished.\n   maximized({0|1})\n                            While Concept is sending data to Excel, the\n                            window will be minimized. When this parameter is\n                            set to 1, it will be maximized afterwards,\n                            otherwise it will be restored to its former size.\n\n   Configuration\n\n   Due to language dependent features in the Excel macro language, which is\n   used to feed Excel with the data from the report, it might be necessary to\n   configure the commands used in the communication process. Concept will be\n   sent out pre-configured for the languages supported by Concept. It might\n   be necessary although to change the configuration later for special\n   purposes.\n\n   servers.ini\n\n   The configuration of the commands used is done in the servers.ini file\n   located in the Concept setup directory. There must at least exist default\n   topics; one for each external Excel server in the languages supported by\n   Concept. The default names for these topics are EXCEL-XX, where XX is the\n   code of the language used (e.g. EXCEL-EN).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Each topic then must contain the following items:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\nItem name       Purpose\nType            A dummy item which should always be set to DDE.\nService         The name of the DDE service. Must be set to EXCEL for communication\n                with Excel.\n                Full path to the Excel executable. If this is not present and the Excel\nStart           executable path is not included in the users PATH environment variable,\n                Excel must be started manually before output can be sent to this\n                server.\nRowReference    Character to be placed in front of every row position value in cell\n                references.\nColumnReference Character to be placed in front of every column position value in cell\n                references.\nAppMinimize     Command to minimize the Excel application window.\nAppMaximize     Command to maximize the Excel application window.\nAppRestore      Command to restore the Excel application window.\nActivate        Command to activate the worksheet window. The name of the worksheet has\n                to be supplied using the @DOC() macro.\nCreate          Command to create a new worksheet.\nSaveAs          Command to store a worksheet with a certain file name. The full file\n                name has to be supplied using the @FILE() macro.\nOpen            Command to open a worksheet with a certain file name. The full file\n                name has to be supplied using the @FILE() macro.\nClose           Command to close the worksheet window.\n                Command to set the default column width for a range of columns. The\n                cell reference for the columns affected by the report output can be\n                supplied using the macro @VALUE(1). It contains a column range in the\nColumnWidth     format\n                \xef\xbf\xbd<ColumnReference><FirstUsedColumn>:<ColumnReference><LastUsedColumn>\xef\xbf\xbd,\n                where <ColumnReference> is the character configured with the\n                ColumnReference item and <FirstUsedColumn> and <LastUsedColumn> are\n                column numbers (e.g. C1:C5 for the English Excel version).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If any of these items are missing, it might make the Excel server\n   interface application fail. The only mandatory item is ''Service''. When\n   this item is missing, the servers.ini topic will be ignored by the\n   interface application. In case of problems outputting to an external\n   server it is possible to debug the communication process using the\n   debugger with the event trace turned on.\n\n   concept.ini, uqsystem.ini\n\n   When another than the default servers.ini topic is to be used for a\n   certain system, it is possible to specify the topic name in the user\n   specific configuration file concept.ini or in the system database\n   (uqsystem.ini). The section ''External'' can be used to associate an\n   external server with a servers.ini section.\n\n   To use a special servers.ini section for the Excel server, add an item\n   with the name ''Excel'' in the ''External'' section, pointing to the\n   servers.ini section.\n\n   [6][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_externalservers.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_externalword.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_external_server_driver.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dde.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_externalexcel.htm\n"

b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       File Directives                                   side\n\n   A file directive is an instruction to the Concept I/O system. The I/O\n   system allows file directives to modify the text read. File directives are\n   typically used to facilitate conditional reading of applications and files\n   in different environments.\n\n   This system is used by the compiler when reading source files and when\n   reading some of the configuration files on the setup directory.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Four groups of directives are defined:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0              Directives                  Description\n   File Inclusion $include                    Insert the contents of another\n                                              file\n   Macros         $constant, $<Variable>      Definition and substitution of\n                                              macro values (constants)\n   Conditions     $if, $elseif, $else, $endif Conditional reading of parts of\n                                              the file\n   Commands       $exit, $message, $break,    Initiate an action\n                  $test-application\n\n   File Inclusion\n\n   $include <File>\n\n   Tells the I/O system to treat the lines in the given file as if they\n   appeared in the source file at the point where the directive appears. The\n   included text can also contain file directives.\n\n   When used from the compiler, the included file must be located in the\n   directories defined in [4]@SOURCE_PATH, otherwise it must be in the same\n   directory as the main (including) file or a complete path must be\n   specified.\n\n   Macros\n\n   $constant <Name> <Value>\n\n   Defines a new macro constant <Name> having the value <Value>. <Name> can\n   only consist of letters or underscores (_). The I/O system will later\n   substitute all occurrences of $<Name> with <Value>. Note that the <Name>\n   and the <Value> are separated by one space; additional spaces will be part\n   of <Value>. All macro definitions will be discarded when the read\n   operation ends, they will not be available to the next file read.\n\n   $<Name>[<Width>]\n\n   Defines a constant to be replaced by the constant value. <Name> must be\n   declared with the $constant directive or be one of the [5]predefined\n   constants.\n\n   <Width> must be an unsigned integer constant indicating how many\n   characters of the <Value> should be used. If <Value> contains fewer\n   characters than the specified <Width>, it is padded with spaces. If\n   <Width> is zero, leading spaces will be stripped from the <Value>. If\n   <Width> is omitted, the actual length of <Value> is used.\n\n   Predefined Constants\n\n   See [6]Macro Values for a complete list of predefined status codes.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Name                     Value\n   $LANGUAGE                Current language code (DK, EN, GE, NO, SW)\n   $OS                      Current operating system (WINDOWS, DOS, UNIX,\n                            VMS, OS2)\n   $WINVER                  Windows version (WIN3, WIN95, WIN98, WINNT,\n                            WIN2000)\n   $OSVER                   Operating system version\n   $OSMODE                  Operating system mode (GUI, CHAR)\n   $UQVERNO                 Concept version\n   $ONLINE                  0 (possible value in @RUNMODE)\n   $BATCH                   1 (possible value in @RUNMODE)\n   $SERVER                  2 (possible value in @RUNMODE)\n   $ENVIRONMENT(<Variable>) The value of the environment variable <Variable>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Conditions\n\n   $if\xc2\xa0<Condition>\n\n   <Lines>\n\n   [$elseif\xc2\xa0<Condition>\n\n   <Lines>]\n\n   [$else\n\n   <Lines>]\n\n   $endif\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Read\xc2\xa0<Lines>\xc2\xa0according\xc2\xa0to\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0conditions\xc2\xa0specified.\xc2\xa0Nested\xc2\xa0if's\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0allowed\xc2\xa0up\xc2\xa0to\xc2\xa020\xc2\xa0levels.\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0<Condition>\xc2\xa0must\xc2\xa0have\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0following\xc2\xa0syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <Macro>\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0<Text>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   or\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <Macro>\xc2\xa0<>\xc2\xa0<Text>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   where <Macro> is a predefined or user-defined macro constant and <Text> is\n   a character string.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   $ifdef\xc2\xa0<constant\xc2\xa0name>\n\n   <Lines>\n\n   [$elifdef\xc2\xa0<constant\xc2\xa0name>\n\n   <Lines>]\n\n   [$else\n\n   <Lines>]\n\n   $endif\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Read\xc2\xa0<Lines>\xc2\xa0according\xc2\xa0to\xc2\xa0wether\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0<constant\xc2\xa0name>\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0defined.\xc2\xa0Nested\xc2\xa0if's\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0allowed\xc2\xa0up\xc2\xa0to\xc2\xa020\xc2\xa0levels.\xc2\xa0\n\n   Commands\n\n   $message\xc2\xa0<Text>\n\n   Concept 4GL Compiler only: Writes <Text> to the output file during\n   compilation.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   $exit\n\n   Terminates the reading of a source file or an include file. $exit\n   simulates end of file, so an include file returns to the main file and a\n   main file terminates reading. Any text after $exit will be ignored.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   $break\n\n   Concept 4GL Compiler only: Aborts a compilation.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   $test-application\xc2\xa0<sub\xc2\xa0application\xc2\xa0name>,<Expected\xc2\xa0result\xc2\xa0(Alphanumeric)>\n\n   Concept 4GL Compiler only: After successful compilation, the sub\n   application is called. If the exported value from the application is\n   different from defined expected result, the compilation is considered to\n   be unsuccessful. The compiler option SkipApplicationTests may be used to\n   force the compiler to ignore the test.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7File directives must be prefixed with a $ (dollar) sign.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A file directive must fit on one line.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A file directive must start in the left-most position of a line. Any\n   other occurrence of $ will be treated as the beginning of a user-defined\n   or a predefined constant. To use a $ in a text value without invoking the\n   substitution process, repeat the character ($$).\n\n   \xc2\xb7File directives may appear anywhere in a source file, but they apply only\n   to the data following their location in the file.\n\n   [7][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_external_server_driver_for_mail.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileformats.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_intsourcedir\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filedir.htm#idh_ma_filedir_predef\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_macro_values.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_filedir.htm\n"

When MS-WORD\n   format is specified, Microsoft Word is automatically invoked to convert\n   from RTF to MS-WORD format and vice versa. It is recommended to use the\n   RTF format instead.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Character set encoding can be specified as a part of the PLAIN format\n   specification using the notation PLAIN/<character set>. If character set\n   is not specified Concept will use the file's extension along with the\n   file-type-charset specification in the PLAIN section of uqdio.ini to\n   encode characters in the file.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filedir.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filefunctions.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_file_functions.htm\n"

This\n   handle is used as an input parameter to the other functions and will\n   uniquely identify the file until it is closed by the file-close function.\n   Please note that the handle value might be reused after the file has been\n   closed.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Files can be opened in any of the [16]file formats supported by Concept\n   but the following limitations of functionality are imposed when using file\n   formats other than BINARY, ASCII or PLAIN:\n\n   \xc2\xb7file-seek, file-tell and file-write will not work, status $UE_FORMAT is\n   returned.\n\n   \xc2\xb7file-read may only be used with parameter length set to -1 (line reading)\n   otherwise status $UE_FORMAT is returned.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please read the documentation for file-read and file-write carefully to\n   see how file-formats affects the results of the functions.\n\n   Using handles in XTRA reports\n\n   Xtra [17]streams can also use file handles, the special [18]file-name\n   syntax @HANDLE(<Handle>) allows stream operations on a file that is opened\n   prior to starting the report. This allows several reports writing to or\n   reading from a single file.\n\n   Please note that the [19]file-format declaration on the stream is ignored\n   when using a handle, since the file format is adopted from the file\n   identified by the handle.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [20][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileformats.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filenames.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_file_functions.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileopen.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileclose.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileread.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filewrite.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileseek.htm\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filetell.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileinfo.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filecopy.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filemove.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filelist.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filedelete.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileformats.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_filename\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_fileformat\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_filefunctions.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          File Names                                     side\n\n   This section explains how Concept -treats file- and directory names in\n   different environments.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   \xc2\xb7Both the file system\'s original syntax and UNIX syntax are allowed.\n   Concept will always try to convert a UNIX name to a valid name on non-UNIX\n   file-systems.\n\n   \xc2\xb7On WINDOWS, DOS and OS/2 forward slash " / " will be converted to\n   backslash " \\ ".\n\n   \xc2\xb7On SINTRAN, the leading and trailing "/ " will be replaced by open and\n   close bracket ( ), and all " / " in between converted to "-". The\n   extension separator " . " will be converted to " : ".\n\n   \xc2\xb7On UNIX all names are converted to lowercase (uppercase names can not be\n   used with Concept). On other systems file names are not case sensitive.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Always use UNIX syntax when specifying file- and directory names in\n   applications. An alternative way of making directory references portable\n   is to use compiler directives to distinguish between operating systems.\n\n   \xc2\xb7To make file names portable, use maximum 8 characters in the file name\n   and maximum 3 characters in the extension.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [4][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filefunctions.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_funcexecution.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_filenames.htm\n'

These events\n   may be implicit events (table and field functions) or explicit events\n   (programmed via on). The function execution starts with the first function\n   in the block to be executed and ends after the last function in the block\n   or when an error occurs.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_filenames.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form_grid.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          Grid Forms                                     side\n\n   A grid form is a form that permits the display of a data structure in a\n   row and column format. The grid is divided into cells, where a cell\n   contains one piece of information. The information that can be represented\n   in a cell can be of any kind for example: strings, numbers, images etc. A\n   grid form provides the Concept 4GL developer with an alternative way of\n   presenting data from a database to the existing mechanism of repeat areas.\n   As grid forms are connected to tables, the maximum number of rows shown is\n   determined by the number of [4]repeat lines defined.\n\n   Grid Types\n\n   There are three different grid types available: standard, dynamic and\n   sizeable.\n\n   Standard grids will always show the defined number of rows. The horizontal\n   scrollbar is fixed and the vertical scrollbar is shown only when needed.\n   The horizontal scrollbar may also include a set of scrolling [5]buttons.\n\n   A dynamic grid will only show the rows that contain data (plus an empty\n   row to allow inserting data if the table access permits it). In a dynamic\n   grid the vertical scrollbar is normally fixed but it can be hidden if all\n   rows fit into the grid. The horizontal scrollbar is only shown when\n   needed. The elevator in the vertical scrollbar is sized according to the\n   number of visible rows in the grid, which means that for a dynamic grid\n   form it will link to the number of qualifying rows in the connected table\n   if the number of rows is less than the repeat count. Dynamic grids also\n   allow local sorting on the grid columns of the form using the sort\n   attribute of the [6]change-form function. Please note that the sorting is\n   only applied to the rows that are in the grid (limited by the repeat\n   count), and not to the set of data that qualifies for the grid.\n\n   Sizeable grids are similar to standard grids - they will show lines for\n   rows not containing data. But the number of rows shown depends on the size\n   of the grid form. The grid will show exactly as many rows as fit into the\n   form. When the form size changes, the number of rows displayed will be\n   adjusted accordingly (the maximum number of lines shown still depends on\n   the number of repeat lines). The vertical scroll bar will not be shown and\n   the horizontal scroll bar will be shown when needed.\n\n   Grid form construction\n\n   A grid form has an optional frame containing grid rows and grid columns. A\n   grid column must contain data elements connected to table fields.\n   Optionally it may contain [7]label elements on top that serve as headings\n   for the columns, [8]top elements on top (but below labels when defined)\n   that i.e. can be used as search fields and [9]bottom elements at the\n   bottom that i.e. can be used to display sum values. Each row of the grid\n   corresponds to one row from a connected [10]table.\n\n   A standard grid\n\n   A dynamic grid\n\n   A sizeable grid\n\n   Supported Element Types\n\n   All [11]element types but the following are supported in grid forms:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7Multi-line INPUT\n\n   \xc2\xb7Multi-line OUTPUT\n\n   \xc2\xb7TREEVIEW\n\n   \xc2\xb7LIST-VIEW\n\n   \xc2\xb7WINDOW\n\n   Grid form run-time behavior\n\n   The vertical scrollbar can be used to scroll through the rows of a grid if\n   the number of rows in the grid is larger than the number of rows that fit\n   into the grid frame.\n\n   The horizontal scroll bar can be used to scroll through the columns of a\n   grid if the number of columns in the grid is larger than the number of\n   columns that fit into the grid frame.\n\n   Use the [12]allow-resize form attribute to enable the user to resize the\n   rows and/or the columns of the grid.\n\n   The header elements have a default popup menu that enables the user to\n   reposition the columns of the grid, save the current layout or remove a\n   previously saved layout. The default menu can be replaced by your own menu\n   by connecting the header element to a field with a popup declaration. The\n   default save and remove actions can be achieved by using the menu\n   commands; \'EVENT GRID-SETTINGS-SAVE <GRID FORM NAME>\' AND \'EVENT\n   GRID-SETTINGS-REMOVE <GRID FORM NAME>\' respectively.\n\n   Locked Columns\n\n   Columns can be "locked" to the left of the grid, that means that they will\n   not be scrolled horizontally. To do so, simply use the separator in the\n   [13]element-sequence twice between the columns that are to be locked and\n   the remaining columns.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_funcexecution.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm#idh_ma_table_repeat\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_buttons\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changeform.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_label\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_top\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_bottom\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_types.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_allowresize\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_elementsequence\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            Images                                       side\n\n   This chapter explains the image handling in Concept. It lists the\n   supported [4]image formats and [5]usage areas and describes the [6]image\n   definition syntax.\n\n   Formats\n\n   The following image file formats are supported: BMP (Windows Bitmaps),\n   JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group), PNG (Portable Network Graphics),\n   TIFF (Tag Image File Format) and ICO (Windows Icons). Icon files may\n   contain multiple versions of the same icon (in different sizes or colour\n   depths).\n\n   Usage\n\n   Images can be used in a number of different ways. The following sections\n   describe each usage area.\n\n   Element Background\n\n   Images can be used as the [7]background for [8]elements, [9]forms and\n   [10]streams.\n\n   Please note that image backgrounds are not supported on elements using\n   Win32 controls (List-Box, Treeview, Listview, Multi-Line Input and\n   Output).\n\n   Image Elements\n\n   Images can be shown in [11]Image elements.\n\n   Button Elements\n\n   Images can be used on [12]Push-Button, [13]Default-Button,\n   [14]Cool-Button, [15]Popup-Button, [16]Combo-Button and [17]Header\n   elements. The image may be used together with a button [18]text. In this\n   case the [19]alignment declaration defines where the image is placed.\n\n   Up to 4 button images can be specified, corresponding to the 4 button\n   states: not pressed, pressed, not pressed with focus and locked. If less\n   than 4 state images are specified, the last specified images is used for\n   the remaining states. If only one state is specified, Concept renders the\n   states automatically. The image states can be specified using one of the\n   following methods:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a semicolon separated image list (e.g.\n   \'up.bmp;down.bmp;focus.bmp;locked.bmp\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the [20]dimension modifier (e.g. \'button.bmp,dimension(1,4)\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a question mark (\'?\') as placeholder in the image file name. The\n   question mark will be replaced with the following letters to find the\n   files for each state: \'U\' for not pressed, \'D\' for pressed, \'F\' for not\n   pressed with focus and \'L\' for locked (\'button?.bmp\' is equivalent to\n   \'buttonu.bmp;buttond.bmp;buttonf.bmp;buttonl.bmp\').\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the text declaration is not used together with the image declaration,\n   it is assumed that the button image includes a frame (except for\n   Cool-Buttons). The [21]image prefix \'@@\' can be used for images not\n   containing a frame. In this case Concept will draw the frame.\n\n   Check-Box and Radio-Button Elements\n\n   Images can be used on [22]Check-Box and [23]Radio-Button elements. Up to 6\n   button images can be specified, corresponding to the 6 button states:\n   unchecked, checked, unchecked with focus, checked with focus, unchecked\n   and locked and checked and locked. If less than 6 state images are\n   specified, the last specified images is used for the remaining states. The\n   image states can be specified using one of the following methods:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a semicolon separated image list (e.g.\n   \'unchecked.bmp;checked.bmp;ufocus.bmp;cfocus.bmp;ulocked.bmp;clocked.bmp\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the [24]dimension modifier (e.g. \'button.bmp,dimension(1,6)\')\n\n   Drop-Down Elements\n\n   Images can be used on Drop-Down Elements ([25]Drop-Down-List-Box and\n   [26]Drop-Down-Combo-Box) to show another image than the down arrow\n   normally displayed on the button that opens the list. The rules are the\n   same as for [27]button elements.\n\n   Treeview Elements\n\n   Images can be used for each node in a [28]Treeview Element. The image\n   defined on the element itself serves as a default image if the Image\n   column in the treeview table is empty. Up to 2 images can be specified,\n   corresponding to the 2 node states: unselected and selected. If only 1\n   state image is specified, the image is used for both states. The image\n   states can be specified using one of the following methods:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using a semicolon separated image list (e.g.\n   \'unselected.bmp;selected.bmp\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the [29]dimension modifier (e.g. \'node.bmp,dimension(1,2)\')\n\n   Listview Forms\n\n   Images can be used for each entry in a [30]Listview Form. Only [31]Icon\n   Images may be used in listviews. The view declaration of the listview\n   defines which icon to show.\n\n   Drop-Down Menus\n\n   Images can be used on [32]menu entries (drop-down and popup). The image\n   will be used alongside the menu text. If the entry uses the "Toggle"\n   command, the same rules as for [33]Check-Box and Radio-Button Elements\n   apply, with the exception that only the first to states are relevant.\n\n   Toolbar Menus\n\n   Images can be used on toolbar [34]menu entries. How the image will be\n   displayed, depends on the value of the text/selective-text parameter and\n   the user\'s toolbar settings. The rules for the image definition are the\n   same as for [35]Button Elements with one exception: the [36]image prefix\n   \'@*\' must be used if Concept is to render the different states.\n\n   Definition\n\n   This section describes the syntax of an image definition.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [\xc2\xa0[37]imagePrefix\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0[38]fileName\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[39]resourceLibrary!resourceId\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[40]internalResource\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[41]cache(\xc2\xa0OFF\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0ON\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa00\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa01\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa02\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa03\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa04\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa05\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa06\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa07\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa08\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa09\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[42]dimension(\xc2\xa0vertical[,\xc2\xa0horizontal]\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[43]display(\xc2\xa0STRETCH\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0CLIP\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0AUTO\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0AUTOSIZE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0TILE\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[44]format(\xc2\xa0BITMAP\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0ICON\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[45]index(\xc2\xa0vertical[,\xc2\xa0horizontal]\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[46]page(\xc2\xa0number\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[47]size(\xc2\xa0height,\xc2\xa0width\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[48]substitute(\xc2\xa0transparentColour[,\xc2\xa0backgroundColour]\xc2\xa0)])\n\n   Image Prefix\n\n   The image prefix defines how the image is to be used. The following\n   prefixes are available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Prefix Description\n   @@     Used to draw a frame around [49]button images not containing\n          frames. Frames are drawn unless a skin background i used.\n   @*     Used to render the states of [50]button images automatically.\n          Frames are drawn around [51]toolbar buttons.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   File Name\n\n   The file name of the image to display. If the file name does not contain a\n   path, the file will be searched for in the image-path.\n\n   Library Resource\n\n   The resource identification of the image to display. The resource\n   identification consists of a resource library file name and a resource ID,\n   separated by an exclamation mark (\'!\').\n\n   Resource Library\n\n   File name of a DLL or executable containing resources. If the file name\n   does not contain a path, the file will be searched for in the image-path,\n   in the executable path and in the directory the Concept executable is\n   stored in. The following predefined resource libraries are available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Resource lib Description\n   @UQ          Predefined Concept resources.\n   @WIN         Predefined Windows resources.\n\n   Resource Id\n\n   The resource identifier of the image to display. If the resource ID is a\n   number, the number must be prefixed with the number sign (\'#\').\n\n   Internal Resource\n\n   The name of an internal resource. The following internal resources are\n   available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Resource  Description\n   @CLOSE    Same as @WIN!#32754\n   @COMBO    Same as @WIN!#32738\n   @RESTORE  Same as @WIN!#32747\n   @RESTORED Same as @WIN!#32744\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Cache\n\n   When the parameter value for this modifier is set to \'ON\' (the default),\n   the image is put into a cache from which the image is read the next time\n   it is used. Images can be put into specific cache slots, numbered from 0\n   to 9. Any image cached in such a slot will be replaced when a new file is\n   read into that slot. To turn caching off, set the parameter value to\n   \'OFF\'.\n\n   Dimension\n\n   When using the dimension modifier, the image will be divided into as many\n   vertical and horizontal parts as specified (defining an image map). This\n   is useful for [52]button images as all the states required can be defined\n   in one image file. Use the dimension modifier together with the [53]index\n   modifier to address a specific part of the map.\n\n   Display\n\n   This modifier specifies how the image is displayed. The following display\n   modes are available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Mode     Description\n   STRETCH  The image is stretched to fill the element (the default).\n   CLIP     The image is clipped at the element boundaries if it does not fit\n            into the element.\n   TILE     The image is repeated to fill the element.\n   AUTO     The image is resized (maintaining the aspect ratio) if it does\n            not fit into the element boundaries.\n   AUTOSIZE The image is resized (maintaining the aspect ratio) to fit the\n            element boundaries.\n\n   Format\n\n   Specifies the format of the image. The following formats are available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Format Description\n   BITMAP Bitmap image (BMP, JPEG, PNG or TIFF; the default)\n   ICON   Icon image (ICO)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The BITMAP format may also be specified when displaying icons or cursors.\n   allowing to resize them instead of displaying them in pre-defined\n   [54]sizes.\n\n   Index\n\n   The index modifier is used to address a specific image in the image map\n   defined by the [55]dimension modifier. The index modifier is automatically\n   used when using the dimension modifier on [56]button images.\n\n   Page\n\n   Specifies the page to display when using multi-page TIFF documents. The\n   parameter is ignored for all other file formats.\n\n   Size\n\n   The size modifier can be used to specify the preferred size for [57]Icon\n   Images. It is also used to force Concept to show an image using th size\n   specified. Please note that the actual image size used depends on the\n   [58]display modifier.\n\n   Substitute\n\n   The substitute modifier is used to specify which parts of an image are to\n   be shown transparent or to replace a given colour in an image with another\n   colour. All pixels in the transparent colour will be transparent if the\n   background colour is not specified. Otherwise these pixels will be drawn\n   in the background colour. Instead of a background colour, the keyword\n   TRANSPARENT may be specified. In that case pixels to be substituted will\n   not be drawn at all.\n\n   Acknowledgements\n\n   The image conversion routines for the JPEG format are based on code of the\n   Independent JPEG Group (version JPEG-6b). Copyright \xc2\xa9 1994-1998, Thomas G.\n   Lane.\n\n   The image conversion routines for the PNG format are based on the freely\n   available pnglib version 1.2.32\n   (http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/src/libpng-LICENSE.txt; Copyright\n   \xc2\xa9,2004,2006-2008 Glenn Randers-Pehrson) and zlib version 1.2.3 (see\n   http://www.zlib.net/zlib_license.html; Copyright \xc2\xa9 1995-2005 Jean-loup\n   Gailly and Mark Adler).\n\n   The image conversion routines for the TIFF format are based on the freely\n   available LibTIFF library (see http://www.libtiff.org/; Copyright \xc2\xa9\n   1988-1997 Sam Leffler Copyright \xc2\xa9 1991-1997 Silicon Graphics, Inc.)\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form_grid.htm\n   2.
