b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                     Intialisation Files                                 side\n\n   Initialisation Files (or short Ini Files) are text files with the\n   following layout:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [Section]\n\n   Item=Value\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The Section and Item names are used to uniquely identify an entry in the\n   file. The [4]initialisation-file function can be used to access the Value\n   stored in an item. The item value may be enclosed in double quotes (") to\n   preserve leading and trailing spaces. The quotes will be stripped away\n   when reading a value.\n\n   Ini Files are normally used by Windows applications to store configuration\n   data.\n\n   Example\n\n   [Environment]\n\n   UNIQUE_HOME=c:\\uqwin\n\n   [Settings]\n\n   Language=EN\n\n   Sound=1\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_initfile.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Internal fields                                   side\n\n   There is a set of predefined internal fields whose name always starts with\n   the character @. Internal fields may be used in expressions just like\n   application fields. Some internal fields may also be changed by the\n   application.\n\n   @A\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an alphanumeric (A(10240)) field with no particular value. It may\n   be freely changed by the application. It\'s value is local to the sub\n   application.\n\n   @ALLOW_ENDSESSION\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an integer field which controls how Visma Enterprise Concept\n   should act on an operating system shutdown. When set to 0 (the default) a\n   dialogue-box warns the user about the shut-down ("You must terminate this\n   program before logoff or shutdown."). When set to a positive value, the\n   operating system is allowed to kill the session. When set to a negative\n   value, the [4]QUERYENDSESSION event is broadcasted to all threads of the\n   system, and the operating system is instructed to wait for the shutdown\n   (the user can still force the shutdown). Please note that this internal\n   field (or the QUERYENDSESSION event) is not handled on the Application\n   Server.\n\n   @APPLICATION\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the current application using the following syntax:\n\n   <application file name>:<application name>\n\n   The application file name is the name of the object file (without\n   extension), the application name the name of the application as defined in\n   the source file.\n\n   @APPLICATION_ACCESS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the access of the current application. The initial access of the\n   application is by default unlimited, but can be reduced by the access\n   parameter of the [5]call, [6]run, [7]start or [8]zoom function used to\n   invoke the application, and by access definitions in Security.\n\n   When the field is changed, the access can never exceed the application\'s\n   initial access.\n\n   See the [9]table component documentation for an explanation of access\n   values.\n\n   @APPLICATION_CONTAINER\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the [10]thread handle of the application containing the current\n   application if the application is [11]started inside an [12]application\n   element.\n\n   @APPLICATION_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the application path as specified for the current system in the\n   uqconfig file.\n\n   @APPSPACE_HEIGHT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   The height of the [13]application element an application is [14]started\n   in, in pixels. The [15]WINSIZE event is triggered when the element is\n   resized.\n\n   If the current application is not run inside an application element, the\n   [16]@WORKSPACE_HEIGHT is returned.\n\n   @APPSPACE_WIDTH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   The width of the [17]application element an application is [18]started in,\n   in pixels. The [19]WINSIZE event is triggered when the element is resized.\n\n   If the current application is not run inside an application element, the\n   [20]@WORKSPACE_WIDTH is returned.\n\n   @AVAILABLE_BROKERS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   This alphanumeric (A(1000)) field contains a semicolon separated list of\n   available brokers defined in UqConfig.\n\n   @B\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an alphanumeric (A(10240)) field with no particular value. It may\n   be freely changed by the application. It\'s value is local to the sub\n   application.\n\n   @BROKER_SESSION\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains an encrypted session identification which is used to identify a\n   client session on a Visma Enterprise Server\'s Broker. The session\n   identification is transferred to a Broker as part of the Unique Job\n   Protocol and expires after a timeout which can be set in the uqconfig\n   (system parameter broker-session-timeout). This value can be passed back\n   to clients by including it in results produced by reports run in the\n   SERVER (e.g. by including it in HTML code generated).\n\n   @BROKER_SESSION_DATA\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This field can be used to assign and retrieve application specific\n   information which is passed between Server clients and Brokers. The value\n   is transferred to Brokers alongside the @BROKER_SESSION value, but is not\n   encrypted so that it can be analysed and manipulated both on the client\n   and on the server.\n\n   @C\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an alphanumeric (A(1024)) field with no particular value. It may\n   be freely changed by the application. It\'s value is local to the sub\n   application.\n\n   @CLIPBOARDTEXT\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an alphanumeric (A(10240)) field that can be used to retrieve or\n   set text in the Windows clipboard.\n\n   @COMPANY\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the current company number. Trying to change the company number\n   to a value not in the list of legal company numbers, will not be allowed.\n\n   @COMPILED\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the date and time when current application was compiled.\n\n   @CURSOR_POS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the current cursor position (horizontal) in an input, output or a\n   closed drop-down-combo-box field. When changed, the current cursor\n   position in the current field is changed so that the next time the cursor\n   enters the field, the initial position will be as defined.\n\n   @D\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is an alphanumeric (A(1024)) field with no particular value. It may\n   be freely changed by the application. It\'s value is local to the sub\n   application.\n\n   @DBMS_SUPPORT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains a semicolon separated list of names identifying the available\n   DBMS interfaces\n\n   @DEFAULT_BUTTON\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of default button of current application.\n\n   @DEFAULT_CSV_SEPARATORS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the default CSV-SEPARATORS for the session. The content of the\n   value is :\n\n   <main separator>,<alpha frame>,<numeric frame>,<escape character>,<decimal\n   character>\n\n   The TOKEN operator can be used to extract single values from the text.\n\n   See the chapter on CSV-SEPARATORS in the Operation Guide for a complete\n   reference on the contents.\n\n   @DESKTOP_BOTTOM\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the bottom position of the available desktop area.\n\n   @DESKTOP_LEFT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the left position of the available desktop area.\n\n   @DESKTOP_RIGHT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the right position of the available desktop area.\n\n   @DESKTOP_TOP\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the top position of the available desktop area.\n\n   @DIRECTORY\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of current active directory.\n\n   @DISKSPACE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains number of bytes free disk space on current drive.\n\n   @DRAG_VALUE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the marked value of an element that has initiated a drag\n   operation. The contents of @DRAG_VALUE is interpreted as :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Element type        Value\n   INPUT, OUTPUT and   The marked (highlighted) part of the value.\n   DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX\n                       The selected value. For multi-selection list boxes it\n                       contains a separated list of values, the first\n   LISTBOX             character denotes the separator used. If the field\n                       connected to the list box is defined with\n                       selection-type(INDEX), selected value refers to the\n                       index of the value.\n   TREEVIEW            The ID of the treeview node selected for the drag\n                       operation.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please note that the contents of @DRAG_VALUE is only defined inside the\n   event handler for the DRAG key.\n\n   @EDITOR\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains a semicolon separated list of available editors for the current\n   system.\n\n   @EDIT_BUFFER\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Valid only inside the [21]@EDIT and the [22]@VALUE_ERROR event handlers\n   (in all other circumstances the contents of @EDIT_BUFFER is empty).\n\n   Contains the value of the input buffer when used inside the [23]@EDIT\n   event handler. @EDIT_BUFFER can be assigned a value to from within an\n   @EDIT event handler.\n\n   Contains the illegal value assigned to a field connected to a\n   LIST-BOX/DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX when used inside the [24]@VALUE_ERROR event\n   handler. Changing the value of @EDIT_BUFFER inside the event handler has\n   no effect.\n\n   @ERROR_BREAK_FUNCTION\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the function that caused an error break. Only to be\n   used inside [25]@ERROR-BREAK event handling.\n\n   @ERROR_BREAK_NAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the object where the error break occurred, use\n   together with @ERROR_BREAK_OBJECT. Only to be used inside [26]@ERROR-BREAK\n   event handling.\n\n   @ERROR_BREAK_OBJECT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the type of the object where the error break occurred, use\n   together with @ERROR_BREAK_NAME. Possible values are FIELD, TABLE-NAME,\n   FORM, STREAM, XTRA and ONLINE. Only to be used inside [27]@ERROR-BREAK\n   event handling.\n\n   @ERROR_BREAK_SOURCE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the full source of the function that caused an error break. Only\n   to be used inside [28]@ERROR-BREAK event handling.\n\n   @EVENT_ELEMENT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the last element that received input. See also\n   [29]@INPUT_ELEMENT.\n\n   @EVENT_NAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the event that triggered an [30]event handler.\n\n   @EVENT_PARAM\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains parameter values associated with the event handled by an\n   [31]event handler. Please note that this value might change while the\n   event handler code is executed because new events have arrived in the\n   meantime. It may therefore be necessary to take a copy of the field value\n   as early as possible in the code handling the event.\n\n   @EVENT_THREAD\n\n   Read-only\n\n   If the current ON event is a [32]registered event or if it is triggered by\n   a [33]send-event function in another thread, this field will contain the\n   thread handle of the source thread, otherwise 0.\n\n   @GROUP_MASTER\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the id of the Security system containing the groups used by the\n   current system. If Security is not active, the id is 0.\n\n   @GROUPIDS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains a semicolon separated list of IDs of the SECURITY groups the\n   current user is a member of.\n\n   @HELP_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the help path of the system. The standard help paths\n   <UNIQUE_HOME>/help-<language code> and <UNIQUE_HOME>/help-en will always\n   be at the end of the system specific help paths.\n\n   @HOME_DIRECTORY\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the current directory at startup.\n\n   @IMAGE_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the image path as specified for the current system in the\n   uqconfig configuration file. If it is not specified in the uqconfig file,\n   the @IMAGE_PATH defaults to @APPLICATION_PATH.\n\n   @INITIALS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the user name initials from the user profile in Security.\n\n   @INPUT_ELEMENT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the element that has input focus. If an INPUT element\n   has focus and a button is clicked using the mouse, @INPUT_ELEMENT will\n   identify the input element and [34]@EVENT_ELEMENT will identify the\n   button.\n\n   @INPUT_EVENT\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the event that triggered the current field function\n   execution chain (the key that terminated the input loop).\n\n   @INPUT_FIELD\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the field which is connected to the element which\n   currently has the input focus. This information can be useful in\n   [35]on...endon declarations on table and application level to identify the\n   field generating the command or event.\n\n   @INSERT_MODE\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains 1 if the input editor is in "insert mode", else 0 "overwrite\n   mode".\n\n   @JOB_STATUS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This internal field (integer4) can be used in XTRA applications that will\n   be run on the Server. It enables the programmer to return a status code to\n   the Server, that will be shown when inspecting the job queue on the\n   Server. If no value is assigned to @JOB_STATUS, the value $OK is used.\n\n   @LANGUAGE\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the current language code.\n\n   @LAST_SQL_SENTENCE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the last SQL sentence.\n\n   @LEGAL_COMPANIES\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the list of legal companies (as defined in SECURITY).\n\n   @LINES\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the number of available lines in the current application window.\n   @LINES is given an integer number in units of cells (see the [36]formular\n   definition). @LINES is given a value when the application window is\n   created. This internal field should thus not be used in the\n   initial-value() property on fields or in the on @VERY-FIRST event handler.\n\n   @LOGINNAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name used during the SECURITY login. This name can be\n   different from the [37]username when the user uses an alias when logging\n   in.\n\n   @LOG_ACTIVE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Indicates whether or not logging is active for the current system. It is 1\n   if logging is active, else 0.\n\n   @MAIL_INTERFACE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the default mail interface for the current system (as defined in\n   the uqconfig file).\n\n   @MAIN_CAPTION\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Changes the title of the main Concept window to the text string assigned\n   to this internal field. If it is set to an empty string (\xef\xbf\xbd\xef\xbf\xbd), the main\n   caption is changed back to the Concept system name.\n\n   @MARK_END\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   When a value is assigned to this internal field, the text in the current\n   edit buffer between @MARK_POS and @MARK_END is marked (selected). The\n   field can be changed in the @EDIT or @CURSOR-IN event handlers.\n\n   @MARK_POS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   When a value is assigned to this internal field, the text in the current\n   edit buffer between @MARK_POS and @MARK_END (@CURSOR_POS if @MARK_END is\n   0) is marked (selected). The field can be changed in the @EDIT or\n   @CURSOR-IN event handlers.\n\n   @MAX_LINES\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the number of lines an application window can grow to when it is\n   maximized. It is in fact the @LINES value of the client area of the\n   Concept main window. @MAX_LINES is given an integer number in units of\n   cells (see the [38]formular definition).\n\n   @OBJECT_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the object path of the current system where compiled 4GL\n   applications are stored (.uco files).\n\n   @PRIVATE_LAYOUT_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the current user\'s layout path.\n\n   @PUBLIC_LAYOUT_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the public layout path of the current system.\n\n   @READ_ERROR_FIELD\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the field that is assigned an erroneous value.\n\n   Only available inside the @READ-ERROR event\n\n   @READ_ERROR_STREAM\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the stream being read. If the error occurs inside the\n   [39]buffer-read function the name is given as \'Buffer READ Stream\'.\n\n   Only available inside the @READ-ERROR event\n\n   @READ_ERROR_VALUE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the value that is erroneous (as a text value).\n\n   Only available inside the @READ-ERROR event\n\n   @READ_ERROR_STATUS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the status code for the error. Possible values are :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_VALUE The numeric value contains an illegal character or an\n                     illegal formatting\n   $UE_TRUNCATED     The alphanumeric value exceeds the length of the\n                     resulting alphanumeric field.\n   $UE_OVERFLOW      The value exceeds the data type limits of the resulting\n                     field\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Only available inside the @READ-ERROR event\n\n   @READ_ERROR_BUFFER\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the complete data record in the original format-\n\n   Only available inside the @READ-ERROR event\n\n   @REPEAT_LINE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the current repeat line number. If current field is not inside a\n   repeat area, repeat line number 1 i returned.\n\n   @RUNMODE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains 0 in interactive mode, 1 batch mode and 2 server mode(for broker\n   and servants).\n\n   @RUNTIME_INFO\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains information describing the runtime system:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Token Interpretation\n         Name of the operating system. Possible values are:\n\n         WIN3 - Microsoft Windows 3.1 or Windows 3.11\n\n         WIN95 - Microsoft Windows 95\n\n         WIN98 - Microsoft Windows 98\n\n         WINNT - Microsoft Windows NT\n\n         WIN2000 - Microsoft Windows 2000\n\n         WINXP - Microsoft Windows XP\n\n         WINVISTA - Microsoft Windows Vista\n\n   1     WIN7 - Windows 7\n\n         WIN2008 - Windows Server 2008\n\n         WIN2008R2 - Windows Server 2008 R2\n\n         WIN8 - Windows 8\n\n         WIN2012 - Windows Server 2012\n\n         WIN8.1 - Windows 8.1\n\n         WIN2012R2 - Windows server 2012 R2\n\n         WIN10 - Windows 10\n\n         WIN10SERVER - Windows server 10\n         The default word size of the program. Possible values are:\n   2\n         16, 32 or 64 bits.\n         User interface types. Possible values are:\n\n   3     WINDOWS - Microsoft Windows\n\n         WINDOWSTS - Microsoft Windows with Terminal Services installed\n   4     Full file name of the current session\'s executable.\n   5     Operating system version in the format <major version>.<minor\n         version>.\n\n   @SCRATCH_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the scratch path of the current system. If no scratch path is\n   defined in the uqconfig configuration file, it is assigned the directory\n   of the environment variable TEMP or, if not available, TMP. If no\n   temporary directory is specified in the Windows environment, then\n   @SCRATCH_PATH defaults to the current directory.\n\n   @SECURITY_SYSTEMNAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the actual system name used by the application with respect to\n   the application file declaration [40]security-system-name and the\n   security-system-name setting in the uqconfig file.\n\n   @SESSIONID\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the unique identification of the OS process running the\n   executable. This has only a meaning in a multi user environment.\n\n   @SETUP_DIR\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the setup path of the current system.\n\n   @SMTP_FROM\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the default SMTP sender address (as defined in the uqconfig\n   system parameter smtp-server).\n\n   Changing this value affects the system routines sending e-mails (e.g. in\n   the Visma Enterprise Server).\n\n   @SMTP_PASSWORD\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the default SMTP sender address (as defined in the uqconfig\n   system parameter smtp-server).\n\n   Changing this value affects the system routines sending e-mails (e.g. in\n   the Visma Enterprise Server).\n\n   @SMTP_REPLY\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the default SMTP reply address (as defined in the uqconfig system\n   parameter smtp-server).\n\n   Changing this value affects the system routines sending e-mails (e.g. in\n   the Visma Enterprise Server).\n\n   @SMTP_SERVER\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the default SMTP server (as defined in the uqconfig system\n   parameter smtp-server).\n\n   Changing this value affects the system routines sending e-mails (e.g. in\n   the Visma Enterprise Server).\n\n   @SMTP_USER\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the default SMTP sender address (as defined in the uqconfig\n   system parameter smtp-server).\n\n   Changing this value affects the system routines sending e-mails (e.g. in\n   the Visma Enterprise Server).\n\n   @SOURCE_PATH\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the source path of the current system where 4GL application\n   source files are stored.\n\n   @SRV_TRACE_FILE\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the name of the current trace output device for tracing on a\n   server. Legal values include @LOCAL(<local file name>), @REMOTE(<a legal\n   path and filename on the server>) and @MAIL(<mail recipient>). When\n   changing the field, errors (like an illegal file name) will not be\n   detected and reported before trace output on the server is attempted.\n\n   @SYSTEMID\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the system id as provided by Security. If Security is not active,\n   the system id is 0.\n\n   @SYSTEMNAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the current system.\n\n   @SYSTEM_LIST\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains a semicolon separated list of systems in the uqconfig file.\n\n   @SYSTEM_SETTINGS\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the list of system settings defined in the uqconfig file. The\n   values of system settings using a special syntax can be obtained by using\n   the system_setting [41]operator.\n\n   @THREAD_HANDLE\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the handle (internal identity) of the current application thread.\n\n   @THREAD_LIST\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains a semicolon separated list of active thread handles in the\n   current session.\n\n   @TIME_ELAPSED\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the time elapsed (in milliseconds) since the current Concept\n   process has been started.\n\n   @TIMEZONE_NAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the current timezone. Example: Vest-Europa\n   (normaltid)\n\n   @TIMEZONE_UTC\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the computers timezone setting regarded to UTC. Example: UTC+1\n\n   @TIMEZONE_MIN_TO_UTC\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the computers timezone offset to UTC given in minutes. Example:\n   -60. This tells us that "UTC" time is currrent time - 1 hour.\n\n   @TRACE_FILE\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the name of the current trace output device. If the field is\n   empty or set to \'@DEBWIN\', the output device is a window, otherwise it is\n   a file with the given name. When changed, the current output device is\n   closed immediately, but the new device is not opened before any trace\n   output is produced. Thus, an error like an illegal file name, will not be\n   detected and reported before trace output is attempted. An error message\n   will then be displayed.\n\n   @TRACE_OPTIONS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   Contains the current trace option flags as a list of the following\n   letters:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Letter Description\n   A      Trace application events\n   B      Trace SERVER operations\n   C      Trace field/element focus information\n   D      Trace database operations\n   E      Trace input and function events\n   F      Trace function execution\n   I      Trace file operations\n   L      Trace LDT expansions\n   N      Do not trace [42]asynchronous events\n   M      Trace performance\n   P      Trace import/export mismatches\n   Q      Trace SQL statements\n   R      Trace INI file operations\n   T      Trace output of the [43]trace function\n   V      Trace field value changes\n   Y      Trace Y2K checks\n   Z      Flush trace output to file immediately\n   .      Step mode\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   When changing the field, two special flags may be used to set a number of\n   trace options at once:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Letter Description\n   *      Combination of common flags\n   +      Combination of all flags\n\n   @TRIGGER_FIELD\n\n   Read-only\n\n   When a field\'s functions are executed due to an explicit compute or\n   execute (including [44]changelistener-for execution), this field will\n   contain the name of the field that is the source of the execution,\n   otherwise it will be blank.\n\n   @UCO_DIRECTORY\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the name of the internal system UCO directory.\n\n   @UJP_HTTP_STATUS\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This field\'s value may be set by applications running on the Visma\n   Enterprise Server to set a secondary HTTP status to be returned to the\n   client. This status is only returned upon a successful run on the server.\n\n   The value is returned in the [45]return-code parameter of [46]order-job.\n   Default value is 200. The text is put into the log in\n   Visma Enterprise Server if the @UJP_HTTP_STATUS is set different to 200.\n\n   @USERID\n\n   Read-only\n\n   Contains the current user ID as provided by Security. If Security is not\n   active, the user ID is 0.\n\n   @USERLONGNAME\n\n   Read-only\n\n   If the user has logged in through SECURITY, the field contains the user\'s\n   long name. It may be freely\n   changed by the application. It may be freely\n   changed by the application. It\'s value is local to the sub application.\n\n   @Z\n\n   Read/Write\n\n   This is a numeric (I4) field with no particular value. The Job Dialogue is in many\n   respects similar to the [5]Ask Stream Dialogue. The main difference is\n   that the Job Dialogue asks for all output devices at once where as the Ask\n   Stream Dialogue will be called for each stream individually.\n\n   The standard Job Dialogue that is included in Concept can be replaced by a\n   custom dialogue by defining it in the Applications section of the System\n   Database (uqsystem.ini; see also Visma Enterprise Concept Operations\n   Guide, System Database, JobDialogue).\n\n   A customized Job Dialogue has to follow a set of rules regarding the\n   values imported and exported by the application. Please contact Visma\n   Unique Service (Concept.Service@visma.no) for an explanation of the\n   application interface.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldt.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderjob.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_ask_stream_dialogue.htm\n'
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                   Language Dependent Text                               side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\n\n   The Language Dependent Text (LDT) mechanism is used to store texts used by\n   applications in external files. The texts are retrieved at run-time,\n   depending on the language Concept is running in, making it possible to\n   write language independent applications. Texts can easily be changed\n   without the need of recompiling the application they are used in.\n\n   LDT Files\n\n   The texts used by the LDT system are either stored in files which use the\n   initialization file format or in files with a special LDT file format.\n\n   The advantage of using the initialization file format, is that these files\n   are easy to maintain - any text editor supporting the UCS character set\n   can be used. Because this file format is fairly slow (especially when\n   accessing huge amounts of data), it is recommended to use this format only\n   in the development phase.\n\n   In a production environment we recommend to use the native LDT format,\n   which is optimized for quick access. This file format cannot be modified\n   directly (e.g. using a text editor). The initialization files used in the\n   development process have to be converted to LDT files. There are commands\n   in the 4GL which support this conversion process. It is also possible to\n   use the LDT conversion tool found in Concept's main menu to convert to and\n   from the LDT format.\n\n   The actual files containing the texts are defined in the Unique System\n   Database (uqsystem.ini). Each file used has to be listed in sections\n   called 'LDT-FILE-<LN>', where <LN> is one of Concept's language codes.\n   Each entry in the section has the following syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <LDTFileName>=[<Path>]<FileName>\n\n   <LDTFileName> is a unique name identifying a set of texts. This is the\n   name that is used in an application using LDT's. Names starting with '@'\n   are reserved for internal use.\n\n   An optional <Path> can be used to specify an exact location for the file\n   containing the texts. When no path is specified, Concept will try to find\n   the file in the application path(s). For LDT file names starting with @,\n   Concept will search in the setup directory.\n\n   <FileName> is the name of the file containing the text definitions. When\n   this file name is specified without an extension, Concept will assume the\n   extension '.ldt'.\n\n   LDT Definitions\n\n   The initialization file format files have to be stored in PLAIN/UCS format\n   and have the following layout:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [LDT-DEF-<LN>]\n\n   <Number>=<Text>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <LN> again is one of Concept's language codes and is must correspond with\n   the language code used in the LDT definition. Each text is identified by a\n   positive integer. The text should not be longer than 250 characters,\n   otherwise it will not be possible to use the LDT conversion tool on the\n   file (longer texts can be split up into several definitions and recombined\n   at runtime).\n\n   The text may contain parameter placeholders that are replaced with\n   parameter values when the LDT is used by an application. The placeholders\n   start with the '^' character, followed by digit (1 to 9). When the '^'\n   itself is to be used in the text, it has to be repeated.\n\n   Using LDT's\n\n   The usage of the LDT's is supported in the 4GL by an operator and a DIO\n   macro. Both of these use an LDT reference to specify the LDT file to use,\n   the number of the text to retrieve and optional parameter values. An LDT\n   reference can be defined like this:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <LDTReference>\xc2\xa0::=\xc2\xa0<LDTFileName>,<Number>[,<Parameter>]*\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <LDTFileName> is the name of an LDT file as described in LDT Files and\n   <Number> is the number of a text as described in LDT Definitions. Up to\n   nine parameter values can be used in the reference, replacing the\n   placeholders described in LDT Definitions.\n\n   Operator\n\n   The operator ldt can be used in expressions and returns the text defined\n   in the file referenced by the operator's parameter expression. The general\n   syntax for the operator is\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ldt(<TextExpression>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   where <TextExpression> must result in an LDT reference as described above.\n\n   DIO macro\n\n   The DIO macro ^LT can be used in element definitions and static form\n   definitions and will be expanded when the element is displayed. The\n   general syntax for the macro is\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ^LT,<LDTReference>;\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   with an LDT reference as described above.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Whenever an LDT reference is used, Concept will try to fetch the text\n   referenced from the file specified in the System Database. When no text\n   with the specified number exists, or the file specified in the LDT\n   definition could not be found, an error message will be returned.\n\n   When the LDT file name used is not defined for the current language,\n   Concept will try to use the definition in the English section\n   (LDT-FILE-EN) by default.\n\n   Important note\n\n   When the LDT definition references a file with the extension '.ldt' (which\n   is also the default when no extension is specified) and this file does not\n   exist, Concept will try to find a file with the same name and the\n   extension '.ini' instead. This is to simplify the LDT file setup. Normally\n   it is sufficient to define the file name without extension and Concept\n   will first look for a file with the extension '.ldt' and then, when this\n   file cannot be found, for a file with the extension '.ini'. When this file\n   does also not exists, Concept will return an error message.\n\n   LDT Functions\n\n   There are two functions supporting the conversion to and from the LDT file\n   format: ldt-load and ldt-unload. As the conversion process is supported by\n   the LDT conversion tool, there should be no need for using these functions\n   in your applications.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_job_dialogue.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_limitations.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_ldt.htm\n"

Note that topics with limitations of theoretical interest only\n   are not described.\n\n   In general, the limitations are common for all machine and operating\n   system platforms supported, and are described in the Limit column of the\n   tables below.\n\n   System\n\n   Describes the limitations at the system level.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Topic                                    Limit\n   Number of applications within one system Limited by disk space only\n\n   Applications\n\n   Describes the limitations per application file. Note that an application\n   file may contain several sub applications.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Topic                                       Limit\n   Number of sub applications                  32767\n   Number of streams                           32767\n   Number of forms                             32767\n   Number of elements                          512000\n   Number of tables                            32767\n   Number of columns accessed in one table     255 (DBMS dependent - may be\n                                               less)\n   Row value length                            32767 bytes\n\n   (the total length of all columns accessed   (DBMS dependent - may be less)\n   in one table)\n                                               10240 bytes\n   SQL expression length\n                                               (DBMS dependent - may be less)\n   Number of fields                            32767\n   Function buffer size                        65535 bytes\n   Expression buffer size                      65535 bytes\n   Function chain buffer size                  65535 bytes\n   Function info buffer size                   65535 bytes\n   Maximum number of functions in an           16383\n   application (see note 1)\n   Value buffer size (see note 2)              16 megabytes\n   Field value length                          10240 bytes\n   Array field length                          32767 bytes\n   Column value length (except for wide        10240 bytes\n   columns)\n                                               (DBMS dependent - may be less)\n   Maximum number of nested loop/forloop       40\n   functions\n   Maximum number of nested group-by functions 15\n   Maximum number of nested scroll functions   15\n   Maximum number of nested xml-scroll         50\n   functions\n   Maximum number of nested if functions       256\n   Token length (see note 3)                   10240 bytes\n   Maximum display length                      10240 characters\n   Maximum width of a matrix field             250 characters\n   Maximum line length in a data file (see     32768 characters\n   note 4)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   1) The practical maximum number of functions in an application is\n   dependant on which functions are used and the number of\n   parameters/expressions used by each function.\n\n   2) The value buffer is used to hold the field values. An integer2 field\n   uses 2 bytes of the value buffer, an integer4 field 4 bytes, and so on.\n   Wide columns are never stored in the value buffer.\n\n   3) The token length is the length of a logical language unit read by the\n   Concept 4GL Compiler from the application source file. For example, the\n   function compute(a=b) is interpreted as 2 tokens: compute and (a=b).\n\n   4) The maximum line length is the maximum number of characters that can be\n   written to or read from a line on a stream with formatting ASCII-DATA,\n   ASCII-FIELDS or CSV.\n\n   Menus\n\n   Describes the limitations in the menu system.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Topic                                   Limit\n   Menu name length                        30 characters\n   Menu item name length                   30 characters\n   Information text length                 256 characters\n   Position specification length           256 characters\n   Menu text or image specification length 128 characters\n   Menu command length                     1024 characters\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Dictionaries\n\n   Describes the limits in dictionary items.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Topic                       Limit\n   Table/Column name length    64 characters\n   Table/Column heading length 64 characters\n   Datatype name length        30 characters\n   Storage code length         40 characters\n   Display code length         40 characters\n   Number of group members     16\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldt.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_listview_form.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        Listview Form                                    side\n\n   A listview form displays a number of items in one of four different views.\n   The view to be used is defined in the [4]view declaration. The following\n   views are available:\n\n   Large Icons\n\n   Item labels and large icon images are displayed. The items are ordered\n   from left to right and from top to bottom.\n\n   Small Icons\n\n   Item labels and small icon images are displayed. The items are ordered\n   from left to right and from top to bottom.\n\n   List\n\n   Item labels and small icon images are displayed. The items are ordered\n   from top to bottom and from left to right.\n\n   Report (default view)\n\n   Item labels and small icon images are displayed in a column with an\n   optional column header. Additional information can be shown in separate\n   columns. The items are ordered from top to bottom.\n\n   Report view with a clickable header, grid lines and full row selection.\n\n   Report view with a non-clickable header, no grid lines and check-boxes.\n\n   Programming Listview Forms\n\n   Listview Form\n\n   Listviews are defined as a [5]form containing output [6]elements and\n   optional header elements, like in this example:\n\n   form="MyListview"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(LISTVIEW)\n\n   \xc2\xa0control-field("MyListview")\n\n   \xc2\xa0element-sequence(\';Name;Discount;Address\')\n\n   \xc2\xa0view(REPORT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0grid-lines(NONE)\n\n   \xc2\xa0buttons(OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0edit-labels(OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0full-row-select(ON)\n\n   \xc2\xa0multi-selection(OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="hName"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(HEADER)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,20)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="hDiscount"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(HEADER)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,10)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="hAddress"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(HEADER)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,15)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="Name"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(OUTPUT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,20)\n\n   \xc2\xa0label("hName")\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="Discount"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(OUTPUT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,10)\n\n   \xc2\xa0label("hDiscount")\n\n   \xc2\xa0alignment(DEFAULT,RIGHT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0element="Address"\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(OUTPUT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(0,15)\n\n   \xc2\xa0label("hAddress")\n\n   \xc2\xa0alignment(DEFAULT,LEFT)\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The\xc2\xa0columns\xc2\xa0defined\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0element-sequence\xc2\xa0declaration\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0shown\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0REPORT\xc2\xa0[7]view.\xc2\xa0In\xc2\xa0all\xc2\xa0other\xc2\xa0views,\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0text\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0first\xc2\xa0column\xc2\xa0(the\xc2\xa0label\xc2\xa0column)\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0shown\xc2\xa0along\xc2\xa0with\xc2\xa0an\xc2\xa0optional\xc2\xa0icon.\n\n   The [8]listview function is used to change the items shown in the\n   listview. Items can be added, modified and deleted. The listview function\n   can be used to modify single items or many items at once. The listview\n   function can also be used to obtain the state of the items (i.e. which\n   items are currently selected) and to change certain visual attributes of\n   the control.\n\n   The [9]control-field declaration defines the field that is to receive\n   input events. The field should be a field of [10]storage type INTEGER4 as\n   it receives the ID of the current item in the listview. The ENTER event\n   will be executed when a list item is activated (by double-clicking it or\n   pressing ENTER in the listview). The [11]@CHANGE event is used to trap\n   changes of an item\'s selection state, check state (when the [12]buttons\n   declaration is ON) and changes to the label text (when the [13]edit-labels\n   declaration is ON). The [14]@DELETE event will be triggered when the user\n   presses the Delete key.\n\n   The [15]grid-lines and the [16]full-row-select declarations influence the\n   visual attributes of the REPORT view. The [17]multi-selection declaration\n   defines whether it is possible to select multiple items or not.\n\n   Listview Elements\n\n   The elements that are defined on the listview form are defined in the same\n   manner as [18]grid-form elements. Only the following four declarations are\n   supported: [19]type, [20]size, [21]label, [22]connect, [23]information and\n   [24]alignment.\n\n   The element types that can be used are OUTPUT and HEADER. If OUTPUT\n   elements without the label declaration are defined, the listview will not\n   contain column headers in REPORT view- even if header elements are defined\n   on the form.\n\n   Only the header elements can be connected to fields. If no header element\n   is connected to a field, the listview header line will be drawn using a\n   "flat" style (non-clickable header) - otherwise the header elements will\n   be clickable. The field functions of the connected field will be executed\n   when clicking the header of a column.\n\n   The height of the size declaration will be ignored - only the width will\n   be used. It is also not possible to define the position of a column as it\n   is defined implicitly through the element-sequence.\n\n   Information is used to provide tooltips for the listview. Please note that\n   the tooltips is column and not item specific.\n\n   The alignment of a column must be defined on the output elements. Only the\n   horizontal alignment will be used - the vertical alignment will be\n   ignored.\n\n   The column header texts, column widths and column alignments can be\n   changed by modifying the element attributes using the [25]change-element\n   function and executing the listview function with the [26]UPDATE command\n   afterwards.\n\n   Drag and Drop\n\n   Listview forms support dragging through the [27]DRAG event programmed on\n   the [28]control-field. The [29]@DRAG_VALUE contains a semicolon separated\n   list of IDs of the items selected for the drag operation.\n\n   Dropping is supported through the [30]drop-types declaration and the\n   [31]DROP event programmed on the control-field. The [32]position attribute\n   of the [33]drop function returns the ID of the listview item where the\n   drop occurred.\n\n   Special Notes on Listviews\n\n   The listview control is implemented on top of Microsoft\xef\xbf\xbds class libraries,\n   and the following limitations are thereby imposed:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Version 4.70 and earlier of comctl32.dll does not support different\n   background colours - the standard @WINDOW colour is the only usable\n   background. Version 4.71 and later of comctl32.dll has full support for\n   background colours (image and gradient colours are not supported though).\n\n   \xc2\xb7Version 4.70 and earlier of comctl32.dll lacks support for foreground\n   colours and use @WINDOWTEXT. Version 4.71 and later of comctl32.dll has\n   full support for foreground (text) colours.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The F2 key is used for label editing and cannot be programmed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using the buttons(\'ON\') attribute of the change-form function any\n   items that has been previously checked will be unchecked.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The comctl32.dll documentation states that column dependent tooltips in\n   report view is only available when the [34]full-row-select attribute is\n   set to ON. Note also that column dependent tooltips support is not present\n   in all versions of the comctl32.dll.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Current version of the comctl32.dll does not support tooltips for header\n   elements in REPORT view.\n\n   [35][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_limitations.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. Concept supports locking on field, element and form\n   level, and this chapter will try to summarize the functionality.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Locking is set by the lock declaration on the [4]field or [5]element\n   component, and can be changed at runtime by the [6]change,\n   [7]change-element or [8]change-form functions.\n\n   The lock state is restored to the initial lock state whenever the record\n   to which an element is connected is cleared. The initial lock state is set\n   by the lock declarations or by using the PERMANENT modifier for lock\n   values in the change or change-element functions.\n\n   The change function applies lock settings to all elements connected to the\n   specified field.\n\n   The change-form function, without the tab-index parameter, applies lock\n   settings to all elements belonging to the form, but does not allow\n   changing the initial lock state. When the tab-index parameter is used the\n   change-form function is used to set the lock state for a tab in a\n   tab-form.\n\n   Example\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   form="MyForm"\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n \xc2\xa0....\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   database=MYDB\n\n   \xc2\xa0table="Customer"\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0field="CustCode"\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           Logging                                       side\n\n   Concept supports logging of database operations in a separate log table.\n   This is useful when you need to keep the history of operations done on a\n   table.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Logging has to be explicitly declared in each application. The log\n   declaration used in a [4]table definition indicates that insert and delete\n   operations on the table will be logged. Used on a [5]field definition,\n   modifications of the field will be logged.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the logging fails, e.g. the log table is full or does not exist, the\n   database operation will be aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The log database must be specified in the uqconfig file. If no log\n   database is specified, the log declarations are ignored.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The log table can be located in any database available to the system\n   including the database of the logged objects.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Security provides applications to inspect the log table. For this purpose\n   the log table must be made available to the system through a database\n   called UQSLOG. So-called [6]Log Description Applications may be defined to\n   provide descriptions for key values stored in the log table.\n\n   The UQLOG table\n\n   The log database must contain a standard table called "UQLOG" which stores\n   information about modifications and contains the following columns:\n\n   Name     Storage   Explanation\n   USER     INTEGER4  The identity of the user who performed the operation.\n                      This identity is found in the Security system.\n   DATE     INTEGER4  The date of the operation. The format is YYYYMMDD.\n   TIME     INTEGER4  The time of the operation. The format is HHMMSS.\n                      A sequential number for an operation, starting at one\n   SEQNO    INTEGER2  and incremented for every row where there are multiple\n                      entries.\n   UQLOG    <group>   The key field, consisting of USER, DATE, TIME and\n                      SEQNO.\n   OPER     ALPHA(2)  Indicates type of operation. I=Insert. D=Delete.\n                      M=Modify. E=Event\n   DB       ALPHA(8)  The name of the database.\n   TABLE    ALPHA(8)  The name of the table.\n   KEYNAME  ALPHA(8)  The name of the main key of the logged row.\n   KEYVAL   ALPHA(40) The value of the field in KEYNAME. For group fields,\n                      each value is separated by a comma.\n   COLNAME  ALPHA(8)  The name of a column which has a new or modified value.\n                      The old and the new value of the column COLNAME. The\n                      layout is: <old value> -> <new value>\n   COLVAL   ALPHA(60)\n                      The layout for each value is the same as for the field\n                      KEYVAL.\n   APPLICAT ALPHA(20) The application name.\n   SYSID    INTEGER4  The system identifier.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The following duplicate keys are also defined on the table:\n\n   Index    Consisting of\n   DATETABL SYSID, DATE, TIME, SEQNO, DB, TABLE.\n   TABLHIST SYSID, DB, TABLE, DATE, TIME, SEQNO\n   KEYVHIST SYSID, DB, TABLE, KEYNAME, KEYVAL\n   COLUHIST SYSID, DB, TABLE, COLNAME, DATE, TIME, SEQNO\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [7][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_locking.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_matrix.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_log_description_applications.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_log.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                      Matrix Definitions                                 side\n\n   This section explains all the definitions used in defining matrix reports.\n   A matrix is defined as a table with columns and rows where the number of\n   columns and rows is defined dynamically at run time. The intersection\n   between a row and a column is called a cell and it is possible to define\n   aggregate operations on it. Values are inserted into the matrix using the\n   insert(field="m") function and are grouped according to the group-by\n   definition. Labels (or headings) can be defined and totals can be added\n   both to columns and rows.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The following is an example layout of a very simple matrix where some\n   value is accumulated for each city, each month:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0   Oslo London Paris\n   JAN 1200 2450   3000\n   FEB 2000 1900   6700\n   MAR 1500 4200   4000\n   APR 1700 2300   5000\n   MAY 3200 2900   8000\n   JUN 1500 2500   4300\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Syntax\n\n   field=<name>\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(MATRIX)\n\n   \xc2\xa0group-by\xc2\xa0(rows([\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0<\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0>\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0]<field>,...),columns(<field>,...)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0cells\xc2\xa0(\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0<AGGRCELL>(<field>)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0count(*[,<display>])\xc2\xa0},...\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0labels\xc2\xa0([rows(<Text\xc2\xa0expression>,...),]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[columns(<Text\xc2\xa0expression>,...),]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[cells(<Text\xc2\xa0expression>,...),]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[totals(<Text\xc2\xa0expression>,...)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0totals\xc2\xa0([rows\xc2\xa0(\xc2\xa0<AGGR>(),...\xc2\xa0),]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[columns(<AGGR>(<index>[,<display>]),...)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0<AGGR>\xc2\xa0:==\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0sum\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0avg\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0min\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0max\xc2\xa0}\n\n   \xc2\xa0<AGGRCELL>\xc2\xa0:==\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0<AGGR>\xc2\xa0}\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Display\n\n   May be used to define the width of columns. Note that column totals can\n   have a separate display code from the cells allowing larger numbers.\n   Default display codes are always derived from the display code of the\n   parameter fields.\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of a field defined in the application. The field must be a simple\n   data type, not a group, array or another matrix field.\n\n   Declarations\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of the matrix field. See field section for rules.\n\n   Group-by\n\n   Defines grouping of values for rows and columns. Each direction supports\n   up to 3 levels. Each level is defined by one field parameter. Example 2\n   has 2 row levels. The rows and columns in the matrix are sorted based on\n   the storage code of the parameter fields and the < | > prefix which\n   specifies sorting in the resulting matrix where < means descending and >\n   means ascending (default).\n\n   Cells\n\n   Defines the values to be aggregated in the matrix. More than one value can\n   be defined and printed as illustrated in example 2.\n\n   If count(*) is used, a counter is incremented by one for each insert in\n   each cell (it is not based on a value in any fields). To use count in\n   totals a sum aggregate should be applied to the count cell index.\n\n   Labels\n\n   Labels is optional and is used when the contents of the group-by values,\n   the name of the cell fields or standard headings for totals are not\n   suitable for printing. In the examples a month number is used for grouping\n   (to have the months sorted correctly) and a month name for printing. The\n   number of parameters to each sub component may be less than the number of\n   parameters in the corresponding declaration in which case default labels\n   will be used for the remaining components.\n\n   Totals\n\n   Column totals are represented as a separate column at the right end of the\n   matrix, one column for each total definition.\n\n   Row totals are added as one row per total definition. Width and aggregate\n   operands are always based on the columns in the matrix. Display code and\n   index can not be defined for row totals.\n\n   <Index> is a numeric reference to the parameters in the cells declaration.\n   1 means the first cell, 2 the second and so on.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The contents of a matrix is built using the insert(field="Matrix field")\n   function. Each time the insert statement is used the current values in the\n   group-by values are used to identify a unique cell in the matrix and the\n   cell values are aggregated into this cell. The matrix is automatically\n   expanded and sorted as new group-by values are inserted. Labels are\n   evaluated the first time a new cell is inserted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The matrix field can only be printed using a form explicitly connected to\n   the matrix field using the matrix form declaration. All totals are\n   calculated and formatted as part of the printing process.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The matrix is cleared (emptied) every time it is printed, no explicit\n   action is required.\n\n   Limits\n\n   \xc2\xb7The maximum width of a matrix field is 250 characters\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [4][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_log.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_matrix.htm\n'

b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                      Progress Dialogues                                 side\n\n   Progress Dialogues are [4]Online applications that are used by the\n   [5]progress-dialogue function to display information about an ongoing\n   operation. They must be implemented according the following set of rules\n   in order to work properly.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Application Interface\n\n   Import\n\n   Field        Storage Description\n   ThreadHandle I4      Thread handle of the application initiating the\n                        Progress Dialogue.\n                        Parameter string as specified in the text parameter\n   Parameters   A(1024) of the progress-dialogue function when initiating the\n                        Progress Dialogue.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Application Startup\n\n   The imported parameter string should be handled during the application\n   startup if needed. How the string is interpreted is up to the Progress\n   Dialogue application. It may e.g. contain the title of the dialogue.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Message Handler\n\n   The application must contain an event handler for the [6]@MESSAGE event to\n   process the messages sent by the progress-dialogue function. Only messages\n   with the type $uqMsgProgress must be read - all other message types should\n   be ignored. How the text received is handled is up to the Progress\n   Dialogue application, with one exception: If the message text \'@TERMINATE\'\n   is received, the application should terminate (this special message text\n   is sent by the progress-dialogue function when the TERMINATE command is\n   used). The following code implements a minimal message handler:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   on\xc2\xa0(@MESSAGE)\n\n   \xc2\xa0read-message(wanted-type($uqMsgProgress),\n\n   \xc2\xa0text("@A"),\n\n   \xc2\xa0status("@X"))\n\n   \xc2\xa0if("@A"\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0\'@TERMINATE\')\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0return()\n\n   \xc2\xa0else\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0*\xc2\xa0---\xc2\xa0handle\xc2\xa0message\n\n   \xc2\xa0endif\n\n   endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Application Termination\n\n   If the application is terminated for other reasons than a \'@TERMINATE\'\n   message, the progress-dialogue function must be used to signal the\n   termination of the dialogue to the Concept Runtime. This is done by\n   executing the TERMINATE command without specifying the dialogue name. If\n   the termination is not signaled to the Runtime, any later attempt to\n   initiate a Progress Dialogue with the same name will fail.\n\n   Application Scope\n\n   Progress Dialogues are started in a thread separate from the one\n   initiating the dialogue. This makes it possible to update the dialogue\n   from any application thread in the current session. A side effect of this\n   behaviour is that the "main" application might still be activated by the\n   user. If you want to prevent this, you can use the lock parameter of the\n   [7]change-session function to lock a thread.\n\n   Example\n\n   The chapter describing the standard Progress Dialogue provided with\n   Concept (\'[8]@UQUProgres\') contains the source code for this application.\n   You may use this code as an example for your own Progress Dialogues.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_relative_sizes_and_positions.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_online.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_progress_dialogue.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onmessage\n   7. file:///dev/html_change_session__.htm#idh_ma_changesession_lock\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_uqprogres.htm\n'
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                 Relative Sizes and Positions                            side\n\n   Positions and sizes for forms and elements can be specified relative to\n   the size of the form or stream that owns them. A set of operators and\n   predefined code words can be used to create expressions that ensure that\n   elements and forms are resized or repositioned when a form or a stream\n   changes its size.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Legal operators (with precedence):\n\n   Operator Description\n   ( )      brackets\n   -        unary minus\n   * /      multiply and divide\n   + -      plus and minus\n   MAX MIN  Maximum and minimum\n            The FROM operator ensures that left hand result is at least the\n            value of the right hand result.\n   FROM TO\n            The TO operator ensures that left hand result is less or equal\n            the value of the right hand result.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Predefined code words Description\n   OH                    Owners inner height\n   OW                    Owners inner width\n   H                     The form/element's own outer height (May only be\n                         used for position)\n   W                     The form/element's own outer width (May only be used\n                         for position)\n   SBH                   The height of a system generated horizontal\n                         scrollbar\n   SBW                   The width of a system generated vertical scrollbar\n   LH                    The height (thickness) of a horizontal line\n   LW                    The width (thickness) of vertical line\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   For an element, the owner is always defined as the form to which it\n   belongs.\n\n   For forms it is either the form specified by the [4]owner-form declaration\n   or the output stream. For online applications the output stream is always\n   defined as the application window. For reports the output stream might be\n   a printer page or a document page as well as a screen window.\n\n   Inner height and width are the height and width inside frames, titles and\n   borders (margins).\n\n   Outer height and width are defined by the total size occupied by an\n   element or form including frame and titles (borders only applied to\n   streams).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The size is always calculated before the position. Therefore the H and W\n   code words can be used for relative positions and not for sizes.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the expression evaluates to a value less than zero, zero is used.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [5][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_progress_dialogues.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexpr.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm#idh_ma_form_ownerform\n   5. file:///dev/html_example_relative_size_and_position.htm\n"
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       SQL Expressions                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The [5]table declarations SQL-WHERE, SQL-ORDER-BY and SQL-GROUP-BY, and\n   the function [6]sql-execute, all use alphanumeric expressions that are\n   supposed to contain parts of or complete SQL statements.\n\n   Concept does not put any restriction on the statements, thus it is the\n   responsibility of the programmer to ensure that these statements follow\n   the rules of the DBMS used. An error will not be detected by the Concept\n   4GL Compiler, but by the DBMS at runtime.\n\n   The syntax of SQL statements may vary between the different DBMS\xef\xbf\xbds, i.e.\n   naming conventions and operators available. If the application is to be\n   portable across DBMS\xef\xbf\xbds, please notice the following:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If possible, utilize the [7]SQL macros described below, especially the\n   macro @CONDITION\n\n   \xc2\xb7Only the comparison operators =, <>, <, >, <= and >= are guaranteed to be\n   portable\n\n   \xc2\xb7Only the logical operators AND, OR and NOT are guaranteed to be portable\n\n   \xc2\xb7Avoid referring columns which are not selected\n\n   SQL Macros\n\n   SQL macros may be used to generate a portable and syntactically correct\n   SQL statement. SQL macros are interpreted by Concept and replaced by text\n   when the actual SQL statement is to be used. The [8]sql-exec parameter\n   result can be used to obtain the result of Concept's macro expansion.\n\n   By default, an SQL macro is identified by the lead-in character @ followed\n   by a macro name. The macro @LEADIN may be used to change the lead-in\n   character and the macro @RAW may be used to turn off macro interpretation.\n\n   <Column Specification> means @ENTITY or @ITEM.\n\n   @ALIASITEM([<Logical Database Name>,][<Logical TableName>.][<ColumnName>])\n\n   The macro returns a table or column name as defined by the parameter. The\n   syntax of the name returned is as expected by the DBMS. If both\n   <TableName> and <ColumnName> are specified the macro returns the alias\n   name generated by Concept, unless it defines the current table and the\n   current table has no declarative joins connected, in which case it returns\n   the physical table name.\n\n   @COLUMN(<FieldName>)\n\n   The macro returns the column name associated with the given field. The\n   syntax of the name returned is as expected by the DBMS, and is always\n   prefixed with the name of the owning table.\n\n   @CONDITION(<LogicalCondition>)\n\n   The macro returns a logical condition in the format expected by the DBMS.\n   Conditions use the following syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   logicalCondition: \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0[NOT]\xc2\xa0condition\n\n   condition:\xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0operand\xc2\xa0compareOperator\xc2\xa0operand\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0operand\xc2\xa0IN\xc2\xa0(operand\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0operand})\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0operand\xc2\xa0BETWEEN\xc2\xa0operand\xc2\xa0AND\xc2\xa0operand\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   compareOperator: \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0<>\xc2\xa0<\xc2\xa0>\xc2\xa0<=\xc2\xa0>=\xc2\xa0LIKE\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   operand: \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0<FieldName>\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0<NumericConstant>\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0'<TextConstant>'\n\n   The\xc2\xa0interpretation\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0operators\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0as\xc2\xa0defined\xc2\xa0by\xc2\xa0standard\xc2\xa0SQL.\n\n   An operand referring to a field name is replaced by a column name if the\n   field belongs to the logical table to which the SQL expression is\n   associated, otherwise it is replaced by the value of the field.\n\n   If the operand before the operator refers to a field name and another\n   operand being a constant, then the constant is reformatted according to\n   the format of the field. Other constants are treated accordingly.\n\n   Note that an apostrophe is represented inside a string by two consecutive\n   apostrophes in a row, such as in \xef\xbf\xbdThe DBMS'\xef\xbf\xbds\xef\xbf\xbd.\n\n   @ENTITY([<Logical Database Name>,][<TableName>.][<ColumnName>])\n\n   The macro returns a table or column name as defined by the parameter. The\n   syntax of the name returned is as expected by the DBMS.\n\n   This macro should be used whenever the table or column referenced is not\n   defined in the application.\n\n   Using the Logical Database Name parameter allows using tables and/or\n   columns from other databases than the one specified as the base of the\n   operation (origin database). Please note that the database in question\n   must exist in the same DBMS server as the origin database, and the user\n   logged in on the origin database must have the appropriate access to the\n   other database.\n\n   @IFNULL(<FieldName>|<Column Specification>,<Value>)\n\n   The macro returns the value specified if the field value is NULL.\n   Otherwise the field value is returned.\n\n   @ITEM([<Logical Database Name>,][<TableName>.][<ColumnName>])\n\n   The macro returns a table or column name as defined by the parameter. The\n   syntax of the name returned is as expected by the DBMS. If both\n   <TableName> and <ColumnName> are specified and the macro is used in an\n   expression that is used on the table referenced, the macro returns the\n   alias names generated by Concept.\n\n   This macro should be used whenever a column referenced is not defined in\n   the application, but the table it belongs to is.\n\n   Using the Logical Database Name parameter allows using tables and/or\n   columns from other databases than the one specified as the base of the\n   operation (origin database). Please note that the database in question\n   must exist in the same DBMS server as the origin database, and the user\n   logged in on the origin database must have the appropriate access to the\n   other database.\n\n   @LEADIN([<Character>])\n\n   The macro is used to change the lead in character for SQL macros from the\n   default @ character. If <Character> is not given, macro interpretation is\n   turned off for the rest of the statement.\n\n   @LOWER(<FieldName>|<Column Specification>|<VALUE>)\n\n   The macro returns the lowercase value of the given field or value.\n\n   @MODULO(<FieldName>|<Column Specification>,<Value>)\n\n   The macro returns the remainder of the value of field <FieldName> divided\n   by <Value>.\n\n   @RAW([<Number>])\n\n   The macro turns off macro interpretation for the next number of characters\n   as defined by <Number>. If <Number> is not given, or the value is less\n   than 1, macro interpretation is turned off for the rest of the statement.\n\n   @SQLCOLUMN(<FieldName>)\n\n   The macro returns the SQL column definition associated with the given\n   field. The syntax of the definition returned is as expected by the DBMS.\n\n   @SUBSTRING(<FieldName>|<Value>|<Column Specification>,<From>,<Length>)\n\n   The macro returns a sub-string of the specified field or value starting\n   from the given position and with the given length.\n\n   @TABLE(<FieldName>)\n\n   The macro returns the name of the table owning the given field. The syntax\n   of the name returned is as expected by the DBMS.\n\n   @UPPER(<FieldName>|<Column Specification>|<VALUE>)\n\n   The macro returns the uppercase value of the given field or value.\n\n   @VALUE(<FieldName>)\n\n   The macro returns the current value of the given field. The format used is\n   as expected by the DBMS for the storage type of the field. The field can\n   not be a group field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Some database interfaces has special requirement for cross database SQL\n   macros. See the Advanced Topic for your interface in Operation Guide for\n   further details.\n\n   [9][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_relative_sizes_and_positions.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_storage.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_sql.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexec.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexpr.htm#idh_de_sqlmacros\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexec.htm#idh_ma_sqlexec_result\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_sqlexpr.htm\n"
