b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                      Style Definitions                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Defines syntax rules for style definitions. Styles define all visible\n   attributes of a window (or [5]stream in Concept terms), a form or an\n   element. A style consists of four parts, the text colour, the background,\n   the text font and a frame definition. Styles are defined in a separate\n   file (uqsystem.ini, see Visma Enterprise Concept Operations Guide) and are\n   referred to from the applications. A style may be overloaded in the\n   application by changing one or more of the style components.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   The following syntax applies both to stream, form and element declarations\n   in Concept.\n\n   \xc2\xa0style(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]name\xc2\xa0)\n\n   background(\xc2\xa0colour(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]colour\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0[10]image(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]image\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0transparent\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\n   \xc2\xa0gradient(\xc2\xa0colour(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]colour\xc2\xa0)[,\xc2\xa0luminance(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]lower,\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]upper\xc2\xa0)][,\xc2\xa0orientation(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]orientation\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0skin(skinReference))\n\n   colour(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]colour\xc2\xa0)\n\n   font(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]logicalFont\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0[25]?[26]predefinedFont\xc2\xa0|\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0faceName\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]points\xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]fontAttribute\xc2\xa0]]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   frame(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]frameType\xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0colour(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]colour\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Remarks\n\n   Background\n\n   \xc2\xb7A luminance value defines a colours luminance in percent. 100% is equal\n   to the colour specified, a higher percentage makes the colour lighter, a\n   lower percentage makes the colour darker.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The default luminance for a gradient background is 0,100.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The default orientation for a gradient background is VERTICAL.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the lower and the upper luminance value of a gradient background are\n   equal, and no orientation is specified, the colour\'s luminance will be\n   changed according to the value specified.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the lower and the upper luminance value of a gradient background are\n   equal, and an orientation is specified, a gradient ranging from the\n   defined value to 100 and back will be used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7For a detailed description of [35]image definitions, please refer to the\n   chapter on [36]images.\n\n   \xc2\xb7skinReference refers to a skin definition defined in the SKINS section of\n   the uqsystem.ini file\n\n   Font\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not advised to use printer specific fonts in a font declaration.\n   Doing so will make the 4GL application dependent on specific hardware or\n   software, which will make distribution of applications to other\n   environments problematic.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to support barcodes in 4GL applications by using a\n   specific barcode font. These fonts translate ASCII characters to an\n   appropriate barcode sequence. The only thing to do is to install a barcode\n   font on the Windows workstation. Then, Concept will show the barcode\n   correctly in the Forms Painter, preview screens, and so on. To print a\n   barcode correctly might require a change in the local printer setup.\n   Barcode fonts are available from several suppliers - many of them have an\n   own Internet site.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The SHADOW font attribute can not be applied on the following element\n   types: TREEVIEW, LIST-BOX and multi line INPUT and OUTPUT as well as\n   elements that are a part of a LISTVEIW form.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If one of the font specifiers are left out it will default to the\n   currently defined font of the element. E.g specifying font(,,BOLD) will\n   result in an element using the currently defined font of the element but\n   with the BOLD attribute set.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Use the NONE font attribute to remove any font attributes defined on \xc2\xa0the\n   font (does not remove attributes defined on the font specification in the\n   font section in the uqSystem.ini file).\n\n   \xc2\xb7If one of the font specifiers are specified as @, it will default to the\n   font defined for the style of the element. E.g specifying font(,,@) will\n   result in an element using the currently defined font of the element but\n   with the attributes defined on the style font set.\n\n   Frame\n\n   \xc2\xb7The frame attributes tool-sizeable, tool-dialogue, dialogue and sizeable\n   are only available on streams.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The pen frame specifies different line-styles for the 4 sides of a frame.\n   In sequential order, it specifies the left side, the top, the right and\n   the bottom side of the frame. If less than 4 line-styles are specified,\n   then the line-style of the unspecified side is the same as the line-style\n   of the last side specified. Thus:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0frame(pen(none,dot,line))\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0will show a frame with no line at the left side, a dotted line at the\n   top, and a single line at the right and the bottom.\n\n   Default styles\n\n   A default style exists for any declaration in the Concept 4GL language.\n   These styles are defined in the uqsystem.ini file distributed with Concept\n   in the setup directory. These styles may be changed, but it is strongly\n   recommended to create your own styles.\n\n   The default style for a stream is named <prefix>-STREAM and for a form\n   <prefix>-FORM.\n\n   For fields and elements, the default style name is equal to the type\n   declaration of the field or element. Note that drop-down-list-box and\n   drop-down-combo-box use <prefix>-LIST-BOX and <prefix>-COMBO-BOX as\n   default style. Also vertical-scroll-bar and horizontal-scroll-bar have a\n   common default style named <prefix>-SCROLL-BAR.\n\n   Focus styles\n\n   A focus style can be defined for each element which has a default style.\n   The focus style has to be defined with the name of the default style\n   followed by -FOCUS (e.g. OL-OUTPUT-FOCUS). A focus style can be used to\n   highlight the element which currently has the input focus, i.e. the\n   current input field.\n\n   Note\n\n   In previous versions OUTPUT elements were automatically highlighted. Now\n   the element with the input focus will not be highlighted at all, unless a\n   focus style has been defined. The system setting "output-element-focus"\n   (see Operations Guide, Unique System Database) can be used to switch on\n   the old behaviour.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   If the system is to run on both graphical monitors and monochrome\n   terminals, care must be taken when using styles. Plan the mapping of\n   colours and fonts in advance!\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [37][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_storage.htm\n   2. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        System Fields                                    side\n\n   In addition to [4]global fields it is possible to define system fields.\n   These fields can be used in any application of the system without having\n   to define them in the application (as is the case with global fields).\n   System fields can have a thread local scope, which means that they are\n   initialized in every new thread, or a session global scope. The first case\n   can be compared to the scope of global fields (with the difference that\n   global field values are copied to the new thread), the latter case makes\n   it possible to share field values between threads. In this case the\n   definition can also contain a modifier telling Concept not to include the\n   field in the list of field values sent to the SERVER when ordering the\n   execution of an application via the [5]order-job function.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   System fields are defined in the system database (uqsystem.ini) and\n   consist of a name, the scope, a storage code and an initial value.\n\n   [SystemFields]\n\n   <Name>={THREAD|SESSION[ NOTRANSFER]};<StorageCode>;<InitialValue>\n\n   Example\n\n   [SystemFields]\n\n   anIntegerField=SESSION;I2;0\n\n   anAlphaField=THREAD;A(64);Concept\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0great!\n\n   System\xc2\xa0fields\xc2\xa0are\xc2\xa0used\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa04GL\xc2\xa0applications\xc2\xa0like\xc2\xa0any\xc2\xa0other\xc2\xa0field.\xc2\xa0The\xc2\xa0name\xc2\xa0defined\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0system\xc2\xa0database\xc2\xa0must\xc2\xa0be\xc2\xa0prefixed\xc2\xa0with\xc2\xa0\'@@\'.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Example\n\n   increment("@@anIntegerField")\n\n   message(\'The\xc2\xa0value\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0"\'\xc2\xa0&\xc2\xa0trim("@@anAlphaField")\xc2\xa0&\xc2\xa0\'"\')\n\n   Limitations\n\n   \xc2\xb7System fields may use any storage code, but it is not possible to define\n   arrays.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not possible to use system fields with the [6]field operator.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_styles.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_tempdb.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm#idh_ma_field_global\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderjob.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorsother\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Temporary Tables                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Concept includes support for a special database type \'TEMP\', in which\n   temporary tables are defined. From the 4GL programmers point of view, a\n   temporary table allows the same 4GL operations as any table connected to a\n   standard (non-relational) single-user DBMS interface without transaction\n   control. The major difference between temporary tables and (normal)\n   database tables is found in the life cycle of the table\'s data. A\n   temporary table is either configured to hold its data throughout a\n   complete Concept session (a \'session persistent\' table), an application\n   thread (\'thread persistent\') or it can be set up to follow the life cycle\n   of an application (\'non-persistent\').\n\n   Information on how to set up a temporary database in the uqconfig\n   configuration file can be found in the Operations Guide. This manual also\n   contains information on how to set up a dictionary for the temporary\n   database. A special type of temporary tables ([5]Automatic Temporary\n   Tables) can be used without having the define a dictionary.\n\n   Temporary Tables Implementation\n\n   A persistent temporary table is physically created the first time it is\n   opened by an application in the session or thread, and data inserted in\n   the table will be available until the Concept session or thread is\n   terminated. A non-persistent temporary table is physically created the\n   first time it is opened in an application hierarchy, and physically\n   removed when the application that created it is terminated, thus allowing\n   any application further down in the application hierarchy to access the\n   table\'s data.\n\n   When a temporary table is created, it is created based on the information\n   found in its dictionary and not on the "logical" layout defined in the\n   application. This allows several application to access the same physical\n   table using different column selections and even different keys.\n\n   Temporary tables support all the standard 4GL database operations. In\n   addition, some extra functionality is built in through the\n   [6]synchronize() function, allowing the 4GL programmer to extract data\n   from a data source into a temporary table and afterwards synchronize\n   changes done to the temporary table back into the original data source.\n   This functionality is achieved through the use of a special internal\n   column UQRCSTAT (of storage integer2) as well as some built-in\n   functionality that keeps track of updated and deleted records in a\n   synchronized table. The value of the UQRCSTAT column is fully maintained\n   by the interface itself and can only be modified through use of the\n   synchronize function.\n\n   When a record is inserted into a temporary table, it will initially get\n   the record status INSERTED and this status will not change until the table\n   is synchronized. This means that if a record with status INSERTED is\n   updated the values of the record are changed and there will be no\n   reference to the original set of data values - if the record is deleted it\n   will be completely removed from the table. After a successful\n   synchronization, the record status is always set to NONE.\n\n   If a record with status NONE is updated it will get record status UPDATED\n   and the interface will keep a copy of the record\'s original data (up until\n   next synchronization). If a record with status NONE or UPDATED is deleted,\n   then the record will get status DELETED and only the original set of data\n   values will be preserved, The record will not be visible to any\n   applications, except through the use of the synchronize() function with\n   the signal-events(ON) parameter.\n\n   The [7]signal-events() parameter of the synchronize() function can be used\n   to distinguish between an internal and an external synchronization. An\n   internal synchronization will rebuild the temporary table by physically\n   removing all original copies of updated and deleted records as well as\n   resetting the UQRCSTAT column (to record status NONE). An external\n   synchronization will enable the programmer to synchronize changes in the\n   temporary table with the original data source. This is achieved by\n   programming the [8]@INSERT/[9]@DELETE/[10]@UPDATE events on the temporary\n   table which is the subject of the synchronize function. To distinguish\n   between normal @INSERT/@DELETE/@UPDATE events and the synchronize events\n   the programmer can test the @EVENT_PARAM field for the value\n   \'TEMP-TABLE-SYNC\'. In the case of an @UPDATE event the [11]OLD operator\n   can be used to retrieve the original data values of the record.\n\n   Automatic Temporary Tables\n\n   A special variant of non-persistent temporary tables can be used in\n   applications by using the pre-defined internal [12]database "UQAPPTMP".\n   For tables belonging to this database, dictionary information is defined\n   directly in the application. As the dictionary information is not\n   available elsewhere, such tables can only be used in the sub-application\n   in which they are defined. [13]Table and [14]column properties that\n   normally are defined in a dictionary - especially the storage code for\n   columns - have to be defined in the application source code. Apart from\n   data being only available in the current application, automatic temporary\n   tables work the same way as normal temporary tables.\n\n   Special Notes on Temporary Tables\n\n   (See Operations Guide for Limitations on Temporary Tables)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7As records are inserted they are also sorted according to the key of the\n   application performing the inserts. If the records are inserted with\n   sequentially increasing key values, it will dramatically improve the\n   performance. Please note that uniqueness for indexes is only checked for\n   the index used when inserting.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Temporary tables might be sorted on any column or columns combination in\n   the table, but only one sort sequence is maintained at a time. This means\n   that if an application has two logical tables accessing the same physical\n   temporary table using different keys, the whole table is re-sorted when\n   the application performs operations on both tables. The performance of the\n   sort operation can be improved by making sure that all the key columns for\n   complex keys are defined "close" to each other in the dictionary, meaning\n   that you should avoid gaps in the sequence numbers between those columns.\n\n   \xc2\xb7[15]Sql-exec with command COUNT(<physical table name>) might be used to\n   return the number of significant rows in the table.\n\n   \xc2\xb7[16]Sql-exec with command MIN(<physical table name>,<column name>) might\n   be used to return the minimum value of the column. The column must be of\n   [17]storage type I1, I2 or I4.\n\n   \xc2\xb7[18]Sql-exec with command MAX(<physical table name>,<column name>) might\n   be used to return the maximum value of the column. The column must be of\n   [19]storage type I1, I2 or I4.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Temporary tables support NULL values if the table is defined to handle\n   null values. It is also possible to configure a temporary table to set the\n   default values of columns not included in an insert to NULL (see\n   Operations Guide).\n\n   \xc2\xb7The data of temporary tables are stored on the scratch path defined by\n   the system. The amount of disk space needed for a temporary table is\n   dependent of the record size, number of records and the amount of changes\n   done to the table between each synchronization. The absolute maximum\n   number of bytes can be calculated as ((record size in bytes + X )*number\n   of records )*2. The value of X might vary from a minimum of 7 bytes to the\n   absolute maximum of 578 bytes, dependent on the number of columns in the\n   table and the storage types of the columns (caused by alignment).\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_system_fields.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_threads.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_tempdb.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_tempdb.htm#idh_ma_tempdb_auto\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_synchronize.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_synchronize.htm#idh_ma_synchronize_signalevents\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_oninsert\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_ondelete\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onupdate\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorsother\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_database.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexec.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexec.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_storage.htm#idh_ma_storage_codes\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sqlexec.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_storage.htm#idh_ma_storage_codes\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           Threads                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The application thread mechanism provides functionality to run parallel\n   applications. Each application thread maintains its own application stack\n   (call hierarchy) which runs independently from the other threads. The user\n   can switch between the topmost applications of each thread either by\n   clicking on the window, or by choosing them from the "Windows" menu. 4GL\n   applications can programmatically change the focus to another thread.\n\n   Starting Threads\n\n   When starting Concept, an initial application thread is automatically\n   started. The [5]start function can be used to start additional threads. It\n   is also possible to start new threads using the event [6]START (e.g. from\n   a menu). The application started becomes the "root application" in the\n   thread. It is then possible to [7]call or [8]run other applications, which\n   then will belong to this application thread. A thread is terminated when\n   it\'s root application is terminated. When running an application from the\n   root application, this application becomes the root application.\n\n   Each active thread can uniquely be identified via it\'s "thread handle".\n   Each application can obtain it\'s own thread handle from the internal field\n   [9]@THREAD_HANDLE. A programmer should make no assumptions about the\n   numeric value of a thread handle other than that it is unique among the\n   active threads.\n\n   Communication\n\n   Communication between threads can be programmed using the [10]send-message\n   and [11]read-message functions. It is also possible to trigger [12]on\n   events in other threads using the [13]send-event function.\n\n   Synchronization\n\n   Running concurrent applications introduces problems when accessing common\n   resources (e.g. files). To make sure that concurrent accesses to such\n   resources don\'t conflict, the synchronization functions\n   [14]enter-critical-section and [15]leave-critical-section may be used.\n   Operations on 4GL level are automatically synchronized. This is especially\n   important for database operations.\n\n   Database operations are carried out by each application thread, but the\n   operations are synchronized so that only one operation is carried out at\n   the time. The granularity of the operations synchronized is on the level\n   of the corresponding 4GL function (e.g. first and next). This means that\n   when two applications i.e. concurrently scroll a table, the first and next\n   operations from the two applications are randomly intermixed but\n   sequentially executed.\n\n   Database resources like connections and cursors are shared between\n   application threads whenever possible. This means that database\n   transactions need special synchronization: When one thread initiates a\n   transaction - either automatically or explicitly through the\n   begin-transaction function - all other threads attempting to do any\n   database operations will be suspended until the transaction is completed.\n\n   Scope\n\n   The fact that older versions of Concept didn\'t support concurrent\n   applications raises some problems in connection with existing systems.\n   This section explains how various functions work when utilizing concurrent\n   threads. In general it can be said that most of the data that previously\n   was known to be "global" (data that was available to all applications in a\n   Concept session) now is "thread local", that means it is available to all\n   applications in one thread, but not in other threads. Data that is\n   available to all application threads is called "session global".\n\n   Temporary Tables\n\n   For [16]temporary tables the old term of "persistency" has been replaced\n   with two "persistence levels". Persistence level 1 (thread persistence)\n   means that the table data is available until the thread initializing the\n   table is terminated. Previously persistent tables will now used\n   persistence level 1. In addition to that it is possible to use persistence\n   level 2 (session persistence). Session persistent data will "live" until\n   the Concept session is terminated.\n\n   Temporary Files\n\n   Temporary files created by using the logical file names \'@TEMP-0\' to\n   \'@TEMP-9\' (e.g. in the stream declaration [17]file-name) are thread local\n   and are deleted when the thread terminates. That means that two concurrent\n   applications can safely use the same temporary file name.\n\n   Temporary files created with the [18]file-open function using the file\n   name \'@TEMP\' however are session global and are deleted when the Concept\n   session terminates.\n\n   Global Fields\n\n   Global field values are stored in a thread local data buffer. That means\n   that [19]global fields cannot be used to share field values among\n   application threads. The current global field values are however copied to\n   new application threads started. We strongly recommend to review your\n   program logic and replace the usage of global fields with [20]system\n   fields where possible.\n\n   Menus\n\n   Menu definitions (menus created with [21]create-menu) are still session\n   global, but each thread has an associated menu (activated via\n   [22]use-menu). That has the implication that the main menu (and/or\n   toolbar) may change when another application thread is activated. It may\n   be necessary to update the state of menu items depending on the current\n   application. Focus changes can therefore be trapped by defining an event\n   handler for the [23]@FOCUS-GAINED event.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_tempdb.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_treeview.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_threads.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_start__.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onstartappl\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_call.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_intthreadhandle\n  10. file:///dev/html_send_message__.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_read_message__.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_send_event__.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_enter_critical_section__.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_leave_critical_section__.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_tempdb.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_filename\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileopen.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm#idh_ma_field_global\n  20. file:///dev/html_system_fields.htm\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_createmenu.htm\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onfocusgained\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Definitions\xc2\xa0>                               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Treeview Element                                  side\n\n   A treeview element displays a hierarchical list of items, each of which\n   consists of a label and an optional bitmap. A treeview is typically used\n   to display the headings in a document, the entries in an index, the files\n   and directories on a disk, or any other kind of information that might\n   usefully be displayed as a hierarchy.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Some definitions in relation to the treeview element are important to be\n   aware of:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Each item in a treeview has a label and can optionally have\n   program-defined bitmaps associated with it.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The top item(s) is called root item(s).\n\n   \xc2\xb7All items below the root are called child items.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Items that have children are called parent items.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Child items are displayed indented below their parent item.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Parent items can have a small "expand/collapse" button to the left of its\n   label.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The items might be connected by lines.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The label of the selected item may be editable.\n\n   Programming treeview elements\n\n   The treeview element component is described by the following syntax (see\n   also [4]Element Component):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Element=MyTreeview\n\n   \xc2\xa0type(TREEVIEW)\n\n   \xc2\xa0size(lines,\xc2\xa0cols)\n\n   \xc2\xa0position(x,\xc2\xa0y)\n\n   \xc2\xa0connect(MyTree)\n\n   \xc2\xa0branch-lines(ALL|CHILDREN|NONE)\n\n   \xc2\xa0buttons(ON|OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0edit-labels(ON|OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0check(ON|OFF)\n\n   \xc2\xa0image(<default\xc2\xa0treeview\xc2\xa0images>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The image property specifies the default images for non-focused and\n   focused items in the treeview, and must be specified if the treeview\n   should have images. (The image is specified for each item in the treeview\n   is only used to overrule the defaults, and has no meaning to the treeview\n   unless the treeview itself specifies the image declaration). The size of\n   the first image specified is used to calculate the image size for the\n   whole treeview, meaning any image specified later in the sequence will be\n   scaled to this size.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Specifying multiple images can be done in the following ways.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the image specification contains an X or Y [5]dimension larger than 1\n   (and has no [6]index specification), index 1 is used for the non-focused\n   bitmap and index 2 is used for the focused bitmap (X direction is\n   preferred to Y direction).\n\n   \xc2\xb7Separate the two bitmap file names with a semicolon.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If only one image is specified it is used both for the non-focused and\n   focused state. To scale the bitmap to a predefined pixel size, use the\n   [7]size attribute for the image specification.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The field connected to the treeview element will receive all the events\n   for the treeview. When the current (focused) item in the treeview changes,\n   the field value is changed and the field functions are executed. When any\n   of the events listed below are triggered, the value of the field will\n   reflect the identification number (ID) of the item to which the event\n   applied (e.g. the @OPEN event might happen on an item not having the\n   focus).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Event       Description\n               The item\'s list of child items is now being expanded; that is,\n   [8]@OPEN    the child items are to be visible. The [9]@EVENT_PARAM field\n               contains a 1 if the item has been expanded before and a 0 if\n               not. This event applies only to parent items.\n               The item\'s list of child items is now being collapsed; that\n   [10]@CLOSE  is, the child items are to be hidden. This event applies only\n               to parent items\n               The label of the current item has been edited or check state\n   [11]@CHANGE has been changed. This event applies only to treeview elements\n               with the [12]edit-labels or the [13]check property set to ON.\n               The [14]error function can be used to stop the action.\n               The user has pressed the DELETE key and the current item is to\n   [15]@DELETE be deleted. The [16]error function can be used to stop the\n               deletion.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Double clicking a treeview item can be trapped on the field connected to\n   the treeview in the following ways (prioritized sequence):\n\n   \xc2\xb7Event ACTIVATE. If programmed, the ACTIVATE event is triggered for all\n   elements in the treeview.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Event ENTER. If programmed, the ENTER event is triggered for treeview\n   elements without child items. For items with children the default\n   functionality of the treeviews are executed (expand/collapse child level).\n\n   \xc2\xb7Activates the default-button, if present in the application.\n\n   How to populate/modify data in a treeview element\n\n   The [17]treeview function is used to populate data in a treeview. Within\n   this function the programmer can specify a table and the command\n   [18]synchronize together with the name of the treeview element that should\n   be populated (or modified). The table specified must have a few predefined\n   columns that are used specifically for the treeview. These columns are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Column   Storage  Required Description\n   ID       Integer4 Yes      A unique identifier that identifies one item in\n                              the treeview\n   PARENTID Integer4 Yes      ID of the parent item (use 0 to indicate root\n                              items)\n   LABEL    A(X)     Yes      Item label\n                              If <> 0, then the item has/or might have child\n   HASCHILD BIT      \xc2\xa0        items (shows the node as a parent item in the\n                              treeview)\n   OPEN     BIT      \xc2\xa0        If <> 0, then do expand the item.\n   ISBOLD   BIT      \xc2\xa0        If <> 0, then the item label is bold-faced.\n                              If = 0, then do sort the item.\n\n   SORT     Integer  \xc2\xa0        If < 0, then insert the new item at the end\n\n                              If > 0, then insert the new item at the\n                              beginning\n                              Used when synchronizing the table with the\n                              treeview. The following values are handled :\n\n                              I Insert a new item\n\n                              D Delete the item identified by ID\n   STATE    A(1)     \xc2\xa0\n                              M Modify the item identified by ID\n\n                              Records with values other than these are\n                              skipped by the [19]treeview function. If the\n                              STATE column is not present, value I is always\n                              assumed.\n                              Non-focused and focused image for the item. The\n   IMAGES   A(X)     \xc2\xa0        image is shown to the left of the item\xef\xbf\xbds label\n                              (see the [20]image paragraph).\n   CHECKED  BIT      \xc2\xa0        If <> 0, then the item check-box will be\n                              checked\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   To avoid conflicts with reserved SQL words, the column names may be\n   prefixed with the letters \'TV\' (e.g. "TVSORT").\n\n   Please note that the IMAGES column is only used if the treeview was\n   initially created with the image declaration!\n\n   Special notes on treeviews\n\n   The treeview element is implemented on top of Microsoft\xef\xbf\xbds class libraries,\n   and the following limitations are thereby imposed:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Version 4.70 and earlier of comctl32.dll has poor support for different\n   background colours, and the standard @WINDOW colour is the only usable\n   background. Version 4.71 and later of comctl32.dll has full support for\n   background colours, image and gradient colours are still not supported.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Version 4.70 and earlier of comctl32.dll lack support for foreground\n   colours, use @WINDOWTEXT. Version 4.71 and later of comctl32.dll has full\n   support for foreground (text) colours.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The F2 key is used for label editing and can not be programmed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The parent of a treeview item can not be changed using the \'M\' STATE and\n   changing the PARENTID. To change the parent of a treeview item it has to\n   be removed from the treeview and then reinserted at the right position.\n   Please remember to reinsert any child items as well.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_threads.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm#idh_ma_images_definition_dimension\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm#idh_ma_images_definition_index\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_images.htm#idh_ma_images_definition_size\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onopen\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_inteventparam\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onclose\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onchange\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_editlabels\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_check\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_error.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_ondelete\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_error.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_treeview.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_treeview.htm#idh_ma_treeview_command\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_treeview.htm\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_treeview.htm#idh_ma_element_treeview_image\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                Application file declarations                            side\n\n   The following declarations may only appear at the top of an application\n   source file, before any application component.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   [4]application-stack-extended-allocation(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   [7]application-stack-size(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   [10]description(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textConstant\xc2\xa0)\n\n   [13]security-system-name(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textConstant\xc2\xa0)\n\n   [16]version-number(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Properties\n\n   Application-Stack-Extended-Allocation\n\n   When the application stack is active and this parameter is set to ON, the\n   DATA and FIELD part of an application is allocated on the regular heap and\n   not on the application stack, causing the application to use less space on\n   the application stack. This might be a good thing for large applications\n   that are not called often (like a main menu that is always present), but\n   avoid this setting for applications that are frequently called.\n\n   Note! Applications that are initially larger than the\n   application-stack-size given on the system, will use extended allocation\n   independent of this parameter setting\n\n   Application-Stack-Size\n\n   When the application stack is active and this parameter is set to a number\n   larger than zero, it denotes a requested size of the application stack (in\n   KB) when this application is loaded. If the current available (free) size\n   of the application stack is less than the size requested, the current\n   application stack is swapped to file and the application is loaded at the\n   bottom of the application stack.\n\n   This is a valuable setting for large applications that call a lot of sub\n   applications (like large reports or large advanced online applications\n   that are used over a period of time).\n\n   Note! If the requested size is larger than the application-stack-size\n   given on the system, it is reduced to the value given by the system.\n\n   Description\n\n   The description can be used to define a general comment for the\n   applications in the source file.\n\n   Security-System-Name\n\n   This declaration can be used to connect applications to SECURITY systems\n   in order to simplify the SECURITY setup when running applications used in\n   several systems.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the application is not defined in the currently running system, the\n   application access will be fetched from the system specified by this\n   parameter. The system name might be mapped to an actual SECURITY system\n   name by the SECURITY system (see uqconfig system parameter\n   security-system-name in the Visma Enterprise Concept Operations Guide).\n\n   Version-Number\n\n   An integer value that can be used as a version number for the source file.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element_treeview.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_online.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_appl_ext_alloc\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_onoff.htm#idh_la_pop_onoff\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_appl_ext_alloc\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_appl-stack-size\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_unsignedinteger.htm#idh_la_pop_unsignedinteger\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_appl-stack-size\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_description\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textconstant.htm#idh_la_pop_textconstant\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_description\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_secsysname\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textconstant.htm#idh_la_pop_textconstant\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_secsysname\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_version\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_la_unsignedinteger.htm#idh_la_pop_unsignedinteger\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm#idh_ma_applfile_decl_version\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                 Online Application Component                            side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The ONLINE component is an [5]application component indicating that the\n   current application is a screen-based application. The component consists\n   of a name identifier and a set of declarations that define general\n   properties of the application.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   online=[6]?[7]Application\n\n   \xc2\xa0[8]default-style-prefix(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textConstant\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[11]export(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[16]illegal-commands(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]functionKey\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]functionKey}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[21]import(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[26]lead-in-character(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]leadInChar,\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]includedOrExcluded\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[31]legal-commands(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]functionKey\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]functionKey\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[36]modal(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]modality\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[39]mouse-scope(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]mouseScope\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[42]popup(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[45]port(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[50]processing-info(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]onOff\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[53]NONE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[54]program-type(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]queryOrUpdate\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[57]purpose(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[60]security-access-control(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[63]on(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]functionKeyOrEvent\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0{[66]?[67]anyFunction}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[68]endon\n\n   Properties\n\n   Application\n\n   The name of the ONLINE application. Concept does not assign a special\n   meaning to the name of the application. The only requirement is that if\n   you have several applications in one file, each application has to have a\n   unique name.\n\n   Default-style-prefix\n\n   A style is a set of attributes that relate to the visibility of an item\n   (text, form, push-button) on the screen. A style name is an alias to a\n   definition that is found in the System Database. This definition may\n   contain information on what colour is to use, what background colour and\n   what font is to use. There is no special format required for style names,\n   but it may be handy to use a prefix for style names. Then, simply by\n   changing the default-style-prefix, another set of styles can be applied in\n   an application.\n\n   The default style prefix for ONLINE applications is OL-, so that for e.g.\n   an INPUT element, the style OL-INPUT is fetched from the System Database.\n   If the style PS-INPUT had been defined in the System Database, then by\n   setting the default-style-prefix to PS- in the application would cause\n   Concept to read the PS- styles instead.\n\n   Explicit style names in the style property of an element component are not\n   touched by the settings of default-style-prefix.\n\n   Export\n\n   A list of expressions (fields, constant values or combinations) which are\n   to be exported. A calling application must use a corresponding\n   [69]import() parameter of the 4GL [70]call(), [71]zoom() or [72]run()\n   functions to receive the values. if the storage type differs between the\n   exported value and the import field the data is converted according to the\n   import field (this does not apply when exporting groups or arrays).\n\n   If the expression denotes a non-database field and there is no\n   corresponding import field in the calling application, the field is\n   initially at application startup set to NULL. This fact can be used to\n   avoid complicated result calculations if the calling application makes no\n   use of the result (does not import the result).\n\n   Illegal-commands\n\n   This property is used to restrict commands available to the end-user when\n   running an application. By default, all commands are available. The\n   possible command values are defined in the [73]on section.\n\n   Import\n\n   The fields listed in the import property are the \'value parameters\' of an\n   ONLINE application. A calling application specifies the same list of\n   fields in the [74]export() parameter of the 4GL [75]call(), [76]zoom() or\n   [77]run() function: it will export values to the application called.\n\n   If any of the fields listed are non-database fields and there is no\n   corresponding export in the calling application, the fields are initially\n   at application startup set to NULL.\n\n   Lead-in-character\n\n   The first parameter here defines the lead-in character. The lead-in\n   character is used in form layout declarations to declare field positions\n   and macros (see [78]form). The default value is ^ (circumflex). The\n   lead-in-character can be changed later by using the ^LI macro (see [79]DIO\n   macros).\n\n   The second parameter defines whether the lead-in-character is part of the\n   field or not. It has no influence on macros.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value    Description\n            The field position starts at the lead-in-character (e.g. ^ ). If\n            the display code is specified in the form description, it is\n   INCLUDED expanded with the first character of the display code. Using this\n            mode, it is possible to position two fields next to each other\n            without spacing.\n   EXCLUDED The field position starts to the right of the lead-in-character.\n            The lead-in-character is replaced by a space. This is default.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The lead-in-character property is only used when the form layout is\n   described using the [80]start-form..end-form syntax. As nowadays form\n   layouts in 4GL applications are described using the [81]element syntax,\n   this property is hardly ever used.\n\n   Legal-commands\n\n   This property is used to specify which commands are available to the\n   end-user when running an application. By default, all commands are\n   available, but if legal-commands are specified in this property, only\n   those listed here will be available. The possible command values are\n   defined in the [82]on section.\n\n   Modal\n\n   When the modal property is set to ON or SYSTEM, menu items in the Concept\n   main window cannot be activated anymore.- all menus except the Windows\n   menu will be locked. When the property is set to SYSTEM it will also not\n   be possible to activate other application [83]threads than the current\n   one.\n\n   The modality of an application is inherited by all applications that are\n   called from this application unless the modal property is set in the\n   called application.\n\n   When set to OFF it will not be possible for calling applications to force\n   a modality to the application.\n\n   Mouse-Scope\n\n   Defines which mouse clicks are handled by the application. When set to\n   APPLICATION (the default), only clicks inside the topmost application\n   window of a [84]thread will be handled by the application. Attempts to\n   click inside inactive application windows of the same thread will result\n   in an error [85]bell. It will still be possible to click in any topmost\n   window of another thread.\n\n   When the parameter is set to THREAD, also clicks inside inactive\n   applications of the current thread will be trapped.\n\n   Activating another thread or clicking "outside" the current window (but\n   inside an inactive window of the current thread) when the mouse scope is\n   THREAD will trigger the [86]@FOCUS-LOST event in the current application.\n\n   Popup\n\n   Defines a popup menu for fields in the application. Popup menus defined on\n   [87]table or [88]field level take precedence over menus defined on\n   application level. When the right mouse button is pressed in a field with\n   a popup menu, the following happens:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field pointed to is not the current field, it is made current,\n   i.e. the cursor is moved to the field and the appropriate cursor movement\n   events are fired.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The <alpha expression> parameter of the popup declaration is evaluated,\n   and if it identifies a valid menu, the menu is shown and the user is\n   allowed to make a selection.\n\n   Port\n\n   The port-property combines the functionality of the export- and\n   import-property. A calling application may send values to a called\n   application and may receive changed values in the same fields. It is like\n   declaring import() and export() with identical parameter lists.\n\n   Note that port() may not be combined with the export() and import().\n\n   Processing-info\n\n   When this parameter is set to ON (the default),.the application is shown\n   in the "Windows" menu (see [89]Threads) and it will be a part of the list\n   of applications that can be accessed using the [90]NEXTAPP/[91]PREVAPP\n   keys. If the parameter value is OFF, system messages that normally are\n   shown in the message line will not be displayed. If it set to NONE, no\n   processing info is shown, the application will not be shown in the\n   "Windows" menu and it will not be in the list of applications accessible\n   using the NEXTAPP/PREVAPP keys.\n\n   Program-type\n\n   The program-type property overrides the [92]access property of a [93]table\n   component. Setting this property to QUERY will restrict access to database\n   tables to query-only. This is a safe way to make sure that the whole\n   application (that maybe consists of many include files) is query-only. If\n   the value of this property is set to DELETE (this is the default), then\n   the access property of the table component defines the table access.\n\n   Purpose\n\n   This property defines a text that is displayed in a dialogue box whenever\n   the user pressed the application help key (event HELPAPPL). The title bar\n   of the dialogue box contains the name of the application. The purpose text\n   may contain formatting options controlling the layout of the text.\n   Available formatting options are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Option Description\n   /,     Indicates that a new line is to be started\n   /n     No justification\n   /l     Left justification\n   /r     Right justification\n   /c     Center justification\n   /x     Disable option processing\n          Change the first character of the formatting option to the\n   /=X    character following the \'=\'. In this case the X is used, so that\n          the formatting option for left justification will be Xl.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the text is to contain the current option leadin character (and option\n   processing is not disabled with the x option), the option leadin character\n   must be written twice. Thus, if the text to be written is runtime\n   dependent and may contain the current leadin character, either disable\n   option processing using the x option, or change the leadin character using\n   the /= option to a character known not to be present in the text.\n\n   Security-access-control\n\n   This property is used to disable the default functionality that the\n   application access is controlled by Security. Due to performance\n   considerations and to reduce the need for registering applications in\n   Security, security-access-control(OFF) should be used whenever possible.\n\n   On\n\n   Declares a set of functions to be executed in response to a given command\n   or event. If the same command/event is defined on table or field level,\n   these levels will take priority. See section on [94]on.\n\n   Notes\n\n   \xc2\xb7Applications can be started from the standard system menu or by use of\n   the [95]call(), [96]zoom() or [97]run() functions.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to define as many [98]applications as wanted in one module\n   (file). Different application types (ONLINE, XTRA) can be mixed within the\n   same module. Calling applications in the same file is faster than calling\n   external applications. However, putting to many applications in the same\n   file will allocate memory for all applications when loaded, even if only\n   one of the applications is required.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not possible to combine the port property with import and export.\n\n   [99][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_applfile_declarations.htm\n   2. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                  Xtra Application Component                             side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The XTRA component is an [5]application component indicating that the\n   current application is a report-based application. The component consists\n   of a name identifier and a set of declarations that define general\n   properties of the application.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   xtra=[6]?[7]Application\n\n   \xc2\xa0[8]allow-abort(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[11]default-style-prefix(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textConstant\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[14]export(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]textExpression}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[19]import(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[24]lead-in-character(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]leadInChar,\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]includedOrExcluded\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[29]port(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[34]processing-info(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]onOff\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[37]NONE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[38]program-type(\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]queryOrUpdate\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[41]security-access-control(\xc2\xa0[42]?[43]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[44]on(\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]functionKeyOrEvent\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0{[47]?[48]anyFunction}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[49]endon\n\n   Properties\n\n   Application\n\n   The name of the XTRA application. Concept does not assign a special\n   meaning to the name of the application. The only requirement is that if\n   you have several applications in one file, each application has to have a\n   unique name.\n\n   Allow-abort\n\n   When the value of this property is set to ON, then the XTRA application\n   may be aborted by the user while it is running. The default value for\n   allow-abort is OFF.\n\n   It is possible to allow aborting the report during a [50]scroll loop by\n   setting the allow-interrupt parameter to ON.\n\n   The output to individual streams can be stopped (without terminating the\n   application) when using the allow-abort declaration on a [51]stream.\n\n   Default-style-prefix\n\n   A style is a set of attributes that relate to the visibility of an item\n   (text, form, push-button) on the screen. A style name is an alias to a\n   definition that is found in the System Database. This definition may\n   contain information on what colour is to use, what background colour and\n   what font is to use. There is no special format required for style names,\n   but it may be handy to use a prefix for style names. Then, simply by\n   changing the default-style-prefix, another set of styles can be applied in\n   an application.\n\n   The default style prefix for XTRA applications is XT-, so that for e.g. an\n   OUTPUT element, the style XT-OUTPUT is fetched from the System Database.\n   If the style PS-OUTPUT had been defined in the System Database, then by\n   setting the default-style-prefix to PS- in the application would cause\n   Concept to read the PS- styles instead.\n\n   Explicit style names in the style property of an element component are not\n   touched by the settings of the default-style-prefix.\n\n   Export\n\n   A list of expressions (fields, constant values or combinations) which are\n   to be exported. A calling application must use a corresponding\n   [52]import() parameter of the 4GL [53]call(), [54]zoom() or [55]run()\n   functions to receive the values. if the storage type differs between the\n   exported value and the import field the data is converted according to the\n   import field (this does not apply when exporting groups or arrays).\n\n   If the expression denotes a non-database field and there is no\n   corresponding import field in the calling application, the field is\n   initially (at application startup) set to NULL. This fact can be used to\n   avoid complicated result calculations if the calling application makes no\n   use of the result (does not import the result).\n\n   Import\n\n   The fields listed in the import property are the \'value parameters\' of an\n   XTRA application. A calling application specifies the same list of fields\n   in the [56]export() parameter of the 4GL [57]call() function: it will\n   export values to the application called.\n\n   If any of the fields listed are non-database fields and there is no\n   corresponding export in the calling application, the fields are initially\n   (at application startup) set to NULL.\n\n   Lead-in-character\n\n   The first parameter here defines the lead-in character. The lead-in\n   character is used in form layout declarations to declare field positions\n   and macros (see [58]form). The default value is ^ (circumflex). The\n   lead-in-character can be changed later by using the ^LI macro (see [59]DIO\n   macros).\n\n   The second parameter defines whether the lead-in-character is part of the\n   field or not. It has no influence on macros.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value    Description\n            The field position starts at the lead-in-character (e.g. ^ ). If\n            the display code is specified in the form description, it is\n   INCLUDED expanded with the first character of the display code. Using this\n            mode, it is possible to position two fields next to each other\n            without spacing.\n   EXCLUDED The field position starts to the right of the lead-in-character.\n            The lead-in-character is replaced by a space. This is default.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The lead-in-character property is only used when the form layout is\n   described using the [60]start-form..end-form syntax. As nowadays form\n   layouts in 4GL applications are described using the [61]element syntax,\n   this property is hardly ever used.\n\n   Port\n\n   The port-property combines the functionality of the export- and\n   import-property. A calling application may send values to a called\n   application and may receive changed values in the same fields. It is like\n   declaring import() and export() with identical parameter lists.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note that port() may not be combined with the export() and import().\n\n   Processing-info\n\n   By default, the property value for processing-info is set to ON. That\n   means that, when the application scrolls a database table, the message\n   line in the Concept environment will show progress information on the\n   number of records read from the database. If the report contains streams\n   with included forms, a progress bar will also show on the system\n   information line. If the property value is OFF, the record count is turned\n   off. If it set to NONE all processing info is removed and the report name\n   will not be shown in the "Windows" menu (see [62]Threads).\n\n   Program-type\n\n   The program-type property overrides the [63]access property of a [64]table\n   component. Setting this property to QUERY will restrict access to database\n   tables to query-only. This is a safe way to make sure that the whole\n   application (that maybe consists of many include files) is query-only. If\n   the value of this property is set to DELETE (this is the default), then\n   the access property of the table component defines the table access.\n\n   Security-access-control\n\n   This property is used to disable the default functionality that the\n   application access is controlled by Security. Due to performance\n   considerations and to reduce the need for registering applications in\n   Security, security-access-control(OFF) should be used whenever possible.\n\n   On\n\n   Declares a set of functions to be executed in response to a given command\n   or event. If the same command/event is defined on table or field level,\n   these levels will take priority. See section on [65]on.\n\n   The event [66]@XTRA can only be defined on this level and for XTRA\n   applications only. This event is used for the main procedure of the\n   application.\n\n   Notes\n\n   \xc2\xb7Applications can be started from the standard system menu or by use of\n   the [67]call, [68]zoom() or [69]run functions.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to define as many [70]applications as wanted in one module\n   (file). Different application types (ONLINE, XTRA) can be mixed within the\n   same module. Calling applications in the same file is faster than calling\n   external applications. However, putting to many applications in the same\n   file will allocate memory for all applications when loaded, even if only\n   one of the applications is required.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not possible to combine the port property with import and export.\n\n   [71][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_online.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. Concept does not assign a special\n   meaning to the name of the application.\n\n   Default-style-prefix\n\n   A style is a set of attributes that relate to the visibility of an item\n   (text, form, push-button) on the screen. A style name is an alias to a\n   definition that is found in the System Database. This definition may\n   contain information on what colour is to use, what background colour and\n   what font is to use. There is no special format required for style names,\n   but it may be handy to use a prefix for style names. Then, simply by\n   changing the default-style-prefix, another set of styles can be applied in\n   an application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The default style prefix for ONLINE applications is OL- and XT- for XTRA\n   applications.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Explicit style names in the style property of an element component are not\n   touched by the settings of default-style-prefix.\n\n   Usage\n\n   Defines in which kind of applications the LAYOUT component is used. The\n   value can either be XTRA or ONLINE.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_layout.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_application.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationname.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationname\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout.htm#idh_ma_layout_application\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout.htm#idh_ma_layout_defaultstyleprefix\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textconstant.htm#idh_la_pop_textconstant\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout.htm#idh_ma_layout_defaultstyleprefix\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout.htm#idh_ma_layout_usage\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_layout.htm#idh_ma_layout_usage\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       On Declarations                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This declaration is used to trap a command or an event. The declaration\n   contains a procedure (sequence of functions) that will be executed when\n   the command is requested or the event occurs.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   on\xc2\xa0(\xc2\xa0<[5]Command>\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0<[6]Event>\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0<[7]Command>\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0<[8]Event>}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0<function>\n\n   \xc2\xa0...\n\n   endon\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   Commands are requests of the user issued using the keyboard, the mouse or\n   by selecting an entry from the drop-down-menu or tool-bar. An application\n   can also request a command using the [9]perform-event function to execute\n   the default action of the command, or using the [10]send-event function.\n\n   When on...endon is specified at\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Level             Trigged\n                     on...endon will be triggered when <command> is requested\n   field level       from the field where on...endon is declared. However, if\n                     on...endon is declared on a group, it will be triggered\n                     when <command> is requested from any group member.\n   table level       on...endon will be triggered when <command> is requested\n                     from any field connected to the table.\n   application level on...endon will be triggered when <command> is requested\n                     from any field within the application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If a command is not trapped in the application, some of the commands have\n   a default action that will be executed. If the command is trapped, the\n   default action is replaced by the code in the on..endon event handler. The\n   default action can be triggered using the perform-event() function. The\n   [11]@DEFAULT event can be used to trap all commands that are not\n   explicitly handled in the application.\n\n   The following table shows all commands, their associated key combinations\n   and their default actions if not trapped by the application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\nCommand                 Key Combination         Default action\n                                                This command is triggered when the user presses the\n                                                ALT key and one of the characters defined in the\n                                                [12]accelerators declaration on the stream.\nACCELERATOR             \xc2\xa0\n                                                The [13]@EVENT_PARAM field contains the character\n                                                pressed. In this case the commands can only be used in a menu definition.\n\n   The commands normally available on a standard keyboard are F1 to F12\n   (including SHIFT and CTRL key combinations). However, an event will often occur as a\n   result of a command. Example: The DELREC command will generate a @DELETE\n   event.\n\n   As opposed to commands, an event has no standard action. It is part of an\n   action.\n\n   The application can trap an event to execute an additional procedure. It\n   is not possible to stop or change the action in progress. If this is\n   needed, the command or commands causing the event must be trapped instead.\n\n   The following table shows a complete list of events and when they are\n   triggered. Can only be\n                                located on stream level.\n                                On field level :\n\n                                This event is triggered whenever a\n                                drop-down-list-box or\n                                drop-down-combo-box is about to be\n                                opened. If this event is trapped, the\n                                standard drop-down mechanism is\n                                disabled. The drop-down functionality\n                                must be programmed within this event.\n                                Normally, this is achieved by doing a\n                                call to an application which is\n                                exporting the selected value. This\n   @OPEN                        value is then assigned to the field.   F (O)S\n                                                                          (X)\n                                This event is also triggered when the\n                                item list of a parent item in a\n                                [113]treeview is expanded.\n\n                                On stream level:\n\n                                This event is triggered right after a\n                                XTRA stream is opened. (Right before\n                                the first form is printed to the\n                                stream). If function execution fails\n                                or is aborted, the application is\n                                aborted with return-code $URC_ABORTED.\n                                <n> is an integer constant and can\n                                take the values 1 to 8. It is used by\n   @PASS-<n>                    the XTRA function [114]process-table.      TX\n                                For more information see separate\n                                section on this function. Can only be\n                                located on table level.\n                                This event is triggered before the\n   @POPUP                       popup menu associated with the field        F\n                                is shown and can be used to change the\n                                menu before opening it.\n                                This event is triggered on the normal\n                                point of insertion for tables with\n                                record-state set to\n   @PROGRAM-INSERT              [115]PROGRAM-INSERT. The @EVENT_PARAM       \xc2\xa0\n                                contains 1 if the event is executed\n                                inside an automatic or programmed\n                                transaction.\n                                This event is triggered when a data\n                                error occurs while scrolling a data\n                                stream or extracting data values using\n                                the [116]buffer-read function.\n                                Handling this event enables the\n                                programmer to handle such errors\n                                without stopping the progress of the\n                                application. See the internal fields\n                                [117]@READ_ERROR_FIELD,\n                                [118]@READ_ERROR_STREAM,\n                                [119]@READ_ERROR_VALUE,\n                                [120]@READ_ERROR_STATUS,\n                                [121]@READ_ERROR_BUFFER for more\n                                information.\n\n                                \xc2\xa0\n\n   @READ-ERROR                  Data errors that are handled includes:    ATF\n\n                                - Illegal characters in numeric fields\n\n                                - Invalid number format\n\n                                - Alphanumeric value too long\n\n                                - Data type overflow (E.g inserting 40\n                                000 into an INTEGER2 field)\n\n                                \xc2\xa0\n\n                                If the function chain of the\n                                @READ-ERROR is aborted (e.g by use of\n                                the [122]error function), Concept will\n                                default to its standard functionality\n                                which is to abort the application.\n                                This event is triggered whenever a end\n   @SAX-ELEMENT-END             tag is encountered in an XML file         ATF\n                                processed by the [123]sax-read\n                                function.\n                                This event is triggered whenever a new\n                                start tag is encountered in an XML\n                                file processed by the [124]sax-read\n   @SAX-ELEMENT-START           function. Please note that this is the    ATF\n                                only event for which one can access\n                                the attributes of the node (using the\n                                [125]sax-get function).\n                                This event is triggered when a value\n                                is encountered in an XML file\n                                processed by the [126]sax-read\n                                function. If the read mode is \'RAW\'\n                                the event will be triggered for all\n                                characters found between tags in the\n   @SAX-ELEMENT-VALUE           XML file (including whitespace            ATF\n                                characters like tab and line feed).\n                                The [127]@EVENT-PARAM field will\n                                contain an indication of where the\n                                value is found. It will contain 0 if\n                                the value is found between a start/end\n                                tag pair and 1 otherwise.\n                                Functions specified inside on @START\n   @START                       are executed when the application is        A\n                                started. Can only be located on\n                                application level.\n                                The event is used to replace the\n                                standard procedure automatically\n                                executed to synchronize database\n                                records according to changes done in\n                                the application, with a customized\n                                procedure. The event is triggered when\n                                records of tables with\n                                [128]control(UNIQUE) are changed, and\n                                it is time to do the synchronization.\n                                As normal for these tables, the events\n                                @DELETE, @INSERT and @UPDATE are\n                                triggered first, and then the\n                                @SYNCHRONIZE event is triggered.\n\n                                The synchronization may most easily be\n                                done using the [129]synchronize\n                                function, or by using the database\n                                functions [130]update, [131]insert or\n                                [132]delete. The synchronization, and\n   @SYNCHRONIZE                 thus the changes, may be rejected          AO\n                                using [133]error function or the\n                                [134]clear database function. The\n                                synchronization may also be ignored or\n                                postponed by not doing anything at\n                                all.\n\n                                To do a manual synchronization\n                                properly, the [135]inquire function\n                                may be useful.\n\n                                Note that when database functions are\n                                executed from the @SYNCHRONIZE event,\n                                they will be carried out as if the\n                                table referred to has the declaration\n                                [136]control(PROGRAM).
