In this situation,\n                                functions located at tables are\n                                executed when the table is scrolled,\n                                i.e. when the rows are retrieved from\n   @XTRA                        the database. If on @XTRA is not used,     AX\n                                execution of functions starts with the\n                                functions located at the first main\n                                table (not join table) in the\n                                application. This "event" is only to\n                                be used in XTRA, on the application\n                                level.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the same <Command> or <Event> is declared on more than one level,\n   only on...endon declared on the highest level will be executed. The\n   priorities of the levels are as follows:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Field\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Group\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Table\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Application\n\n   \xc2\xb7When a <Command> is trapped, the standard action is not performed. To\n   execute the standard action, use the [147]perform-event() function with\n   <Command>.\n\n   \xc2\xb7<Command>s and <Event>s used in an on-declaration handling more than 1\n   event or command cannot appear in an on-declaration as a single event or\n   command (example: an on-declaration for (F2) and one for (F2,S+F2) will\n   give a compiler error).\n\n   \xc2\xb7When an event occurs, pending input will be committed and the functions\n   on the field changed will be executed before the event is handled. There\n   are a few exceptions to this rule. The following events do not commit\n   changes because they might happen while the user is entering data,\n   therefore interfering with the user\'s actions: WINMOVE, WINSIZE,\n   WORKWINSIZE,WORKWINMOVE, @TIMER, @MM, @MESSAGE and @FOCUS-GAINED. To make\n   sure that user input is committed when receiving one of these events, a\n   "normal" event handler must be executed (via the [148]send-event function)\n   to commit pending changes. The NOP command is designed to be used in such\n   circumstances.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The following events are executed asynchronously, that means that the\n   corresponding event handler is also executed while Concept is already\n   executing a function chain: @TIMER, @MM, @MESSAGE, @FOCUS-GAINED.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [149][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Stream Component                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A stream is defined as a window, file or printer to which results are\n   written, or a file from which input is taken. An application can write to\n   several different streams by declaring appropriate stream components. All\n   output from an XTRA report is done through streams. In ONLINE\n   applications, only one stream can be defined (the application window).\n\n   A stream component consists of a name identifier and a set of declarations\n   that define the properties of the stream. Most of the stream properties\n   concern XTRA applications (file, printer), but there are a few\n   declarations concerning output to the screen that can be used in ONLINE\n   applications.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   stream=[5]?[6]Stream\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Common\xc2\xa0properties:\n\n   \xc2\xa0[7]background(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]background\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[10]font(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]font\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[13]formular(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[16]frame(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]frame\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[19]docking(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]placement\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[22]line-gap(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[25]maximized(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[28]position(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[33]pixel-position(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[36]?[37]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[38]size(\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[41]?[42]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[43]pixel-size(\xc2\xa0[44]?[45]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[48]style(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]styleName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[51]title(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[54]type(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]streamType\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[63]abort-on-error(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[66]active(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]logicalExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[78]bb(\xc2\xa0[79]?[80]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[81]bin-in(\xc2\xa0[82]?[83]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[84]collate(\xc2\xa0[85]?[86]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[87]column-lines(\xc2\xa0[88]?[89]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[90]column-width(\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[93]condition(\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]logicalExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[96]copies(\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[99]crlf(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[102]csv-separators(\xc2\xa0[103]?[104]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[111]formatting(\xc2\xa0[112]?[113]formatting\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[114]full-file-name(\xc2\xa0[115]?[116]applicationField\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[117]horizontal-columns(\xc2\xa0[118]?[119]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[120]lb(\xc2\xa0[121]?[122]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[123]include-fields(\xc2\xa0[124]?[125]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[126]?[127]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[128]include-forms(\xc2\xa0[129]?[130]formName\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[131]?[132]formName}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[133]ob(\xc2\xa0[134]?[135]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[136]orientation(\xc2\xa0[137]?[138]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[139]pl(\xc2\xa0[140]?[141]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[142]print-mode(\xc2\xa0[143]?[144]printMode\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[145]printer-dialogue(\xc2\xa0[146]?[147]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[148]pw(\xc2\xa0[149]?[150]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[151]row-width(\xc2\xa0[152]?[153]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[154]stop-on-new-page(\xc2\xa0[155]?[156]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[157]tb(\xc2\xa0[158]?[159]integer\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[160]vertical-columns(\xc2\xa0[161]?[162]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[163]wide-column(\xc2\xa0[164]?[165]applicationField\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ONLINE\xc2\xa0properties:\n\n   \xc2\xa0[166]accelerators(\xc2\xa0[167]?[168]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[169]horizontal-scroll-bar(\xc2\xa0[170]?[171]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[172]vertical-scroll-bar(\xc2\xa0[173]?[174]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[175]show(\xc2\xa0[176]?[177]windowMode\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[178]maximum-size(\xc2\xa0[179]?[180]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[181]?[182]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[183]minimum-size(\xc2\xa0[184]?[185]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[186]?[187]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Keywords\n\n   Stream\n\n   The name of the stream. It is used when referring to a stream, for example\n   in the [188]scroll function.\n\n   Abort-on-error\n\n   XTRA only. If the value of this property is ON, the application aborts if\n   an output device specified by the user returns an error status when it is\n   opened. If abort-to-error is set to OFF (the default), the user will be\n   prompted to give a new output device.\n\n   Active\n\n   XTRA only. The stream is written to only if the result of the expression\n   is true. In contradiction to [189]condition, this parameter is evaluated\n   each time a form included on the stream is printed.\n\n   Allow-abort\n\n   XTRA only. If allow-abort is set to ON, output to the stream can be\n   aborted (stopped) during report execution. This is only applicable to\n   streams that include forms. If it is set to OFF, output can not be\n   aborted, unless the [190]application itself is aborted. (stopping the\n   output to a stream does not abort the application).\n\n   Append\n\n   XTRA only. If the value of this property is set to ON, output will be\n   appended to the output file if it already exists. If not, the file will be\n   created.\n\n   Note: When calling an application, the called application cannot use the\n   append declaration on the same file as the calling application. Instead,\n   use the hierarchic structure shown in the figure:\n\n   If application B calls C directly, Concept does not close the file X. This\n   leads to a multi-user conflict when C accesses the file. Instead, B should\n   call C via A, since Concept closes X when B returns to A. The same is\n   achieved if B calls C using the [191]run function.\n\n   When the append property is set to OFF, the contents of the stream is\n   written from the beginning of the output file. Existing contents in the\n   output file are overwritten. This is the default.\n\n   Condition\n\n   XTRA only. The stream is opened and written to only if the result of the\n   expression is true.\n\n   File-name\n\n   XTRA only. A separate topic has been spent on describing the features\n   behind this stream declaration. Read the [192]Stream declarations -\n   file-name topic.\n\n   Font\n\n   Defines the default font for the stream. See style attribute [193]font for\n   a description of the font property.\n\n   Full-file-name\n\n   If file-name refers to an OS file the field referred to by this property\n   will receive the complete file name including drive/path and extension. If\n   it refers to a printer name or an @EXTERNAL macro, the full\n   printer/external specification is copied into the field.\n\n   Include-fields\n\n   XTRA only. Contains a list of fields to be written to or read from a file.\n   This declaration can only be used if the stream has been formatted as\n   BINARY,CSV, ASCII-DATA or ASCII-FIELDS.\n\n   Include-forms\n\n   XTRA only. Contains a list of forms to be printed in this stream. If only\n   one stream is specified, all forms are connected to it by default.\n\n   Wide-column\n\n   XTRA only. The parameter must be the name of a wide column field\n   containing text. Defines the wide column field to be the source to read\n   from. The [194]scroll function will fetch one line at the time and copy it\n   to a field defined with include-fields. See example #3.\n\n   On ... endon\n\n   The following events are available at stream level in XTRA applications:\n   [195]@END-PAGE, [196]@ERROR, [197]@ERROR-BREAK, [198]@FETCH, [199]@INIT,\n   [200]@NEW-PAGE \xc2\xa0and [201]@OPEN.\n\n   The following events are available at stream level in ONLINE applications:\n   [202]@CLOSE, [203]@ERROR and [204]@ERROR-BREAK\n\n   See section [205]on for details.\n\n   Declarations concerning page layout:\n\n   Formular\n\n   Defines the output formular used by the stream. The formular defines the\n   size of a coordinate system cell. Formulars are defined in the system\n   database section [FORMULAR]. By default, streams of Online applications\n   uses the OnlineDefault formular and streams of Xtra applications uses the\n   XtraDefault formular.\n\n   Cell sizes are given in points, where a point is defined as 1/72 inch.\n   Because all sizes sooner or later are converted to a number of pixels, the\n   definition of a formular also contains a precision specification being\n   either high or pixel. High precision should be used in formulars used in\n   Xtra applications: it ensures precise positioning of elements anywhere on\n   a printer page. Pixel precision should be used in formulars used in Online\n   applications: it ensures that element positions are mapped to pixels in a\n   predictable way. This is done by rounding off the cell size definitions to\n   a whole number of pixels.\n\n   Example of system database formular definition:\n\n   [formular]\n\n   ;name=height,width,not\xc2\xa0used,precision\n\n   MyFormular=9,6,0,high\n\n   MyFormular defines a coordinate system that will give 8 (72/9) cells per\n   inch vertically and 12 (72/6) cells per inch horizontally.\n\n   By combining formular and font definitions it is possible to get the\n   exactly wanted line spacing. To be able to relate a font size definition\n   to a coordinate system cell definition, the following rules applies:\n\n   \xc2\xb7Font sizes are normally specified in number of points of the character\n   height.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The character height plus the internal-leading height is known as the\n   character cell height.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In the [FONTS] section of the system database font sizes are specified in\n   terms of character height using a negative value and in terms of character\n   cell height using a positive value.\n\n   \xc2\xb7For a coordinate system cell to be high enough to hold a given font, the\n   coordinate system cell height must be greater or equal to the fonts\n   character cell height (and not the fonts character height).\n\n   Column-lines\n\n   XTRA only. Indicates the number of lines in the area specified by\n   vertical-columns and/or horizontal-columns.\n\n   Column-width\n\n   XTRA only. Indicates the width of the area specified by vertical-columns\n   and/or horizontal-columns.\n\n   Horizontal-columns\n\n   XTRA only. Indicates how many horizontal columns one report page is to\n   consist of. Default value is 1.\n\n   Vertical-columns\n\n   XTRA only. Indicates how many vertical columns one report page is to\n   consist of. Default value is 1.\n\n   bb\n\n   XTRA only. Sets bottom border, where 0 means "no border" and -1 means\n   "using default value when outputting to printer or fixed default value\n   (see below) when outputting to screen or file".\n\n   lb\n\n   XTRA only. Sets left border, where 0 means "no border" and -1 means "using\n   default value when outputting to printer or fixed default value (see\n   below) when outputting to screen or file".\n\n   ob\n\n   XTRA only. Sets right border, where 0 means "no border" and -1 means\n   "using default value when outputting to printer or fixed default value\n   (see below) when outputting to screen or file".\n\n   pl\n\n   XTRA only. Sets page length. Default value is device dependent. Value -1\n   means \xef\xbf\xbdusing default value when outputting to printer\xef\xbf\xbd\n\n   pw\n\n   XTRA only. Indicates the page width. Default value is device dependent.\n   Value -1 means \xef\xbf\xbdusing default value when outputting to printer\xef\xbf\xbd\n\n   tb\n\n   XTRA only. Sets top border, where 0 means \xef\xbf\xbdno border\xef\xbf\xbd and -1 means \xef\xbf\xbdusing\n   default value when outputting to printer or fixed default value (see\n   below) when outputting to screen or file\xef\xbf\xbd.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Default values :\n\n   \xc2\xa0  Values\n   tb 2\n   bb 2\n   lb 12\n   ob 8\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Declarations concerning formatting\n\n   These declarations are available to XTRA applications only.\n\n   Crlf\n\n   This parameter is used to control the use of the end-of-line marker when\n   scrolling records to or from a stream. The end-of-line marker on some\n   platforms is line-feed (lf) while on others it is carriage-return (cr) and\n   line-feed. This is particularly useful when using formatting ASCII-DATA,\n   ASCII-FIELDS or BINARY in which no form definitions are present. When\n   formatting techniques which use form definitions are used, then the form\n   attribute no-line-feed may be used instead.\n\n   For BINARY formatted streams the default is OFF, else the default is ON.\n\n   File-format\n\n   If the report is written to a file, you may specify a file format.\n   File-format can not be used together with the formatting mode BINARY.\n   Default value is defined in uqconfig using the default-file-format\n   setting.\n\n   If the stream is opened for reading, the file-format is overruled if\n   Concept is able to detect the file-format from the file header. This is\n   the case for all formats but PLAIN.\n\n   The parameter must evaluate to one of the following values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value        Description\n                Uses the value defined in uqconfig parameter\n   DEFAULT      default-file-format.. It must be one of the other legal\n                values.\n   MS-WORD      The file is a Microsoft Word for Windows version 2.0 or 6.0\n                document.\n   ND-SFORMAT   The file is a NOTIS S-format file.\n                The file is a standard text file with one byte per character\n                and a line terminator. This file format requires a second\n                parameter <CS>: the character set. Any character set\n   PLAIN[/<CS>] available to Concept can be specified. See Unique Character\n                Set section. If /<CS> is omitted, the file extension will\n                decide the character set. This mapping is defined in\n                uqdio.ini (see Visma Enterprise Concept Operations Guide).\n   RTF          The file is a Microsoft Rich Text Format file.\n   UNIPLEX      The file is a UNIPLEX version 7 document.\n   UNIQUE       The file is a Concept document. This is a Concept specific\n                file format not readable to other programs.\n   UTF-8        The file is a UTF-8 encoded file with Byte Order Mark (BOM)\n   WP           The file is a Word Perfect file of version between 5.0 and\n                6.1.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Formatting\n\n   Value        Description\n   ASCII-DATA   A textual file with a fixed record length and layout defined\n                by the display codes of the fields included on the stream.\n   ASCII-FIELDS A textual file with a comma separated list of the fields\n                included on the stream.\n   BINARY       A binary file with a fixed record length and layout defined\n                by the storage codes of the fields included on the stream.\n                A textual file with a list of the fields included on the\n   CSV          stream, where each field is separated or enclosed according\n                to a set of CSV separators. See the csv-separator parameter.\n   NONE         No page formatting is done.\n   DIRECT       XTRA makes the output directly, i.e. the page layout will be\n                as defined by the parameters specified on the stream.\n                The page formatting depends on whether the output is to be\n                written to a file or a printer. When printing to files, no\n   AUTO         page formatting is done, but - different from using NONE -\n                the page header and tail are written. When printing to\n                printers, the output is written directly (see DIRECT).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The formatting ASCII-DATA, ASCII-FIELDS, BINARY and CSV is only meaningful\n   on streams used as destination or source in the [206]scroll function.\n   NONE, DIRECT and AUTO can only be used on streams that contain forms, i.e.\n   written using the [207]print-form function.\n\n   Csv-separators\n\n   This parameter applies to formatting=csv only, and is used to override the\n   default CSV separators defined by the corresponding uqconfig system\n   command. The parameter expression is evaluated when the stream is opened,\n   and\n\n   must be a comma separated list of separator characters in the following\n   sequence:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <main>,<alpha>,<numeric>,<escape>,<decimal>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A separator is defined using any of the following syntax\'s:\n\n   \xc2\xb7A single non-numeric character except the characters comma, single quote\n   and double quote.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A single character enclosed in single or double quotes.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A sequence of numeric characters giving the UCS value of the separator.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The text TAB indicating the tab character (UCS value 9).\n\n   \xc2\xb7The text NONE indicating that no separator should be used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7An empty definition indicating the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The meaning and default values of the separators are defined as follows.\n\n   <main> is the character separating fields within a record. The <main>\n   character can not be set to none. The default value is language dependent,\n   but usually \',\' (comma).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <alpha> is the character put before and after a character field. This may\n   be NONE. The default value is \'"\' (double quote).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <numeric> is a character put before and after a numeric field. This may be\n   NONE, which is also the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <escape> is a character used to indicate that the next character is part\n   of a field, and should not be treated as a special character, i.e.\n   separator or delimiters. The <escape> character can not be set to the same\n   as any of the other separators. If set to NONE, no characters in the field\n   value may be the same as a separator. NONE is the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <decimal> defines the character used to indicate the decimal point. The\n   default value is language dependent, but usually \'.\' (dot). Note that when\n   the decimal point is set by the decimal-point parameter (in the uqconfig\n   file) to comma, then the default <decimal> CSV separator is automatically\n   changed to semicolon.\n\n   Row-width\n\n   Standard line length (CRLF excluded). Largest legal value is 32768. The\n   default value is 0 (dynamic), that means that the actual row-width will be\n   the total length of all fields defined in the [208]include-fields list. If\n   the string to be written is shorter than the specified line length, the\n   rest of the line is filled with blanks. Row-width should only be used\n   together with the formatting parameters BINARY, ASCII-DATA or\n   ASCII-FIELDS.\n\n   Declarations concerning printing:\n\n   Note: The following printer parameters are ignored if the current printer\n   system does not support that facility.\n\n   These declarations are available to XTRA applications only.\n\n   Adjust-to-printable-area\n\n   XTRA only. Windows platforms only.\n\n   The unprintable area is a small border along the edges of a printer page\n   which is inaccessible for printing. The size of this area depends on the\n   printer type. When ON, all margins are calculated within the printable\n   area (this is default when the application uses "start-form/endform"\n   syntax). When OFF, all margins are calculated from the edges of the paper,\n   thus making the printout more accurately aligned between different printer\n   types.\n\n   Bin-in\n\n   Selects the source tray (bin) for the first page. See the separate section\n   on [209]source trays for a detailed explanation of this attribute.\n\n   To change the source tray during the execution of a report, use the\n   [210]change-stream function or the [211]DIO macro BN.\n\n   Collate\n\n   The collate property box indicates whether to collate the pages if\n   multiple copies are being printed. If the printer driver does not support\n   collation, this property has no effect.\n\n   Copies\n\n   Number of copies to print. Default = 1.\n\n   Orientation\n\n   If the expression evaluates to 1, portrait printing is selected. If the\n   value is 2, landscape printing is selected. Other values are illegal. The\n   default value is defined in the printer configuration.\n\n   Print-mode\n\n   Sets the mode of printing :\n\n   Mode      Description\n   IMMEDIATE Send output directly to the printer (default)\n             All printer output is formatted and stored temporarily in a\n   DELAYED   file. When the report is finished, the contents are send to the\n             printer (and the file is deleted).\n             As for DELAYED, but when the output file is sent to the printer,\n   CONFIRMED the user must confirm that the printout is ok. If not he/she can\n             resend the output.\n   PREVIEW   As for DELAYED, but the result can be previewed and any\n             page/page range can be selected for printing.\n\n   Printer-dialogue\n\n   If the expression evaluates to 1, a printer set-up dialogue is called\n   before printing. In this dialogue the user may change orientation, copies,\n   in tray and, depending on the printer type, other settings. The initial\n   values in the dialogue are taken from the declarations bin-in, copies and\n   orientation.\n\n   Declarations concerning output to screen:\n\n   Note: These declarations are mainly used for ONLINE applications. They can\n   also be defined on XTRA streams, but they will only be used when the\n   output is a window. This will be the case when the CON or PREVIEW output\n   is used. If an XTRA stream does not have these declarations, suitable\n   default values will be used.\n\n   Accelerators\n\n   A list of characters that should be returned in the [212]ACCELERATOR key\n   command. The command is triggered when the combination of the ALT key and\n   a character in the list is pressed. In this case the [213]@EVENT_PARAM\n   field will contain the character pressed. Please note that the accelerator\n   keys have precedence over accelerator keys defined in the menu and on\n   elements in the application.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the background pattern for the stream. See style attribute\n   [214]background for a description of the <background> parameter.\n\n   Docking\n\n   This property is only valid when used together with type(TOOLBOX).\n\n   Defines the appearance of the window. Read the [215]Stream declarations -\n   type topic for more information.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Specifies the frame type for the output window.\n\n   Frame type    Description\n                 Defines a sizeable window with a thick frame. If a title is\n   SIZEABLE      given the window will have a thick title bar with a system\n                 menu and MAXIMIZE, MINIMIZE and CLOSE buttons.\n                 Defines a non sizeable window with a thick frame. If a title\n   DIALOGUE      is given the window will have a thick title bar with a\n                 system menu and a CLOSE button.\n                 Defines a non sizeable window. If a title is given the\n   LINE          window will have a thick frame and a thick title bar with a\n                 system menu and a CLOSE button. If no title is given the\n                 window will have a thin frame.\n   NONE          No frame. Note: If the stream has a title the frame type is\n                 set to LINE.\n                 Defines a sizeable window with a thick frame. If a title is\n   TOOL-SIZEABLE given the window will have a thin title bar with a CLOSE\n                 button.\n                 Defines a non sizeable window with a thick frame. If a title\n   TOOL-DIALOGUE is given the window will have a thin title bar with a CLOSE\n                 button.\n\n   Horizontal-scroll-bar\n\n   If the parameter is ON, the scroll-bar will be on permanently. In the same\n   way OFF turns it off permanently. If omitted, the scroll-bars will be\n   enabled and disabled automatically whenever the layout is larger than the\n   window.\n\n   Line-gap\n\n   This option is provided for backward compatibility only, and should not be\n   used in new applications. It provides a mechanism to define a line gap or\n   spacing between lines in a form layout, and may be used in Online\n   applications using the old start-form - endform syntax to define form\n   layout. The parameter defines the line gap in number of units defined by\n   the system database item LINE-GAPS-PER-LINE of the [SETTINGS] section.\n\n   The result of defining a line gap will be that element positions, form\n   positions, form sizes and stream sizes will be adjusted according to the\n   line gap specification. For example, if the line gap is 2 and the line gap\n   unit size is 0.075, an element defined in vertical position 2 will get a\n   real position of 2.15. Note that the line gap does not modify the\n   co-ordinate system of the stream.\n\n   The default line gap is 0. For Online applications, this may be changed by\n   modifying the system database item LINE-GAP of section [SETTINGS]. Note\n   that this should only be done for systems which has utilized the old and\n   equivalent functionality of the old defaults.ini file. To suppress the\n   default line gap, use the stream declaration line-gap(0).\n\n   Maximized\n\n   For ONLINE applications: the window will be maximized, i.e. it will occupy\n   the entire work area. No caption (title line) or borders will be\n   displayed. If the frame-type is sizeable, the user can restore the window\n   to its original size.\n\n   For XTRA applications: the preview window for the report output will be\n   maximized.\n\n   NB: From Concept version 7 on the [216]show parameter should be used\n   instead. Use show(NORMAL) instead of maximized(OFF) and show(MAXIMIZED)\n   instead of maximized(ON).\n\n   Maximum-Size\n\n   Defines the maximum size of the application window in element units. The\n   window cannot be sized beyond this limit, and it cannot be maximized.\n\n   Minimum-Size\n\n   Defines the minimum size of the application window in element units. The\n   window cannot be sized beyond this limit.\n\n   Position, Pixel-Position\n\n   Specifies where the stream window will be displayed on the screen.\n\n   <Numeric expression1>:Line position of the upper left corner (in element\n   units for position and pixels for pixel-position).\n\n   <Numeric expression2>:Column position of the upper left corner (in element\n   units for position and pixels for pixel-position).\n\n   The parameters can be replaced by >< or >>. >< means centered, while >>\n   means at current cursor position.\n\n   The expressions are evaluated when the stream is opened.\n\n   The size of the usable area of the Concept main window is available in the\n   internal fields [217]@WORKSPACE_HEIGHT and [218]@WORKSPACE_WIDTH.\n\n   Show\n\n   Specifies the display mode for the window. Can be one of the following\n   values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Display mode Description\n   NORMAL       The window will be displayed in the normal state with the\n                size given. This is the default.\n   HIDDEN       The window will not be shown initially and restored to the\n                size given.\n   MAXIMIZED    The window will initially be shown maximized and restored to\n                the size given.\n   MINIMIZED    The window will initially be shown minimized and restored to\n                the size given.\n                The window will initially be shown as in the NORMAL mode.\n   RESTORED     When leaving the application, the current size and position\n                will be stored in the concept.ini file and used the next time\n                the application is started.\n\n   Size, Pixel-Size\n\n   Declares the size of the stream i.e. how much space it requires when\n   displayed on the screen.\n\n   <Numeric expression1>:Number of lines (in element units for size and\n   pixels for pixel-size).\n\n   <Numeric expression2>:Number of columns (in element units for size and\n   pixels for pixel-size).\n\n   The parameters can be replaced by a question mark (?). Concept will then\n   calculate the size according to the size of the forms to be displayed in\n   the stream.\n\n   If the window is maximized, this will be the restore size.\n\n   The expressions are evaluated when the stream is opened.\n\n   The size of the usable area of the Concept main window is available in the\n   internal fields [219]@WORKSPACE_HEIGHT and [220]@WORKSPACE_WIDTH. To\n   create a normal window that fills the whole work area use the following\n   size definition:\n\n   pixel-size("@WORKSPACE_HEIGHT","@WORKSPACE_WIDTH")\n\n   Stop-on-new-page\n\n   XTRA only.\n\n   Value Description\n   ON    When a page on the screen is full, the user is asked to press a key\n         to see the next page. This is default.\n   OFF   When a page on the screen is full, there will be no pause before\n         showing the next page.\n\n   Style\n\n   This property defines the style used by the stream. A style consists of\n   four parts: the text colour, the background colour, the text font and a\n   frame definition. Styles are defined in a separate file and are referred\n   to from within the style property. A style may be overloaded by changing\n   one or more of the style components. The style property itself overrides\n   the default [221]style identified by the form type - see the type property\n   for more information.\n\n   Refer also to the [222]default-style-prefix property of the application\n   components.\n\n   Title\n\n   This text appears as a heading in the window.\n\n   Type\n\n   This declaration defines the type of the window. Read the [223]Stream\n   declarations - type topic for more information.\n\n   Vertical-scroll-bar\n\n   If the parameter is ON, the scroll-bar will be on permanently. In the same\n   way OFF turns it off permanently. If omitted, the scroll-bars will be\n   enabled and disabled automatically whenever the layout is larger than the\n   window.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7VERTICAL-COLUMNS and HORIZONTAL-COLUMNS are used to divide one report\n   page into several sections. The COLUMN-LINES option may be used to specify\n   the number of rows to list in a section. The COLUMN-WIDTH option may be\n   used to specify the width of the display area inside a section.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When a section has been filled, the filling continues in the next section\n   on its right.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Note: All the sections specified will have the same size. It is important\n   to make sure that the width of, and number of lines in, each section do\n   not unintentionally add up to more than the values specified by PW and PL.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the formatting parameters BINARY, ASCII-DATA, or ASCII- FIELDS are\n   used, one of the following declarations must be specified on the stream:\n   CRLF, ROW-WIDTH, or INCLUDE-FIELDS. This is to decide the width of one row\n   when reading/writing from/to the stream.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [224][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm\n   2. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        Form Component                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   In [5]XTRA, a form is an area in the report output which is written as one\n   unit. Forms are written either manually using the [6]print-form function,\n   or automatically through a form property setting like page-heading.\n\n   In [7]ONLINE, a form defines a rectangular area of the application window.\n   The application window may contain one or more forms.\n\n   The contents of a form is defined using [8]element components.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   form=[9]?[10]Form\n\n \xc2\xa0[98]no-page-head\n\n   \xc2\xa0[99]no-page-tail\n\n   \xc2\xa0[100]page-heading\n\n   \xc2\xa0[101]page-tail\n\n   \xc2\xa0[102]suppress-page-tail\n\n \xc2\xa0[121]allow-resize(\xc2\xa0[122]?[123]gridResize\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[124]alternating-row-style(\xc2\xa0[125]?[126]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[139]element-sequence(\xc2\xa0[140]?[141]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[142]full-row-select(\xc2\xa0[143]?[144]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[145]grid-lines(\xc2\xa0[146]?[147]frame\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[148]horizontal-scroll-bar(\xc2\xa0ON\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0AUTO\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[155]multi-selection(\xc2\xa0[156]?[157]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[158]selection(\xc2\xa0QUEUE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0SINGLE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[159]show(\xc2\xa0[160]?[161]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[162]show-on-sort(\xc2\xa0CURRENT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0FIRST\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[163]tab-depth(\xc2\xa0[164]?[165]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[166]tab-index(\xc2\xa0[167]?[168]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[169]tab-style(\xc2\xa0[170]?[171]styleName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[172]table-connection(\xc2\xa0[173]?[174]tableName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[175]title-style(\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0[176]?[177]styleName\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0NONE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[178]vertical-scroll-bar(\xc2\xa0ON\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0AUTO\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[179]vertical-splitter(\xc2\xa0[180]?[181]formName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[182]view(\xc2\xa0[183]?[184]viewType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[185]on(\xc2\xa0[186]?[187]event\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0{[188]?[189]anyFunction}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[190]endon\n\n   Properties\n\n   additional-style-prefix\n\n   Specifies an additional prefix to the style of the form and all elements\n   owned by the form (unless they specify style directly). The text\n   expression is added to the style name as follows ;\n   <def-style-prefix><additional-style-prefix><default style name>.\n\n   Form\n\n   The name of the form component. Concept does not assign a special meaning\n   to the name of the form. But the name needs to be unique in the current\n   application.\n\n   The form is owned by the previously declared [191]stream component. This\n   stream is used to output the form and its contents to. If more than one\n   stream component is declared before the form ([192]XTRA applications), the\n   [193]include-forms property of the stream component has to be used to\n   connect a form to a stream. The forms listed in this stream property will\n   then be output on to the device the stream describes. In this case, the\n   form could have multiple owning streams.\n\n   Forms can also be owned by other forms; they are then called sub-forms. If\n   a form should be owned by another form, the owner-form property has to be\n   specified.\n\n   Active-row-style\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID. It declares the style\n   used to mark the active row when navigating within the grid form. If this\n   property is set to NONE, only one element in the grid form is selected and\n   not the entire row. Not specifying an active-row-style will cause Concept\n   to use the default row style as defined in the System Database\n   (uqsystem.ini). Active-row-style does not have influence on the frame\n   setting of the elements in the grid form.\n\n   Allow-resize\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID and DYNAMIC-GRID. It\n   declares how the columns and rows of a grid can be sized by the user at\n   run-time. Possible values are COLUMNS (this is the default), ROWS, BOTH\n   (columns and rows) and NONE.\n\n   Alternating-Row-Style\n\n   This property applies only to [194]grid-forms.It defines whether the\n   background of grid rows is to be drawn using an alternating colour. The\n   original colour of the background will be darkened slightly for every\n   other row.\n\n   Append-new-page\n\n   A form feed will be sent to the output stream after this form has been\n   written as part of an XTRA report.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the appearance of the background of the form. See the style\n   definition for [195]background for a description of the syntax of this\n   property.\n\n   Back-page\n\n   The form is the very last to be written in an XTRA report. A form feed\n   will be inserted before this form is written.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID and LISTVIEW.\n\n   Grid\n\n   If this property has value ON, then the [196]grid-form window contains two\n   small buttons in the right-hand lower corner that can be used to request\n   the next or previous page of data from the database. Thus the repeat area\n   that is represented by the grid-form is refreshed with the next (or\n   previous) chunk of data that is part of the result set of a database\n   query. By default, the value of this property is OFF, meaning that these\n   buttons are not shown.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Listview\n\n   If this property has value ON, each item (line) in the listview will\n   contain a check-box that can be checked or unchecked. See the\n   [197]listview documentation for further information.\n\n   Colour\n\n   This property defines the colour used for the title text of the form. See\n   the style definition for [198]colour for a description of the syntax of\n   this property.\n\n   If the form is connected to a file, wide column or matrix, the colour\n   specified is applied to the contents of the form as well.\n\n   Condition\n\n   The form is written to the output stream only if the logical expression\n   defined in this property is true.\n\n   Control-field\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW. The field defined by\n   the control-field property receives input events from the listview. See\n   the [199]listview documentation for further information.\n\n   Edit-labels\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW. When set to ON the\n   listview enables the user to edit the contents of the first column in the\n   listview. See the [200]listview documentation for further information.\n\n   Element-sequence\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID and LISTVIEW.\n\n   The expression is a list of element names that are to be contained or\n   owned by a grid or listview form. The first character in the list of names\n   is used as the separator for the rest of the list. The order of the\n   elements in the element-sequence property is the same as the order of\n   columns in the [201]grid-form or [202]listview.\n\n   Grid\n\n   The elements named in the list must be connected to fields belonging to\n   the table referred in the [203]table-connection property. Optional\n   [204]label, [205]top and [206]bottom elements can be defined for each\n   element named in the list.\n\n   Listview\n\n   The elements named in the list can not be connected to fields. If the\n   [207]label element declaration is used and header elements are defined,\n   the listview will contain column headers in REPORT view. If all or some of\n   the header elements are connected to a field the column header will appear\n   as clickable and the connected fields will be triggered when the\n   responding column header is clicked. If none of the header elements are\n   connected the column header will appear as non-clickable. See the\n   [208]listview documentation for further information.\n\n   Empty-table\n\n   The form is written to the output stream when the database table scan\n   referred to in a [209]scroll..endscroll loop has no resulting records. A\n   typical use for this property is a form containing text telling the user\n   that the report run did not result in any records found in the database\n   for the given selection criteria.\n\n   External-form\n\n   If this property is used for the form component, then an [210]external\n   form file is searched for additional properties for the form. The\n   properties that can be specified in an external form are those listed to\n   be \'Common\' or \'Online\'. If the external-form property is defined, these\n   \'Common\' and \'Online\' properties cannot be combined with external-form,\n   apart from position() and title().\n\n   The sub-parameters of this property are:\n\n   name\n\n   The expression used here must evaluate to a form name in an external form\n   file in the format <FileName>:<FormName>. The file FileName is searched\n   for in the LAYOUT-PATH, which is obtained either from SECURITY or from the\n   uqconfig configuration file.\n\n   connect\n\n   Forms contain elements, also in an external forms file. But it is not wise\n   to use the [211]connect parameter on the elements in order to connect them\n   to fields, as these do not reside in the form file but in the application\n   source file (.uni). If done so, it makes it hard to share an external form\n   file amongst several different applications. By using the connect\n   parameter of external-form, the connection between an element and a field\n   can also be established. Use the format <ElementName = FieldName>, where\n   ElementName is the name of the element in the external form, and FieldName\n   is the name of the field found in the current application.\n\n   Any elements from the external form with an unresolved connect will be\n   hidden.\n\n   Drop-types\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW. Defines the drop\n   types accepted by the listview. If drop-types declaration includes both\n   TEXT and FILE and the dragged object supports both formats, FILE is\n   prioritized. The SHOW-POSITION modifier can be used to specify whether\n   Concept is to show the insert position or not. See the [212]listview\n   documentation for further information.\n\n   File-name\n\n   Used to print the contents of the file identified by the name used in this\n   parameter.\n\n   If the output stream is unformatted (stream attribute formatting(none) and\n   output to file), printing this form will be equivalent to appending the\n   given file to the stream output file. Otherwise, if the output is\n   formatted, the file will be printed line by line where the width of the\n   form defines the line length and the height of the form the line height.\n\n   [213]DIO macros within the file will be expanded.\n\n   First-possible-line\n\n   The expression stated in this property is evaluated before the form is\n   written out, and defines a minimum offset from the top of the page to\n   which the form will be written.\n\n   If the value is negative, the lines are counted "from the bottom".\n\n   Font\n\n   This property defines the font used for the title text of the form. See\n   the style definition for [214]font for a description of the syntax of this\n   property.\n\n   If the form is connected to a file, wide column or matrix, the font\n   specified is applied to the contents of the form as well.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   CONVERT-TO-FRAME,CONVERT-TO-TABLE or CONVERT-TO-TABLE-HEADER\n\n   If this property is defined for the form component, and the owning stream\n   is a file of one of the supported file formats, the contents of the form\n   is supposed to have either a frame-based (CONVERT-TO-FRAME) or a\n   table-based (CONVERT-TO-TABLE and CONVERT-TO-TABLE-HEADER) layout. When\n   Concept processes the file stream, the individual element components in\n   the form are grouped together in a frame or as a table in the resulting\n   document. CONVERT-TO-TABLE-HEADER will define the form as header section\n   of a table.\n\n   In order for the conversion to succeed, the form layout has to be\n   well-designed when it comes to positioning the individual elements\n   (horizontal and vertical alignment), otherwise the resulting table could\n   contain misplaced or dummy table cells.\n\n   In the current version of Concept, the only document interface that\n   interprets this property is the interface for RTF (Rich Text Formatted)\n   files.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   TEXT\n\n   This formatting can be applied to forms using the [215]file-name or\n   [216]wide-column property. When such a form is written to a stream using\n   page [217]formatting, Concept will try to extract as much text as possible\n   before breaking it into lines, causing a layout that looks better for\n   variable pitch fonts.\n\n   Frame\n\n   This property defines the frame used for the form. See the style\n   definition for [218]frame for a description of the syntax of this\n   property.\n\n   Front-page\n\n   The form is the very first to be written in an XTRA report. It is followed\n   by a form feed.\n\n   Full-row-select\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW. When this attribute\n   is set to on, an item (line) in the listview can be selected by clicking\n   in any column of the item and the selection colour will spawn all of the\n   item. When set to OFF only the first column can be used for selection and\n   the selection colour spawns this column only. \xc2\xa0The default is OFF.\n\n   Grid-lines\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID and LISTVIEW. It declares\n   the style of the line to draw both horizontally and vertically between the\n   elements of the grid form. Listviews accepts only line style NONE and\n   LINE.\n\n   Horizontal-Scroll-Bar\n\n   Used on forms of [219]type DYNAMIC-GRID. When set to AUTO (the default),\n   the horizontal-scroll-bar is only shown when the total width of the grid\n   columns exceeds the visible width of the grid. When set to ON, the\n   horizontal-scroll-bar is always shown, but is inactive if the total width\n   of the grid columns is less or equal to the visible width of the grid.\n\n   Horizontal-Splitter\n\n   When using this parameter, the current form will be linked to the form\n   specified. The two forms will be separated by a splitter bar that can be\n   moved up and down, automatically adjusting the vertical [220]position of\n   the current form and the [221]height of the linked form. The height of the\n   linked form will be overridden so that it\'s bottom border is adjacent with\n   the top border of the current form. If a [222]relative position is used on\n   the current form, it will be used to calculate the initial position of the\n   splitter when the application starts. After that the position will be\n   adjusted internally so that the splitter bar stays in the same relative\n   position when resizing owning objects. The [223]inquire-form function will\n   return the adjusted values. To change the position of the splitter bar,\n   use the [224]height parameter of the change-form function.\n\n   The linked form should be placed above the current form. When resizing\n   forms using the splitter bar, the splitter bar cannot be moved outside the\n   space occupied by the two forms. When the forms contains elements with\n   static sizes or positions, the minimum space required by these elements\n   will be used to determine how far the splitter bar may be moved.\n\n   Include-fields\n\n   XTRA only. Contains a list of fields to be written to a data\n   [225]formatted stream. This declaration can only be used if a stream\n   including the form is formatted as BINARY,CSV, ASCII-DATA or ASCII-FIELDS.\n\n   Insert-on-page\n\n   If the form causes a form feed, the form defined is written on top of the\n   new page before the current form. This process is recursive.\n\n   Last-possible-line\n\n   The expression stated in this parameter is evaluated before the form is\n   written and defines a maximum offset from the top of the page to which the\n   form will be written.\n\n   If the value is negative, the lines are counted "from the bottom", meaning\n   that there must be at least as many lines available on the bottom of the\n   page as given in the parameter.\n\n   Local-routing\n\n   Defines how the fields in the sub-form should be integrated in the global\n   routing.\n\n   If ON, the fields will have a local routing as if the form was the only\n   form available. To exit from the sub-form, the NEXTFIELD or PREVFIELD\n   (normally the tabulator keys) must be used. This definition is normally\n   preferred when the sub-form contains a group of radio-buttons.\n\n   If OFF, the fields are merged into the general routing as if they were\n   defined in the main form.\n\n   Matrix\n\n   Used to print the contents of the given matrix field. The functionality of\n   this attribute is equivalent that of the file-name attribute.\n\n   Note: The matrix printout is made using semi graphical characters. For\n   this to be correctly drawn, the font used must be a fixed width font, e.g\n   Courier New.\n\n   Multi-selection\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW. When this attribute\n   is set to on, the listview allows multiple items (lines) to be selected.\n   When set to OFF only one item in the listview can be selected. Default is\n   OFF.\n\n   No-line-feed\n\n   This declaration should only be used on forms which is only one line high,\n   and it defines that no line feed is generated after the line. This means\n   that the first line of the next form printed will be output to the same\n   physical output line.\n\n   This functionality is normally used in connection with grouping as\n   demonstrated below:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   form="Department"no-line-feed\n\n   form="Employee"\n\n   start-form\n\n   1Dept\xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Employee\n\n   1^\n\n   2^\n\n   endform\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   on\xc2\xa0@XTRA\n\n   \xc2\xa0scroll(source="Staff")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0print-form("Department")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0group-by("Dept.code")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0print-form("Employee")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0endgroup\n\n   \xc2\xa0endscroll\n\n   endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   And\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0result\xc2\xa0may\xc2\xa0look\xc2\xa0like\xc2\xa0this:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Dept \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Employee\n\n   1 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0ALLEN\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0MARK\n\n   2 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0OLSEN\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   No-page-head\n\n   If the form is to be written on top of a new page, no page heading is\n   written.\n\n   No-page-tail\n\n   If the form is causing a form feed, no page tail is written. As an\n   example, assume that form A has specified no-page-tail. If form A is\n   written out at the end of a page, and there is not enough space left on\n   the page to print A, Concept will place form A on the next page - thus\n   inserting a form feed before A. In this respect is form A causing a form\n   feed. The page before the one that will contain A will then not have a\n   page tail. See also suppress-page-tail.\n\n   Owner-form\n\n   The form name specified here is defined to be the owner of the form. This\n   property has to be used if a form is to appear inside another form.\n   Deleting or hiding the owner form using the [226]change-form() function\n   will delete or hide this form as well.\n\n   Note: A form should either be completely outside or completely inside\n   other forms.\n\n   Page-heading\n\n   The form is written on the top of every page in an XTRA report.\n\n   Page-tail\n\n   The form is written at the bottom of every page in an XTRA report.\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of the form within its owner. By default, the owner\n   is the stream, but this may be changed using the owner-form attribute.\n   Position(0,0) indicates the upper left corner of the owner. The position\n   parameter is given in (<line>,<column>) or (<y>,<x>).\n\n   Note: If a form is to appear inside another form, the owner-form attribute\n   should be used.\n\n   See also [227]Relative size and positions\n\n   Read-only\n\n   This property is only valid when used together with the external-form\n   property.\n\n   [228]External forms can be modified at run-time in the Forms Painter. This\n   makes it possible to user-define the layout of reports and screens. The\n   application logic cannot be touched, as this is residing in the standard\n   .uco file. To disable modification access to external forms, set the\n   read-only property on the form to ON. However, it is then still possible\n   to modify the position and the title of the form. Default is OFF.\n\n   Selection\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type LISTVIEW.\n\n   When set to SINGLE, Concept will keep only the last item selection in the\n   input queue, overriding any previous unhandled selections. Use this\n   setting when item selections are time consuming and when only the latest\n   selection is important to the application. The SINGLE setting can not be\n   combined with [229]multi-selection(ON). Please also note that the LISTVIEW\n   deselect event ([230]@CHANGE) is suppressed when [231]selection is set to\n   SINGLE.\n\n   Default is QUEUE.\n\n   Show\n\n   Defines the initial state of a sub form. If the parameter is on, the sub\n   form is part of the window when the application starts. The form can later\n   be displayed or removed from the window using the [232]change-form()\n   function.\n\n   Show-On-Sort\n\n   This parameter defines how the data should be presented when a [233]header\n   sort is performed in a [234]grid form. When the parameter is set to\n   \'CURRENT\' (the default), the currently selected row is put into the first\n   grid line and the grid is filled with the following records (depending on\n   the sort order). When the parameter is set to \'FIRST\', a [235]first\n   operation is performed on the table and the cursor is placed in the first\n   grid line.\n\n   Size\n\n   Defines the size of a form. The size parameters (as (<lines>,<columns>) or\n   (<y>),<x>)) need to be constant values. The special value ? or a value\n   less or equal to zero may be used to have the corresponding size evaluated\n   at runtime to be the minimum size to hold the contents of the form.\n\n   XTRA: If the form is connected to a file, wide column or matrix, the\n   <columns> parameter is used to specify the line length. Lines from files\n   or wide columns are "word wrapped" at this length, lines from matrixes are\n   cut off at this length.\n\n   If the form is not connected to a file, wide column or matrix, the\n   <columns> parameter should be 0 except for forms (connected to streams)\n   used to make label reports.\n\n   See also [236]Relative size and positions\n\n   Suppress-page-tail\n\n   The page on which the form is written will not contain a page tail.\n\n   Style\n\n   This property defines the style used by the form. A style consists of four\n   parts: the text colour, the background colour, the text font and a frame\n   definition. Styles are defined in a separate file and are referred to from\n   within the style property. A style may be overloaded by changing one or\n   more of the style components. The style property itself overrides the\n   default [237]style identified by the form type - see the type property for\n   more information.\n\n   Refer also to the [238]default-style-prefix property of the application\n   components.\n\n   Tab-depth\n\n   Defines the form to be a tab-form containing the number of tabs specified\n   in this parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The title of each tab is defined by the title attribute.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Elements or sub-forms of this form are assigned to the desired tab using\n   the tab-index property on form or element.\n\n   \xc2\xb7By default, the first tab becomes the initially active tab.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The form event @ACTIVE-TAB-INDEX is generated when the active tab index\n   is changed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [239]change-form() function may be used to change the active tab\n   index.\n\n   Tab-index\n\n   If the owner of this form is a tab form, this attribute may be used to\n   define the tab index in which the current form is to appear. Tab index 0\n   is used to define that the form is to appear in all tabs of the owner\n   form.\n\n   Tab-Style\n\n   Used on tab forms. Defines the style to use when drawing the tab row of\n   the form.\n\n   Table-connection\n\n   This property applies only to forms of type GRID: it connects a grid-form\n   to the named table. The table should have a repeat declaration for it to\n   be useful. The number of rows in the grid-form will be equal to the number\n   of repeat lines defined on the table declaration.\n\n   Table-heading\n\n   The form will be written once per region just before the first row of the\n   table referenced by this parameter is written.\n\n   Table-tail\n\n   The form is written after the final row in the region has been written.\n\n   Title-style\n\n   Defines the style of the title part of the form. If set to NONE the style\n   is written as in earlier versions (as a part of the frame).\n\n   When set to a style name, the font and the lower frame of that style is\n   used to create a title that is placed inside the frame of the form. The\n   height of the title is a combination of the height of the font, the\n   thickness of the frame \xc2\xa0and the upper and lower margins defined by the\n   FORM-TITLE-MARGINS in the DEFAULT-SETTINGS.<default-style-prefix> section\n   of the uqsystem.ini file. This setting also defines the left and right\n   margins for the title and the line below it.\n\n   The default for title-style is defined by the value of the\n   FORM-TITLE-STYLE setting (in the DEFAULT-SETTINGS.<default-style-prefix>\n   section of the uqsystem.ini file) at compile time.\n\n   Title\n\n   Defines the title of the form. The title is only used if a frame is\n   defined.\n\n   If the form is a tab form, the expression here must be a semicolon\n   separated list of tab titles.\n\n   Top-of-page\n\n   A form feed will be written before the form is written. The form is\n   therefore printed on top of a new page.\n\n   Transparent\n\n   This is a synonym for the form declaration background(transparent). This\n   parameter is only for backwards compatibility.\n\n   Trigger-forms\n\n   A form using this declaration will not be written until one of the forms\n   in its parameter list is about to be written. The form is then written\n   prior to the form that trigged it.\n\n   A form can only be trigged once, i.e. as soon as the form has been\n   written, it will not be written again (even if several (all) of the forms\n   in the trigger list are written).\n\n   This mechanism is often used with owner - member structures to make sure\n   that the owner isn\'t written unless it has members.\n\n   Type\n\n   Describes the type of the form. By default, a form is of type NORMAL. In\n   ONLINE applications, this means that the form is a kind of group box for\n   elements. In XTRA applications, the behaviour of the form is influenced by\n   additional properties, like table-heading and page-tail. In ONLINE\n   applications, the type could also be TAB (for a tab-form),\n   GRID/DYNAMIC-GRID/SIZEABLE-GRID (for a [240]grid-form) or LISTVIEW (for a\n   [241]listview). TAB is in fact redundant, as the tab-depth property is\n   used by Concept to determine if a form is to be treated as a tab-form.\n\n   The type property will also have an impact on the default style used for a\n   form.\n\n   E.g for a form of type TAB the compiler will search uqsystem.ini for a\n   style named <Default-style-prefix>TAB-FORM and use it if found, otherwise\n   it will use <Default-style-prefix>-FORM (which is required). For sizeable\n   and dynamic grid form types the search hierarchy is\n   <Default-style-prefix><SIZEABLE | DYNAMIC>-FORM,\n   <Default-style-prefix>GRID-FORM and <Default-style-prefix>-FORM. For\n   listviews the search hierarchy is <Default-style-prefix>LISTVIEW-FORM and\n   <Default-style-prefix>-FORM.\n\n   Vertical-Scroll-Bar\n\n   Used on forms of [242]type DYNAMIC-GRID. When set to AUTO, the\n   vertical-scroll-bar is only shown, if more rows than fit into the grid are\n   shown. When set to ON (the default), the vertical-scroll-bar is always\n   shown, but is inactive if less rows than fit into the grid are shown.\n\n   Vertical-Splitter\n\n   When using this parameter, the current form will be linked to the form\n   specified. The two forms will be separated by a splitter bar that can be\n   moved left and right, automatically adjusting the horizontal [243]position\n   of the current form and the [244]width of the linked form. The width of\n   the linked form will be overridden so that it\'s right border is adjacent\n   with the left border of the current form. If a [245]relative position is\n   used on the current form, it will be used to calculate the initial\n   position of the splitter when the application starts. After that the\n   position will be adjusted internally so that the splitter bar stays in the\n   same relative position when resizing owning objects. The [246]inquire-form\n   function will return the adjusted values. To change the position of the\n   splitter bar, use the [247]width parameter of the change-form function.\n\n   The linked form should be placed to the left of the current form. When\n   resizing forms using the splitter bar, the splitter bar cannot be moved\n   outside the space occupied by the two forms. When the forms contains\n   elements with static sizes or positions, the minimum space required by\n   these elements will be used to determine how far the splitter bar may be\n   moved.\n\n   View\n\n   Defines the initial view of a [248]listview form. Possible values are\n   LARGE (large icons), SMALL (small icons), LIST (list) and REPORT (details;\n   the default).\n\n   Wide-column\n\n   Used to print the contents of the given wide column field. The\n   functionality of this attribute is equivalent that of the file-name\n   attribute.\n\n   \'Old\' layout definition\n\n   The start-form - endform declaration in an application is an easy way to\n   define a simple layout for an application. This declaration was used in\n   the Concept versions before version 5. Starting version 5, a more advanced\n   layout declaration mechanism is used with the element syntax (in\n   co-operation with the Forms Painter). However, the \'old\' (line/column\n   based) layout syntax can still be applied.\n\n   Start-form - endform\n\n   Defines the layout of the form. Layout may only be defined for forms not\n   connected to a matrix field, a wide column field or a file.\n\n   In XTRA applications, it is possible to define the layout for all forms of\n   the application inside one start-form - endform block. The first character\n   of each line must then be non-blank, and a new character in this position\n   indicates the start of the layout definition of the next form.\n\n   The layout definition may contain 3 different component types:\n\n   DIO macros\n\n   The lead-in character (normally ^) followed by one of the reserved macro\n   names defines a macro. A macro has one or more parameters separated by a\n   comma and is always terminated by a semicolon. A macro changes an\n   attribute (like font or tabulators) in the form. The new value is valid\n   until a new macro changes the value. Some macros does not change a value,\n   but returns a text (like PN and DA). If a layout line contains nothing but\n   macros defining an attribute, the line will not generate a line-feed. All\n   legal macros are listed in section [249]DIO macros.\n\n   Field elements\n\n   The lead-in character not followed by a DIO macro name defines the\n   position of an element connected to a field. The type of the element is\n   implicitly defined by a corresponding [250]field declaration.\n\n   If the [251]element type is menu-entry, push-button, radio-group or\n   check-box, the lead-in character should be followed by a semicolon\n   defining the extent of the element. Between the lead-in and the semicolon,\n   the label of the element is defined. The ampersand character within a\n   label is used to define the following character to be the accelerator key\n   of the element. For backward compatibility, menu entry element may have a\n   special accelerator key for a defined by a letter and a comma immediately\n   following the lead-in character.\n\n   For other element types the lead-in may be followed by a [252]display\n   code.\n\n   Text elements\n\n   Everything not recognized as a DIO macro or field element is interpreted\n   as text elements. To achieve intended alignment of elements even when\n   using proportional fonts, a text string is by default split in two text\n   elements when two words are separated by more than one space character.\n   The compiler option one-word-per-element may be used to change the default\n   to make every word into one element.\n\n   Note: endform is the only 4GL keyword that must be written starting at the\n   first position of the source line in order for the 4GL compiler to be\n   recognized.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [253][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1.
