b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                      Element Component                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The element component declares a visible item within a [5]form. Examples\n   of elements are labels, input controls, check boxes and push buttons. Most\n   elements can be used in both [6]ONLINE and [7]XTRA applications, but some\n   of them (like push-buttons) are only appropriate for ONLINE applications.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   element=[8]?[9]Element\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]alignment(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]alignmentCode,\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]alignmentCode\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]background(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]background\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]bottom(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]elementName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]branch-lines(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]branchLines\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]buttons(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]check(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]colour(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]colour\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]connect(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]applicationField\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]cursor(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]cursorId\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]display(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]displayCode\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]drop-down-lines(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]drop-types(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]dropTypes\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[48]edit-labels(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[51]focus-behaviour(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]focusBehaviour\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[54]font(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]font\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]font-angle(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]integer\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]formatting(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]multilineFormatting\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]frame(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]frame\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]image(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]image\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[69]information(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]elementText\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[72]label(\xc2\xa0[73]?[74]elementName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[75]local-sort(\xc2\xa0[76]?[77][>|<]\xc2\xa0[78]?[79]elementName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[80]lock(\xc2\xa0[81]?[82]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[83]mask-character(\xc2\xa0[84]character\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[85]multi-line(\xc2\xa0[86]?[87]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[88]multi-selection(\xc2\xa0[89]?[90]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[91],position(\xc2\xa0[92]?[93]positionExpression,\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[96][,selection(\xc2\xa0QUEUE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0SINGLE\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[97]show(\xc2\xa0[98]?[99]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[100],size(\xc2\xa0[101]?[102]sizeExpression,\xc2\xa0[103]?[104]sizeExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[105]end-position(\xc2\xa0[106]?[107]sizeExpression,\xc2\xa0[108]?[109]sizeExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[110]sort(\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0[[UNIQUE|AMBIGUOUS],]\xc2\xa0[111]?[112][>|<]\xc2\xa0[113]?applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[114]?[115][>|<]\xc2\xa0[116]?applicationField\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[117]style(\xc2\xa0[118]?[119]styleName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[120]tab-index(\xc2\xa0[121]?[122]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[123]?[124]unsignedInteger}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[125]text(\xc2\xa0[126]?[127]elementText\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[128]top(\xc2\xa0[129]?[130]elementName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[131]type(\xc2\xa0[132]?[133]elementType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Properties\n\n   Element\n\n   The name of the element. Concept does not assign a special meaning to the\n   name of the element. But the name needs to be unique in the current\n   application.\n\n   Alignment\n\n   This property can be used to specify the horizontal and vertical alignment\n   of the text on the element. Only elements that are associated with a text\n   string (like a TEXT or an INPUT element) can have this attribute\n   specified. Possible values here are DEFAULT, CENTER, LEFT, RIGHT,\n   SIGNED-RIGHT (for horizontal alignment), TOP and BOTTOM (for vertical\n   alignment) : the first value is for the vertical alignment, the second for\n   the horizontal alignment. Specifying DEFAULT is the same as not specifying\n   the alignment property for the element component.\n\n   The SIGNED-RIGHT alignment takes a minus sign at the end of the element\n   value into account, making sure that numeric values are correctly aligned.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the appearance of the background of the element. This property\n   will override the background specification that is part of the style\n   definition for the element. See the style definition for [134]background\n   for a description of the syntax of this property.\n\n   Bottom\n\n   This property can only be used on elements that are owned by forms of\n   [135]type GRID, DYNAMIC-GRID or SIZEABLE-GRID. Every element referred to\n   in the element-sequence property of the form may have this property\n   specified. The property declares a bottom element for the grid column.\n\n   Branch-lines\n\n   Branch-lines is a property that can only be used with elements of\n   [136]type TREEVIEW. The following values can be specified:\n\n   Value    Description\n            The treeview element has lines linking child items to their\n   ALL      corresponding parent items in the hierarchy, including the root\n            item.\n   CHILDREN The treeview element has lines linking child items to their\n            corresponding parent items, excluding the root item.\n   NONE     The treeview has no lines.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If this property is not specified, ALL is assumed.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   If the value for this property is set to ON, a TREEVIEW element adds a\n   small button to the left of each item that has sub-items. The button is\n   used to expand and collapse the sub-items (or: 'children') of the item. By\n   default, this property is set to ON.\n\n   Check\n\n   If the value for this property is set to ON, a TREEVIEW element adds a\n   check box to the left of each item. The @CHANGE event on the connected\n   field is triggered when the state of the check box changes . By default,\n   this property is set to OFF.\n\n   Colour\n\n   This property defines the colour used for the text used in the element.\n   This property will override the colour specification that is part of the\n   style definition for the element. See the style definition for [137]colour\n   for a description of the syntax of this property.\n\n   Connect\n\n   The field name given for the connect property is the name of the field\n   that is to be associated with the element. Such an association is needed\n   to present the contents of a field in an application (like an alphanumeric\n   field presented in an OUTPUT element). What the exact effects are of an\n   element-field association depends on the element [138]type.\n\n   Cursor\n\n   Defines the cursor shape that should be used when the mouse pointer is\n   moved over the element. See [139]Cursor definition for more details.\n\n   Display\n\n   The display property defines how the textual contents of the element is to\n   be displayed. The parameter is a standard Concept 4GL [140]display code.\n   Specifying a display code on an element will override the display code of\n   the connected field or the display code of the database column the\n   connected field is related to. Unlike the display code on a field, the\n   display code on an element has no other functionality than to specify how\n   a value is shown in an application.\n\n   Drop-down-lines\n\n   Defines the number of lines a DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX or a DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX\n   should have in the dropped-down state.\n\n   Drop-types\n\n   Defines the drop types accepted by the element. If drop-types declaration\n   includes both TEXT and FILE and the dragged object supports both formats,\n   FILE is prioritized. The SHOW-POSITION modifier can be used to specify\n   whether Concept is to show the insert position or not.\n\n   Edit-labels\n\n   If the value for this property is set to ON, it is possible to change the\n   text label for each item in a TREEVIEW at run-time. By default, this\n   property is set to OFF.\n\n   End-position\n\n   Is used only for line elements, and describes the position of the\n   end-point of the line. Lines are drawn starting from the coordinates given\n   in the position property to those given in the end-position property.\n\n   See also [141]Relative size and positions\n\n   Focus-Behaviour\n\n   This property can be used to specify the element's behaviour when it\n   receives the input focus. The following parameter values can be used\n   (separated by comma):\n\n   Value                 Description\n                         The original style of the element is to be used when\n   NO-STYLE-CHANGE       the element has the input focus. This prevents e.g.\n                         the highlighting of the current element in a\n                         grid-form.\n                         Shows the drop-down button on DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOXes\n   SHOW-DROP-DOWN-BUTTON and DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOXes only when the cursor is\n                         inside the element.\n\n   Font\n\n   This property defines the font used for the text of the element. It will\n   override the font specification that is part of the style definition for\n   the element. See the style definition for [142]font for a description of\n   the syntax of this property.\n\n   Font-angle\n\n   This property applies only to TEXT elements.\n\n   Specifies the rotation of the text in degrees and must be a value between\n   -180 and 180. Default is 0.\n\n   Please note that some fonts does not allow rotation (e.g. MS Sans Serif).\n\n   Formatting\n\n   This property can be used when the [143]multi-line property is set to 'ON'\n   on elements of [144]type 'INPUT' or 'OUTPUT'. Normally multi-line fields\n   must contain the character combination Cr/Lf to force line breaks. This\n   character combination can cause problems in connection with column values\n   in databases. In these situation the value 'UNIQUE' can be used to\n   automatically convert the character combination '/,' (line break) to Cr/Lf\n   when showing field values in the element and back when the element value\n   is changed and stored in the connected field. The value 'CRLF' (default)\n   means that the values passed between element and field are not changed. A\n   value of 'PLAIN' converts all characters in the element buffer with an\n   ASCII value less than 32 to spaces when storing changed element values in\n   the field.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Specifies the frame style surrounding the element. It will override the\n   frame specification that is part of the style definition for the element.\n   See the style definition for [145]frame for a description of the syntax of\n   this property.\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines one or more [146]images used by the element. The usage of this\n   property depends on the element [147]type.\n\n   Information\n\n   If the cursor is rested for a predefined period of time on top of the\n   element, a small window is shown containing the text specified in the\n   information property (often referred to as \xef\xbf\xbdtooltip\xef\xbf\xbd). If this property is\n   not specified, the window will not appear. If the text is to span several\n   lines, the macro '/,' can be used to force line breaks.\n\n   Label\n\n   This property can only be used on elements that are owned by forms of\n   [148]type GRID, DYNAMIC-GRID or SIZEABLE-GRID. Every element referred to\n   in the element-sequence property of the form may have this property\n   specified. The property declares a label element for the grid column.\n\n   Local-Sort\n\n   This property may only be used on elements of [149]type HEADER in\n   [150]DYNAMIC grid forms and defines the sort order which is to be used\n   when the user clicks on the element. If the user clicks on a HEADER\n   element which uses the local-sort declaration, the sorting of the\n   [151]form to which the header belongs will be changed accordingly. If the\n   user clicks on the same header once more (without having clicked on\n   another header in the meantime), the sort order will be reversed.\n\n   The way the sort order is defined is similar to the one used in the\n   [152]change-form function. An empty field list will cause Concept to\n   restore the sort order to the one defined on the table.\n\n   Lock\n\n   If the element is not locked, the user is allowed to navigate (to position\n   the cursor) into the element. Possible values are ON and OFF (OFF is the\n   default). See the chapter on [153]locking for more details.\n\n   Mask-character\n\n   The mask-character property has only meaning to an element of [154]type\n   INPUT. It defines the character to be shown in the input element when\n   typing text into this element. This feature is often applied to input\n   fields for passwords where the actual text is hidden by a special\n   character. When no parameter is specified in mask-character(), an asterisk\n   ('*') is used as masking character.\n\n   Multi-line\n\n   If this property is set to ON, an INPUT, OUTPUT, BUTTON, TEXT, CHECK-BOX\n   or RADIO-BUTTON element is enhanced to contain more than one line of text.\n\n   Text in a multi-line element is auto wrapped - a vertical scrollbar will\n   appear in INPUT or OUTPUT elements when the text cannot be contained in\n   the element. The character combination Cr/Lf (Carriage Return/Line Feed)\n   can be used in the value of the connected field to force lines breaks. The\n   [155]formatting property can be used to automatically convert to and from\n   Cr/Lf.\n\n   For multi-line TEXT, BUTTON, CHECK-BOX or RADIO-BUTTON \xc2\xa0elements the text\n   is auto wrapped only if the width of the element is not dynamic (other\n   than 0), no scrollbars are applied even if the text doesn't fit into the\n   elements area. The special character combination '/', can be used to\n   denote forced line breaks in the text. Use the [156]FROM_CRLF operator to\n   assign text containing the ascii CR LF characters into multi line text\n   elements.\n\n   Multi-selection\n\n   If this property is set to ON, the user is able to select one or more\n   items in a LIST-BOX,DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX or DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX.Default is\n   OFF.\n\n   Please note that this will only work when the connected field has\n   alphanumeric storage and as long as the storage length of the field is\n   large enough to hold the selected list of values (including the\n   separator).\n\n   Position\n\n   The element is positioned at the co-ordinates (<y>,<x>) relative to the\n   owning form. Position (0,0) equals the upper left corner of the form. The\n   position is specified using the [157]formular setting in the application.\n\n   See also [158]Relative size and positions\n\n   Selection\n\n   This property applies only to TREEVIEW elements.\n\n   When set to SINGLE, Concept will keep only the last item selection in the\n   input queue, overriding any previous unhandled selections. Use this\n   setting when item selections are time consuming and when only the latest\n   selection is important to the application.\n\n   Default is QUEUE.\n\n   Show\n\n   Defines if the element is visible or not. If the element should be visible\n   in the form, the property must be ON, otherwise the property should be set\n   to OFF. The show property has a default value of ON.\n\n   Size\n\n   The <width> parameter specifies the horizontal size of the element; the\n   <height> parameter specifies the vertical size of the element. The size is\n   specified using the [159]formular setting in the application. A zero in\n   the width and/or height parameter is handled as a dynamic size request\n   (the size is calculated by the contents of the element).\n\n   See also [160]Relative size and positions\n\n   Sort\n\n   This property may only be used on elements of [161]type HEADER and defines\n   the sort order which is to be used when the user clicks on the element. If\n   the user clicks on a HEADER element which uses the sort declaration, the\n   sorting of the [162]table connected to the [163]grid form to which the\n   header belongs will be changed accordingly. If the user clicks on the same\n   header once more (without having clicked on another header in the\n   meantime), the sort order will be reversed.\n\n   The way the sort order is defined is similar to the one used in the\n   [164]change function. The field list can be preceded by the key type\n   (UNIQUE or AMBIGUOUS) and a comma. The default key type is AMBIGUOUS. An\n   empty field list will cause Concept to restore the sort order to the one\n   defined on the table.\n\n   Style\n\n   This property defines the style used by the element. A style consists of\n   four parts: the text colour, the background colour, the text font and a\n   frame definition. Styles are defined in a separate file and are referred\n   to from within the style property. A style may be overloaded by changing\n   one or more of the style components. The style property itself overrides\n   the default [165]style identified by the element [166]type.\n\n   Refer also to the [167]default-style-prefix property of the application\n   components.\n\n   Tab-index\n\n   If the owner form of this element is a tab form, this property may be used\n   to define the tab index in which the element is to appear. Tab index 0 is\n   used to define that the element is to appear in all tabs of the owner\n   form. If the element should appear in a subset of the available tabs,\n   specify the tab indices separated by a comma.\n\n   Text\n\n   Defines a text string used by the element. The usage of the text string\n   depends on the element [168]type.\n\n   Top\n\n   This property can only be used on elements that are owned by forms of\n   [169]type GRID, DYNAMIC-GRID or SIZEABLE-GRID. Every element referred to\n   in the element-sequence property of the form may have this property\n   specified. The property declares a top element for the grid column.\n\n   Type\n\n   Defines the element type. [170]See element types for details.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_form.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. A database with this name must be defined\n   in the configuration file uqconfig and made available to the current\n   system (using the available-database configuration item in uqconfig). The\n   following databases are automatically available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Database Description\n   UQTEMP   Temporary tables used by Concept\n   UQAPPTMP [7]Automatic Temporary Tables\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The declaration sets the database current, which means that it is assumed\n   that following [8]table[****]declarations refer to tables in the current\n   database unless overruled with the database.table syntax.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The database name is a logical database name, i.e. not necessarily a\n   physical database name. Two methods in the configuration file may be used\n   to map physical to logical database names: the alias keyword of the system\n   command available-database and the db-physical-name database command. This\n   is exemplified below where the application accesses database A which is\n   mapped to the physical database C:\n\n   Application \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Configuration file (uqconfig)\n\n   database=A \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0database:\xc2\xa0B\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0db-physical-name=C\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0system:\xc2\xa0DEMO\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0available-database=A\xc2\xa0alias\xc2\xa0B\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7The declaration is ignored if there are no references to tables in the\n   database.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [9][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_database.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_databasename.htm#idh_la_pop_databasename\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_database.htm#idh_ma_database_database\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_tempdb.htm#idh_ma_tempdb_auto\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_database.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Table Component                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The table component defines a database table to be accessed by the\n   application\n\n   Syntax\n\n   [[5]repeat\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0[8]times]\n\n   table=[[9]?[10]databaseName.][11]?[12]tableName\n\n   \xc2\xa0[13]access(\xc2\xa0[FORCED\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]accessCode\xc2\xa0{+\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]accessCode}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[18]automatic-fetch(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[21]automatic-show(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[24]cache(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[27]concurrency-control(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]concurrencyControl\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[30]control(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]controlType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[33]current-record(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[36]db-table(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]name\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[39]join-type(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]joinType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[42]key-column(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]columnName\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]columnName}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[47]key-field(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]applicationField\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[50]key-type(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]keyType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[53]log\n\n   \xc2\xa0[54]match(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]matchType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[57]popup(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[60]sort(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]sorting\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[63]sql-where(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[66]sql-group-by(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[69]sql-order-by(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[72]store-after-key(\xc2\xa0[73]?[74]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[75]verify(\xc2\xa0[76]?[77]logicalExpression,\xc2\xa0[78]?[79]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0[80]on(\xc2\xa0[81]?[82]functionKeyOrEvent\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0{[83]?[84]anyFunction}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[85]endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0<table\xc2\xa0declaration\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0field\xc2\xa0functions>\n\n   [[86]endrepeat]\n\n   Key words\n\n   Repeat <repeat count> times ... endrepeat\n\n   The repeat declaration is used when more than one row from the same table\n   is wanted. <repeat count> defines the number of rows to be fetched at a\n   time when the [87]first, [88]last, [89]next or [90]previous command is\n   given. Fields connected to a table with a repeat definition are only\n   declared once within repeat ... endrepeat and are automatically expanded\n   to <repeat count> occurrences. However, all visible fields must be defined\n   <repeat count> times in the form layout.\n\n   It is possible to have several repeat blocks in one application, but not\n   nested. If two repeat blocks are to be placed next to each other in the\n   layout, this must be done by use of sub-forms.\n\n   Fields connected to the same logical table can not be defined both inside\n   and outside a repeat block.\n\n   Table\n\n   The name of the table. The name should indicate the use of the table and\n   is used when references to this table are made.\n\n   The name should be the same as in the database. It is, however, possible\n   to give the table another name and use the db-table declaration to refer\n   to the [91]database.\n\n   All commands enclosed by square brackets are table declarations. This\n   means that they declare properties for a table which remain effective\n   while the application is running. Each of the declarations is described\n   below, or in separate sections.\n\n   Table declarations\n\n   Defines all fields connected to the table. Field declarations are\n   described in the [92]field section.\n\n   All fields connected to a table are cleared when the row is cleared and\n   updated when a row is fetched from the database. Note the use of scope\n   declaration on the field. If the field is bound to a column in the table,\n   the field name should be the same as the column name or the column(<column\n   name>) declaration must be used. If the field should be connected to the\n   table, but has no column connection, the local declaration must be\n   defined. If the field is not to be connected to any table (i.e. not\n   cleared with the row), the static declaration must be defined.\n\n   General declarations\n\n   Access\n\n   Specifies the access right of the application to the table. Possible\n   values of <access code> are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Access Description\n   NONE   No access\n   QUERY  Read/query only\n   UPDATE Update columns\n   INSERT Insert new rows\n   DELETE Delete existing rows\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If only one <access code> is specified, it is interpreted as composite\n   access right including all access rights at lower levels. Example:\n\n   INSERT\n\n   is equivalent to\n\n   QUERY+UPDATE+INSERT\n\n   Thus, to get one single access right higher than QUERY, the access right\n   NONE must be used as a part of the access definition. Example:\n\n   NONE+INSERT\n\n   gives the INSERT access right only. Note: Some DBMS interfaces may take\n   advantage of such simple access rights yielding better performance than a\n   composite access right. For example, in an application only inserting\n   records, the NONE+INSERT access right definition should be used.\n\n   Note that the actual access right obtained when running an application may\n   be lower than that specified using this table declaration. Access rights\n   may be reduced by Security, and through the access parameter of the\n   [93]start, [94]call, [95]run or [96]zoom functions used to activate the\n   application. To force Concept to use the access code defined - regardless\n   of the SECURITY access and/or the imported access - the access code can be\n   preceded with the keyword \'FORCED\' (with at least one space before the\n   access code).\n\n   This access right can be changed at run-time for each individual row by\n   using the [97]change function.\n\n   Cache\n\n   This property defines the table cache strategy for the table. To enable\n   caching, use a cache size in the range 1 to 255, meaning the maximum\n   number of rows to be cached. Use cache size 0 to disable the default table\n   caching. The default table caching for a given table is specified in the\n   system database. (The system database is stored in the uqsystem.ini file\n   in the application path.) The section [TABLE CACHE] may contain lines on\n   the format\n\n   <database name>.<table name> = <cache size>\n\n   where <database name> is the logical database name, and <table name> is\n   the table name as defined in the database dictionary. The specification in\n   the system database is used by all tables qualifying to be cached and not\n   having an application local cache specification.\n\n   The declaration may only be used on join tables with query access only,\n   and can not be combined with the declarations SQL-WHERE, SQL-ORDER-BY and\n   SQL-GROUP-BY.\n\n   The table cache is a mechanism to reduced database usage and network\n   traffic: A row fetched from the database is stored in the local table\n   cache so that the next time the same row is requested, it is fetched from\n   the cache and not from the database.\n\n   Warning: In a multi-user application, this declaration must be used with\n   great care and normally only on tables which are static, i.e. not possibly\n   concurrently updated by other users.\n\n   The table cache is implemented by storing row key values in memory and row\n   data in a temporary file on the scratch path. (The file has extension\n   .tac.) When the table cache is full, i.e. it contains the defined maximum\n   number of rows, a new row will replace the least recently accessed row.\n\n   The table cache for a given table is cleared if the physical table to\n   which it is connected is updated (through an insert, delete update\n   function) or through another (not cached) table in the same session. Also,\n   the table cache is cleared when the session is terminated.\n\n   Two different table definitions connected to the same physical table will\n   share the same table cache if the definitions of the tables are identical\n   with respect to table key, number of columns fetched and the sequence of\n   the column definitions.\n\n   Generally, the table cache size should be specified as small as possible:\n   A small cache is both faster to search in and requires less memory and\n   disk space. Note that it is the first definition of a given table cache\n   that defines the size of the cache. This size is not changed by later\n   definitions. (In a development phase, you have to terminate the session\n   and restart to test a new table cache size.)\n\n   The table cache is currently only utilized by the 4GL functions [98]find\n   and [99]join.\n\n   Concurrency-control\n\n   This property defines which concurrency control strategy is to be used for\n   the table. A concurrency control strategy is needed to handle multi-user\n   conflicts, that is situations where more than one user attempts to update\n   a table record at the same time.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value      Description\n              This is the default option: The optimistic approach is based on\n              the assumption that conflicts do normally not arise. Thus, no\n              table or record locking is done at the time of fetch, but the\n              update operation itself is carried out in such a way that\n              multi-user conflicts are detected. If a concurrent update is\n   OPTIMISTIC detected, the operation is aborted.\n\n              On SQL DBMS\'s, the OPTIMISTIC strategy is normally implemented\n              by using a where clause of the update and delete statements\n              containing the condition that all table columns referred to in\n              the application should have the same value as at the time of\n              fetch.\n              No explicit concurrency control is done. However, some\n              multi-user conflicts will be detected, like an attempt to\n   OFF        modify or delete an already deleted record. This option should\n              only be used when there is no need for concurrency control. In\n              such cases, a performance gain can be achieved by using it.\n\n   Control\n\n   This property defines who is in control of certain aspects of table\n   handling - the automatics of Concept Runtime identified by the keyword\n   UNIQUE, or the programmer through the application code, identified by the\n   keyword PROGRAM.\n\n   In ONLINE applications Unique control is the default, whereas in XTRA\n   applications program control is the default.\n\n   The declaration affects the following aspects of table handling:\n\n   Execution of table functions\n\n   On tables with Unique control, the database functions [100]first,\n   [101]last, [102]next, [103]previous, [104]find and [105]join automatically\n   execute table functions if a record is found.\n\n   Note that whether the database functions [106]scroll and [107]group-by\n   executes table functions or not is controlled by whether the application\n   utilizes the @XTRA event or not, and not by this declaration.\n\n   Also note that the user commands available in an ONLINE application to\n   navigate a table, like FIRSTREC, LASTREC, NEXTREC and PREVREC do not\n   distinguish between Unique and program controlled tables: Table functions\n   are always executed when records are found. Thus, on a program controlled\n   table the code "[108]on(FIRSTREC) first(...) endon()" implies a real\n   change to the FIRSTREC user command, whereas on a Unique controlled table,\n   it does not imply a real change.\n\n   Database updates\n\n   A Unique controlled table is automatically updated when certain conditions\n   are true, like the condition that the user moves the cursor out of the\n   changed table. A program controlled table is never updated automatically,\n   i.e. the update must be manually done using the [109]insert, [110]update\n   or [111]delete functions.\n\n   If more than one Unique controlled table are changed when an automatic\n   database update is initiated, all updates are performed as one transaction\n   to achieve that either all or none are carried out.\n\n   If a database update of a Unique controlled table fails, the record is\n   automatically re fetched from the database.\n\n   Note: Avoid the combination of changing fields of a Unique controlled\n   table which is scrolled using the SCROLL function - the results may not be\n   as expected.\n\n   Hint: To achieve program control of database updates of Unique controlled\n   tables, the [112]@SYNCHRONIZE event may be utilized.\n\n   The KEY function\n\n   For Unique controlled tables, the KEY keyword has a functional behavior in\n   addition to its declarative nature: It attempts to find the record\n   identified by the given key value, and if the record is not found and\n   besides depends on some other table declarations, a new record is prepared\n   for insertion.\n\n   Current-record\n\n   This property controls the current record mechanism of the table:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value Description\n         This is the default option: When leaving the application, the\n         current record of the table will be remembered by recording the\n         record id or key value, together with the logical table name and the\n   ON    physical key name. When entering any application containing the same\n         table as a top level table (not a member or join table), a\n         previously remembered record of a table with the same logical table\n         name and physical key name will automatically be fetched.\n   OFF   Current records will neither be remembered nor fetched.\n\n   Db-table\n\n   Specifies the name of the corresponding table in the database. This\n   function is only needed if the Concept table name is different from the\n   table name in the database. This function is necessary in the following\n   circumstances:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If tables from different databases have identical names.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the same table within a database is used more than once within the\n   application.\n\n   Key-type\n\n   Key-type can take two possible values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value     Description\n   UNIQUE    Duplicate key values are not allowed.\n   AMBIGUOUS Duplicate key values are allowed.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Default is as defined in the database schema. When a key is ambiguous,\n   giving a new key value will not result in a check for an existing row with\n   the given key value. A new row will always be inserted.\n\n   Log\n\n   Defines insert and delete operations on the table to be logged. See\n   general section on [113]logging for details.\n\n   Popup\n\n   Defines a popup menu for fields on the table. Popup menus defined on\n   [114]field level take precedence over menus defined on table level. When\n   the right mouse button is pressed in a field having this declaration, the\n   following happens:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field pointed to is not the current field, it is made current,\n   i.e. the cursor is moved to the field and the appropriate cursor movement\n   events are fired.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The <alpha expression> parameter of the popup declaration is evaluated,\n   and if it identifies a valid menu, the menu is shown and the user is\n   allowed to make a selection.\n\n   Sort\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value      Description\n   ASCENDING  The rows will be sorted in ascending order. This is the default\n              mode.\n              The rows will be sorted in descending order. This mode is\n   DESCENDING particularly useful with date keys, so that the oldest or the\n              newest columns can be listed first.\n              The rows will not be sorted in any particular order. Meaningful\n              only for SQL databases, for other database systems ASCENDING\n   NONE       will be assumed. When ordering is not important, this mode will\n              give better performance since the SQL engine will not be\n              instructed to sort the resulting data set. This mode is only\n              allowed in XTRA applications.\n\n   Sql-where\n\n   The <textExpression> is evaluated when any of the database operations\n   [115]first, [116]last or [117]find  are executed. The resulting text is an\n   extra predicate AND\'ed to the static predicate used when fetching rows\n   from the table. The static predicate is implicitly defined through the\n   table relationships of the application, and through the use of the range\n   property.\n\n   The extra predicate is used in the where clause of the SQL select\n   statement automatically generated to implement the operation. If the\n   original statement contains a where clause, the extra predicate is AND\'ed\n   to the existing clause, otherwise the extra predicate is used as the where\n   clause of the statement.\n\n   A set of macros are available to ease the task of writing correct and\n   portable SQL predicates, see [118]SQL expressions.\n\n   The sql-where property only applies to SQL databases.\n\n   Store-after-key\n\n   When you enter a new value for the field that is part of the key of the\n   table, Concept tries to find a record according to the values of the key\n   fields. If it does not find such a record, it is assumed that you want to\n   insert a new record in the database table. When the store-after-key\n   parameter is set to ON, the record is inserted as soon you have entered a\n   new value for (one of) the key field(s). If it is set to OFF, you need to\n   enter new data for another field in the record before Concept inserts the\n   record in the table. This enables you also to specify new values for all\n   fields that are part of a group key before the actual record is stored. By\n   default, store-after-key is set to OFF.\n\n   Verify\n\n   This property is used to ensure that only rows that meet certain criteria\n   are inserted/updated in the database.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0                    Description\n                        Any legal 4GL expression returning a logical value,\n   <logical expression> which must be TRUE for the row to be inserted or\n                        modified. If FALSE is returned, the update is\n                        refused.\n   <alpha expression>   A message to be displayed to the user if the\n                        insert/update condition is not satisfied.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   verify could be written as:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   on\xc2\xa0@INSERT\n\n   \xc2\xa0if\xc2\xa0(NOT\xc2\xa0<logicalExpression>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0error(<textExpression>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0endif\n\n   endon\n\n   on\xc2\xa0@UPDATE\n\n   \xc2\xa0if\xc2\xa0(NOT\xc2\xa0<logicalExpression>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0error(<textExpression>)\n\n   \xc2\xa0endif\n\n   endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   On ... endon\n\n   Defines procedures to be connected to events. See general section [119]on\n   for details.\n\n   Declarations to be used on join tables only\n\n   Join-type\n\n   Defines the relational type of [120]join to be executed. An inner join\n   will deselect any owner rows not having a match in the joined table. Outer\n   and dynamic joins will fill the columns in the joined table with empty\n   values if the joined row does not exist.\n\n   Inner and outer joins will be done by the database server whenever\n   possible (if the actual DBMS supports this join) while the dynamic join\n   will always be executed in the application. With dynamic joins it is\n   possible to calculate the key value to be column(s) in the main table.\n\n   Use of inner and outer join will achieve faster execution in reports\n   (applications defined with xtra=), but may result in poorer response in\n   ONLINE applications. This is especially the case when the main table is\n   large (more than 10000 rows).\n\n   We recommend that all joins in a report should be defined as inner or\n   outer, and in ONLINE applications as dynamic.\n\n   Key-column\n\n   The column name of the table key. Should be used if the column has a\n   different name than key-field.\n\n   Match\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value    Description\n   EXACT    will look for the indicated row. This is the default.\n   BACKWARD means that if the row is not found, the row before or equal to\n            the specified key-field value is returned.\n   FORWARD  means that if the row is not found, the row after or equal to the\n            specified key-field value is returned.\n\n   Key-field\n\n   The name of the field in the main table from which the key value is\n   retrieved. Default is the same as the field where the JOIN is located.\n\n   Note:\n\n   For inner joins, the key-field (or all members of the key-field) declared\n   in the joined table must all belong to the main table or be of type\n   [121]static.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Declarations to be used on main tables only\n\n   Automatic-fetch\n\n   This property is only allowed on member tables and specifies whether or\n   not the row(s) of this member table are to be retrieved automatically when\n   the owner is fetched. If set to OFF the row(s) of the table will be\n   cleared before the owner is fetched. Thus allowing the programmer to\n   program fetching of the row(s) of the member as a table function on the\n   owner. This is especially useful in online screens where a tab form is\n   used to show several different member tables (on different tabs), and one\n   would like to avoid fetching of other tables than the one shown at the\n   current tab.\n\n   Please note that the owner table must be declared with automatic-show(ON).\n\n   Automatic-show\n\n   This property allows the user to specify if member rows are to be\n   retrieved automatically. It is to be used on the owner table.\n\n   Sql-group-by\n\n   The <textExpression> is evaluated when any of the database operations\n   [122]first, [123]last or [124]find  is executed, and the resulting text is\n   used as the "group by" clause of the SQL statement implementing the\n   operation.\n\n   A set of macros are available to ease the task of writing syntactically\n   correct SQL statements, see [125]SQL expressions.\n\n   The sql-group-by property only applies to SQL databases.\n\n   Sql-order-by\n\n   The <textExpression> is evaluated when any of the database operations\n   [126]first or [127]last is executed, and the resulting text is used as the\n   "order by" clause of the SQL statement implementing the operation.\n\n   This property takes priority over the standard sorting mechanism defined\n   by the SORT table declaration. This, in turn, removes the difference\n   between the two database operations FIRST and LAST, because their\n   implementation requires the standard sorting mechanism to be used. This\n   also means that the result of changing the scroll direction is\n   unpredictable when using this declaration.\n\n   A set of macros are available to ease the task of writing syntactically\n   correct SQL statements, see [128]SQL expressions.\n\n   Note: Take care if using sql-order-by in ONLINE applications. This is\n   caused by the fact that it is not possible for Concept to generate a\n   correct statement for finding previous/next record without any knowledge\n   about the order-by clause.\n\n   The sql-order-by property only applies to SQL databases.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the syntax table=<table> is used, the table is connected to the\n   current database which has been set with the most recent data-base\n   declaration. If the syntax table=<database>.<table> is used, the table\n   name is explicitly linked to <database>.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The specified table name will apply to all subsequent fields until a new\n   table name is specified or is overruled locally by the <table>.<field>\n   notation.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Tables without following field declarations will also be \'opened\' in the\n   database. This can be utilized to open tables indirectly referred to by\n   for example set definitions (SIBAS) or specials.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The table name must be unique within the application. If two tables have\n   the same names, one of them must be renamed using the db-table\n   declaration. Note: The same table declaration can appear several times,\n   but the fields then all belong to this same table.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Some database interfaces has special requirement for cross database SQL\n   macros/operations. See the Advanced Topic for your interface in Operation\n   Guide for further details.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   With a DBMS not supporting inner and outer join, Concept will simulate\n   this operation, but there will be no performance improvements.\n\n   sql-where, sql-order-by and sql-group-by are specific for SQL databases.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [129][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Components\xc2\xa0>                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       Field Component                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The field component defines a new field. A field is an object having the\n   capability to hold a value like a text string or a number, and a function\n   chain. The value is often associated with a database column to which the\n   field is connected. The value may be shown on screen or in a report output\n   through [5]element(s) connected to the field. The function chain is\n   executed in various ways, e.g. through the [6]execute function.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   [(]\xc2\xa0field=[[7]Table.][8]?[9]Field\xc2\xa0[)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[10]alternative-key\n\n   \xc2\xa0[11]auto-increment-column\n\n   \xc2\xa0[12]automatic-return\n\n   \xc2\xa0[13]background(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]background\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[16]bitmap(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]image\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[19]callback(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]Application\xc2\xa0[,[22]export([23]?[24]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,[25]?[26]textExpression})]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[27]cells(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]cellParam\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]cellParam}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[32]changelistener-for(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,[35]?[36]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[37]colour(\xc2\xa0[38]?[39]colour\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[40]column-name(\xc2\xa0[41]?[42]columnName\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]columnName}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[45]consists-of(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]applicationField\xc2\xa0{[48]?[49]consistOfSeparator\xc2\xa0[50]?[51]applicationField}\xc2\xa0;\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[52]default-value(\xc2\xa0[53]?[54]expression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[55]display(\xc2\xa0[56]?[57]displayCode\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[58]font(\xc2\xa0[59]?[60]font\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[61]frame(\xc2\xa0[62]?[63]frame\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[64]global(\xc2\xa0[[65]?[66]storage]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[67]group-by(\xc2\xa0[68]rows(\xc2\xa0[69]?[70]sortCriteria\xc2\xa0),\xc2\xa0[71]columns(\xc2\xa0[72]?[73]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[74]?[75]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[76]hot-key(\xc2\xa0[77]?[78]functionKey\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[79]information(\xc2\xa0[80]?[81]textExpression\xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[82]line(\xc2\xa0[83]?[84]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[85]initial-value(\xc2\xa0[86]?[87]expression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[88]input-error(\xc2\xa0[89]?[90]inputErrorParam\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[91]input-timeout(\xc2\xa0[92]?[93]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[94]labels(\xc2\xa0[95]?[96]labelsParam\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]labelsParam}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[99]letter-type(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]letterType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[102]local(\xc2\xa0[[103]?[104]storage]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[105]lock\n\n   \xc2\xa0[106]log\n\n   \xc2\xa0[107]mandatory\n\n   \xc2\xa0[108]on(\xc2\xa0[109]?[110]functionKeyOrEvent\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0{[111]?[112]anyFunction}\xc2\xa0[113]endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0[114]popup(\xc2\xa0[115]?[116]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[117]purpose(\xc2\xa0[118]?[119]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[120]query(\xc2\xa0[121]?[122]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[123]range(\xc2\xa0[124]?[125]expression\xc2\xa0(:\xc2\xa0[126]?[127]expression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[128]reset-on-input(\xc2\xa0[129]?[130]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[131]selection-type(\xc2\xa0[132]?[133]selectionType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[134]separator(\xc2\xa0[135]?[136]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[137]show(\xc2\xa0[138]?[139]onOff\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[140]size(\xc2\xa0[141]?[142]unsignedInteger,\xc2\xa0[143]?[144]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[145]sql-column(\xc2\xa0[146]?[147]textConstant\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[148]static(\xc2\xa0[[149]?[150]storage]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[151]style(\xc2\xa0[152]?[153]styleName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[154]storage(\xc2\xa0[155]?[156]storage\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[157]totals(\xc2\xa0[158]?[159]totalsParam\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[160]?[161]totalsParam}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[162]type(\xc2\xa0[163]?[164]elementType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[165]values(\xc2\xa0[166]?[167]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Keywords\n\n   Table\n\n   By default, a field which is not defined as static or global, is owned by\n   the current table (set by the most resent [168]table[****]declaration).\n   Using the <Table>.  syntax, the field is owned by the given table instead\n   of the current table.\n\n   Field\n\n   This is the name of the field. A field name must not start with the\n   character \' \' (space) and must not contain the character \'"\' (double\n   quote), and may otherwise contain any character. If the space character or\n   single quote (\xef\xbf\xbd) character is used within a field name, or the field name\n   begins with a digit, the name must be enclosed in double quotes ("). The\n   name must not be more than 64 characters long. There may only be one field\n   with the given name within the application file.\n\n   If the field is owned by a table and the column declaration is not used,\n   the field is connected to a column with the same name as the field. The\n   column connection means that the field will receive the value of the\n   column when a table row is fetched, and that the column will be changed\n   according to changes in the field value.\n\n   If the application uses the start-form - end-form syntax to define\n   [169]form layout, brackets enclosing the field declaration is used to\n   declare that the field is not to appear in the form, otherwise the field\n   will appear in the corresponding field position (normally designated by\n   the lead-in ^ character).\n\n   Alternative-key\n\n   This property is only valid on fields connected to a database column, and\n   it declares the field to be an alternative key field. This means that the\n   application user when using the built in search functionality may select\n   this field as the main selection and sort field, as an alternative to the\n   main key field (defined with the key declaration). On none SQL databases,\n   the column to which the alternative key field is connected, must be\n   indexed.\n\n   Auto-increment-column\n\n   This property is only valid on fields connected to a database column.\n   Fields with this property are expected to have their value assigned by the\n   underlying DBMS and will not be a subject of change in insert and update\n   clauses. See the chapter on [170]Using auto increment columns for more\n   details.\n\n   Automatic-return\n\n   On data entry in an element connected to this field, the user does not\n   have to press the return or enter key to terminate field input as long as\n   the last position of the field is given a value. This functionality is\n   normally only used in fields where the user is expected to always give a\n   value to all positions of the field (e.g. a bank account number), and it\n   is often combined with the reset-on-input declaration.\n\n   Background\n\n   The background property is only to be used in applications using the\n   start-form - end-form syntax to define [171]form layout. It defines the\n   initial background of the element connected to the field. See style\n   attribute [172]background for a description of the syntax of <background>.\n\n   Note: Use the [173]change function to change the background at run time.\n\n   Bitmap\n\n   The bitmap property is only to be used in applications using the\n   start-form - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines images to\n   be used by the element connected to the field. The element must be of type\n   push-button, default-button or image. See style attribute [174]background\n   for a description of the syntax of <bitmap>.\n\n   Callback\n\n   Valid for fields connected to a [175]callback element only. See the\n   [176]callback documentation for details.\n\n   Cells\n\n   Valid for matrix fields only. See section [177]matrix for details.\n\n   Changelistener-for\n\n   The changelistener-for property is used to define a set of application\n   fields which can indirectly trigger the field\'s functions. Indirect\n   triggering occurs when the functions of a field in the set are executed\n   (e.g through an execute, compute or by input). Using changelistener-for is\n   equivalent to putting an execute(<Field>) at the end of the function chain\n   on each of the fields in the set.\n\n   Events triggered but not trapped on a field in the set can be trapped on\n   the changelistener-for field (except for special listview, treeview and\n   list-box events).\n\n   Changelistener-for fields may be specified with a storage code.\n\n   Colour\n\n   The colour property is only to be used in applications using the\n   start-form - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines the initial\n   colour of the element connected to the field. The syntax of the <colour>\n   parameter is\n\n   <colour> ::= <foreground> on <background>\n\n   where the syntax of <foreground> is the same as that defined for the\n   [178]colour style attribute, and the syntax of <background> is the same as\n   that defined for the [179]background style attribute.\n\n   Note: Use the [180]change function to change the colour at run time.\n\n   Column-name\n\n   Defines the field to be connected to the given database column(s). The\n   columns referred must exist in the table owning the field. More than one\n   <column> parameter is only to be used if the field is a group field and\n   there exist no corresponding composite column/index in the table. Then\n   each group member field must be connected to a corresponding database\n   column.\n\n   The multiple column connection is only supported by SQL databases.\n\n   A blank column name (" ") is equivalent to declaring the field as local.\n\n   It is not necessary to use this declaration to connect a field to a column\n   if the name of the field is the same as the name of the column, and the\n   multiple column connection is not needed.\n\n   Consists-of\n\n   The consists-of property is used to define a group field consisting of the\n   member fields listed in the property. The member field separator is\n   normally a comma, but in [181]ONLINE applications one of the commas may be\n   replaced by a semicolon, or a semicolon may be added after the last member\n   field, to gain a special effect further described below.\n\n   There are several reasons why defining a group field may be useful or\n   required:\n\n   \xc2\xb7To utilize a composite column/index as a table key, a group field must be\n   defined, connected to the composite column/index, and defined as main key\n   or alternative key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7On SQL databases, a group field connected to individual columns and\n   defined as main key or alternative key, will give the same functionality,\n   although not the same speed, as if there was a corresponding composite\n   column/index defined.\n\n   \xc2\xb7To make a one-to-many relation between two tables A and B, a group field\n   must be defined on table B, having some member fields from table A.\n\n   \xc2\xb7To split the value of an ordinary (none composite) database column into\n   several fields. E.g. the first and second half of an alphanumeric(20)\n   database column may be accessed through two alphanumeric(10) fields if the\n   two fields are used as member fields in a group field connected to the\n   database column.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In ONLINE, navigating out of the group field (moving the cursor from a\n   member field to a non-member field or out of the last member field), the\n   functions on the group field are executed if the following conditions are\n   met: at least one member field has been changed and the semicolon\n   separator is not used in the member field list or all changed member\n   fields appear to the right of the semicolon separator in the member field\n   list.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In ONLINE, a radio group field is defined using this declaration\n   referring to fields connected to by radio-button elements, combined with a\n   values declaration. The field must not be a connected to a composite\n   column/index, but rather have a storage type capable of holding the values\n   of the value list.\n\n   Default-value\n\n   Defines a default value for the field. The declaration is a macro\n   generating the code\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   on\xc2\xa0DEFAULT\n\n   \xc2\xa0compute(<field>\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0<expression>)\n\n   endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   where\xc2\xa0<field>\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0name\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0current\xc2\xa0field.\n\n   Display\n\n   To define how the value of the field is to be shown in the element\n   connected to it, specify the display property on the [182]element. If this\n   property is not specified, the display code on the field is being used\n   (the syntax of display codes are defined in section [183]display codes).\n   If the property on the field is not used either, and the field is\n   connected to a database column, the display code is read from the data\n   dictionary by the compiler. As a last option, the default display code\n   associated with each storage code is used.\n\n   Note: Display codes may also be defined within a start-form - end-form\n   definition.\n\n   The table below shows the default display codes:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Storage code        Default display code\n   ALPHANUMERIC(n)     X(n)\n   BIT                 9\n   INTEGER1            ZZ9\n   INTEGER2            ZZZZ9\n   INTEGER4            Z(9)9\n   DATETIME            DD/MM/YYYY HH\':\'MM\':\'SS\n   DATE                DD/MM/YYYY\n   TIME                HH\':\'MM\':\'SS\n   PACKED DECIMAL(n,m) Z(n-1)9.9(m)\n   UNPACKED DECIMAL    Z(n-1)9.9(m)\n   REAL4               -9.9(6)E-99\n   REAL8               -9.9(15)E-99\n\n   Font\n\n   The font property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines the initial font of\n   the element connected to the field. See style attribute [184]font for a\n   description of the syntax of <font>.\n\n   Note: Use the [185]change function to change the font at run time.\n\n   Frame\n\n   The frame property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define [186]form layout. It defines the initial frame\n   of the element connected to the field. See style attribute [187]frame for\n   a description of the syntax of <frame>.\n\n   Note: Use the [188]change function to change the frame at run time.\n\n   Global\n\n   Defines the field to be global. The name, storage length and value of a\n   global field is kept in an area common to all applications started in the\n   current thread. Thus, referring the same global field (identified by name)\n   from different applications will refer the same field value.\n\n   All global values defined in a thread are automatically copied to new\n   threads started from this thread. Later changes to the values in the\n   starting thread are not propagated to other threads. [189]System fields\n   can be used to share field values among application threads.\n\n   Warning: It is not possible to have two global fields with the same name,\n   but different storage lengths. If such a situation occurs, no message is\n   given and the new definition quietly replaces the old one.\n\n   Group-by\n\n   Valid for matrix fields only. See section [190]matrix for details.\n\n   Hot-key\n\n   Defines a function key to be the hot key of the field. Hot keys are used\n   to trig the execution of field functions independent of in which field the\n   cursor is located.\n\n   Definitions of hot keys are prioritized before on function key\n   definitions.\n\n   There may be only one hot key defined per field, and there may be only one\n   hot key definition for a given function key per application.\n\n   Information\n\n   Defines a text which will be written to the given message line when the\n   user navigates the cursor into an element connected to the field.\n\n   The declaration is a macro generating the code\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   on\xc2\xa0@CURSOR-IN\n\n   \xc2\xa0message(<alpha\xc2\xa0expression>,\xc2\xa0line(<numeric\xc2\xa0expr>))\n\n   endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The\xc2\xa0syntax\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0line\xc2\xa0parameter\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0same\xc2\xa0as\xc2\xa0that\xc2\xa0for\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0[191]message\xc2\xa0function.\xc2\xa0The\xc2\xa0default\xc2\xa0value\xc2\xa0for\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0line\xc2\xa0parameter\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa02.\n\n   Initial-value\n\n   This property is used to assign an initial value to a field. The time of\n   assignment depends on the scope of the field:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field is static, the initial value is assigned and field functions\n   executed before the event [192]@START is trigged.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field is owned by a table and is a part of the main key field, the\n   initial value is assigned when moving the cursor into an empty row.\n   Functions are not executed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field is owned by a table and is not part of the main key field,\n   the initial value is assigned after a new key value is given and it is\n   established that the row does not already exist in the database. Functions\n   are not executed.\n\n   Example:\n\n   data-base="ORDBASE"\n\n   table="ORDLINE"\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="ORDERNO"\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="PARTNO"\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0join-key(table="PART")\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="PART"."PARTPRICE"\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="ORDPART"\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0consists-of("ORDERNO","PARTNO")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0key\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="ORDPRICE" \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0initial-value("PARTPRICE")\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This example demonstrates how to extract the initial value from a joined\n   record. The initial-value is located on a field which is not part of the\n   key, so "ORDPRICE" will therefore be initiated as soon as a key value of a\n   non-existing row is entered into the key field. Since the join is executed\n   before the key function, the field "PARTPRICE" will be correct when the\n   initial-value declaration is evaluated.\n\n   Input-error\n\n   Defines the handling of error conditions occurring after user input in the\n   field. Error conditions can occur in several ways, for example if an\n   [193]error function is executed or a [194]join function with parameter\n   abort-on-error=on is executed and fails. Legal options are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ASK-FOR-NEW-VALUE\n\n   This is the default handling: A dialogue box appears describing the error\n   condition (if such a message exists) and asks the user to give a new (and\n   correct) value. If a new value is given, the value is copied into the\n   field and field functions are executed as if the value had been entered\n   directly into the field. If input is aborted, as an attempt to reestablish\n   a non-erroneous condition, the old field value is copied into the field\n   before field functions are executed.\n\n   This option is only suitable if it is possible for the user to correct the\n   error by entering a new value. Also note that the dialogue used to ask the\n   user for a new value does not allow the user to use the function keys\n   available in the original field.\n\n   COMPUTE-OLD-VALUE\n\n   If a message describing the error condition exists, it is shown in a\n   dialogue box. As an attempt to reestablish a non-erroneous condition, the\n   old field value is copied into the field before the field functions are\n   executed.\n\n   If the ASK-FOR-NEW-VALUE option may not be used, this option should be\n   preferred unless the execution of field functions after the old field\n   value is copied into the field has undesirable side effects.\n\n   ASSIGN-OLD-VALUE\n\n   If a message describing the error condition exists, it is shown in a\n   dialogue box. The old field values of all fields affected by the erroneous\n   input are then copied into their respective fields, but field functions\n   are not executed.\n\n   Warning: This option should be used with care, as it may result in\n   inconsistency. The functions of the field are executed with different\n   field values before and after the error condition occurred.\n\n   Input-timeout\n\n   Specifies an input time-out value in tenths of a second. The time-out\n   value is evaluated each time the field is entered.\n\n   If the time-out value is larger than zero, the time-out functionality is\n   activated when the user changes the value of the field. If the time-out\n   value is less than zero, it is activated when the user enters the field.\n   If the time-out value is zero, input time-out is turned off.\n\n   An input time-out event ends the input loop, executes the field\'s\n   functions (if the field value has been changed) and then triggers the\n   [195]@INPUT-TIMEOUT event.\n\n   When the time-out functionality is activated any mouse or keyboard input\n   will reset the timeout period.\n\n   Key\n\n   This property is both a declaration and a function. It defines that the\n   field is to be the main key of the table (and may thus only be used on\n   fields owned by a table). The definition of a main key and the syntax of\n   the keyword is fully defined in the [196]key function section.\n\n   Labels\n\n   Valid for matrix fields only. See section [197]matrix for details.\n\n   Letter-type\n\n   Defines case conversion for alphanumeric fields. The parameter may take on\n   one of the following four values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Letter type Description/Sample\n   UPPERCASE   "ALL CHARACTERS IN UPPER CASE"\n   LOWERCASE   "all characters in lower case"\n   TEXTCASE    "First letter is upper case, the rest lower case"\n   NAMECASE    "First Character Of Each "Word" In Upper Case"\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Case conversion takes place on user input and assignment to the field. In\n   XTRA applications, case conversion also takes place on display (printing)\n   of the field value.\n\n   This declaration is often used on key fields to ensure that they are\n   stored in a consistent manner. This is necessary to ensure that queries\n   and lookups are successful.\n\n   Local\n\n   Defines the field as belonging to the current table and may therefore only\n   be used on fields defined after a table definition. A local field is\n   treated the same way as a field connected to a database column, except\n   that when a new row is fetched its value will be cleared.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Defines that it should not be legal for the user to move the cursor into\n   an element connected to this field. Legal values are ON or OFF (the\n   default). See the chapter on [198]locking for more details.\n\n   Log\n\n   This property may only be used on fields connected to a database column,\n   and it defines that modifications to the field value should be registered\n   (logged) in the Log Database. See section [199]logging for more details.\n\n   Mandatory\n\n   This declaration may only be used on fields owned by a table, and it\n   defines that before the user is allowed to insert a new row, the field\n   must be given a value, (but the value may be space or zero).\n\n   The declaration may not be used on main key fields.\n\n   On ... endon\n\n   Declares functions to be executed as a result of an event or function key\n   given by the user. See section [200]on for further details.\n\n   Popup\n\n   Defines a popup menu for the field. When the right mouse button is pressed\n   in a field having this declaration, the following happens:\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field pointed to is not the current field, it is made current,\n   i.e. the cursor is moved to the field and the appropriate cursor movement\n   events are fired.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The <alpha expression> parameter of the popup declaration is evaluated,\n   and if it identifies a valid menu, the menu is shown and the user is\n   allowed to make a selection.\n\n   \xc2\xb7\n\n   On fields connected to [201]HEADER elements the popup parameter can be\n   empty (\'popup()\') to force Concept to show the default grid header popup\n   menu.\n\n   Purpose\n\n   Defines a help text for the field. For fields connected to a database\n   column, this purpose text replaces (overrides) any purpose text defined in\n   the data dictionary.\n\n   The user may see the purpose text in a Help Window by pressing the\n   HELPFIELD function key.\n\n   The syntax of the expression is the same as that defined for the text\n   parameter of the [202]dialog-box function.\n\n   Query\n\n   Defines whether the field can be used as search criteria in the [203]QUERY\n   event or not. The default is ON.\n\n   Range\n\n   This property is only to be used on main or alternative key fields, and it\n   defines a range of legal key values. When querying the table, only rows\n   with a key value within the defined range will be selected, and it will\n   only be possible to insert rows with a key value within the defined range.\n\n   On SQL databases, more advanced selection criteria\xef\xbf\xbds may be defined using\n   the [204]sql-where table declaration. For all DBMS\xef\xbf\xbds, the [205]select\n   table function may be used for the same purpose, but be aware of the\n   potential performance penalties associated with that function.\n\n   Reset-on-input\n\n   Defines whether or not the current field value should be cleared as soon\n   as the user starts inputting a new value. The default is ON for numeric\n   fields and OFF for other fields.\n\n   Selection-type\n\n   Default : VALUE\n\n   The field contains a list of the selected values (VALUE) or indexes\n   (INDEX) of the selected items of a\n   drop-down-list-box/drop-down-combo-box/list-box. The values or indexes are\n   separated by the character specified by the separator parameter. This\n   parameter should only be used on fields connected to elements of the\n   following types : drop-down-list-box/drop-down-combo-box/list-box. Indexes\n   start with 1.\n\n   Separator\n\n   This declaration is only to be used in connection with the value\n   declaration, and it defines the character used as a value list separator.\n   The default separator is semicolon (;).\n\n   Show\n\n   The show property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines whether or not the\n   element connected to the field is initially shown in the form it is\n   defined.\n\n   Size\n\n   The size property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define [206]form layout. It defines the size of the\n   element generated for the field.\n\n   For the [207]drop-down-list-box and [208]drop-down-combo-box element type\n   the <lines> parameter defines the "dropped down" height.\n\n   For all list box element types, to maintain backward compatibility, the\n   given sizes are adjusted with frame width and height.\n\n   Sql-Column\n\n   An [209]SQL expression which is used in the list of columns fetched from\n   the table and must therefore conform with the rules for select lists in\n   SQL. SQL columns may be used to retrieve calculated values, aggregate\n   values, results of sub-selects etc.\n\n   A set of macros is available to ease the task of writing correct and\n   portable [210]SQL expressions.\n\n   The sql-column property can only be used with SQL databases.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Limitations: any @value() or other expressions must be valid when the\n   application is loaded. This means that static/local fields within the\n   application will not have value when application is loaded.\n\n   If application "ApplA:SubApplA" do call(\'AppllA:SubAppllB\'), then static()\n   fields from SubApplA may be used in @value().\n\n   Static\n\n   A field not owned by a database table is called static. This is by default\n   the case if there is no current table at the point where the field is\n   define, even if the [211]local declaration is defined on the field.\n   However, if a current table is defined, this declaration must be used to\n   explicitly define the field as static.\n\n   [212]Global fields are treated as static fields that are initialized with\n   the value stored in the global storage area.\n\n   Note: It is not possible to have static fields within a repeat area.\n\n   Storage\n\n   This property should only be used on fields not connected to a database\n   column, and it defines the [213]storage type of the field. For fields\n   connected to a database [214]column, the storage type of the field is\n   determined by the connected database column, and overruling this (by this\n   declaration) should normally not be done.\n\n   When specifying the name of a field in the application, the storage code\n   from the given field is used. Note: The field name must be enclosed in\n   double quotes.\n\n   See also the COLUMN storage code in the [215]Storage Codes documentation.\n\n   Style\n\n   The style property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines the initial [216]style\n   of the element connected to the field.\n\n   Totals\n\n   Valid for matrix fields only. See section [217]matrix for details.\n\n   Type\n\n   The type property is only to be used in applications using the start-form\n   - end-form syntax to define form layout. It defines the type of the\n   element generated for the field.\n\n   See the type [218]element declaration for further details.\n\n   For backward compatibility, the a matrix field may be defined by the\n   declaration\n\n   type(matrix)\n\n   but the new storage type [219]matrix is preferred.\n\n   Also, for backward compatibility, a radio group field may be defined by\n   the declaration\n\n   type(radio-group)\n\n   but the implicit definition through defining a storage code for a group\n   field is preferred.\n\n   Values\n\n   Defines the fields value list. A value list is a text string containing a\n   set of values separated with the value list separator (defined by the\n   separator declaration). The value list is not to be confused with the\n   fields value, but it is used in various situations to establish the fields\n   value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7If there is an element of any list box type connected to the field, the\n   value list defines the possible selections which can be made in the list\n   box.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the field is a radio group, i.e. a field with a storage type and a\n   consist-of declaration (possibly referring to fields which are connected\n   to by radio-button elements), the value list is used to determine which\n   radio group member is "turned on" , and which are not.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If there is an element of check-box type connected to the field, the\n   value list defines the values to be associated with the ON and OFF state\n   of the check-box. The first value is the ON value, the second value is the\n   OFF value. A value different from the ON value is treated as the OFF\n   value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The value list (and value list separator) of a field may be changed at run\n   time by the [220]change function, and the string [221]operator is suitable\n   for manipulating value list type strings.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   2.
