b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Assignment        side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         ACCUMULATE()                                    side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function is used to accumulate the value of one field (source) into\n   another field (destination)\n\n   Syntax\n\n   accumulate(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]fieldName\xc2\xa0into\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Source Field\n\n   A field name defined in the current application. The name may NOT be post\n   fixed. The default value of <Source field> is the current field.\n\n   Destination Field\n\n   A field name defined in the current application. The name may NOT be post\n   fixed.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7XTRA: Accumulate(A into B) is equivalent to compute(B=B+A), i.e. the\n   value of A is added to the value of B.\n\n   \xc2\xb7ONLINE: Accumulate(A into B) is equivalent to compute(B=B+ A - old(A)),\n   i.e. the difference between the old and the new value of A is added to B.\n   Example:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0accumulate("B")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0field="B"\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0Assuming A=12, B=10 and A receives the new value 17, then B will\n   get the new value 15 like this:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0NewValueB = OldValueB+(NewValueA - OldValueA) = 10+(17-12)=15\n\n   \xc2\xb7ONLINE: When a row is deleted, all accumulate functions located on the\n   table it belongs to will be executed in reverse, which means that the\n   value of the source field is subtracted from the destination field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note: For this to work correctly, the accumulate function should not be\n   conditioned using [9]if or [10]loop.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [11][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_assign.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_accumulate.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm#idh_ma_accumulate_source\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm#idh_ma_accumulate_destination\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_if.htm\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_loop.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_accumulate.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Assignment        side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           ASSIGN()                                      side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function is used to evaluate an expression and store the result in a\n   field. Unlike the [5]compute function, the <Destination field> will not be\n   executed.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   assign(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]<Destination\xc2\xa0field>\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]<Expression>\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Destination field\n\n   A field where the result of the expression evaluation is stored. The field\n   name may be post fixed.\n\n   Expression\n\n   Any legal 4GL expression that results in a text or numeric value\n   corresponding to the destination field type.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7This function is identical to the [10]compute function with the exception\n   that the destination field\'s functions are not executed after the value\n   has been stored.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to assign a text to a numeric field provided the text\n   value contains nothing but numeric characters and the value is within the\n   field\'s legal range.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to assign a numeric value to a text field provided the\n   text field is wide enough to hold all digits in the value. The value will\n   be left justified (trailing spaces) in the text field. Note: It is\n   possible to use operators like FORMAT and NUMBER to control the conversion\n   between text and numbers.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The following statements are equivalent:\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0compute("B"="A"+"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0assign("B"="A"+"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0execute("B")\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [11][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_buffer_read.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_assign.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compute.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_assign.htm#idh_ma_assign_destfield\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_expression.htm#idh_la_pop_expression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_assign.htm#idh_ma_assign_expression\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compute.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_assign.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Assignment        side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        BUFFER-READ()                                    side\n\n   This function makes it possible to extract CSV, ASCII-DATA and ASCII-FIELD\n   formatted data from a string.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   buffer-read(\xc2\xa0[4]text(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]textExpression)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0,[7]fields(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]csv-separators(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]formatting(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]separator(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]textExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]status(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]fieldName)]\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Csv-separators\n\n   This parameter applies to formatting=csv only, and is used to override the\n   default CSV separators defined by the corresponding uqconfig system\n   command. The parameter must evaluate to a comma separated list of\n   separator characters in the following sequence:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <main>,<alpha>,<numeric>,<escape>,<decimal>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A separator is defined using any of the following syntax\'s:\n\n   \xc2\xb7A single non-numeric character except the characters comma, single quote\n   and double quote.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A single character enclosed in single or double quotes.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A sequence of numeric characters giving the UCS value of the separator.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The text TAB indicating the tab character (UCS value 9).\n\n   \xc2\xb7The text NONE indicating that no separator should be used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7An empty definition indicating the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The meaning and default values of the separators are defined as follows.\n\n   <main> is the character separating fields within a record. The <main>\n   character can not be set to none. The default value is language dependent,\n   but usually \',\' (comma).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <alpha> is the character put before and after a character field. This may\n   be NONE. The default value is \'"\' (double quote).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <numeric> is a character put before and after a numeric field. This may be\n   NONE, which is also the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <escape> is a character used to indicate that the next character is part\n   of a field, and should not be treated as a special character, i.e.\n   separator or delimiters. The <escape> character can not be set to the same\n   as any of the other separators. If set to NONE, no characters in the field\n   value may be the same as a separator. NONE is the default value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <decimal> defines the character used to indicate the decimal point. The\n   default value is language dependent, but usually \'.\' (dot). Note that when\n   the decimal point is set by the decimal-point parameter (in the uqconfig\n   file) to comma, then the default <decimal> CSV separator is automatically\n   changed to semicolon.\n\n   Fields\n\n   The text expression should evaluate to a list of fields in the\n   application. Each element in the list must be delimited by the character\n   defined by the [22]separator parameter. The sequence defines the order in\n   which data is extracted from the value of the [23]text parameter (See the\n   [24]include-fields parameter for the [25]Stream component).\n\n   Formatting\n\n   Value        Description\n   ASCII-DATA   A textual file with a fixed record length and layout defined\n                by the display codes of the fields included on the stream.\n   ASCII-FIELDS A textual file with a comma separated list of the fields\n                included on the stream.\n                A textual file with a list of the fields specified by the\n   CSV          [26]fields parameter, where each field is separated or\n                enclosed according to a set of CSV separators. See the\n                [27]csv-separator parameter.\n\n   Text\n\n   The string from which data is to be extracted.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Expression defining a single character used as separator in the [28]fields\n   list. Default value is \';\' (semicolon).\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible error codes (see [29]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                      Description\n   $OK \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 Success.\n   $UE_FORMAT                  An illegal format was specified for the\n                               [30]formatting parameter.\n   $UE_CONNECT                 An illegal field name was found in the\n                               [31]fields parameter\n                               An illegal field was specified in the\n                               [32]fields parameter. Fields defined as an\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_FIELD           sql-column, group or fields defined outside\n                               the current sub application can not be\n                               specified.\n   $UE_OVERFLOW                Too many fields defined in the [33]fields\n                               parameter.\n                               No fields defined in the [34]fields parameter\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR             or an empty element specified in the\n                               [35]fields parameter\n                               CSV/ASCII-FIELDS element not properly ended.\n                               This is probably caused by a line break inside\n   $UE_EOL                     a CSV/ASCII-FIELDS element. Keep a copy of the\n                               current buffer and concatenate with the next\n                               buffer read from the source and then retry the\n                               operation.\n\n   Notes\n\n   \xc2\xb7The buffer-read function will trigger the [36]@READ-ERROR event if any\n   error occurs when extracting data.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Assignment        side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          COMPUTE()                                      side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function is used to evaluate a numeric or text expression, store the\n   result in a field and execute the field\'s functions.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   compute(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]destinationField\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]expression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Destination field\n\n   The name of a field defined in the current application. The [9]field will\n   receive the result of the computation. The rules are the same as those\n   referring to a field in expressions.\n\n   It is possible to assign a value to a part of an alphanumeric field using\n   substring notation. An element in an array may be assigned a value using\n   the normal array notations. A field in a specific repeat line may be\n   addressed using the # operator on the destination field.\n\n   Expression\n\n   Any legal 4GL [10]expression that results in a text or numeric value\n   corresponding to the destination field type.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Text can be assigned to a numeric field provided the text value contains\n   nothing but numeric characters and the value is within the legal range of\n   the field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is possible to assign a numeric value to a text field provided the\n   text field is wide enough to hold all digits in the value. The value will\n   be left-justified (trailing spaces) in the text field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Use [11]operators like FORMAT and NUMBER to control the conversion\n   between text and numbers.\n\n   \xc2\xb7After a successful computation, the functions on the destination field\n   will be executed. To avoid unwanted recursion, this is only done, if the\n   destination field is not the field on which the compute function is\n   programmed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Care should be taken not to produce compute statements which generate\n   infinite loops, e.g. like:\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"compute("B"=...)\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="B"compute("A"=...)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7The following definitions are equivalent:\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0compute("B"\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0"A"\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0assign("B"\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0"A"\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0execute("B")\n\n   \xc2\xb7The definition\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0compute("A"\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0"A"\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0will not generate an infinite loop, because it is equivalent to\n\n   \xc2\xa0field="A"\xc2\xa0assign("A"\xc2\xa0=\xc2\xa0"A"\xc2\xa0+\xc2\xa0"C")\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [12][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_buffer_read.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_decrement.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_compute.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compute.htm#idh_ma_compute_destinationfield\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_expression.htm#idh_la_pop_expression\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_compute.htm#idh_ma_compute_expression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_field.htm\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_compute.htm\n'

The\n   null value is used to represent missing or inapplicable information.\n\n   \xc2\xb7SQL allows columns to be created with the NOT NULL restriction. \xc2\xa0,[146]value(\xc2\xa0[147]?[148]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0,[149]position(\xc2\xa0[150]?[151]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n \xc2\xa0[,[158]status(\xc2\xa0[159]?[160]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   Defines the operation to carry out. Legal values are INSERT, DELETE, SORT,\n   LOOKUP, COUNT, UPDATE, CONVERT_TO_ARRAY and CONVERT_FROM_ARRAY.\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of an alphanumeric field defined in the application. For all commands\n   except CONVERT_FROM_ARRAY it defines the field that contains the list\n   value. For command CONVERT_FROM_ARRAY it should define a field defined\n   with storage(A(X) REPEAT n) that is to be converted into a list value.\n\n   Match\n\n   For command DELETE,LOOKUP,MOVE,RELATIVE-MOVE and UPDATE it defines how the\n   value parameter is compared to existing values in the list. If set to\n   CASE-INSENSITIVE the comparison is case insensitive (AB=ab). For these\n   commands CASE-SENSITIVE is the same as EXACT. Default is EXACT.\n\n   For command INSERT and SORT it defines how the list is sorted. If set to\n   EXACT the sort is based on the binary value of each element. If set to\n   CASE-SENSITIVE it is sorted according to the language specific sort order\n   (defined by the uq<language>.uso file). If set to CASE-INSENSITIVE it is\n   sorted according to the case insensitive language specific sort order\n   (defined by the uqnc<language>.uso file). Default is EXACT.\n\n   New-value\n\n   Used with command UPDATE. Defines the new value for the item defined by\n   the value or position parameter.\n\n   New-position\n\n   Used with commands MOVE and RELATIVE-MOVE. Defines the new position for\n   the item defined by the value or position parameter. The following rules\n   are applied:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command       Negative values                       Positive values\n   MOVE          Insert at (n-1) places from back (-1, Absolute position\n                 at the end)\n   RELATIVE-MOVE Move backward n places                Move forward n places.\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of a value in the list. The first element has\n   position 1.\n\n   Result\n\n   Defines either a value or a position as a result of the INSERT, LOOKUP,\n   DELETE and COUNT commands. For the CONVERT_FROM_ARRAY command it defines a\n   field to receive the converted list. For the CONVERT_TO_ARRAY command it\n   should define a field defined with storage(A(X) REPEAT n) that is to\n   receive the values from the list.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Expression defining a single character used as separator in the list.\n   Default value is ';' (semicolon).\n\n   Sort\n\n   Defines sorting order. Legal values are ASCENDING and DESCENDING. When\n   used with command(INSERT), the new element will be inserted correctly into\n   a sorted list.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to 0 if the operation is successful. Possible error\n   values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status Description\n   1      Value or position not found\n   2      Overflow on attempt to insert a new element or when\n          modifying/moving an existing element\n   3      The length of a single element exceeded the length of an array\n          element for command CONVERT_TO_ARRAY.\n   4      The number of elements in the list exceeds the number of possible\n          elements in the array for command CONVERT_TO_ARRAY.\n   5      Illegal field for the field or result parameter.\n   6      Illegal operation.\n   7      Illegal new-position (less than 1)\n\n   Type\n\n   Defines how existing values are handled by the INSERT command. Using\n   UNIQUE ensures that a value is unique in the list. AMBIGUOUS is the\n   default.\n\n   Value\n\n   Defines a single element. The separator is not included.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7All string operations are by default case sensitive. The match(OFF)\n   parameter can be used to turn off this behaviour for some of the commands.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(INSERT) will append the new element specified by value to the end\n   of the list unless sort or position is specified. If sort is specified,\n   value will be inserted into a position that makes the result a sorted\n   list. If result is specified, it will receive the position of the new\n   element. The result value will always be 1 when inserting into a list with\n   no sorting. Status is set to 2 if an overflow occurs (The storage of the\n   list field is to short to receive the new value).\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(DELETE) will delete the element specified either by position or\n   value. If the result parameter is used, the value or position of the\n   deleted element will be returned.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(LOOKUP) will use either position or value, find the corresponding\n   element in field and return the value or position in result. Status is set\n   to 1 if not found.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(COUNT) will return the number of elements in the field in result.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(SORT) will sort field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(UPDATE) will use either position or value, find the corresponding\n   element in field and substitute the elements value by the value given by\n   new-value. Status is set to 1 if not found, or 2 if an overflow occurs.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(CONVERT-TO-ARRAY) will split the list into single values that are\n   inserted into separate array elements in the field defined by the result\n   parameter (The first element goes into the first array element and so on).\n   Status is set to 5 if the result field is not defined with storage(A(<X>)\n   repeat <n>) or 3 if a the length of a single element exceeds the value of\n   <X> or 4 if the number of elements in the list exceeds the value of <n>.\n   If the operation is successful the status is set to a negative value\n   indicating the number of converted values.\n\n   \xc2\xb7command(CONVERT-FROM-ARRAY) will create a list separated by separator of\n   each of the elements in the array. Please note that there is no treatment\n   of the array values, so if an element in the array contains the separator\n   character the list will contain more elements than the array. The list\n   will always contain at least the same amount of elements as the array.\n   Status is set to 5 if the field is not defined with storage(A(<X>) repeat\n   <n>), or 2 if an overflow occurs.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [161][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_nullassign.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. Use this\n   parameter if the value needs to contain trailing white spaces. If this\n   parameter is left out the [30]Value parameter is right trimmed.\n\n   Match\n\n   Must evaluate to either CASE-INSENSITIVE or CASE-SENSITIVE and decides\n   whether letter case is handled when searching for the search pattern in\n   the source text. Default is CASE-INSENSITIVE.\n\n   New-length\n\n   Number of significant characters for the [31]New-value parameter. Use this\n   parameter if the new value needs to contain trailing white spaces. If this\n   parameter is left out the [32]New-value parameter is right trimmed.\n\n   New-Value\n\n   The substitution text.\n\n   Result\n\n   Receives the result text after the substitution. If the result length is\n   larger than the length of the field specified by the result parameter,\n   substitution is carried out, but status $UE_TRUNCATED is returned in the\n   status parameter.\n\n   Status\n\n   Status of the operation. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error codes\n   (see [33]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n                     The field specified by the result parameter was not\n                     large enough for the result of the function and the\n   $UE_TRUNCATED     result text has been truncated. Please note that this is\n                     treated as an OK status, the function chain is not\n                     aborted if the status parameter is not used.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_MATCH The parameter value for the match parameter was illegal.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7By not specifying the result parameter, the function can be used to count\n   number of occurrences of value inside source.\n\n b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Branching         side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          FORLOOP()                                      side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The forloop function is an extension to the [5]loop function and is used\n   to repeat the execution of functions.\n\n   Syntax 2\n\n   forloop(\xc2\xa0[[6]field(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]applicationField\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]from(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]to(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]increment(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]values(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]separator(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   \xc2\xa0[while(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]logicalExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   \xc2\xa0[until(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]logicalExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   \xc2\xa0[[28]escape()]\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   endloop\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Field\n\n   A field name used as iterative control field.\n\n   When the values parameter is not used, the field is set to [29]from, and\n   then the forloop is executed repeatedly until the control field has a\n   value greater (or less, if the value of increment is less than zero) than\n   [30]to. [31]Field is automatically incremented or decremented by the\n   [32]increment parameter value for each iteration.\n\n   When the values parameter is used the control field will receive the list\n   value (by position) according to the [33]from parameter, and then the\n   forloop is executed repeatedly until the the position of the list exceeds\n   the value set in [34]to or the number of elements in the list. The\n   position in the list is automatically incremented or decremented by the\n   [35]increment parameter value for each iteration.\n\n   Increment\n\n   A numeric [36]expression, which controls the increment/decrement of the\n   forloop index for each iteration. Default value is 1.\n\n   From\n\n   A numeric [37]expression, which is the initial value of [38]field or\n   position in values. Default value is 1.\n\n   Separator\n\n   A text expression returning a single character used as a separator between\n   elements in the [39]values list. Default is ';' (semicolon).\n\n   To\n\n   A numeric expression, which is the last value of [40]field. If the\n   [41]increment parameter is positive this value is assumed to be larger\n   than [42]from, if it is negative it is assumed to be less than [43]from.\n   Default and maximum value if the [44]values parameter is given is the\n   number of elements in the values list. The default if the [45]values\n   parameter is omitted is dependant on the value of the [46]increment\n   parameter, $I4_MAX if the increment value is equal or larger than zero,\n   $I4_MIN if the increment value is less than zero.\n\n   Values\n\n   A text expression returning a list of elements separated by the character\n   specified by the [47]separator parameter.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7A forloop structure is executed repeatedly until it is stopped by the\n   control field, or it is stopped through an [48]escape, while or until\n   statement.\n\n   \xc2\xb7endloop acts as a 'Goto beginning of forloop' until the condition for\n   exiting the forloop is fulfilled. Then it acts as a 'Goto first function\n   after forloop'.\n\n   \xc2\xb7[49]escape terminates the forloop unconditionally.\n\n   \xc2\xb7while(<logical expression>) will make the forloop terminate if the\n   condition supplied is false.\n\n   \xc2\xb7until(<logical expression>) will make the forloop terminate if the\n   condition supplied is true.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Nested forloop/loop structures are allowed. Maximum nested levels are\n   specified in the chapter [50]Sizes and Limitations.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Each forloop must have a matching endloop.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The control field can be any storage type, but it is always handled as if\n   it was a numeric integer field, causing a significant decrease in\n   performance if the field is a non-numeric integer field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7All expressions are evaluated at the start of the forloop and the control\n   of the forloop is handled internally, meaning that assignments inside the\n   forloop to the control [51]field, [52]values expression, [53]increment\n   expression or the [54]to expression WILL NOT influence the repeat count of\n   the forloop.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [55][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Branching         side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          GROUP-BY()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function is used to group rows with fields of equal values. It may be\n   used in [5]XTRA applications only.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   group-by(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]Field\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]Field}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   endgroup()\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of field which defines a row group. The field must belong to the\n   source table or stream being scrolled by the surrounding [10]scroll block.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7group-by may only be used from inside a [11]scroll block, and the source\n   of the surrounding scroll block is also the source of the group-by\n   function.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A group-by block scrolls the source the same way a scroll block does, but\n   the scrolling is stopped when a row is read which has a change in one or\n   more of the group defining field values. Thus, functions before the\n   group-by block are executed when the first row of a new row group is\n   found, functions within the group-by block are executed for every row of\n   the row group, and functions after the group-by block are executed after\n   the whole row group is found.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In order for group-by to work properly, the table must be sorted on the\n   group definition field(s). (If this is not the case, scroll the table to a\n   temporary stream, sort it using the [12]order-by function and then scroll\n   and group the sorted stream.)\n\n   \xc2\xb7When nesting group-by blocks, the group definition fields of an outer\n   level must also be used as the first group definition fields of the inner\n   levels.\n\n   \xc2\xb7[13]select statements outside group-by should also be repeated inside the\n   group-by block.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not possible to use the [14]mark and [15]rewind functions within a\n   group-by block.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [16][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_forloop.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_if.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_group_by.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_groupby.htm#idh_ma_groupby_field\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_groupby.htm#idh_ma_groupby_field\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_select.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_mark.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_rewind.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_groupby.htm\n'

There may be any number of elseifs\n\n   \xc2\xb7Nested ifs are allowed. There is no practical limit to how many nested\n   levels may be defined.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [11][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_groupby.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_loop.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_if.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_logicalexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_logicalexpression\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_if.htm#idh_ma_if_logicalexpression\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_logicalexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_logicalexpression\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_if.htm#idh_ma_if_logicalexpression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_if.htm\n'

b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Branching         side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       PROCESS-TABLE()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This process-table() function executes functions for a specified table.\n   This function is available in [5]XTRA only.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   process-table(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]Table\xc2\xa0[,[8]pass(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]unsignedInteger\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Table\n\n   Name of table to be processed.\n\n   Pass\n\n   The values specified in this parameter must be an integer constant in the\n   range 1 to 8.\n\n   Only functions within the corresponding on [11]@PASS-<n> ... endon for the\n   target table will be executed. If pass is not specified, all table\n   functions will be executed.\n\n   Programming sequence\n\n   Functions after process-table(<table>) are executed after all functions on\n   <table> are executed.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Be careful when using process-table in applications utilizing the\n   [12]@XTRA event. In such applications table functions are automatically\n   executed on table scroll, thus endless recursion will occur if the\n   processed table contains functions scrolling itself, as in the example\n   below:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0on\xc2\xa0@XTRA\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0process-table(X)\n\n   \xc2\xa0endon\n\n   \xc2\xa0table=X\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0scroll\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0print-form(Myform)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0endscroll\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [13][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_loop.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_process_table.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_tablename.htm#idh_la_pop_tablename\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_processtable.htm#idh_ma_processtable_table\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_processtable.htm#idh_ma_processtable_pass\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_unsignedinteger.htm#idh_la_pop_unsignedinteger\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_processtable.htm#idh_ma_processtable_pass\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onpass\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onxtra\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_processtable.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Branching         side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Functions\xc2\xa0>                                                   til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           SCROLL()                                      side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Scrolls a table or stream.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   scroll(\xc2\xa0[[5]allow-interrupt(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]onOff\xc2\xa0)][,[8]destination(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]Destination\xc2\xa0)][11],source(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]Source\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0:\n\n   endscroll\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Allow-interrupt\n\n   Defines whether the user may interrupt (abort) the application during the\n   scroll loop or not. When allowing to interrupt the loop, Concept checks if\n   an ABORT event has been generated. The effect of the ABORT event depends\n   on the setting of the allow-abort parameter on [14]application and\n   [15]stream level. During the scroll loop the allow-interrupt parameter\n   takes precedence over the application declaration [16]allow-abort.\n\n   If the parameter is not given, the uqconfig file parameter ALLOW-INTERRUPT\n   defines the default. Thus allow-interrupt should explicitly be set to OFF\n   in all cases where interruption should not be allowed.\n\n   Destination\n\n   Defines that a destination stream should be generated as a result of the\n   scrolled source. The rows of the destination stream are written by the\n   endscroll function.\n\n   If the purpose of the destination stream is to have a stream which can be\n   [17]sorted and later scrolled in sorted order, a temporary stream\n   identified by @STREAM-<n> may be used. <n> may be a number between 1 and 8\n   or a letter between A and Z.\n\n   When using letters, the temporary stream will be local to the current\n   application, and thus it can also be used as a destination stream when\n   scrolling streams with the [18]include-fields declaration.\n\n   When using numbers, the stream will also be available in applications\n   further down in the application hierarchy when calling other applications.\n   Please take care when using numbers since other applications in the call\n   hierarchy can overwrite the content of the stream.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Source\n\n   Defines a table or stream as the source of the scroll. If the function\n   appears on table level and the source is to be the same table, the\n   parameter may be left out.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The scroll - endscroll defines a scroll loop where the rows of the scroll\n   source are read.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The first iteration of the scroll loop opens the scroll source and\n   destination of type stream, and after the last row of the source is read,\n   the scroll source and destination of type stream are closed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The Destination parameter must not be used on events triggered before the\n   @XTRA/@START events.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Temporary streams are designated by a stream name @STREAM-<n> where <n>\n   is a digit between 1 and 8 or a letter between A and Z. When using digits\n   the source stream must be a table. Temporary streams may not be explicitly\n   defined in a stream declaration. A temporary stream is stored on a\n   temporary file (stored on the scratch path) which will be deleted on\n   program exit.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When scrolling a CSV, ASCII-DATA or ASCII-FIELDS stream it is possible to\n   program the [19]@READ-ERROR on event for handling data errors. If an error\n   occurs and the [20]@READ-ERROR event is handled in the hierarchy of the\n   field where the error occurs it is up to the programmer to reassign the\n   field and continue the scroll. The default handling for Concept for such\n   errors is to abort the application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [21][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_processtable.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_call.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_scroll.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_allowinterrupt\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_onoff.htm#idh_la_pop_onoff\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_allowinterrupt\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_destination\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_scrolldestination.htm#idh_la_pop_scrolldestination\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_destination\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_source\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_la_scrollsource.htm#idh_la_pop_scrollsource\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm#idh_ma_scroll_source\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm#idh_ma_xtra_allowabort\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_allowabort\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm#idh_ma_xtra_allowabort\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm#idh_ma_stream_includefields\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onread_error\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onread_error\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_scroll.htm\n'
b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling           side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Applications\xc2\xa0>                                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            CALL()                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The call function is used to invoke other 4GL applications as if they were\n   subroutines. On exit from the called application, Concept will return to\n   the calling application and the original screen picture will be restored\n   with the same data.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   call(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Application\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]access(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]export(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,[13]?[14]textExpression}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]import(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,[18]?[19]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]modal(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]parameters(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]port(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,[29]?<[30]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]preserve-currency(\xc2\xa0{OFF|ON|AUTO}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[32]release-resources(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[35]return-code(\xc2\xa0[36]?[37]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[38]status(\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   Any legal Concept 4GL expression that results in a text being the name of\n   a Concept 4GL [41]application or an application file. If the called\n   application is located within the same file as the calling application,\n   the expression must return the name of the called application. If,\n   however, the called application is located within another file, the\n   expression must return the name of the file.\n\n   When a call is made to an application within another file (module), the\n   first application within that module will be called. To call another\n   application in the module, the parameter must be in the form <module\n   name>:<sub name> . <sub name> identifies a specific application within the\n   <module name> file.\n\n   Access\n\n   The parameter takes an alphanumeric expression yielding an access-right.\n   The access right is used in the called application to reduce the table\n   access right definitions. The parameter may typically be used to call a\n   full access application as a query only application.\n\n   The syntax of an access right definition is given in the [42]table\n   declaration chapter.\n\n   Export\n\n   A list of expressions (fields, constant values or combinations) which are\n   to be exported. The called application must use a corresponding import\n   statement at application level to receive the values. If the storage type\n   differs between the exported value and the import field the data is\n   converted according to the import field (this does not apply when\n   exporting groups or arrays). \xc2\xa0An empty expression will cause a\n   corresponding non-database import field to be NULL at startup in the\n   called application.\n\n   Import\n\n   A list of field names to be imported from the called application. The\n   fields do not need to have the same name as in the called application. A\n   corresponding export list must exist in the called application. When\n   returning to the calling application, these fields will have values copied\n   from the exported fields in the called application. An empty field name\n   will cause a corresponding non-database export field to be set to NULL at\n   startup in the called application.\n\n   Modal\n\n   Defines the [43]modality of the application to be called. Note that it is\n   not possible to downgrade the modality set in the called application or to\n   change the modality of an application with modal(OFF) set. Any other\n   values than 'ON' and 'SYSTEM' are ignored.\n\n   Parameters\n\n   The name of a file containing parameters to be passed on to the\n   application called. Parameter files are described in the Visma Enterprise\n   Concept Operations Guide, Command Line Options.\n\n   Port\n\n   A list of fields from the current application which are to be both\n   exported and imported. The called application must have a corresponding\n   port statement. The port command is equivalent to one export and import\n   statement with the same parameter list. Note: The port command may not be\n   combined with the export and import commands. \xc2\xa0An empty expression will\n   cause the corresponding non-database import and export field to be set to\n   NULL at startup in the called application.\n\n   Preserve-Currency\n\n   This parameter defines how Concept is to remember the [44]current records\n   for the tables in the application before executing the call. When this\n   parameter is set to OFF (the default value), current records are\n   remembered for all tables in the application, even if they do not contain\n   a record. That means that current records already remembered by another\n   application may be cleared by a call. When setting the parameter to ON, a\n   current record will only be remembered for records actually containing\n   data - any already remembered currencies will be preserved. When setting\n   this parameter to AUTO, the parameter value will be ON in the startup\n   phase of an application (until functions on the @START event handler have\n   been executed) and OFF afterwards.\n\n   Release-Resources\n\n   ON All database resources used by the current application are released\n   before the new application is called, and reallocated after the\n   application call. The option is useful when available database resources\n   like cursors are limited. It may also be used to allow records referenced\n   in the current application to be updated in the called application without\n   getting a multi user conflict error messages. However, due to performance\n   considerations, the option should be used with care. An alternative way to\n   avoid the multi-user conflict problem is to use the [45]clear function on\n   the record(s) causing the conflict prior to the call function, combined\n   with a [46]find on the same record(s) afterwards.\n\n   OFF No database resources are released before the application call. This\n   is the default.\n\n   Return-Code\n\n   The parameter identifies a field which receives the return code of the\n   application called. Possible return codes are (see [47]Macro Values for\n   the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Code                   Description\n   $URC_NORMAL \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0    The application terminated normally.\n   $URC_EXIT_REQUESTED    The application terminated because an EXIT was\n                          requested.\n   $URC_ABORTED \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0   The application was aborted.\n   $URC_APPL_ERROR        The application was terminated due to a fatal\n                          application error (e.g. array index out of range).\n   $URC_APPL_ACCESS_ERROR The application could not be started because of an\n                          illegal access code or SECURITY access 'NONE'.\n                          The application was terminated due to an error\n   $URC_STREAM_OPEN_ERROR while trying to scroll a stream or write to a\n                          stream.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Using the return-code parameter affects the behaviour of Concept when\n   receiving [48]EXIT events. The programmer may have execute the [49]exit\n   function when receiving a $URC_EXIT_REQUESTED return code.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the call. The\n   field receives the value $OK if the call was successful. Possible error\n   codes are (see [50]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                 Description\n   $UE_APPLICATION        Application name missing.\n   $UE_INTERNAL_APPL      Attempt to call a system application.\n   $UE_UNABLE_TO_SYNC_DB  Database synchronization failed (with\n                          release-resources(ON)).\n   $UE_IO                 Loading of application failed due to I/O error.\n   $UE_VERSION            Illegal UCO version.\n   $UE_STACK_ALLOC        Application stack error.\n   $UE_MEMORY_EXHAUSTED   Unable to allocate memory needed.\n   $UE_UNKNOWN_SUBAPPL    Unknown sub application name.\n   $UE_UNKNOWN_DB         Application references an unknown (unavailable)\n                          database.\n   $UE_UB_NOT_LOADED      Required database interface not loaded.\n   $UE_WRONG_UCO_DB_GROUP Application not compiled against database with same\n                          format group.\n   $UE_FAILED             General error.\n   $UE_THREAD_ERROR       Thread error.\n   $UE_EXTDRV_ERROR       Error during the execution of an [51]External\n                          Server Driver.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Other error codes may be returned due to database errors.\n\n   If the status parameter is not used and an error occurs, function\n   execution terminates at the call statement. If the status parameter is\n   used, function execution continues even if an error occurs.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7export, import and port are used to pass parameters to and from the\n   called application.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using parameters, the ordering of the parameter values (field list)\n   must correspond in the two applications, and so must the data types. The\n   parameter names, however, do not have to be identical.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If an error occurs during execution of the call function and the status\n   parameter is not used, the function execution is aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7There is no predefined limit for how many levels of call there may be in\n   a Concept system. However, an application allocates resources, for\n   instance memory. Each time a new application is called, it requires more\n   resources. Thus, too many levels of call may lead to exhausted resources.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   \xc2\xb7File names should not contain more than 8 characters since some operating\n   systems, e.g. MS-DOS, are limited to this length.\n\n   \xc2\xb7release-resources(ON) in applications accessing tables using ambiguous\n   keys may not be portable on all DBMS.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n The same rules as for the [5]EXIT event apply, with the\n   exception that the application executing the exit function does not\n   receive an EXIT event itself.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_call.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderjob.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_exit.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm#idh_de_onexit\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling           side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Applications\xc2\xa0>                                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         ORDER-JOB()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function order jobs to be executed on a Visma Enterprise Server.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   order-job(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Application\xc2\xa0name\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[7]application(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[10]server(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]capabilities(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]end-time(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]export(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]handle(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]hold(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]interval(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]language(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]mail-recipient(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]password(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]priority(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]result(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[48]return-code(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[51]start-time(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[54]status(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]stream(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]time-out(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]title(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]user(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   An expression that yields the name of a 4GL application. When a call is\n   made to an application within another file, the first application within\n   the file that will be started by default. To start other applications in\n   the file, the expression yielded must conform to the syntax:\n\n   <file\xc2\xa0name>:<sub-application\xc2\xa0name>\n\n   Example: Report:subroutine_4.\n\n   Capabilities\n\n   A semicolon-separated list of capabilities that must be supported by the\n   printers the user can select from when the stream parameter is used (and\n   contains a question mark). A capability is a text string typically\n   reflecting a printer\'s output options. Predefined capabilities include:\n   colour, landscape and portrait. Custom capabilities can be defined through\n   the broker console. A printer must support all capabilities in order to be\n   included in the list of printers available to the user.\n\n   End-time\n\n   A datetime value that specifies the date and time when the period for a\n   periodic job elapses. Used together with the start-time and interval\n   parameters.\n\n   Export\n\n   A list of expressions (fields, constant values or combinations) which are\n   to be exported. The called application must use a corresponding import\n   statement at application level to receive the values. If the storage type\n   differs between the exported value and the import field the data is\n   converted according to the import field (this does not apply when\n   exporting groups or arrays). \xc2\xa0 An empty expression will cause a\n   corresponding non-database import field to be NULL at startup in the\n   called application.\n\n   If the [69]file operator is used on any of the export expressions, the\n   file specified in the expression is transferred to the SERVER as an\n   attachment to the job request. Before execution of the application on the\n   SERVER, the attachment is unloaded to a temporary file and the name of\n   this temporary file is exported to the application instead of the original\n   file name.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Handle\n\n   Returns the job number in Server if the job was accepted (check the status\n   value prior to use this value). The job number is set to (-1) if the hold\n   parameter is set to OFF.\n\n   Hold\n\n   If this parameter is set to ON, the client will wait until the requested\n   application has been run on the server. This is particularly useful if\n   further execution is dependent on completion of the job. The [70]time-out\n   parameter can be used to define how long Concept should wait for the\n   application to finish.\n\n   The default value is OFF.\n\n   Interval\n\n   When used, the job will be executed periodically. This is useful to run\n   weekly reports, to run garbage collection routines every night etc. The\n   interval parameter specified here is a numeric expression that may take\n   the following values.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Range       Description\n   0           Not periodic\n   1001 - 1999 Every <x> minutes\n   2001 - 2999 Every <x> hours\n   3001 - 3999 Every <x> days\n   4001 - 4999 Every <x> weeks\n   5001 - 5999 Every <x> months\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The value <x> is calculated from the last 3 digits in the interval code.\n\n   Example:1015 means every 15 minutes\n\n   5001 means every month\n\n   Language\n\n   Specifies the language code which should be used by the server when\n   executing the job. Default value is the language code of the client that\n   orders the job.\n\n   Mail-recipient\n\n   If used, a mail message will be sent to this mail address when the job has\n   been completed. The expression should yield an address understood by your\n   Mail Transport Agent (e.g. MS Exchange).\n\n   Password\n\n   Used together with the [71]user parameter. Specifies the password for the\n   user requesting a job.\n\n   Priority\n\n   Specifies the priority to be used for the job. Possible values are -1\n   (High), 0 (Normal) and 1 (Low).\n\n   Result\n\n   When the order-job is successful this field retrieves a semicolon\n   separated list of the output media the report output is sent to. If the\n   order-job function returns with $UE_ILLEGAL_LOCAL_FILE status, the result\n   parameter will also contain the name of one or more temporary files which\n   holds the result for the local files that failed. The temporary file name\n   is added to the local file in the semicolon separated list with the\n   following format; <local file name>|<temporary file name>.\n\n   When the order-job fails this field will retrieve a description of the\n   error\n\n   Return-code\n\n   Used together with the hold(\'ON\') parameter. After a successful run on the\n   server it will contain the value of [72]@UJP_HTTP_STATUS set by the server\n   application. See the rules section for limitations.\n\n   Server\n\n   The broker to which the job request is sent. This broker has to be\n   available to the current system.\n\n   Start-time\n\n   A datetime value that specifies the date and time when the job should be\n   executed on the server.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to 0 ($OK) if the operation is successful. Possible\n   error values (see [73]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                 Description\n   $UE_CANCEL             The user has canceled the job request.\n   $UE_BROKER_NOT_RUNNING The requested broker is not running.\n   $UE_NO_BROKERS_RUNNING There are no available brokers running.\n   $UE_NO_BROKER_DEVICES  There are no output devices on the requested\n                          broker.\n   $UE_NO_USER_PROFILE    The current user has no user profile on the broker.\n   $UE_SRV_ERROR          Generic SERVER error\n   $UE_SRV_C_CONN_OPEN    Unable to open a connection to the server\n   $UE_SRV_SOCKET_SEND    Unable to send data to the socket\n   $UE_SRV_SOCKET_RECEIVE Unable to receive data from the socket\n   $UE_BROKER_NAME        Unable to resolve broker name\n                          One or more local files could not be created or\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_LOCAL_FILE written to. The results are in those cases written\n                          to a temporary file for which the name can be found\n                          in the result parameter.\n   $UE_NO_ACCESS          The user has been denied an operation on the server\n   $UE_TIMEOUT            The operation has timed out\n\n   Stream\n\n   A text expression that can be used to specify file-names for the streams\n   in the application. The following syntax is supported :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <streamName>=<output\xc2\xa0media>[,file-format,orientation,copies,collate\xc2\xa0copies][;<streamName>=...]\n\n   Where : \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\n\n   <streamName>: name of a stream in the application. Stream names may\n   include application, sub application and a title in the following syntax :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0<title>\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0<Application>\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0:\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0<sub\xc2\xa0application>\xc2\xa0"\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0!\xc2\xa0]<stream\xc2\xa0name>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <output media>: One of the following\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Output media               Description\n   ?                          Present the user a dialogue from where he can\n                              choose an output media supported by the server.\n   [74]@PRINT-WIN(..)         Send output to a named printer on the server.\n   @MAIL(<mail addresses>)    Send the result file as a mail attachment to\n                              the user(s) listed.\n                              Store the result file on a registered path on\n                              the server. The <path alias> will be replaced\n                              with the name of a physical directory on the\n                              server. This path will then be concatenated\n   @REMOTE(<path alias>,<file with the <file name> and the result will be\n   name>)                     stored in the corresponding file on the server.\n\n                              The character \',\' cannot be used in the <path\n                              alias> and the character combination \'..\'\n                              cannot be used in the <file name>.\n                              Store the result file in local file on the\n   @LOCAL(<file name>)        client. The hold parameter is automatically set\n                              to ON when using @LOCAL output. Local output\n                              cannot be used in periodic jobs.\n   @NULL                      Discard the output (send the output to the Null\n                              device).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   E.g\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   "Title\xc2\xa0for\xc2\xa0stream\xc2\xa0main\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0subAppl\xc2\xa0for\xc2\xa0Appl"|"Appl":"subAppl"!main=@PRINT-WIN(....)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   When @PRINT-WIN is used the file-format parameter is ignored.\n\n   In addition to the normally supported [75]file formats, the virtual file\n   format \'PDF\' may be specified, which allows to produce PDF files when\n   requesting jobs on the Application Server.\n\n   The stream name @UQ_DEF_STREAM@ is a special stream name. Its parameters\n   are used whenever the runtime cannot find parameters for a stream.\n\n   Read the section [76]Stream Handling with the Server for a more exhaustive\n   discussion.\n\n   Time-Out\n\n   When starting applications with the [77]hold parameter set to \'ON\', this\n   numeric value specifies the number of seconds Concept is to wait for the\n   result before an error status ($UE_SRV_ERROR) is returned. Legal values\n   are 0 to 32767.\n\n   When the parameter is omitted, set to 0 or set to a value outside the\n   legal range, no timeout is used. That means that the application executing\n   the order-job function will block until the ordered application is\n   finished or results in an error.\n\n   Title\n\n   A text that will be attached to the job that will be displayed in queues,\n   status messages and logs. It will also be used in the mail sent back to\n   the user to identify the job. If omitted the <application name> will be\n   used as title.\n\n   User\n\n   Specifies the name of the user requesting the job. If not specified, the\n   job is requested on behalf of the current user. When requesting jobs on\n   behalf of another user, it might be necessary to specify a [78]password as\n   well. This depends on the SECURITY configuration of the system.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7A question mark can be used in any of the following parameters;\n   start-time, end-time, interval, hold, server, language, timeout, priority\n   and stream (see stream description), to display a user dialogue ([79]Job\n   Dialogue) in which the user can set the parameters. If a value is\n   specified along with the question mark it is used as a default value (E.g\n   interval(\'?1001\') )\n\n   \xc2\xb7[80]Return-code is only handled when SECURE-MODE=ON is set in the BROKER\n   section of the configuration file (UqConfig). SECURE-MODE has additional\n   requirements, see the Operation Guide.\n\n   Backward compatibility\n\n   The internal application @uqMgrAsk1 is still supported for backward\n   compatibility, but its use is strongly discouraged. For documentation on\n   @uqMgrAsk1 see the reference manual of a Concept version prior to version\n   6.01.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [81][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. If there is no previous application, it will\n   depending on system configuration. The user is either returned to the\n   menu, or Concept is terminated and the user is brought back to the\n   operating system.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   return()\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7By default the RETURN key is programmed to perform the equivalent of the\n   return function.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [5][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderjob.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_return.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_return.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling           side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Applications\xc2\xa0>                                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            RUN()                                        side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The run function executes another Concept 4GL application after having\n   terminated the current application.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   run(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Application\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]access(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]export(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression}\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   Any legal Concept 4GL [15]expression that results in a text being the name\n   of a 4GL application or an application file. If the application is located\n   within the same file as the application from which run is executed, the\n   expression must return the name of the application (as defined in\n   online/xtra=). If, however, the application is located within another\n   file, the expression must return the name of the file.\n\n   When run is made to an application within another file (module), the first\n   application within that module will be invoked. To invoke another\n   application in the module, the parameter must be in the form <module\n   name>:<sub name> . <sub name> identifies a specific application within the\n   <module name> file.\n\n   Access\n\n   The parameter takes an alphanumeric expression yielding an access-right.\n   The access right is used in the invoked application to reduce the table\n   access right definitions. The parameter may typically be used to run a\n   full access application as a query only application.\n\n   The syntax of an access right definition is given in the [16]table\n   declaration chapter.\n\n   Export\n\n   A list of expressions (fields, constant values or combinations) which are\n   to be exported. The called application must use a corresponding import\n   statement at application level to receive the values. If the storage type\n   differs between the exported value and the import field the data is\n   converted according to the import field (this does not apply when\n   exporting groups or arrays). \xc2\xa0An empty expression will cause a\n   corresponding non-database import field to be NULL at startup in the\n   called application.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using run, the current application will be terminated before the\n   called application is started. When using [17]call, the current\n   application will not be terminated before the called application is\n   started. This is the main difference between the call and the run\n   functions.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   \xc2\xb7File names should contain no more than 8 characters since some operating\n   systems, e.g. MS-DOS, are limited to this length.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [18][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_return.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_start__.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_run.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_application\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_access\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_access\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_export\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_export\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_run.htm#idh_ma_run_export\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_call.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_run.htm\n'

If the storage type\n   differs between the exported value and the import field the data is\n   converted according to the import field (this does not apply when\n   exporting groups or arrays). \xc2\xa0An empty expression will cause a\n   corresponding non-database import field to be NULL at startup in the\n   called application.\n\n   Thread-handle\n\n   This parameter is used to retrieve an INTEGER4 number identifying the\n   thread in which the application started. The thread handle is needed for\n   communication between threads. The internal field [36]@THREAD_HANDLE may\n   be used to get the handle of the current thread.\n\n   Priority\n\n   This parameter can be used to set the priority of the new thread. If set\n   to LOW, the thread is given a lower priority than NORMAL (which is the\n   default) and thus the thread is not scheduled to run unless all other\n   threads with a higher priority are either finished or blocked.\n\n   Return-Code\n\n   The parameter identifies a field which receives the return code of the\n   initial phases of starting the requested application (see Rules). Possible\n   return codes are (see [37]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                         Description\n   $URC_NORMAL                    No error encountered during the initial\n                                  phases.\n                                  The application was terminated due to a\n   $URC_APPL_ERROR \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0        fatal application error (e.g. unknown\n                                  database ).\n                                  The application could not be started\n   $URC_APPL_ACCESS_ERROR \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 because of an illegal access code or\n                                  SECURITY access \'NONE\'.\n\n   Status\n\n   The status parameter has the same specification as in the [38]call\n   function. The start function returns when the\n   application is loaded and initialised so far that database tables used are\n   "opened", but before the application starts executing.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The started application is called the root application of the application\n   thread. When the root application terminates, the application thread\n   terminates, except in the case the root application is terminated as a\n   result of using the [40]run function. Then the application thread\n   continues with a new root application.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The started application thread does not automatically get user focus. You\n   may use the new [41]change-session function with the focus-handle command\n   to do that.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When starting sub applications in the current application file, a new\n   instance of this file will be loaded. The application should use the same main key as the local\n   [38]join to the table.\n\n   If the application called is located within the same file as the\n   application calling, the expression must return the name of the called\n   application. The parameter may typically be used to call a\n   full access application as a query only application.\n\n   The syntax of an access right definition is given in the [40]table\n   component chapter.\n\n   Import\n\n   A list of field names that are to be imported from the called application.\n   The fields do not need to have the same name as in the called application.\n   A corresponding export list must exist at application level in the called\n   application. The programmer may have execute the [45]exit\n   function when receiving a $URC_EXIT_REQUESTED return code.\n\n   Status\n\n   The status parameter has the same specification as in the [46]call\n   function.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7export, import and port are used to pass parameters to and from the\n   called application. For more information about import/export see the\n   section on "porting".\n\n   \xc2\xb7A zoom function must have a [47]join on the table where the zoom is\n   performed.\n\n   Programming
