b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling External  side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Programs\xc2\xa0>                                                    til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            DDE()                                        side\n\n   A set of functions that allow you to perform Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE)\n   between Concept for the Microsoft Windows Operating Systems and other\n   programs that support DDE.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   dde(\xc2\xa0[4]EXECUTE\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[5]command(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[8]handle(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]status(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   dde(\xc2\xa0[14]INITIATE\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[15]command(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[18]handle(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[21]service(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]status(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[27]topic(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   dde(\xc2\xa0[30]POKE\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[31]handle(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[34]item(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[37]status(\xc2\xa0[38]?[39]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[40]value(\xc2\xa0[41]?[42]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   dde(\xc2\xa0[43]REQUEST\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[44]handle(\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[47]item(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[50]status(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[53]value(\xc2\xa0[54]?[55]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   dde(\xc2\xa0[56]TERMINATE\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[57]handle(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]status(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   EXECUTE\n\n   Sends a command, or set of commands, to a DDE server.\n\n   INITIATE\n\n   Initiates a conversation with a DDE server. This command must be\n   successfully executed before calling the others.\n\n   POKE\n\n   Sends data to a DDE server.\n\n   REQUEST\n\n   Reads data from a DDE server.\n\n   TERMINATE\n\n   Terminates a conversation with a DDE server.\n\n   Command\n\n   For dde(EXECUTE): A command is a server specific set of commands that are\n   to be executed by the server.\n\n   For dde(INITIATE): This parameter is used when the requested DDE service\n   is not running. The text expression should evaluate to a OS command line\n   for starting the requested DDE server. If the text expression evaluates to\n   an empty string, the dde(INITIATE) function makes no attempt to start the\n   DDE server and a status value is returned. If left out the default action\n   is to try and start the DDE server using a OS command line that is equal\n   to the service name.\n\n   Handle\n\n   If a dde(INITIATE) request is successful, a conversation is established\n   and the field name specified receives a handle that identifies the\n   conversation. Use this handle in subsequent dde() calls to obtain data\n   from the server.\n\n   Item\n\n   An item name is a string that identifies a unit of data that a server can\n   pass to a client during a transaction. For example, an item name might\n   identify an integer, a string, several paragraphs of text, or a bitmap.\n\n   Service\n\n   A service name is a string that a server application responds to when a\n   client attempts to establish a conversation with the server. A client must\n   specify this service name to be able to establish a conversation with the\n   server.\n\n   Topic\n\n   A topic name is a string that identifies a logical data context. For\n   servers that operate on file-based documents, topic names are typically\n   filenames; for other servers, they are other application-specific strings.\n   A client must specify a topic name along with a server's service name when\n   it attempts to establish a conversation with a server. Most servers\n   support the special System topic which can provide information on items of\n   general interest to any DDE client, e.g. a list of other topics currently\n   supported by the server.\n\n   Status\n\n   For the dde(INITIATE) function, status values >= 32 and < 16384 indicate\n   that the function executed successfully. When the command parameter is\n   used, values < 32 indicate an error in starting the external program (see\n   Error Codes below), otherwise a value of zero indicates that the function\n   executed successfully.\n\n   For the other dde() functions, a status value of zero indicates that the\n   function executed successfully.\n\n   Values >= 16384 indicate a DDEML error and may occur during any dde()\n   function. Refer to the table below for the error codes and their meanings.\n\n   Value\n\n   The contents of the value field are sent to the DDE server when using the\n   dde(POKE) function and filled by the server when using the dde(REQUEST)\n   function.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Dynamic Data Exchange always takes place between a client application and\n   a server application. Using these functions, Concept may be a client\n   application. It is the client that initiates the exchange by establishing\n   one or more conversations with one or more server applications. When a\n   conversation is established, the client can then request data and services\n   from the server. The client may also send data to the server. Finally, the\n   client terminates a conversation when it no longer requires a server's\n   data or services.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A DDE server uses a three-level hierarchy - service name, topic name, and\n   item name - to uniquely identify a unit of data that the server can\n   exchange during a conversation. To a client, these names are the keys that\n   make it possible for the client to establish a conversation with a server\n   and to receive data from the server. These elements are described in more\n   detail above.\n\n   Error Codes\n\n   Value Meaning\n   0     System was out of memory, executable file was corrupt, or\n         relocations were invalid.\n   2     File was not found.\n   3     Path was not found.\n   5     Attempt was made to dynamically link to a task, or there was a\n         sharing or network-protection error.\n   6     Library required separate data segments for each task.\n   8     There was insufficient memory to start the application.\n   10    Windows version was incorrect.\n   11    Executable file was invalid. Either it was not a Windows application\n         or there was an error in the .EXE image.\n   12    Application was designed for a different operating system.\n   13    Application was designed for MS-DOS 4.0.\n   14    Type of executable file was unknown.\n   15    Attempt was made to load a real-mode application (developed for an\n         earlier version of Windows).\n   16    Attempt was made to load a second instance of an executable file\n         containing multiple data segments that were not marked read-only.\n   19    Attempt was made to load a compressed executable file. The file must\n         be decompressed before it can be loaded.\n   20    Dynamic-link library (DLL) file was invalid. One of the DLL's\n         required to run this application was corrupt.\n   21    Application requires Microsoft Windows 32-bit extensions.\n   16384 A request for a synchronous advise transaction has timed out.\n   16385 The response to the transaction caused the DDE_FBUSY bit to be set.\n   16386 A request for a synchronous data transaction has timed out.\n         A DDEML function was called without first calling the DdeInitialize\n   16387 function, or an invalid instance identifier was passed to a DDEML\n         function.\n         An application initialized as APPCLASS_MONITOR has attempted to\n   16388 perform a DDE transaction, or an application initialized as\n         APPCMD_CLIENTONLY has attempted to perform server transactions.\n   16389 A request for a synchronous execute transaction has timed out.\n         The application used a data handle initialized with a different\n         item-name handle than that required by the transaction. The\n         application used a data handle that was initialized with a different\n         clipboard data format than that required by the transaction.\n   16390\n         The application used a client-side conversation handle with a\n         server-side function or vice versa.\n\n         The application used a freed data handle or string handle. More than\n         one instance of the application used the same object.\n         A DDEML application has created a prolonged race condition (where\n   16391 the server application outruns the client), causing large amounts of\n         memory to be consumed.\n   16392 A memory allocation failed.\n   16393 A client's attempt to establish a conversation has failed.\n   16394 A transaction failed.\n   16395 A request for a synchronous poke transaction has timed out.\n   16396 An internal call to the PostMessage function has failed.\n         An application instance with a synchronous transaction already in\n   16397 progress attempted to initiate another synchronous transaction, or\n         the DdeEnableCallback function was called from within a DDEML\n         callback function.\n         A server-side transaction was attempted on a conversation that was\n   16398 terminated by the client, or the server terminated before completing\n         a transaction.\n   16399 An internal error has occurred in the DDEML.\n   16400 A request to end an advise transaction has timed out.\n         An invalid transaction identifier was passed to a DDEML function.\n   16401 Once the application has returned from an XTYP_XACT_COMPLETE\n         callback, the transaction identifier for that callback is no longer\n         valid.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   This function is only available under Microsoft Windows. It will be\n   ignored with all other operating systems.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [63][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_zoom.htm\n   2. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling External  side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Programs\xc2\xa0>                                                    til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           EDITOR()                                      side\n\n   Concept provides the editor function to edit files and wide columns. When\n   the editor function is called for a wide column, the wide column is\n   retrieved from the database, copied to a temporary file and control is\n   passed to the editor. If the text is edited, Concept updates the database\n   automatically when exiting from the editor.\n\n   NOTE: It is possible to use spreadsheets, image editors, video players and\n   other presentation tools instead of a text editor.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function can be used to edit wide columns. Wide columns are columns\n   of unrestricted length unsuitable for presentation in a fixed form.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It may be used as a traditional file editor.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the initial-document parameter and the [4]DIO macro facility, it\n   may be used as a form generator.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   [5]editor(\xc2\xa0[6]editor(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]access(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]accessCode\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]call-back(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]document(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]initial-document(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]mode(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]position(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]integer,\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]integer\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]size(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]integer,\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]integer\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]title(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Editor\n\n   Defines the editor to use. The editor referred must be defined in the\n   configuration file uqconfig.\n\n   Access\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Access Description\n   UPDATE This allows updating of wide columns. This is the default.\n   QUERY  The wide column will not be updated even if the document has been\n          changed in the editor.\n   INSERT The wide column will be stored even if the initial document has not\n          been modified.\n\n   Document\n\n   Defines either the name of a file or the name of a wide column to be used\n   as source in the editor. If the parameter is given in the form\n   document("TEXT") and TEXT is a wide column field, the content of the wide\n   column will be edited. Otherwise the parameter is assumed to be a file\n   name. If this parameter is omitted, the editor is started without a\n   document.\n\n   Initial-document\n\n   Defines the name of a file to be copied to the document/wide column if the\n   document/wide column is empty (first time used). During the copying,\n   macros are expanded (see section [39]DIO macros). The edited file will be\n   saved to the document/wide column given by document, not to the\n   initial-document file. The expanded text will only be stored in a wide\n   column if it is changed and saved by the user. To force storing the\n   initial document in a wide column use access(INSERT).\n\n   An initial document file must be stored in a format understood by Concept.\n   If the file format of the editor (as specified in uqconfig) is the same as\n   the file format in the initial document, all information in the file is\n   copied and macros are expanded in text elements. If the formats are\n   different, only plain text elements are copied and expanded.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters for the internal Editor only\n\n   Call-back\n\n   Defines the name of a user written application that may be called to\n   delete, change or insert text in the document. The call-back application\n   must have two sub-applications defined as follows:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   online="popup"\n\n   \xc2\xa0port("line",\xc2\xa0"pos",\xc2\xa0"changed")\n\n   ....\n\n   (field="line") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage(INTEGER4)\n\n   (field="pos") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage(INTEGER2)\n\n   (field="changed") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage(INTEGER2)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   xtra="init"\n\n   \xc2\xa0export("MenuText",\xc2\xa0"MenuInfo")\n\n   ....\n\n   (field="MenuText") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage(ALPHA(30))\n\n   (field="MenuInfo") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage(ALPHA(80))\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The "init" application is called when the editor is started and should\n   return text to be put in the main menu to activate the call-back\n   application "popup". The entry will appear under the "Insert"\n   drop-down-menu. "MenuText" is the menu text and "MenuInfo" the information\n   text as used in the [40]define-menu function. The BLOWUP (Alt+Down) key is\n   defined as a hot-key for this entry.\n\n   The "popup" application is called when the user selects the call-back\n   entry in the menu or presses BLOWUP. "Line" and "pos" identify the exact\n   position of the cursor in the document. Inspecting, updating, inserting\n   and deleting text in the document is done through standard database\n   operations on the internal table "UQMEMTAB" using "line" as key. The\n   "changed" parameter can be used to notify the editor application on return\n   whether the currently edited file has been changed by the call-back or\n   not. It has to be set to 1 when the file has been changed, to 0 otherwise.\n   When the file has already been marked modified in the editor, it is not\n   possible to set this value back to 0.\n\n   Mode\n\n   Is a string containing characters to set different modes. The following\n   characters are understood:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Mode Description\n   A    Append mode. The document read may not be changed, but new text may\n        be added at the end of the document.\n   R    Read only mode.\n\n   Position\n\n   If the size parameter has been used, position is used to indicate where on\n   the screen the editor will appear. If position is not defined, Concept\n   will find a suitable position for the window relative to the current\n   cursor position.\n\n   Size\n\n   Defines the size of the editor window. If omitted, a full screen window\n   will be used.\n\n   Title\n\n   If size is defined, this parameter will define a text to be written in the\n   caption of the window.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If neither document nor initial-document are specified, the editor will\n   be called without any file connected.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If initial-document is specified while document is omitted, the editor\n   will be called with a temporary file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When a wide column is retrieved for updating, Concept tries to reserve\n   the owning row in the database, thus avoiding multi-user conflicts. If\n   this is not possible, the access is reduced to QUERY only.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When a file or a wide column is retrieved, Concept makes no assumption on\n   the contents of the file/wide column. It is passed on to the editor as is.\n   It is important that the editor understands the file format to be able to\n   edit it.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The initial-document parameter may be repeated up to 4 times. The initial\n   documents will then be appended to the document.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   If the parameters to document or initial-document are file names, they\n   should not use file system dependent notations. See section on\n   [41]directory and file names. We recommend the use of UNIX file syntax.\n   Concept will translate a UNIX file name to a legal file name for the\n   current file system.\n\n   Also note that different editors often use different file formats which\n   may not be compatible. Consequently, files (and data in wide columns) may\n   not be portable without conversion.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [42][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dde.htm\n b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Calling External  side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Programs\xc2\xa0>                                                    til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           SHELL()                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The shell function is used to execute operating system (OS) commands.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   shell(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Command\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]clear-screen(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]hold(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]os-status(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]show(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]windowMode\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]status(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   Any legal Concept 4GL [22]expression that returns a text corresponding to\n   the name of a legal operating system command or of an executable program.\n   The expression can also be the file name of a document. If the execution\n   of the command fails, Concept will show the document with the associated\n   program (like opening the document in the Windows Explorer or File\n   Manager). In this case, the hold parameter has no effect: the execution of\n   the 4GL application will continue immediately.\n\n   Clear-screen\n\n   This parameter is not used anymore and has no effect.\n\n   Hold\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value Description\n         The execution of the application will stop until the execution of\n   ON    the shell command is finished (synchronous execution). This is the\n         default value.\n   OFF   The execution of the application will continue right after the shell\n         command has been started (asynchronous execution).\n\n   Os-status\n\n   The field used in this parameter will receive the status code of the OS\n   upon execution of the shell command. The status code is not modified by\n   Concept, and is thus platform dependent. The storage type of the field\n   needs to be INTEGER4 in order to prevent an overflow on status number\n   values.\n\n   If the hold parameter has been set to OFF, the os-status field will\n   contain the result code of starting the shell command, not the completion\n   code of the shell command. So, if the command or program started\n   successfully, os-status will receive the value $OK. As Concept has no\n   contact with the program anymore when hold is OFF, there is no way for\n   Concept to know in what status the command/program completed.\n\n   Show\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value     Description\n   NORMAL    If the command creates a window, it will be shown on the\n             desktop.\n             The window created by the command will be hidden. Do not use\n   HIDDEN    this mode if the command expects user input as the thread will\n             block while waiting for input.\n   MAXIMIZED The window created by the command will be shown maximized.\n   MINIMIZED The window created by the command will be shown minimized.\n\n   Status\n\n   The field used in this parameter will receive the value 0 if the command\n   has completed successfully, and 1 if an error occurred. Use the os-status\n   parameter to receive a detailed status code.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the hold parameter is set to ON and an error occurs, a dialogue box\n   is shown stating the error situation. When the hold parameter is set to\n   OFF and an error occurs, no dialogue box is shown. The programmer has then\n   to check the status parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In Microsoft Windows, a DOS command can be activated by prefixing the\n   command with the name of the command interpreter (cmd.exe /c). Note that\n   the command interpreter in Windows 9x is called command.com instead.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   This function is, in general, not portable since it is dependent on the\n   operating system in use.\n\n   The internal field [23]@RUNTIME_INFO contains information about operating\n   system and version at runtime and can be used to write portable code.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [24][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_editor.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_shell.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_command\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_clearscreen\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_onoff.htm#idh_la_pop_onoff\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_clearscreen\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_hold\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_onoff.htm#idh_la_pop_onoff\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_hold\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_osstatus\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_osstatus\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_show\n  17. file:///dev/html_lexical__windowmode.htm#idh_la_pop_windowmode\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_show\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_status\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm#idh_ma_shell_status\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_intruntimeinfo\n  24. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_shell.htm\n'

The special DLL\n   can export values using the uspExport routine. Any import fields that are\n   not exported from the special DLL will receive a zero value. An empty\n   field name will cause the the corresponding uspExport to be ignored.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the special\n   call. The field receives the value that are returned from the uspMain\n   routine in the special DLL.\n\n   If the status parameter is left out and the return value from uspMain is\n   different from 1 further function execution is aborted.\n\n   Possible Concept generated return values include :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                    Description\n   $UE_USP_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND The special DLL was not found.\n   $UE_USP_NO_MAIN_ROUTINE   The requested special DLL does not contain a\n                             uspMain routine\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Concept calls the Windows API function CoInitialize once in each thread\n   that executes the special function. This makes it possible to use COM\n   routines in special DLL's. CoUninitialize will be called when the thread\n   is terminated.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The special name @UQUNLOAD_DLL can be used to unload the DLL from memory.\n   It may only be used in the same thread that used the DLL in for the first\n   time. If this thread is not active anymore, this special name may be used\n   in any thread.\n\n   See also\n\n   For more information about using and building special DLL's have a look in\n   the help file (uqspeci31.hlp/uqspeci.hlp) that can be found in the sdk16\n   or sdk32 sub directory of your installation.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_shell.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_clear.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_la_name.htm#idh_la_pop_name\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_service\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_service\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_name.htm#idh_la_pop_name\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_service\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_error_text\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_error_text\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_export\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_export\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_export\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_import\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_import\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_import\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_status\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  24. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_special.htm#idh_ma_special_status\n"

For tables\n   without repeated lines, the record in question is the single record of the\n   table. Currently, this is the case with\n   operations performed by the [76]SQL-EXECUTE function.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The parameters table and database can not be combined.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   The interpretation db-main-error, db-sub-error and message  is DBMS\n   dependent. b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Database          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Operations\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        DB-OPERATION()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function can be used to perform database operations on the specified\n   table.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   db-operation(\xc2\xa0[5]command(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]execute-status-field(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[11]table(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]status(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   Text expression that must evaluate to one of the following commands:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command              Description\n   FIRST                Finds the [17]first table row.\n   LAST                 Finds the [18]last table row.\n   NEXT                 Finds the [19]next table row.\n   PREVIOUS             Finds the [20]previous table row.\n   FIND                 [21]Finds the exact table row according to the\n                        table's key values.\n   FIND-FORWARD         [22]Finds the next matching table row according to\n                        the table's key values.\n   FIND-BACKWARD        [23]Finds the previous matching table row according\n                        to the table's key values.\n                        [24]Finds the exact table row according to the\n   FIND-NEXT            table's key values and the next rows on repeated\n                        tables.\n                        [25]Finds the exact table row according to the\n   FIND-PREVIOUS        table's key values and the previous rows on repeated\n                        tables.\n   CLEAR                [26]Clears the current table row or repeat area.\n   UPDATE               [27]Updates the current table row.\n   UPDATE-IN-SCROLL     [28]Updates the current table row during [29]scroll\n                        operations.\n   INSERT               [30]Inserts a new table row according to the table's\n                        field values.\n   DELETE               [31]Deletes the current table row.\n   DELETE-FIND-NEXT     [32]Deletes the current table row and finds the next\n                        row.\n   DELETE-FIND-PREVIOUS [33]Deletes the current table row and finds the\n                        previous row.\n   DELETE-IN-SCROLL     [34]Deletes the current table row during [35]scroll\n                        operations.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the text expression is a simple expression (contained inside a single\n   pair of single quotes) the compiler will check the validity of the command\n   and issue a high level warning if the command is erroneous.\n\n   Execute-Status-Field\n\n   Text expression that must evaluate to one of the following values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value Description\n   OFF   The field defined by the status parameter is not executed when the\n         function returns (default).\n   ON    The field defined by the status parameter is always executed when\n         the function returns.\n   ERROR The field defined by the status parameter is executed if the status\n         returned is different from $OK.\n\n   Table\n\n   Text expression that must evaluate to the name of a table in the current\n   sub-application. The text expression may include a repeat line reference.\n   If the text expression is a simple expression (contained inside a single\n   pair of single quotes) the compiler will check the existence of the table\n   and issue a high level warning if the table is not found in the\n   application.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. In addition to status codes returned\n   by the actual database operations (see [36]status operator) the following\n   values may be returned (see [37]Macro Values for the numeric values of\n   these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status             Description\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_CMD    Illegal command name specified in the [38]command\n                      parameter.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_TABLE  Illegal table name specified in the [39]table\n                      parameter.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_REPEAT Illegal repeat value specified in the [40]table\n                      parameter.\n                      One of the [41]commands UPDATE, DELETE,\n                      DELETE-FIND-NEXT or DELETE-FIND-PREVIOUS is used during\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_NOW    a [42]scroll operation, or one of the commands\n                      UPDATE-IN-SCROLL or DELETE-IN-SCROLL is used while not\n                      scrolling a table.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The same rules as for the corresponding database operation functions\n   apply.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Function execution will be aborted if an error occurs and the [43]status\n   parameter has been omitted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the [44]execute-status-field parameter is used the field given in\n   the [45]status parameter must evaluate to a simple application field.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [46][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Database          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Operations\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           DELETE()                                      side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Delete one table row from a database table.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   delete(\xc2\xa0[5]table(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]tableName\xc2\xa0[#\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]numberExpression]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]abort-on-error(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]find(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]findWhat\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Table\n\n   The name of the [16]table where current row is to be deleted. A specific\n   repeat line may be designated using the # operator after the table name.\n\n   Abort-on-error\n\n   If the operation fails, the function execution will be aborted if this\n   parameter is set ON. In ONLINE, ON is the default, in XTRA, OFF is the\n   default. Use the [17]status operator to check the result of the operation.\n\n   Find\n\n   This parameter may only be used on program controlled tables and not if\n   the function is executed from within a [18]scroll loop, and it defines\n   whether a new row should be automatically retrieved after the current row\n   has been deleted. The parameter values are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value                Description\n   NEXT \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 The next row in the data set will be fetched\n                        (default).\n   PREVIOUS \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0     The row prior to the deleted row will be fetched.\n   NONE \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 No new row will be fetched.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function deletes the current row of the table, i.e. it is necessary\n   to fetch a row before it can be deleted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7On Unique controlled tables, the next row of the table is automatically\n   fetched after a successful deletion.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is not legal to execute the function from within a [19]group-by loop.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the function is executed from within a [20]scroll loop, and the table\n   referred to is the same as the table being scrolled, the following must be\n   noticed:\n\n   \xc2\xb7The status operator should not be used inside the scroll loop to test the\n   result of the delete. The record is in fact deleted during the execution\n   of the endscroll function and as such the status of the delete function\n   can only be tested upon after the endscroll.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Warning: Execution will fail if the function is put on a field and\n   indirectly executed with the [21]execute function.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [22][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_db_operation.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_deleteallrows.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_delete.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_table\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_tablename.htm#idh_la_pop_tablename\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_table\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_numberexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_numberexpression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_table\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_abortonerror\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_onoff.htm#idh_la_pop_onoff\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_abortonerror\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_find\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_findwhat.htm#idh_la_pop_findwhat\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_delete.htm#idh_ma_delete_find\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorsstatus\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_groupby.htm\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_execute.htm\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_delete.htm\n'

This is default when the join is\n   located at field level.\n\n   OFF\n\n   Function execution continues as normal and the [21]status(<table>)\n   operator can be used to get the status of the performed join. Usual status\n   values are (using predefined compiler constants) $ok and $not_found. This\n   is the default when the function is located at table level.\n\n   Ignore-null\n\n   ON\n\n   If the join key value is null (0 or ' ' for all join key fields), the row\n   will cleared and no database operation performed.\n\n   OFF\n\n   No special handling of join key null value.\n\n   Match\n\n   Defines how the value of the join key is used to identify the joined\n   record:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value    Description\n   EXACT    The joined record must have a key value equal to the join key\n            value. This is the default.\n   BACKWARD The joined record must have a key value less or equal to the join\n            key value.\n   FORWARD  The joined record must have a key value greater or equal to the\n            join key value.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function may only be applied on join tables. (The definition of a\n   join table is a table with the [22]key field on another table (and thus\n   has no field with the declaration key)).\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the join table is not defined explicitly, the first join of the\n   application implicitly declares the join table with a join key field being\n   the field having the function.\n\n   \xc2\xb7All the function parameters may also be supplied as join [23]table\n   declarations. The function parameters will overrule the corresponding join\n   table declarations.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If [24]join type is INNER or OUTER and not DYNAMIC (static join), and the\n   function appears on table level of the join owner and the table is handled\n   by a relational DBMS, the function is ignored because it at this stage is\n   assumed that the join is performed by the DBMS.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Static joins work across logical database boundaries if the DBMS of the\n   main table supports this and the user logged on to the main tables's\n   database has access to the joined table.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The match parameter may only be used if the join type is DYNAMIC.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [25][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_insert.htm\n   2. The member tables\n   key field must be a group field where the first members of the group is\n   owned by the owner table.\n\n   \xc2\xb7On non-relational DBMS\xef\xbf\xbds, only columns defined with a table index can be\n   used as a main key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The key function performs the equivalent of a [5]find function when\n   executed, i.e. it attempts to get the row identified by the main key\n   value. If the row is not found and the table has insert access, the row is\n   marked as "ready for insert" or "to be inserted" if the table declaration\n   store-after-key(on) is used. "ready for insert" means that additional\n   input in another table field is required to change row status to "to be\n   inserted".\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [6][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_join.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_last.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_key.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_find.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_key.htm\n'
b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Database          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Operations\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            LAST()                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Get last table row from a database.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   last(\xc2\xa0table(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Table\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Table\n\n   Name of the [7]table from which to get the last row.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7On relational databases, the function will generates a new result set by\n   executing an SQL select command.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The last row of a table is per definition the first row of the result set\n   achieved by an SQL select statement with a selection criteria (where\n   clause) and sorting (order by clause) according to the application table\n   definition, where the order by clause specifies an opposite sort direction\n   of what is defined on the table. (This definition also applies for\n   non-relational databases.)\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function may not be used on tables where the sql-order-by declaration\n   is used. This is because it is not possible to then automatically generate\n   an opposite sorting.\n\n   \xc2\xb7In ONLINE applications on tables not manually controlled (table\n   declaration [8]control(UNIQUE)), when a row is found, the table functions\n   will be executed before the function returns.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the table is Unique controlled, the function operates on all repeat\n   lines, else it operates on the current repeat line, unless overridden by\n   an explicit repeat line specification after the table name (<name>#<repeat\n   line expression>). If the table is Unique controlled and the number of\n   rows in the result set is larger or equal to the number of repeat lines,\n   the last row will be put in the last repeat line, the second last row in\n   the second last repeat line, and so on. If the number of rows in the\n   result set is less than the number of repeat lines, the function will be\n   equivalent to a first function.\n\n   \xc2\xb7To find out if a row was successfully found, use the [9]status(<Table>)\n   operator. Normal status values are (using predefined compiler constants)\n   $ok and $not_found.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_key.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_mark.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_last.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_tablename.htm#idh_la_pop_tablename\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_last.htm#idh_ma_last_table\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_table.htm#idh_ma_table_control\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorsstatus\n'

b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Database          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Operations\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          SQL-EXEC()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Execute a SQL statement directly bypassing Concept 4GL database interface.\n   This is useful for executing SQL calls not supported by Concept 4GL, like\n   stored procedures.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   sql-exec(\xc2\xa0[5]command(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]bind-list(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]applicationField\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]applicationField}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]bind-table(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]tableName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]count(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]database(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[22]ignore-null-value(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[25]table(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]tableName[****][#repeatLine]\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[28]timeout(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]result(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[34]status(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   [37]SQL expression to execute. Please read the chapter on [38]SQL\n   expressions on how to use portable object names.\n\n   Using the command \'TRUNCATE(tableName)\' on a [39]temporary table will\n   delete the contents of the temporary table indicated in the \'tableName\'\n   parameter. If bind-list is used, it returns the number of significant rows\n   in the table before truncation.\n\n   Using command \'COUNT(tableName)\' on a temporary table will return the\n   number of rows in the table into the field indicated in the bind-list\n   parameter.\n\n   Using the command \'MIN(tableName,columnName)\' on a temporary table will\n   return the minimum value of the column into the field indicated in the\n   bind-list parameter. The column must be of [40]storage type I1, I2 or I4\n   and the bind-list parameter field must be of the same storage type.\n\n   Using the command \'MAX(tableName,columnName)\' on a temporary table will\n   return the maximum value of the column into the field indicated in the\n   bind-list parameter. The column must be of [41]storage type I1, I2 or I4\n   and the bind-list parameter field must be of the same storage type.\n\n   For both the TRUNCATE and COUNT commands, the bind-list field parameter\n   must be of type INTEGER4 or INTEGER2.\n\n   Using command \'@QUERY\' along with the table and result parameters will\n   return the currently defined search criteria\'s (CTRL+ALT+F3) for the\n   table.\n\n   Bind-list\n\n   If the SQL command generates a result (select statements), the column\n   values of the first row returned will be inserted in the listed fields. As\n   only the first row will be returned, it is not possible to scroll the\n   result set. Use the [42]bind-table parameter to copy the result into a\n   table which can be processed subsequently.\n\n   Bind-table\n\n   If the SQL command generates a set of results, they will be inserted into\n   the table given by tableName. The table must be defined in the application\n   and its layout must match exactly to the result set of the SQL-EXEC\n   command. (NOTE: If the result table is a [43]temporary table, the internal\n   column UQRCSTAT is automatically removed from the table layout). When\n   inserting into the result table, no functions and no events are triggered.\n   If insertion of a table record fails, the whole operation will be stopped\n   and the status parameter (and [44]db-info()) will give the reason for\n   failure.\n\n   Count\n\n   Returns the number of rows affected by the command. This number is\n   returned by the underlying DBMS and the interpretation my vary between the\n   different DBMS implementations. If the number is unavailable for the SQL\n   command issued, the return value is set to -1. In conjunction with the\n   [45]bind-table parameter, count will return the number of rows inserted\n   into the bound table.\n\n   Database\n\n   Name of a database. Default is current database defined by most recent\n   [46]database declaration. Note that the database name is an expression and\n   not a name reference.\n\n   Ignore-Null-Value\n\n   Used together with the [47]bind-list parameter. If the text expression\n   evaluates to \'OFF\' (or 0), fields specified in the bind-list parameter may\n   receive NULL values (see the [48]isnull operator). If it evaluates to \'ON\'\n   (or 1; the default value), no NULL values are returned.\n\n   Table\n\n   The name of a table defined in the application that should be used when\n   evaluating the @VALUE and @CONDITION sql macros. By default the current\n   repeat line is used, but this may be overruled using the # operator.\n\n   Must be combined with the [49]result parameter.\n\n   Time-out\n\n   Defines an interval after which the operation will abort if not completed\n   yet. Setting a value of 0 will disable the time-out mechanism. Defining a\n   negative value will not abort the operation immediately, but displays a\n   dialogue box every -<Seconds>. The dialogue text tells that a SQL command\n   is in progress and the user may abort the command if he/she wants to.\n\n   Time-out is supported for SYBASE databases only.\n\n   Result\n\n   When using this parameter, the [50]command will not be executed on the\n   database server. All macros found in the command will be expanded instead\n   and the result of the expansion will be returned in the result field. This\n   parameter can not be used together with the [51]bind-list or\n   [52]bind-table parameter.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status code of the operation. See the documentation of the\n   [53]status operator for further details on return codes. The special\n   status code $UE_DB_NO_BIND might be returned if [54]bind-list is defined\n   but no results are returned by the issued SQL command (E.g. if the command\n   is an SQL update, delete or insert). Please note that the operation may\n   have been executed correctly in the DBMS in those circumstances.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The command parameter is not validated by Concept. It is sent directly to\n   the RDBMS.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The database name must be defined in the configuration file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The section "[55]SQL expressions" defines how to use macros to write\n   portable SQL statements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [56]@INSERT event will be triggered for each record inserted when\n   using the bind-table parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [57]ignore-null-value parameter can only be used together with the\n   [58]bind-list parameter.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   \xc2\xb7This function is portable across operating systems.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is the programmer\'s responsibility to achieve portability across\n   different RDBMS using standard SQL features only.\n\n   \xc2\xb7This function is not supported for SIBAS, ISAM and INFORMIX-CISAM.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Database          side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Operations\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        SYNCHRONIZE()                                    side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The synchronize() function has two different modes of operation. In the\n   first mode ([5]syntax 1), it synchronizes records changed in the\n   application with the corresponding records in the database(s). In the\n   second mode ([6]syntax 2), it synchronizes changes made in the contents of\n   a temporary table.\n\n   Syntax 1\n\n   synchronize(\xc2\xa0[[7]status(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Status\n\n   The value returned in this field is either $OK or $ERROR (see [10]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function should only be used from within the [11]@SYNCHRONIZE event\n   handler.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The following code is equivalent to the standard synchronization function\n   used when the @SYNCHRONIZE event is not used:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0on\xc2\xa0(@SYNCHRONIZE)\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0synchronize()\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0endon\n\n   \xc2\xb7The function synchronizes what is left to synchronize when the function\n   is executed. That means that other database functions may be used to\n   explicitly synchronize some records, and synchronize() used to "do the\n   rest".\n\n   \xc2\xb7To support the task of doing the correct operations manually, the\n   internal field [12]@EVENT_PARAM contains information describing the need\n   for synchronizing. The first word of the field describes the seriousness\n   of the event:\n\n   MANDATORY The synchronization must be done now\n   OPTIONAL  The synchronization may be done later (without getting lost)\n\n   \xc2\xb7The next word identifies the reason for a synchronization being\n   requested:\n\n   FINISH     The application is about to finish.\n   ABORT      The application is about to abort (after a fatal error).\n   NAVIGATION The user has moved the cursor out of a record.\n   DBOP       A database operation is requested that may overwrite the\n              current application copy.\n   REQUEST    An explicit request to synchronize is done.\n\n   \xc2\xb7To do a manual synchronization properly, the [13]inquire function may be\n   useful.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Syntax 2\n\n   synchronize(\xc2\xa0[14]table(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]tableName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]signal-events(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]status(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Table\n\n   A table defined in the application. The table must be a [23]temporary\n   table (belong to a database defined in the uqconfig configuration file\n   with db-type \'TEMP\').\n\n   Signal-events\n\n   If this parameter is set to OFF the temporary table is physically rebuild\n   and the status of each record in the table is set to NONE.\n\n   If set to ON, the table will additionally be read record by record and\n   (depending on the status of the record) one of the 4GL events\n   [24]@INSERT/[25]@DELETE or [26]@UPDATE will be invoked (if programmed on\n   the table given by the table parameter).\n\n   Status\n\n   The status code of the operation (see [27]Macro Values for the numeric\n   values of predefined status code constants).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7A synchronize with signal-events(ON) can be aborted by using the\n   [28]error function (inside [29]@INSERT/[30]@DELETE/[31]@UPDATE). If the\n   event handling is aborted, the status of the synchronize function is set\n   to $ERROR.\n\n   \xc2\xb7@INSERT/@DELETE and @UPDATE events caused by a synchronize can be\n   identified by checking the [32]@EVENT_PARAM field. In the case of a\n   synchronize for a temporary table, its value will be TEMP-TABLE-SYNC.\n\n   \xc2\xb7During a synchronize with signal-events(ON) all other operations\n   (including a secondary synchronization) against the same physical\n   temporary table as given by the table parameter, will fail with error\n   $TABLE_RESERVED.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When processing a @UPDATE synchronize event the [33]OLD operator can be\n   used to retrieve the original values of each column in the record.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [34][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. This means that\n   the status operator may not be used to check the result of the operation -\n   only to check whether the operation is legal, i.e. not stopped by access\n   restrictions imposed by the application.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is illegal to indirectly execute the update function from a [12]scroll\n   .. endscroll block.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The status of the operation may be inspected by the [13]status(<Table>)\n   operator. For the LENGTH\n   command, it is set to the number of bytes in the wide column. The value is\n   0 if the wide column is empty or the query fails.\n\n   Not set for other commands.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. The value is $OK if successful,\n   otherwise an error value is returned. See the [17]status operator for\n   possible values.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7There must exist a current row when this function is executed, i.e. a row\n   must have been fetched from the database.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the operation fails and no status field is defined, the function\n   execution is aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [18][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_update.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_change.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_wide_column.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_command\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_wccommand.htm#idh_la_pop_wccommand\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_command\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_field\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_field\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_result\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_result\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_status\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm#idh_ma_widecolumn_status\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_operators.htm#idh_de_operatorsstatus\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_widecolumn.htm\n'
b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           CHANGE()                                      side\n\n   Change [4]field, [5]form, [6]stream or [7]table attributes.\n\n   When the change function is used to change an attribute which otherwise is\n   defined at compile time using a declaration, and unless otherwise stated,\n   the syntax rules are the same for the change function as for the\n   corresponding declaration, except that change functions often takes\n   expression parameters and declarations often takes constant parameters\n   only.\n\n   Note that the sequence of sub functions to the change function may be\n   significant.\n\n   Syntax 1: Change Field Attributes\n\n   change(\xc2\xa0field(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,background(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,colour(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,font(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,frame(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,lock(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,position(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,refresh(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,separator(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,show(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,style(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,status(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]fieldname\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,type(\xc2\xa0{{\xc2\xa0PUSH-BUTTON\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0DEFAULT-BUTTON\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0INPUT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0OUTPUT\xc2\xa0}}\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,values(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of the [36]field to change.\n\n   Background\n\n   Change the background of the elements connected to the field.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Changes the current text colour of the elements connected to the field.\n\n   Font\n\n   Change the font of the characters in the elements connected to the field.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Changes the frame type of the elements connected to the field.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Permits or prohibits movement of the cursor into elements connected to a\n   field. Legal values are ON, OFF, PERMANENT ON and PERMANENT OFF. See the\n   chapter on [37]locking for more details.\n\n   Position\n\n   Change the position of the last element connected to the field.\n\n   Refresh\n\n   Force or stop refresh of the given field. The parameter value may be a\n   numeric or an alphanumeric expression. To refresh, a numeric value must\n   evaluate to 1 or an alphanumeric value to 'ON', any other values will stop\n   refresh of the field.\n\n   This parameter is especially useful for CALLBACK elements where the\n   displayed value and/or information value is dependant on more than the\n   fields own value.\n\n   Separator\n\n   A text containing the separator character in the values parameter (see\n   below).\n\n   Show\n\n   Makes [38]elements connected to the field visible or hidden. The parameter\n   value may be a numeric or an alphanumeric expression. To show, a numeric\n   value must evaluate to 1 or an alphanumeric value to 'ON', any other\n   values will hide the connected elements. If the value corresponds to the\n   current state of the field, the function has no effect\n\n   Style\n\n   Change the style of the elements connected to the field.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the function.\n   The field receives the value $OK if the call was successful. Possible\n   error codes are (see [39]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_FIELD An illegal field was specified\n   $UE_STYLE         Illegal value for the style parameter\n   $UE_FONT          Illegal value for the font parameter\n   $UE_FRAME         Illegal value for the frame parameter\n   $UE_COLOUR        Illegal value for the colour parameter\n   $UE_BACKGROUND    Illegal value for the background parameter\n   $UE_LOCK          Illegal value for the lock parameter\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ONOFF Illegal value for the show parameter\n\n   Type\n\n   Change the type of the elements connected to a field. Only a few type\n   changes are allowed:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Current Type   Possible New Types\n   PUSH-BUTTON    DEFAULT-BUTTON\n   DEFAULT-BUTTON PUSH-BUTTON\n   INPUT          OUTPUT\n   OUTPUT         INPUT\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Setting a new default-button will automatically change the previous\n   [40]default-button to a [41]push-button.\n\n   Values\n\n   A text containing a new list of values for a list-box or\n   drop-down-list-box field separated by the separator character which\n   defaults to ';'.\n\n   Notes\n\n   The difference between the change function and the [42]change-element\n   function is defined as follows:\n\n   \xc2\xb7The change function changes the colour, frame, background, font, style,\n   lock, show and type attributes for any element connected to the field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the change function is used with the colour, frame, background, font\n   and lock attributes, the changes are reset if the record of the field is\n   cleared. For the change-element function this applies only to the lock\n   attribute.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is recommended to use the change-element function if the special\n   functionality of the change function is not needed.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Syntax 2: Change Form Attributes\n\n   It is recommended to use the [43]change-form() function instead of the\n   change function for all parameters except include-fields.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   change(\xc2\xa0form(\xc2\xa0[44]?[45]formName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,active-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,background(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,frame(\xc2\xa0[50]?[51]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,include-fields(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,lock(\xc2\xa0[54]?[55]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,show(\xc2\xa0[56]?[57]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,status(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]fieldname\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,style(\xc2\xa0[60]?[61]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,tab-index(\xc2\xa0[62]?[63]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,title(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Form\n\n   Name of the [66]form to change.\n\n   Active-Tab-Index\n\n   Set the active [67]tab index of the form.\n\n   Note: The form event [68]@ACTIVE-TAB-INDEX is generated when the active\n   tab index is changed.\n\n   Background\n\n   Change the background of the form.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Change the frame of the form.\n\n   Font\n\n   Change the font used on the title of the form.\n\n   Include-fields\n\n   Only allowed in XTRA programs and for forms with an initial\n   i[69]nclude-fields declaration. Changes the [70]include-fields list for\n   the given form. Specifying an empty text will reset the include-fields\n   list to the original declared value for the form.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The text expression should evaluate to a list of fields in the\n   application. Each element in the list must be delimited by the character\n   defined by the separator parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Maximum number of fields in the list is 255.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Can only be used on tab forms and must be specified together with the\n   tab-index parameter. Legal values are ON and OFF.\n\n   See the chapter on [71]locking for more details.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Expression defining a single character used as separator in the\n   include-fields list. Default value is ';' (semicolon).\n\n   Show\n\n   Makes the form visible or hidden. The parameter value may be a numeric or\n   an alphanumeric expression. To show, a numeric value must evaluate to 1 or\n   an alphanumeric value to 'ON'. All other values will result in the form\n   being hidden. If the value corresponds to the current state of the form,\n   the function has no effect\n\n   All text and fields declared in the form as well as all forms which are\n   owned by the form will be hidden or shown. When a form is hidden, the\n   underlying text will be refreshed. All fields will assume the previous\n   state (style, lock etc.) when the form is re shown.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the function.\n   The field receives the value $OK if the call was successful. Possible\n   error codes are (see [72]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ONOFF Illegal value for the lock or show parameter\n   $UE_STYLE         Illegal value for the style parameter\n   $UE_FONT          Illegal value for the font parameter\n   $UE_FRAME         Illegal value for the frame parameter\n   $UE_COLOUR        Illegal value for the colour parameter\n   $UE_BACKGROUND    Illegal value for the background parameter\n   $UE_LOCK          Illegal value for the lock parameter\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED Include-fields was specified for a form with no initial\n                     include-fields declaration.\n   $UE_OVERFLOW      The include-fields list contained more than 255 fields.\n   $UE_CONNECT       An illegal field name was found in the include-fields\n                     list\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_FIELD A group field, a Sql-column or a field from another sub\n                     application was found in the include-fields list.\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR   A blank field name was found inside the include-fields\n                     list.\n\n   Style\n\n   Change the style of the form.\n\n   Tab-Index\n\n   This parameter is used to identify a tab index of a tab form.\n\n   Title\n\n   Change the title of the form.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Note that when the frame or the font is changed it might increase or\n   decrease the interior size of the form. Thus any object inside the form\n   might be moved.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Include-fields are only allowed in XTRA programs. All other parameters\n   are only allowed in ONLINE programs.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Syntax 3: Change Stream Attributes\n\n   It is recommended to use the [73]change-stream() function instead of the\n   change function for the style, background,frame and title parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   change(\xc2\xa0stream(\xc2\xa0[74]?[75]streamName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,background(\xc2\xa0[76]?[77]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,formatting(\xc2\xa0[78]?[79]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,frame(\xc2\xa0[80]?[81]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,status(\xc2\xa0[82]?[83]fieldname\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,style(\xc2\xa0[84]?[85]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,title(\xc2\xa0[86]?[87]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Stream\n\n   Name of the [88]stream to change.\n\n   Background\n\n   Change the background of the stream. This parameter can only be used in\n   online programs.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   This parameter can only be used in XTRA programs and on device formatted\n   streams (formatting DIRECT or NONE). If the expression evaluates to NONE\n   further page formatting in the report is turned off. If the expression\n   evaluates to DIRECT, page formatting is turned ON.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Change the frame of the stream. This parameter can only be used in online\n   programs.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the function.\n   The field receives the value $OK if the call was successful. Possible\n   error codes are (see [89]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status         Description\n   $UE_STYLE      Illegal value for the style parameter\n   $UE_FRAME      Illegal value for the frame parameter\n   $UE_BACKGROUND Illegal value for the background parameter\n   $UE_LOCK       Illegal value for the lock parameter\n\n   Style\n\n   Change the style of the stream. This parameter can only be used in online\n   programs.\n\n   Title\n\n   Change the title (caption) of the stream. This parameter can only be used\n   in online programs.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Syntax 4: Change Table Attributes\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   change(\xc2\xa0table(\xc2\xa0[90]?[91]tableName\xc2\xa0[#repeatLine])\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,access(\xc2\xa0[92]?[93]accessCode\xc2\xa0{+\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]accessCode}\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,db-table(\xc2\xa0[96]?[97]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,key-type(\xc2\xa0[98]?[99]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,record-state(\xc2\xa0INSERT\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,sort(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,status(\xc2\xa0[102]?[103]fieldname\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Table\n\n   A [104]table defined in the application. The change function may apply to\n   a single row only. By default the current repeat line is used, but this\n   may be overruled using the # operator.\n\n   Access\n\n   This function provides a means of restricting access to rows in a table.\n   It sets the access for individual rows found in the database. This\n   contrasts with the table declaration access, which sets access rights for\n   all rows in the table.\n\n   The <access> value is an expression and follows the rules of the\n   [105]access declaration on tables.\n\n   Db-Table\n\n   Use this function to change the name of the [106]table being accessed in\n   the database at run time. The new table name may be a view or a another\n   table, but it must be located in the same database as the declared table\n   name.\n\n   All columns referred to must exist in the new table and have compatible\n   storage codes. Indexes do not have to be identical.\n\n   The current region will be cleared by this function. Restoring the current\n   row will be the responsibility of the programmer.\n\n   Key-Type\n\n   This parameter changes the [107]key-type of the table. It should be used\n   in connection with the sort parameter to specify whether the sort key used\n   is unique or not.\n\n   Record-state\n\n   Legal values for record-state includes:\n\n                  This value is only allowed on tables with a key containing\n                  an auto-increment-column. When set the identified record is\n                  prepared for insertion; all non-key fields including the\n   INSERT         auto-increment-column are cleared, initial-values are set\n                  for non-key fields and the @CREATE event is triggered on\n                  the table. See the chapter on [108]Using auto increment\n                  columns for more details.\n                  This value is only allowed on tables with an\n                  [109]@PROGRAM-INSERT event handler. When set the identified\n                  record is prepared for insertion; all fieldsare cleared,\n                  initial-values are set for non-key fields and the @CREATE\n                  event is triggered on the table. At the point where Concept\n   PROGRAM-INSERT normally would automatically INSERT the record the\n                  @PROGRAM-INSERT event is triggered and the application is\n                  responsible for assigning key values and insert the record.\n                  When inside the [110]@PROGRAM-INSERT event all database\n                  operations are executed as if the corresponding table was\n                  declared with [111]control(PROGRAM).\n\n   Sort\n\n   This parameter is used to change the sort order of the table. The\n   parameter cannot be used on join tables. The text expression must return a\n   comma separated list of application fields that defines the sorting\n   sequence. The fields can be preceded by a '>' (sort ascending) or a '<'\n   (sort descending) and the field names can be quoted if they contain '>',\n   '<', comma or spaces. The fields must be simple database columns (no\n   groups allowed) and must belong to the table identified by the table\n   parameter or a joined table if the join is a static (INNER/OUTER) join. If\n   a joined field is used and the underlying database system does not support\n   the static join, an error is returned in the status parameter.\n\n   The new sort order will take effect when a [112]first, [113]last or\n   [114]find database operation is performed.\n\n   Status\n\n   The parameter identifies a field to receive the status of the function.\n   The field receives the value $OK if the call was successful. Possible\n   error codes are (see [115]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                 Description\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_TABLE      The sort parameter can not be used on join tables.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_FIELD      An illegal field is specified for the sort or\n                          key-field parameters.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_VALUE      The maximum of 254 fields in the sort parameter is\n                          exceeded.\n   $UE_UNKNOWN_FIELD      A field name specied in the sort parameter was not\n                          found in the application\n                          A field from a joined table was specified, but the\n   $UE_DSQL_ILLEGAL_FIELD join was not static (INNER/OUTER) or the underlying\n                          database system do not support the static join.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If only one access code is used, it is accumulative. In other words, if\n   access('UPDATE') is used, both QUERY and UPDATE access will be granted. If\n   several codes are used (separated by +), the parameters are selective.\n   Thus, access('QUERY+DELETE') means QUERY and DELETE, but not UPDATE\n   access.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The change(..access()) function can only be used on existing rows. It is\n   therefore meaningless to set the access mode INSERT.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The access can not be changed to a higher level than the one defined by\n   the access declaration or the access defined in Security.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [116][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_widecolumn.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3.
