b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       CHANGE-ELEMENT()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Changes the attributes of an existing [5]element.\n\n   The attributes that can be set for the element are similar to the\n   attributes that can be specified when the element is declared in the\n   application. Main difference is, that the change-element() function only\n   takes expressions for the element attributes.\n\n   The change-element() function should be used instead of the general\n   change() function. Support for the change() function will be discontinued.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   change-element(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[9]handle(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[12]grid-column(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[15]grid-row(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]alignment(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]application(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]background(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]bottom(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]branch-lines(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]buttons(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]colour(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]connect(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]cursor(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]display(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[48]drop-down-lines(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[51]drop-types(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[54]edit-labels(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]end-x(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]end-y(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]focus-behaviour(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]font(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[69]font-angle(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[72]frame(\xc2\xa0[73]?[74]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[75]header(\xc2\xa0[76]?[77]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[78]height(\xc2\xa0[79]?[80]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[81]image(\xc2\xa0[82]?[83]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[84]information(\xc2\xa0[85]?[86]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[87]lock(\xc2\xa0[88]?[89]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[90]mask-character(\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[93]multi-line(\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[96]multi-selection(\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[99]owner(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[102]owner-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[103]?[104]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[105]position(\xc2\xa0[106]?[107]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[108]?[109]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[110]reference-form(\xc2\xa0[111]?[112]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[113]show(\xc2\xa0[114]?[115]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[116]size(\xc2\xa0[117]?[118]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[119]?[120]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0,[121]end-position(\xc2\xa0[122]?[123]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[124]?[125]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[126]sort(\xc2\xa0[127]?[128]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[129]status(\xc2\xa0[130]?[131]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[132]style(\xc2\xa0[133]?[134]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[135]text(\xc2\xa0[136]?[137]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[138]top(\xc2\xa0[139]?[140]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[141]type(\xc2\xa0[142]?[143]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[144]width(\xc2\xa0[145]?[146]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[147]x(\xc2\xa0[148]?[149]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[150]y(\xc2\xa0[151]?[152]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Alignment\n\n   This parameter can be used to specify the vertical and horizontal\n   alignment of the text in an element. The text expression is expected to\n   contain two values separated by a comma. The first value is for the\n   vertical alignment (possible values : DEFAULT,TOP,CENTER and BOTTOM), the\n   second is for the horizontal alignment (possible values: DEFAULT, LEFT,\n   RIGHT and CENTER).\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the element. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out it is assumed that the element belongs to the current sub application.\n   Used together with the name parameter.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the background of the element. See style attribute [153]background\n   for a description of the syntax to be used in the background expression.\n\n   If the background value is empty, the background will be reset to the\n   value defined in the [154]style used by the element.\n\n   When changing elements using a style with different backgrounds for the\n   different states, all states will use the same background.\n\n   Bottom\n\n   Defines the name of a [155]bottom element for the element.\n\n   Branch-lines\n\n   Only valid for use with elements of type TREEVIEW. See element declaration\n   [156]branch-lines for further details. Legal values are ALL,CHILDREN or\n   NONE - default is ALL.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Only valid for use with elements of type TREEVIEW. See element declaration\n   [157]buttons for further details. Legal values are ON or OFF - default is\n   OFF.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Defines the colour to be used on the element. See style attribute\n   [158]colour for a description of the syntax to be used in the colour\n   expression.\n\n   If the colour value is empty, the colour will be reset to the value\n   defined in the [159]style used by the element.\n\n   When changing elements using a style with different colours for the\n   different states, all states will use the same colour.\n\n   Connect\n\n   The expression must evaluate to the name of a field in the current\n   application to which the element should be connected. The element will\n   then display the value represented by this field.\n\n   Cursor\n\n   The expression in this parameter defines the [160]cursor shape that should\n   be used when the mouse pointer is moved over the element.\n\n   Display\n\n   Defines how the textual contents of the element is to be displayed. The\n   parameter is a standard Concept 4GL display code. If display code is not\n   given the display code of the connected field or the display code of the\n   database column the connected field is related to will be used. Unlike the\n   display code on a field, the display code on an element has no other\n   functionality than to specify how a value is shown in an application.\n   Please note that the inquire-element function only returns a value for\n   display if a display code is defined explicitly for the element.\n\n   Specifying an empty display code will remove any display code previously\n   defined on the element.\n\n   Drop-down-lines\n\n   Only valid for use with elements of type DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX or\n   DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX. It indicates the number of lines to be shown when the\n   drop-down box is opened.\n\n   Drop-types\n\n   Defines the accepted [161]drop-types for the element.\n\n   Edit-labels\n\n   Only valid for use with elements of type TREEVIEW. See element declaration\n   [162]edit-labels for further details. Legal values are ON or OFF - default\n   is OFF.\n\n   End-position\n\n   Defines the end position of a line element within its owner. End-position\n   (0,0) indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   End-x\n\n   This parameter is used to give line elements an end column (x) position\n   that is relative to the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the\n   text expression must be a valid [163]size expression, which is further\n   described in . [164]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   End-y\n\n   This parameter is used to give line elements an end line (y) position that\n   is relative to the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [165]size expression, which is further\n   described in . [166]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Focus-Behaviour\n\n   Defines the element's behaviour when it receives the input focus. See the\n   create-element() parameter[167]focus-behaviour for details.\n\n   Font\n\n   Font to be used in the element. See style attribute [168]font for a\n   description of the syntax of a font.\n\n   If the font value is empty, the font will be reset to the value defined in\n   the [169]style used by the element.\n\n   When changing elements using a style with different fonts for the\n   different states, all states will use the same font.\n\n   Font-angle\n\n   Only valid for use with elements of type TEXT. See element declaration\n   [170]font-angle for further details.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Frame used on the element. See style attribute [171]frame for a\n   description of the syntax of a frame.\n\n   If the frame value is empty, the frame will be reset to the value defined\n   in the [172]style used by the element.\n\n   When changing elements using a style with different frames for the\n   different states, all states will use the same frame.\n\n   Grid-column\n\n   The text expression must evaluate to the name of a grid element in the\n   application (not header, top or bottom element). The element found is used\n   to identify a complete column in the grid to which the requested changes\n   are applied.\n\n   The following parameters are allowed when change-element is used with\n   grid-column : [173]alignment, [174]application, [175]background,\n   [176]colour, [177]cursor, [178]display, [179]drop-down-lines,\n   [180]drop-types, [181]focus-behaviour, [182]font, [183]frame, [184]image,\n   [185]information, [186]lock, [187]mask-character, [188]status, [189]style,\n   [190]text, [191]width.\n\n   When changing the [192]width parameter, the change will also include any\n   label, top or bottom elements defined for the grid column.\n\n   Grid-row\n\n   The text expression must evaluate to the name of a grid element in the\n   application (not header, top or bottom element). The element found is used\n   to identify a complete row in the grid to which the requested changes are\n   applied. \xc2\xa0\n\n   The following parameters are allowed when change-element is used with\n   grid-row : [193]alignment, [194]application, [195]background, [196]colour,\n   [197]cursor, [198]display, [199]focus-behaviour, [200]font, [201]frame,\n   [202]information, [203]lock, [204]status, [205]style.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify an element. The result of the text expression must be an integer\n   value that have been obtained using the [206]result parameter of either\n   [207]create-element or [208]inquire-element. The handle parameter enables\n   the change-element and [209]inquire-element functions to change and\n   inquire elements in other applications than the one that is currently\n   active (as long as the element itself exists!).\n\n   Header\n\n   Defines the name of a [210]label element for the element.\n\n   Height\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a height that is relative to\n   the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text expression\n   must be a valid [211]size expression which is further described in .\n   [212]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines an image for the element. See the element declaration [213]image\n   for further details.\n\n   Information\n\n   Defines the tooltips text associated with the element. See the element\n   declaration [214]information for further details.\n\n   Lock\n\n   If an element is locked, the user is not able to navigate (to position the\n   cursor) into the element. Legal values for the lock-parameter are ON, OFF,\n   PERMANENT ON and PERMANENT OFF. See the chapter on [215]locking for more\n   details.\n\n   Mask-character\n\n   If the element is of type INPUT, the actual text is hidden by the\n   character specified. When no parameter is specified in mask-character(),\n   an asterisk ('*') is used as the mask character.\n\n   Multi-line\n\n   The [216]multi-line property can only be changed on TEXT and BUTTON\n   elements.\n\n   Multi-selection\n\n   If this property is set to ON, a LIST-BOX or an opened DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX\n   or DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX element allow selection of more than one item at a\n   time.. Legal values are ON or OFF - default is OFF.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the element in the application.\n\n   Owner\n\n   The result of the expression must be the name of a form within the same\n   stream as the element itself. This form will become the new owner of the\n   element. The element will be moved to this form keeping a position that is\n   the same relative to the top left corner of the new form.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   If the owner form is a [217]tab-form, the owner-tab-index specifies on\n   which tab the element should be placed. See element declaration\n   [218]tab-index for further details\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of the element within its owner. Position (0,0)\n   indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   If an element from an [219]external form file is to be referenced, name\n   the form in this parameter. If this parameter is omitted, the first\n   element that has a name given in the Name parameter is found (which may be\n   the incorrect element).\n\n   Show\n\n   Makes the element visible or hidden. Legal values are ON or OFF - default\n   is ON.\n\n   Size\n\n   Specifies the size of the element in (<vertical size>,<horizontal size>).\n   If the size specified is less than or equal to zero, the element size will\n   be determined dynamically by the space needed to fit the element text on\n   the element.\n\n   Sort\n\n   Changes the sort order associated with the element. See the element\n   declaration [220]sort for details.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [221]status table in the [222]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   The new base [223]style to be used by the element. If the style value is\n   empty, the element will get the default style (based on its type).\n\n   Text\n\n   The text associated with the element. See the element declaration\n   [224]text for further details.\n\n   Top\n\n   Defines the name of a [225]top element for the element.\n\n   Type\n\n   Changes the [226]type of the element. It is possible to change the type of\n   an element to any other type inside the following groups:\n\n   \xc2\xb7PUSH-BUTTON, DEFAULT-BUTTON, COOL-BUTTON, HEADER and MENU-ENTRY\n\n   \xc2\xb7INPUT, OUTPUT, DROW-DOWN-COMBO-BOX and DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX\n\n   Please note that if a PUSH-BUTTON is changed to a DEFAULT-BUTTON, any\n   other DEFAULT-BUTTON in the same window is changed to a PUSH-BUTTON.\n\n   Width\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a width that is relative to the\n   size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text expression must be\n   a valid [227]size expression which is further described in . [228]Relative\n   sizes and positions.\n\n   x\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a column (x) position that can\n   be relative to both it's own size and the size of the form that owns it.\n   The contents of the text expression must be a valid [229]position\n   expression which is further described in . [230]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   y\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a line (y) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form that owns it. The\n   contents of the text expression must be a valid [231]position expression\n   which is further described in . [232]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [233]handle, [234]name, [235]grid-row and [236]grid-column parameters\n   are exclusive\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [237]handle parameter can not be combined with the [238]application\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the [239]handle, [240]name, [241]grid-row or [242]grid-column\n   parameter must be specified..\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the [243]connect parameter fails unless the element identified\n   exists in the current application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [244][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        CHANGE-FORM()                                    side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Changes the attributes of an existing [5]form.\n\n   The attributes that can be set for the form are similar to the attributes\n   that can be specified when the form is declared in the application. Main\n   difference is, that the change-form() function only takes expressions for\n   the form attributes.\n\n   The change-form() function should be used instead of the general change()\n   function. Support for the change() function will be discontinued.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   change-form(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[9]handle(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]active-row-style(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]active-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]allow-resize(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]application(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]background(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]buttons(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]colour(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]drop-types(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]element-sequence(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]font(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]frame(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]grid-lines(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[48]height(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[51]insert-tab(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[54]lock(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]new-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]owner(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]owner-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]position(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[69]?[70]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[71]reference-form(\xc2\xa0[72]?[73]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[74]remove-tab(\xc2\xa0[75]?[76]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[77]show(\xc2\xa0[78]?[79]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[80]size(\xc2\xa0[81]?[82]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[83]?[84]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[85]sort(\xc2\xa0[86]?[87]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[88]sort-header(\xc2\xa0[89]?[90]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[91]status(\xc2\xa0[92]?[93]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[94]style(\xc2\xa0[95]?[96]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[97]tab-index(\xc2\xa0[98]?[99]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[100]title(\xc2\xa0[101]?[102]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[103]view(\xc2\xa0[104]?[105]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[106]width(\xc2\xa0[107]?[108]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[109]x(\xc2\xa0[110]?[111]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[112]y(\xc2\xa0[113]?[114]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Active-row-style\n\n   Only valid when changing grid forms. See the [115]active-row-style\n   declaration on grid forms for further information.\n\n   Active-tab-index\n\n   Only valid when changing tab forms. The expression of the active-tab-index\n   parameter denotes the tab of the tab-form (indicated by the name\n   parameter) that will get focus. This tab will then be shown in the\n   tab-form.\n\n   Allow-resize\n\n   Only valid when changing grid forms. See the [116]allow-resize declaration\n   on grid forms for further information. Legal values are ROW, COLUMNS, BOTH\n   and NONE.\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the form. The sub application must be active and\n   must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left out it\n   is assumed that the form belongs to the current sub application. Used\n   together with the name parameter.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the background of the form. See style attribute [117]background\n   for a description of the syntax to be used in the background expression.\n\n   If the background value is empty, the background will be reset to the\n   value defined in the [118]style used by the form.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Only valid when changing standard grid forms. See the [119]buttons\n   declaration on grid forms for further information. Legal values are ON and\n   OFF\n\n   Colour\n\n   Defines the colour to be used on the title of the form. See style\n   attribute [120]colour for a description of the syntax to be used in the\n   colour expression.\n\n   If the colour value is empty, the colour will be reset to the value\n   defined in the [121]style used by the form.\n\n   Drop-Types\n\n   Only valid when changing listview forms. Defines the [122]drop-types\n   supported by the listview.\n\n   Element-sequence\n\n   Only valid when changing grid forms. See the [123]element-sequence\n   declaration on grid forms for further information.\n\n   Font\n\n   Font used in the title of the form. See style attribute [124]font for a\n   description of the syntax of a font.\n\n   If the font value is empty, the font will be reset to the value defined in\n   the [125]style used by the form.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Frame used on the form. See style attribute [126]frame for a description\n   of the syntax of a frame.\n\n   If the frame value is empty, the frame will be reset to the value defined\n   in the [127]style used by the form.\n\n   Grid-lines\n\n   Only valid when changing grid forms. See the [128]grid-lines declaration\n   on grid forms for further information.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify a form. The result of the text expression must be an integer\n   value that have been obtained using the [129]result parameter of either\n   [130]create-form or [131]inquire-form. The handle parameter enables the\n   change-form and [132]inquire-form functions to change and inquire forms in\n   other applications than the one that is currently active (as long as the\n   form itself exists!).\n\n   Height\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a height that is relative to the\n   size of the form or the stream that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [133]size expression which is further described\n   in . [134]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Insert-tab\n\n   Only valid when changing tab forms. The expression of the insert-tab\n   parameter denotes the tab-index within the tab-form where a new tab should\n   be inserted. Tab indices are ordered sequentially: to append a tab in a\n   tab form with 3 tabs, use tab-index 4 in the insert-tab parameter. The\n   title of the new tab should be specified by the title-parameter. If the\n   result of the expression evaluates to -1 the new tab becomes the last tab\n   of the tab form.\n\n   It is not possible to change a normal form to a tab-form using this\n   parameter.\n\n   Lock\n\n   If the form defines a tab-form and the tab-index parameter is specified\n   the referenced tab is locked/unlocked. If a tab is locked the user is not\n   able to navigate (to position the cursor) on the tab or on any elements of\n   the tab. In this case legal values for the lock-parameter are ON, OFF,\n   PERMANENT ON and PERMANENT OFF.\n\n   If the tab-index parameter is not specified or the form defined is not a\n   tab-form, the lock parameter is applied to all elements belonging to the\n   form. In this case legal values for the lock-parameter are ON and OFF.\n\n   See the chapter on [135]locking for more details.\n\n   Note:\n\n   When individual tabs on a tab form are locked, the cursor is placed on an\n   element on the next visible tab and the tab label is locked. Concept does\n   not lock the elements on the tab that is locked. If all visible tabs on a\n   tab form are locked, there is no next tab to place the cursor on and it\n   therefore stays on the current tab - even if the tab label is locked, the\n   elements are still open. These situations must be handled explicitly, e.g.\n   by hiding the tab form.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the form in the application.\n\n   New-tab-index\n\n   Only valid when changing tab forms. The expression of the new-tab-index\n   parameter denotes the new value of the tab-index of the tab specified in\n   the tab-index parameter. This parameter makes it possible to move tabs in\n   a tab-form.\n\n   The maximum value for new-tab-index is equal to the number of tabs in the\n   tab-form.\n\n   Owner\n\n   Denotes the new owner owning the form. If the owner-expression is set to\n   @TOPLEVEL, ownership of the form is shifted to the stream.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   Denotes the new tab the form is connected to. This parameter is only valid\n   when used with the owner-parameter.\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of the form within its owner. Position (0,0)\n   indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   If a form from an [136]external form file is to be referenced, name the\n   form in this parameter. If this parameter is omitted, the first form that\n   has a name given in the Name parameter is found (which may be an incorrect\n   form).\n\n   Remove-tab\n\n   Only valid when changing tab forms. Denotes the tab of the tab-form\n   (indicated by the name parameter) that is to be removed. Please note that\n   the tab-index of any subsequent tabs will be decremented by one.\n\n   Show\n\n   Changes the visibility of a form. Legal values are ON and OFF.\n\n   If a tab-index is specified, this tab on the tab form is either hidden or\n   displayed. When only one tab on the tab form is visible, making this tab\n   hidden will cause the whole form to be hidden.\n\n   Size\n\n   Changes the size of the form.\n\n   Sort\n\n   Only valid when changing dynamic grid forms.\n\n   Enables local sorting of rows based on a column of a dynamic grid. The\n   expression must return the name of an element that belongs to the grid\n   (not including header elements), or blank to turn of local sorting. An\n   element name may be preceded by a '>' or a '<' to indicate ascending (the\n   default) or descending sort respectively. Please note that the sorting is\n   only done when the requested element is a part of the\n   [137]element-sequence of the grid.\n\n   Sort-Header\n\n   Only valid when changing grid forms.\n\n   Use this command to specify the name of the header element that should\n   show arrows to visualise the current sort order of the grid (an empty\n   value means no arrows should be displayed). The name of the header element\n   can be prefixed with '<' or '>' indicating which arrow to show, '<' is the\n   sort descending arrow and '>' is the sort ascending arrow (default).\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [138]status table in the [139]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   The [140]style used by form. If the style value is empty, the form will\n   get the default style (based on its type).\n\n   Tab-index\n\n   Only valid when changing tab forms. This parameter is used in combination\n   with new-tab-index (to move the tab from position tab-index to position\n   new-tab-index) and with the title-parameter (to change the title of a\n   single tab).\n\n   Title\n\n   Change the title of the form. If the tab-index parameter is also\n   specified, then the title of the identified tab will be changed. Not valid\n   when changing grid forms.\n\n   View\n\n   Changes the view of a [141]listview form. Possible parameter values are\n   'LARGE' (large icons), 'SMALL' (small icons), 'LIST' (list) and 'REPORT'\n   (details).\n\n   Width\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a width that is relative to the\n   size of the form or stream that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [142]size expression which is further described\n   in . [143]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   x\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a column (x) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form or stream that\n   owns it. The contents of the text expression must be a valid [144]position\n   expression which is further described in . [145]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   y\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a line (y) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form or stream that\n   owns it. The contents of the text expression must be a valid [146]position\n   expression which is further described in . [147]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The handle parameter can not be combined with the name or application\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the handle or name parameter must be specified..\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [148][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changeelement.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       CHANGE-SESSION()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Changes attributes of the current Concept session.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   change-session([[5]cursor(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]focus-thread(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]numericExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]thread-handle(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]numericExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]hourglass(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]lock(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]show(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]status(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Cursor\n\n   The expression in this parameter defines the cursor shape that should be\n   used when the mouse pointer is moved over a window in the specified\n   thread. \xc2\xa0Specifying a blank value turns cursor handling back to default.\n\n   Note that the cursor setting will overrule any default cursor handling\n   such as the WAIT cursor and cursors defined on elements belonging to\n   windows of the thread. See [26]Cursor definition for more details.\n\n   Focus-Thread\n\n   Identifies the thread that is to get user focus.\n\n   Thread-handle\n\n   A unique identifier for a single thread in the session. Legal values can\n   be obtained from "@THREAD_HANDLE", "@THREAD_LIST" or inquire-session with\n   the focus-thread parameter.\n\n   Hourglass\n\n   The text expression must evaluate to either \'OFF\' or \'DEFAULT\'. If set to\n   \'OFF\' the default handling for the WAIT cursor is turned off (the WAIT\n   cursor is shown by default when Concept starts a potential long lasting\n   operation). If set to \'DEFAULT\' the default handling for the WAIT cursor\n   is turned on.\n\n   Lock\n\n   The text expression must evaluate to either OFF, ON, 0 or 1. If set to ON\n   or 1, the thread identified by the thread-handle parameter will not be\n   able to receive input anymore, otherwise it will be unlocked.\n\n   Show\n\n   If the parameter value is empty, no action will be performed.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Expression value   Handle        Result\n                                    The window of the topmost application in\n                                    the thread identified by the\n                                    [27]thread-handle parameter will be put\n   TOP                Specified     in the foreground (on top of all other\n                                    windows). Please remember that windows of\n                                    type [28]POPUP or [29]TOOLBOX always will\n                                    be on top of "normal" windows.\n   TOP                Not specified Error ($UE_SHOW)\n                                    The top window of \xc2\xa0the thread identified\n                                    by the [30]thread-handle parameter will\n   FLASHING           Specified     start to flash the caption bar (change\n                                    from active to inactive state) until the\n                                    user activates the window.\n                                    The Concept main window and \xc2\xa0taskbar\n   FLASHING           Not specified button will start to flash (change from\n                                    active to inactive state) until the user\n                                    activates the Concept session.\n   MINIMIZED          Not specified Minimizes the Concept main window.\n   MAXIMIZED          Not specified Maximizes the Concept main window.\n   NORMAL             Not specified Restores the Concept main window to its\n                                    normal state.\n   MINIMIZED |        Specified     Error ($UE_SHOW). Use the\n   MAXIMIZED | NORMAL               [31]change-stream function.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status\n\n   Numeric field to receive the status of the operation. Possible values\n   include:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                    Description\n   $OK                       Operation was successful\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_THREAD_HANDLE The thread-handle or focus-thread parameter\n                             specified an illegal value.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_VALUE         The value for the hourglass parameter was\n                             illegal.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ONOFF         The value for the lock parameter was illegal\n   $UE_SHOW                  The value for the show parameter was illegal\n\n   (see [32]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When changing the focus, the [33]@FOCUS-GAINED event handler of the\n   thread receiving the focus will be executed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The thread-handle parameter must be specified when the cursor and/or the\n   hourglass parameter is used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When changing the cursor the cursor shape is not changed unless the mouse\n   pointer is located inside a window belonging to the thread specified.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The cursor shape is automatically updated when the mouse pointer is moved\n   or when Concept refreshes the screen. To ensure that a cursor shape is\n   updated immediately, use the [34]refresh function.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [35][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changeform.htm\n \xc2\xa0[,[36]duplex(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]frame(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]lb(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]numberExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]maximum-size(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[50]minimum-size(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[53]?[54]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[55]new-page(\xc2\xa0[56]?[57]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[58]ob(\xc2\xa0[59]?[60]numberExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[61]orientation(\xc2\xa0[62]?[63]numberExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[64]position(\xc2\xa0[65]?[66]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[69]pixel-position(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[72]?[73]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[74]show(\xc2\xa0[75]?[76]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[77]size(\xc2\xa0[78]?[79]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[80]?[81]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[82]pixel-size(\xc2\xa0[83]?[84]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[85]?[86]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[87]status(\xc2\xa0[88]?[89]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[90]tb(\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]numberExpression)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[93]title(\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[96]update-footer(\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[99]update-header(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Accelerators\n\n   Changes the list of characters that should be returned in the\n   [102]ACCELERATOR key command. The command is triggered when the\n   combination of the ALT key and a character in the list is pressed. In this\n   case the [103]@EVENT_PARAM field will contain the character pressed.\n   Please note that the accelerator keys have precedence over accelerator\n   keys defined in the menu and on elements in the application.\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the stream. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out, it is assumed that the stream belongs to the current sub application.\n\n   Background\n\n   Changes the background of the stream. See style attribute [104]background\n   for a description of the syntax to be used in the background expression.\n\n   If the background value is empty, the background will be reset to the\n   value defined in the [105]style used by the stream.\n\n   Bb\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the bottom border of the stream for the following\n   pages. Please note that if the bottom border is set less than the height\n   of page-tail forms written to the stream, the end result is unpredictable.\n   See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Bin-in\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the [106]source tray (bin) for the following pages. See\n   the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the colour mode for the following pages. The value OFF\n   sets the printer to monochrome mode, the value ON turns colour printing on\n   (if supported by the printer). . See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   If the colour value is empty, the colour will be reset to the value\n   defined in the [107]style used by the stream.\n\n   Copies\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the number of copies for the following pages. See the\n   Rules section for more details.\n\n   Docking\n\n   Changes the docking state of the stream.\n\n   Duplex\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the duplex settings for the next page to be printed and\n   all following pages. The text expression must evaluate to one of the\n   following values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value      Description\n   OFF        Normal (non duplex) printing.\n   HORIZONTAL Short-edge binding, that is, the long edge of the page is\n              horizontal.\n   VERTICAL   Long-edge binding, that is, the long edge of the page is\n              vertical.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Frame used on the stream. See style attribute [108]frame for a description\n   of the syntax of a frame.\n\n   If the frame value is empty, the frame will be reset to the value defined\n   in the [109]style used by the stream.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify a stream. The result of the text expression must be an integer\n   value that have been obtained using the [110]result parameter of the\n   [111]inquire-stream function. The handle parameter enables the\n   change-stream and [112]inquire-stream functions to change and inquire\n   streams in other applications than the one that is currently active (as\n   long as the stream itself exists!).\n\n   lb\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the left border of the stream for the following pages.\n   See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Maximum-Size\n\n   Defines the maximum size of the application window in element units. The\n   window cannot be sized beyond this limit, and it cannot be maximized. If\n   the current size of the window is larger than the specified maximum size,\n   the window is automatically resized.\n\n   Minimum-Size\n\n   Defines the minimum size of the application window in element units. The\n   window cannot be sized beyond this limit. If the current size of the\n   window is less than the specified minimum size, the window is\n   automatically resized.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the stream in the application.\n\n   New-page\n\n   Xtra only. New-page('ON') will force a page shift on the stream before the\n   next form is written. New-page('OFF') can be used to turn off a forced\n   page shift. See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Ob\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the right border of the stream for the following pages.\n   See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Orientation\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the orientation of the stream for the following pages.\n   Legal values are 1 (Portrait) and 2 (Landscape). If the pw and pl\n   declarations are not set for the stream, the page size for the stream will\n   be adjusted to the page orientation and the following output for the\n   stream will be according to the new sizes. See the Rules section for more\n   details.\n\n   Position, Pixel-Position\n\n   Defines the position of the stream on the Concept desktop (in element\n   units for position or pixels for pixel-position). Position (0,0) indicates\n   the upper left corner of the desktop. Changing the position of the stream\n   with this function will not trigger a [113]WINMOVE event.\n\n   Show\n\n   Changes the display mode of the window. The text expression must evaluate\n   to one of the following values: NORMAL, HIDDEN, MAXIMIZED or MINIMIZED.\n   Can only be used in ONLINE applications.\n\n   Size, Pixel-Size\n\n   Specifies the size of the stream in (in element units for size or pixels\n   for pixel-size). Changing the size of the stream with this function will\n   not trigger a [114]WINSIZE event.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [115]status table in the [116]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   Changes the [117]style used by stream.\n\n   tb\n\n   Xtra only. Changes the top border of the stream for the following pages.\n   Please note that if the top border is set less than the height of\n   page-heading forms written to the stream, the end result is unpredictable.\n   See the Rules section for more details.\n\n   Title\n\n   Changes the title for the stream.\n\n   Update-footer\n\n   Xtra only. If the stream is writing to a file using the extended file\n   interface (which is able to handle advanced colour attributes and table\n   creation in the resulting document - e.g. in the RTF document interface),\n   this parameter can be used to force an update of the footer in the\n   resulting document. If an element in a [118]page-tail form is changed\n   (e.g. by using the change-element() function), this change will not be\n   visible until a change-stream() has been issued with update-footer('ON').\n   The updated footer will be visible on the 'next' page.\n\n   If an update-footer('OFF') is issued on the same document page on which an\n   update-footer('ON') was issued previously, the footer will not be updated.\n\n   This parameter is of course only useful when the [119]formatting property\n   on the stream is not equal to 'NONE', because in that case the footer\n   handling is left to the 4GL programmer who has to program an explicit\n   print-form() on the page-tail form.\n\n   Legal values are ON and OFF.\n\n   Update-header\n\n   Xtra only. If the stream is writing to a file using the extended file\n   interface, this parameter can be used to force an update of the header in\n   the resulting document. If an element in a [120]page-heading form is\n   changed, this change will not be visible until a change-stream() has been\n   issued with update-header('ON'). The updated header will be visible on the\n   'next' page.\n\n   If an update-header('OFF') is issued on the same document page on which an\n   update-header('ON') was issued previously, the header will not be updated.\n\n   This parameter is of course only useful when the [121]formatting property\n   on the stream is not equal to 'NONE', because in that case the header\n   handling is left to the 4GL programmer who has to program an explicit\n   print-form() on a the page-heading form.\n\n   Legal values are ON and OFF.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The handle parameter can not be combined with the name, application, bb,\n   bin-in, colour, copies, duplex, lb, new-page, ob, orientation and tb\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the handle or name parameter must be specified..\n\n   \xc2\xb7The bin-in, duplex, colour and copies parameters are ignored if the\n   identified stream is not directed to a printer.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The tb, bb, lb,ob, new-page and orientation parameters will not be\n   applied if the identified stream has formatting(NONE) and is directed to a\n   file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Changes to the tb, bb, lb,ob, bin-in, colour, copies, duplex and\n   orientation parameters are always applied to the next and following pages\n   and not the current. Changes done before the first form is written to a\n   stream (before the [122]@OPEN event is triggered on the stream) are\n   applied to the first and all following pages.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       CREATE-ELEMENT()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Creates a new [5]element on a given form.\n\n   The attributes that can be set for the new element are similar to the\n   attributes that can be specified when the element is declared in the\n   application. Main difference is, that the create-element() function only\n   takes expressions for the form attributes.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   create-element(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]alignment(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]application(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]background(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]bottom(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]branch-lines(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]buttons(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]check(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]colour(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]connect(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]cursor(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]display(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]drop-down-lines(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]drop-types(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[48]edit-labels(\xc2\xa0[49]?[50]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[51]end-x(\xc2\xa0[52]?[53]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[54]end-y(\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]focus-behaviour(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]font(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]font-angle(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]fomatting(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[69]frame(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[72]header(\xc2\xa0[73]?[74]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[75]height(\xc2\xa0[76]?[77]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[78]image(\xc2\xa0[79]?[80]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[81]information\xc2\xa0(\xc2\xa0[82]?[83]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[84]lock(\xc2\xa0[85]?[86]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[87]mask-character(\xc2\xa0[88]?[89]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[90]multi-line(\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[93]multi-selection(\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[96]owner(\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[99]owner-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[102]position(\xc2\xa0[103]?[104]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[105]?[106]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[107]reference-form(\xc2\xa0[108]?[109]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[110]result(\xc2\xa0[111]?[112]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[113]show(\xc2\xa0[114]?[115]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[116]size(\xc2\xa0[117]?[118]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[119]?[120]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[121]end-position(\xc2\xa0[122]?[123]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[124]?[125]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[126]status(\xc2\xa0[127]?[128]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[129]style(\xc2\xa0[130]?[131]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[132]text(\xc2\xa0[133]?[134]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[135]top(\xc2\xa0[136]?[137]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[138]type(\xc2\xa0[139]?[140]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[141]width(\xc2\xa0[142]?[143]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[144]x(\xc2\xa0[145]?[146]positionExpression)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[147]y(\xc2\xa0[148]?[149]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Alignment\n\n   This parameter can be used to specify the vertical and horizontal\n   alignment of the text in an element. The text expression is expected to\n   contain two values separated by a comma. The first value is for the\n   vertical alignment (possible values : DEFAULT,TOP,CENTER and BOTTOM), the\n   second is for the horizontal alignment (possible values: DEFAULT, LEFT,\n   RIGHT and CENTER).\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the element. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out it is assumed that the element belongs to the current sub application.\n   Used together with the name parameter.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the background of the element. See style attribute [150]background\n   for a description of the syntax to be used in the background expression.\n\n   Bottom\n\n   Defines the name of a [151]bottom element for the element.\n\n   Branch-lines\n\n   Only valid when used for creation of TREEVIEW elements. See element\n   declaration [152]branch-lines for further details. Legal values are\n   ALL,CHILDREN or NONE - default is ALL.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Only valid when used for creation of TREEVIEW elements. See element\n   declaration [153]buttons for further details. Legal values are ON or OFF -\n   default is OFF.\n\n   Check\n\n   Only valid when used for creation of TREEVIEW elements. See element\n   declaration [154]check for further details. Legal values are ON or OFF -\n   default is OFF.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Defines the colour to be used on the element. See style attribute\n   [155]colour for a description of the syntax to be used in the colour\n   expression.\n\n   Connect\n\n   The expression in this parameter is the name of the field in the current\n   application to which the element must be connected. The element will then\n   display the value represented by this field.\n\n   Cursor\n\n   The expression in this parameter defines the [156]cursor shape that should\n   be used when the mouse pointer is moved over the element.\n\n   Display\n\n   Defines how the textual contents of the element is to be displayed. The\n   parameter is a standard Concept 4GL display code. If display code is not\n   given the display code of the connected field or the display code of the\n   database column the connected field is related to will be used. Unlike the\n   display code on a field, the display code on an element has no other\n   functionality than to specify how a value is shown in an application.\n   Please note that the inquire-element function only returns a value for\n   display if a display code is defined explicitly for the element.\n\n   Drop-down-lines\n\n   This parameter is only valid when used with the type-parameter set to\n   DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX or DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX. It indicates the number of\n   lines to be shown when the drop-down box is opened.\n\n   Drop-types\n\n   Defines the accepted [157]drop-types for the element.\n\n   Edit-labels\n\n   Only valid when used for creation of TREEVIEW elements. See element\n   declaration [158]edit-labels for further details. Legal values are ON or\n   OFF - default is OFF.\n\n   End-position\n\n   Defines the end position of a line element within its owner. End-position\n   (0,0) indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   End-x\n\n   This parameter is used to give line elements an end column (x) position\n   that is relative to the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the\n   text expression must be a valid [159]size expression, which is further\n   described in . [160]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   End-y\n\n   This parameter is used to give line elements an end line (y) position that\n   is relative to the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [161]size expression, which is further\n   described in . [162]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Focus-Behaviour\n\n   This property can be used to specify the element's behaviour when it\n   receives the input focus. The parameter value must evaluate to one of the\n   following values:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value           Description\n                   The original style of the element is to be used when the\n   NO-STYLE-CHANGE element has the input focus. This prevents e.g. the\n                   highlighting of the current element in a grid-form.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   An empty parameter value turns off all focus behaviours.\n\n   Font\n\n   Font to be used in the element. See style attribute [163]font for a\n   description of the syntax of a font.\n\n   Font-angle\n\n   Only valid when used for creation of TEXT elements. See element\n   declaration [164]font-angle for further details.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   [165]Formatting used on multi-line elements of type 'INPUT' or 'OUTPUT'.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Frame used on the new element. See style attribute [166]frame for a\n   description of the syntax of a frame.\n\n   Header\n\n   Defines the name of a [167]label element for the element.\n\n   Height\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a height that is relative to\n   the size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text expression\n   must be a valid [168]size expression which is further described in .\n   [169]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Image\n\n   How the image parameter is used in the create-element() function depends\n   on the type-parameter. Read the topic on [170]elements to find out more\n   about the use of images.\n\n   Information\n\n   Defines the tooltips text associated with the new element. The combination\n   '/,' can be used in the text to force line breaks.\n\n   Lock\n\n   If an element is locked, the user is not able to navigate (to position the\n   cursor) into the element. Legal values for the lock-parameter are ON and\n   OFF - default is OFF.\n\n   Mask-character\n\n   If the element is of type INPUT, the actual text is hidden by a the\n   character specified. When no parameter is specified in mask-character(),\n   an asterisk ('*') is used as masking character.\n\n   Multi-line\n\n   [171]Multi-line property of the element.\n\n   Multi-selection\n\n   If this property is set to ON, a LIST-BOX or an opened DROP-DOWN-LIST-BOX\n   or DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX element allow selection of more than one item at a\n   time.. Legal values are ON or OFF - default is OFF.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the element in the application.\n\n   Owner\n\n   The new element will be owned by the form given in the expression of the\n   owner-parameter. An element owned by a form will appear inside the owner\n   form.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   If the owner form is a [172]tab-form, the owner-tab-index specifies on\n   which tab the new element should be placed. See element declaration\n   [173]tab-index for further details\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of the new element within its owner. Position (0,0)\n   indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   If an element from an [174]external form file is to be referenced, name\n   the form in this parameter. If this parameter is omitted, the first\n   element that has a name given in the Name parameter is found (which may be\n   the incorrect element).\n\n   Result\n\n   The field specified by the result parameter will receive an internal\n   unique identifier of the element created. The returned value can be used\n   in any subsequent calls to [175]inquire-element or [176]change-element\n   using the [177]handle parameter. The value returned is an integer4 value.\n\n   Please note that when the element is deleted (either by the\n   [178]delete-element function or when the application is terminated) the\n   identifier value may be reused by another element, form or stream.\n\n   Show\n\n   Makes the element visible or hidden. Legal values are ON or OFF - default\n   is ON.\n\n   Size\n\n   Specifies the size of the new element in (<vertical size>,<horizontal\n   size>). If the size specified is less than or equal to zero, the element\n   size will be determined dynamically by the space needed to fit the element\n   text on the element.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. Possible error\n   values are given in the [179]status table below:\n\n   Style\n\n   The [180]style used by element. If this parameter is not specified, the\n   default style for elements is used.\n\n   Text\n\n   The text associated with the element. For PUSH-BUTTONS this is the text on\n   the button, for RADIO-BUTTONS this is the text next to the button, etc.\n\n   Top\n\n   Defines the name of a [181]top element for the element.\n\n   Type\n\n   Defines the element type that will be created. The possible element types\n   can be found in the [182]element topic.\n\n   Width\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a width that is relative to the\n   size of the form that owns it. The contents of the text expression must be\n   a valid [183]size expression which is further described in . [184]Relative\n   sizes and positions.\n\n   x\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a column (x) position that can\n   be relative to both it's own size and the size of the form that owns it.\n   The contents of the text expression must be a valid [185]position\n   expression which is further described in . [186]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   y\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a line (y) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form that owns it. The\n   contents of the text expression must be a valid [187]position expression\n   which is further described in . [188]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The owner,type and position (or x and y) parameters are mandatory.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The size parameter can not be used for line type elements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The end-position,end-x,end-y parameters can only be used for line type\n   elements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The height, width,end-y and end-x parameters can not be combined with the\n   size parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The y and x parameters can not be combined with the position parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The multi-line parameter can only be used for INPUT, OUTPUT and TEXT\n   elements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the connect parameter fails unless the element is created in the\n   current application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Possible status values returned by create/change and\n   inquire-element/form/stream.\n\n   (See [189]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND     The element/form referenced by the name or handle\n                     -parameter was not found.\n   $UE_DUPLICATE     An element or a form with this name already exists\n   $UE_CONNECT       The field the element should be connected to, cannot be\n                     found\n                     The element type given is not valid. May also be\n   $UE_TYPE          returned if a special parameter (like multi-line) is\n                     used with an element type that doesn't allow the\n                     combination.\n   $UE_OWNER         The element cannot be owned by this owner; or the owner\n                     does not exist\n   $UE_LOCK          The lock-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_SHOW          The show-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_POSITION      The position-parameter contains an error (like negative\n                     values)\n   $UE_COLOUR        The colour-parameter is not recognized as a legal colour\n                     syntax\n   $UE_BACKGROUND    The background-parameter is not recognized as a legal\n                     background syntax\n   $UE_FRAME         The frame-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_FONT          The font-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_STYLE         The style-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_TAB   The tab index specified is outside the range of legal\n                     tabs (between 1 and the number of tabs available + 1)\n   $UE_TAB_NOT_FOUND The tab specified was not found in the tab-form\n                     indicated\n                     The function cannot be executed because the element or\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_NOW   form is not available yet (e.g. if change-element() is\n                     used in a field with an initial value)\n   $UE_APPLICATION   Illegal sub application specified.\n   $UE_END_POSITION  The end-position parameter contains an error\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED The requested operation is not supported. E.g. setting\n                     size on a line element\n   $UE_ALIGNMENT     The alignment-parameter contains an error\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_CMD   Invalid parameter to a sub command.\n   $UE_UNKNOWN_FIELD A field specified in one of the inquire functions did\n                     not exist.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ONOFF An illegal on off value was specified.\n   $UE_DISPLAY       An illegal display code was specified.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [190][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changestream.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        CREATE-FORM()                                    side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Creates a [5]form on the current stream at run-time.\n\n   The attributes that can be set for the new form are similar to the\n   attributes that can be specified when the form is declared in the\n   application. Main difference is, that the create-form() function only\n   takes expressions for the form attributes.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   create-form(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]application(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]background(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]colour(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]font(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]formatting(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]frame(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]height(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[30]owner(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]owner-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[36]position(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[41]result(\xc2\xa0[42]?[43]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[44]show(\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[47]size(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[50]?[51]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[52]status(\xc2\xa0[53]?[54]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[55]style(\xc2\xa0[56]?[57]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[58]tab-depth(\xc2\xa0[59]?[60]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[61]title(\xc2\xa0[62]?[63]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[64]width(\xc2\xa0[65]?[66]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[67]x(\xc2\xa0[68]?[69]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[70]y(\xc2\xa0[71]?[72]positionExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application to which the form belongs. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out it is assumed that the form should be created in the current sub\n   application.\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the background of the form. See style attribute [73]background for\n   a description of the syntax to be used in the background expression.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Defines the colour to be used in the form. See style attribute [74]colour\n   for a description of the syntax to be used in the colour expression.\n\n   Font\n\n   Default font for the form. See style attribute [75]font for a description\n   of the syntax of a font.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   [76]Formatting used on the new form.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Frame used on the new form. See style attribute [77]frame for a\n   description of the syntax of a frame.\n\n   Height\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a height that is relative to the\n   size of the form or the stream that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [78]size expression which is further described\n   in . [79]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the new form in the stream.\n\n   Owner\n\n   The new form will be owned by the form given in the expression of the\n   owner-parameter. A form owned by another form will appear inside the owner\n   form. If this parameter is set to @TOPLEVEL, the owner will be the current\n   stream. When using the create-form function in XTRA applications the form\n   must always be in the hierarchy of a form defined in the application in\n   order to have the form printed (the print-form function requires an\n   existing form) In XTRA all forms owned by a defined form is written along\n   with the defined form.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   If the owner form is a [80]tab-form, the owner-tab-index specifies on\n   which tab the new form should be placed. This parameter may only be used\n   if the owner-parameter is specified as well.\n\n   Position\n\n   Defines the position of the new form within its owner. Position (0,0)\n   indicates the upper left corner of the owner.\n\n   Result\n\n   The field specified by the result parameter will receive an internal\n   unique identifier of the form created. The returned value can be used in\n   any subsequent calls to [81]inquire-form or [82]change-form using the\n   [83]handle parameter. The value returned is an integer4 value.\n\n   Please note that when the element is deleted (either by the\n   [84]delete-form function or when the application is terminated) the\n   identifier value may be reused by another element, form or stream.\n\n   Show\n\n   Makes the form visible or hidden. Legal values are ON or OFF - default is\n   ON.\n\n   Size\n\n   Specifies the size of the new form in (<vertical size>,<horizontal size>).\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [85]status table in the [86]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   The [87]style used by form. If this parameter is not specified, the\n   default style for forms is used.\n\n   Tab-depth\n\n   If the new form should be a tab-form, then this parameter specifies the\n   number of tabs in the new form.\n\n   Title\n\n   Title used for the form. For tab-forms, this text must be a semicolon\n   separated list of the titles of the different tabs.\n\n   Width\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a width that is relative to the\n   size of the form or stream that owns it. The contents of the text\n   expression must be a valid [88]size expression which is further described\n   in . [89]Relative sizes and positions.\n\n   x\n\n   This parameter is used to give the form a column (x) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form or stream that\n   owns it. The contents of the text expression must be a valid [90]position\n   expression which is further described in . [91]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   y\n\n   This parameter is used to give the element a line (y) position that can be\n   relative to both it's own size and the size of the form or stream that\n   owns it. The contents of the text expression must be a valid [92]position\n   expression which is further described in . [93]Relative sizes and\n   positions.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The owner and position (or x and y) parameters are mandatory.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The height and width parameters can not be combined with the size\n   parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The y and x parameters can not be combined with the position parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [94][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       DELETE-ELEMENT()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Deletes an existing [5]element.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   delete-element(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]application(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]reference-form(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]status(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the element. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out it is assumed that the element belongs to the current sub application.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the element in the current application.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   If an element from an [18]external form file is to be referenced, name the\n   form in this parameter.
