\xc2\xa0[,[140]text(\xc2\xa0[141]?[142]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[143]top(\xc2\xa0[144]?[145]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[146]type(\xc2\xa0[147]?[148]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[149]width(\xc2\xa0[150]?[151]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[152]x(\xc2\xa0[153]?[154]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[155]y(\xc2\xa0[156]?[157]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Alignment\n\n   Returns the [158]alignment defined on the element.\n\n   Application\n\n   See the [159]application parameter on [160]create-element.\n\n   Background\n\n   Returns the style attribute [161]background for the element\n\n   Bottom\n\n   Returns the [162]bottom of the element.\n\n   Branch-lines\n\n   Returns the [163]branch-lines setting for treeview elements.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Returns an on/off value that reflects the setting of the [164]button\n   declaration for treeview elements.\n\n   Check\n\n   Returns an on/off value that reflects the setting of the [165]check\n   declaration for treeview elements.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Returns the style attribute [166]colour for the element\n\n   Connect\n\n   Returns the name of the field [167]connected to the element.\n\n   Cursor\n\n   Returns the current cursor definition for the element.\n\n   Display\n\n   Returns the [168]display code explicitly defined for the element. NB! It\n   does not return the display code of the connected field.\n\n   Drop-down-lines\n\n   Returns the [169]drop-down-lines setting for drop-down-list-box and\n   drop-down-combo-box elements.\n\n   Drop-types\n\n   Returns the [170]drop-types setting for the element.\n\n   Edit-labels\n\n   Returns an on/off value that reflects the setting of the [171]edit-labels\n   declaration for treeview elements.\n\n   End-position\n\n   Returns the actual Y and X position in element units for the end point of\n   a line element. Positions are always defined relative to the top left\n   corner of the owner. See the element declaration [172]end-position for\n   more details.\n\n   End-x\n\n   Returns the [173]X position expression for the end point of a line element\n   if defined, or the actual X position of the end point if not.\n\n   End-y\n\n   Returns the [174]Y position expression for the end point of a line element\n   if defined, or the actual X position of the end point if not.\n\n   Focus-Behaviour\n\n   Returns the focus behaviour of the element. See the create-element()\n   parameter[175]focus-behaviour for details.\n\n   Font\n\n   Returns the style attribute [176]font for the element.\n\n   Font-angle\n\n   Returns the font-angle defined on TEXT elements. See element declaration\n   [177]font-angle for further details.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   Returns the [178]formatting attribute of the element.\n\n   Frame\n\n   Returns the style attribute [179]frame for the element\n\n   Handle\n\n   See the [180]handle parameter on [181]change-element.\n\n   Header\n\n   Returns the [182]header of the element.\n\n   Height\n\n   Returns the [183]height expression if defined or the actual height of the\n   element if not.\n\n   Image\n\n   Returns any [184]image definitions for the element.\n\n   Information\n\n   Returns any [185]information (tool tips) definitions for the element.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the [186]lock status of the\n   element.\n\n   Mask-character\n\n   Returns any [187]mask-character definitions for the element.\n\n   Multi-line\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the [188]multi-line setting of the\n   element.\n\n   Multi-selection\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the [189]multi-selection setting of\n   the element.\n\n   Name\n\n   Name of the element that is to be inquired.\n\n   Owner\n\n   Returns the name of the form that owns the element.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   If the owner of the element is a tab form it returns the tab index on\n   which the identified element is placed. See the element declaration\n   [190]tab-index for more details.\n\n   Position\n\n   Returns the actual Y and X position in element units for the element.\n   Positions are always defined relative to the top left corner of the owner.\n   See the element declaration [191]position for more details.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   See the [192]reference-form parameter on [193]create-element.\n\n   Result\n\n   If the name parameter is specified it returns an internal unique\n   identifier of the element identified. The returned value can be used in\n   any subsequent calls to inquire-element or change-element using the handle\n   parameter. The value returned is an integer4 value. Please note that when\n   the element is deleted (either by the delete-element function or when the\n   application is terminated) the identifier value may be reused by another\n   element, form or stream.\n\n   If the handle parameter is used it returns the name of the identified\n   element.\n\n   Show\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the visibility of the element.\n\n   Size\n\n   Returns the actual height and width in element units for the element. If\n   the element's height or width initially was set to be dynamic (using 0),\n   negative values are returned . See the element declaration [194]size for\n   more details.\n\n   Sort\n\n   Returns the sort order associated with the element. See the element\n   declaration [195]sort for details.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [196]status table in the [197]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   Returns the name of the base [198]style used by the element.\n\n   Text\n\n   Returns the value of the element.\n\n   Top\n\n   Returns the [199]top of the element.\n\n   Type\n\n   Returns the [200]type of the element.\n\n   Width\n\n   Returns the [201]width expression if defined or the actual width of the\n   element if not.\n\n   X\n\n   Returns the [202]X position expression if defined or the actual X position\n   of the element if not.\n\n   Y\n\n   Returns the [203]Y position expression if defined or the actual Y position\n   of the element if not.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The end-y and-x parameters can only be used for line elements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The size,height and width parameters can not be used for line elements.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The y, x, height, width, end-y and-x parameters returns an empty string\n   if the requested size or position is a constant and not an expression.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The handle parameter can not be combined with the name or application\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the handle or name parameter must be specified..\n\n   \xc2\xb7on/off values is either 0 or 1 if the receiving field is numeric or\n   ON/OFF if the receiving field is alphanumeric\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using the connect parameter fails unless the element identified exists in\n   the current application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [204][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inquire.htm\n   2. b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        INQUIRE-FORM()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Retrieves the current attributes of a [5]form.\n\n   A form, either declared in an application or created dynamically using the\n   [6]create-form() function, has a set of attributes that can be fetched\n   using the inquire-form() function. By using this function, attributes that\n   do not have a certain wanted value, can be modified using the\n   [7]change-form() function.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   inquire-form(\xc2\xa0[8]name(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[11]handle(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]active-row-style(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]active-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]allow-resize(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]application(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]background(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]buttons(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[32]colour(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[35]elements(\xc2\xa0[36]?[37]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[38]element-sequence(\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[41]font(\xc2\xa0[42]?[43]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[44]frame(\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[47]grid-lines(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[50]height(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[53]lock(\xc2\xa0[54]?[55]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[56]member-elements(\xc2\xa0[57]?[58]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[59]member-forms(\xc2\xa0[60]?[61]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[62]mode(\xc2\xa0[63]?[64]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[65]owner(\xc2\xa0[66]?[67]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[68]owner-tab-index(\xc2\xa0[69]?[70]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[71]position(\xc2\xa0[72]?[73]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[74]?[75]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[76]reference-form(\xc2\xa0[77]?[78]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[79]result(\xc2\xa0[80]?[81]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[82]separator(\xc2\xa0[83]?[84]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[85]show(\xc2\xa0[86]?[87]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[88]size(\xc2\xa0[89]?[90]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[93]status(\xc2\xa0[94]?[95]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[96]style(\xc2\xa0[97]?[98]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[99]tab-depth(\xc2\xa0[100]?[101]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[102]tab-index(\xc2\xa0[103]?[104]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[105]title(\xc2\xa0[106]?[107]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[108]type(\xc2\xa0[109]?[110]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[111]width(\xc2\xa0[112]?[113]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[114]x(\xc2\xa0[115]?[116]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[117]y(\xc2\xa0[118]?[119]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Active-row-style\n\n   Returns a value that reflects the setting of the [120]active-row-style\n   declaration on grid forms.\n\n   Active-tab-index\n\n   When the form identified is a tab form, this parameter will return the\n   index of the tab in the tab-form that has focus (or: that is shown in the\n   tab-form).\n\n   Allow-resize\n\n   Returns a value that reflects the setting of the [121]allow-resize\n   declaration on grid forms.\n\n   Application\n\n   See the [122]application parameter on [123]create-form.\n\n   Background\n\n   Returns the style attribute [124]background of the form\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Returns an on/off value that reflects the setting of the [125]button\n   declaration on grid forms.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Returns the style attribute [126]colour of the form\n\n   Elements\n\n   The field name given in this parameter needs to be declared as an\n   alphanumeric field. After the inquire-form() call, this field will contain\n   a list of either names or handles (dependent on the mode parameter) for\n   all elements and forms owned directly by the form. Each list member is\n   separated by a character as described in the separator-parameter.\n\n   If the identified form is a tab form and the tab-index parameter is used,\n   the list will only contain forms and elements that belongs to the tab\n   given by tab-index.\n\n   Element-sequence\n\n   Returns the current [127]element-sequence for a grid form.\n\n   Font\n\n   Returns the style attribute [128]font of the form\n\n   Frame\n\n   Returns the style attribute [129]frame of the form\n\n   Grid-lines\n\n   Returns a value that reflects the setting of the [130]grid-lines\n   declaration on grid forms.\n\n   Handle\n\n   See the [131]handle parameter on [132]change-form.\n\n   Height\n\n   Returns the [133]height expression if defined or the actual height of the\n   form if not.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the lock status of the form. If the\n   identified form is a tab form and the tab-index parameter is used, the\n   returned value gives the lock status for the tab given by tab-index.\n\n   Member-elements\n\n   The field name given in this parameter needs to be declared as an\n   alphanumeric field. After the inquire-form() call, this field will contain\n   a list of either names or handles (dependent on the mode parameter) for\n   all elements owned directly by the form. Each list member is separated by\n   a character as described in the separator-parameter.\n\n   If the identified form is a tab form and the tab-index parameter is used,\n   the list will only contain elements that belongs to the tab given by\n   tab-index.\n\n   Member-forms\n\n   The field name given in this parameter needs to be declared as an\n   alphanumeric field. After the inquire-form() call, this field will contain\n   a list of either names or handles (dependent on the mode parameter) for\n   all forms owned directly by the form. Each list member is separated by a\n   character as described in the separator-parameter.\n\n   If the identified form is a tab form and the tab-index parameter is used,\n   the list will only contain forms that belongs to the tab given by\n   tab-index.\n\n   Mode\n\n   If the mode parameter evaluates to INDEX the member-elements and\n   member-forms requests returns a list of handles rather than a list of\n   names.\n\n   Name\n\n   Name of the form that is to be inquired.\n\n   Owner\n\n   Important to know here is, that if the form is owned by the stream, the\n   inquire-form() function will return @TOPLEVEL in the owner-parameter.\n\n   Owner-tab-index\n\n   If the owner of the form is a tab form it returns the list of tab indexes\n   on which the identified form is placed. Each element in the list is\n   separated by a character as described in the separator-parameter. See the\n   form declaration [134]tab-index for more details.\n\n   Position\n\n   Returns the actual Y and X position in element units for the form.\n   Positions are always defined relative to the top left corner of the owner.\n   See the form declaration [135]position for more details.\n\n   Reference-form\n\n   See the [136]reference-form parameter on [137]create-element.\n\n   Result\n\n   If the name parameter is specified it returns an internal unique\n   identifier of the form identified. The returned value can be used in any\n   subsequent calls to inquire-form or change-form using the handle\n   parameter. The value returned is an integer4 value. Please note that when\n   the form is deleted (either by the delete-form function or when the\n   application is terminated) the identifier value may be reused by another\n   element, form or stream.\n\n   If the handle parameter is used it returns the name of the identified\n   form.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Used in conjunction with the owner-tab-index,member-forms and\n   member-elements parameters. Denotes the separator character to be used to\n   separate each element in the list returned by those-parameters. If this\n   parameter is not given, the semicolon character is used as separator.\n\n   Show\n\n   Returns an on/off value that describes the visibility of the form. If the\n   identified form is a tab form and the tab-index parameter is used, the\n   returned value gives the visibility status for the tab given by tab-index.\n\n   Size\n\n   Returns the actual height and width in element units for the form. If the\n   form's height or width initially was set to be dynamic (using 0), negative\n   values are returned . See the form declaration [138]size for more details.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [139]status table in the [140]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   Returns the name of the base [141]style used by the form.\n\n   Tab-depth\n\n   Returns a value that reflects the setting of the [142]tab-depth\n   declaration on tab forms.\n\n   Tab-index\n\n   If the identified form is a tab form, this parameter affects the end\n   result of the following queries : [143]elements, lock,\n   [144]member-elements, [145]member-forms, [146]show an [147]title. See each\n   parameter for details.\n\n   Title\n\n   Return the title of the form. For grid forms the title is always blank.\n   For tab forms it is a semicolon separated list of the titles on each tab,\n   unless the tab-index parameter is given. If the tab-index parameter is\n   given it returns the title of the tab identified by the tab-index.\n\n   Type\n\n   Dependent of the form type it returns either GRID, TAB or NORMAL.\n\n   Width\n\n   Returns the [148]width expression if defined or the actual width of the\n   form if not.\n\n   X\n\n   Returns the [149]X position expression if defined or the actual X position\n   of the form if not.\n\n   Y\n\n   Returns the [150]Y position expression if defined or the actual Y position\n   of the form if not.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The handle parameter can not be combined with the name or application\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the handle or name parameter must be specified..\n\n   \xc2\xb7on/off values is either 0 or 1 if the receiving field is numeric or\n   ON/OFF if the receiving field is alphanumeric\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [151][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inquireelement.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                      INQUIRE-SESSION()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Inquires attributes of the current Concept session.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   inquire-session([[5]application(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]cursor(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]focus-thread(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]thread-handle(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]numericExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]hourglass(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]history(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]lock(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]separator(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]status(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[32]title(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[35]type(\xc2\xa0[36]?[37]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Application\n\n   Returns the name of the current application for the thread identified by\n   the thread-handle parameter. The name is returned as "<application\n   name>:<sub application name>.\n\n   Cursor\n\n   Returns the [38]cursor set for the specified thread. Blank if no session\n   cursor is set.\n\n   Focus-thread\n\n   Returns the handle of the thread currently having focus.\n\n   Thread-handle\n\n   A unique identifier for a single thread in the session. Legal values can\n   be obtained from [39]"@THREAD_HANDLE", [40]"@THREAD_LIST" or\n   inquire-session with the focus-thread parameter.\n\n   Hourglass\n\n   Returns OFF if the default handling for the WAIT cursor is turned off and\n   DEFAULT if not.\n\n   History\n\n   Returns the current call hierarchy for the thread identified by the\n   thread-handle parameter. Application names are returned as "<application\n   name>:<sub application name> and each level in the hierarchy is separated\n   by a character as described in the separator-parameter. The first\n   application in the list is the current top application for the thread.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Returns the current lock state of the thread identified by the\n   thread-handle parameter.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Used in conjunction with the history parameter. Denotes the separator\n   character to be used to each element in the list returned by the history\n   parameter. If this parameter is not given, the semicolon character is used\n   as separator.\n\n   Status\n\n   Numeric field to receive the status of the operation. Possible values\n   include $OK, $UE_ERROR and $UE_ILLEGAL_HANDLE (see [41]Macro Values for\n   the numeric values of these constants).\n\n   Title\n\n   Alphanumeric field to receive the title of the current application for the\n   thread identified by the thread-handle parameter. For Xtra applications\n   and Online applications without a title defined on the [42]stream, the\n   [43]name of the application will be returned. For hidden applications (see\n   [44]processing-info) the title returned will be empty.\n\n   Type\n\n   Returns the type of the current application for the thread identified by\n   the thread-handle parameter. Possible value are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value    Description\n   ONLINE   Online application\n   XTRA     Xtra application\n   INTERNAL An internal system (like the Forms painter)\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Inquiring the thread having focus returns $ERROR if no thread running has\n   an online application.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The thread-handle parameter must be specified when using the application,\n   history,type, cursor and hourglass parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [45][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inquireform.htm\n   2. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       INQUIRE-STREAM()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Retrieves the current attributes of a [5]stream.\n\n   A stream has a set of attributes that can be fetched using the\n   inquire-stream() function. By using this function, attributes that do not\n   have a certain wanted value, can be modified using the [6]change-stream()\n   function.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   inquire-stream(\xc2\xa0[7]name(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]accelerators(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]application(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]background(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]bb(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[22]bin-in(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[25]colour(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[28]copies(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]docking(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]placement\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[34]duplex(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[37]formular(\xc2\xa0[38]?[39]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[40]frame(\xc2\xa0[41]?[42]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[43]handle(\xc2\xa0[44]?[45]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[46]lb(\xc2\xa0[47]?[48]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[49]member-forms(\xc2\xa0[50]?[51]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[52]minimum-size(\xc2\xa0[53]?[54]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[55]?[56]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[57]mode(\xc2\xa0[58]?[59]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[60]new-page(\xc2\xa0[61]?[62]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[63]ob(\xc2\xa0[64]?[65]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[66]orientation(\xc2\xa0[67]?[68]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[69]position(\xc2\xa0[70]?[71]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[72]?[73]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[74]pixel-position(\xc2\xa0[75]?[76]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[77]?[78]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[79]result(\xc2\xa0[80]?[81]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[82]selection(\xc2\xa0[83]?fieldname\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[84]separator(\xc2\xa0[85]?[86]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[87]show(\xc2\xa0[88]?[89]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[90]size(\xc2\xa0[91]?[92]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[93]?[94]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[95]pixel-size(\xc2\xa0[96]?[97]fieldName,\xc2\xa0[98]?[99]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[100]status(\xc2\xa0[101]?[102]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[103]style(\xc2\xa0[104]?[105]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[106]tb(\xc2\xa0[107]?[108]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[109]title(\xc2\xa0[110]?[111]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Accelerators\n\n   Returns the list of characters that is returned in the [112]ACCELERATOR\n   key command. The command is triggered when the combination of the ALT key\n   and a character in the list is pressed. In this case the [113]@EVENT_PARAM\n   field will contain the character pressed. Please note that the accelerator\n   keys have precedence over accelerator keys defined in the menu and on\n   elements in the application.\n\n   Application\n\n   The expression of the application parameter denotes the name of the sub\n   application that defines the stream. The sub application must be active\n   and must reside in the same application file. If this parameter is left\n   out, it is assumed that the stream belongs to the current sub application.\n\n   Background\n\n   Returns the background of the stream. See style attribute [114]background\n   for a description of the syntax of a background expression.\n\n   Bb\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the bottom border of the current page.\n\n   Bin-in\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the [115]source tray (bin) of the current page.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the colour mode set for the current page. Please note that colour\n   mode does not indicate whether the printer is a colour printer or not.\n\n   Copies\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the number of copies set for the current page.\n\n   Docking\n\n   Returns the docking state of the stream.\n\n   Duplex\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the duplex setting for the current page. See the\n   [116]change-stream parameter [117]duplex for a list of values.\n\n   Formular\n\n   The field used in this parameter will receive the name of the formular\n   used on the stream.\n\n   Frame\n\n   The field used in this parameter will receive the frame used on the\n   stream. See style attribute [118]frame for a description of the syntax of\n   a frame.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify a stream. The result of the text expression must be an integer\n   value that have been obtained using the [119]result parameter of the\n   inquire-stream function. The handle parameter enables the\n   [120]change-stream and inquire-stream functions to change and inquire\n   streams in other applications than the one that is currently active (as\n   long as the stream itself exists!).\n\n   Lb\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the left border of the current page.\n\n   Member-Forms\n\n   The field name given in this parameter needs to be declared as an\n   alphanumeric field. After the inquire-stream() call, this field will\n   contain a list of either names or handles (dependent on the mode\n   parameter) for all forms owned directly by the stream. Each list member is\n   separated by a character as described in the separator-parameter.\n\n   Minimum-Size\n\n   Only available in Online applications\n\n   Returns the minimum size of the application window in element units.\n\n   Mode\n\n   If the mode parameter evaluates to INDEX the member-forms request returns\n   a list of handles rather than a list of names.\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the stream in the application.\n\n   New-page\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns ON if the next print-form will force a page shift. OFF if not.\n\n   Ob\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the right border of the current page.\n\n   Orientation\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the orientation of the current page. Possible values are 1\n   (Portrait) and 2 (Landscape).\n\n   Position, Pixel-Position\n\n   Only available in Online applications\n\n   Returns the current position of the stream in the Concept desktop (in\n   element units for position or pixels for pixel-position). Position (0,0)\n   is the upper-left corner of the client area inside the Concept desktop.\n\n   Result\n\n   The field specified by the result parameter will receive an internal\n   unique identifier of the stream identified by the name parameter. The\n   returned value can be used in any subsequent calls to inquire-stream or\n   [121]change-stream using the [122]handle parameter. The value returned is\n   an integer4 value.\n\n   Please note that when the stream is deleted (when the application is\n   terminated) the identifier value may be reused by another element, form or\n   stream.\n\n   Selection\n\n   Used to get a semicolon separated list of currently selected fields\n   including repeat.\n\n   Separator\n\n   Used in conjunction with the member-forms parameter. Denotes the separator\n   character to be used to each element in the list returned by the\n   member-forms parameter. If this parameter is not given, the semicolon\n   character is used as separator.\n\n   Show\n\n   Only available in Online applications\n\n   Returns the display mode of the window (one of the values NORMAL, HIDDEN,\n   MAXIMIZED or MINIMIZED).\n\n   Size, Pixel-Size\n\n   Pixel-Size only available in Online applications\n\n   Returns the size of the stream (in element units for size or pixels for\n   pixel-size).\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. See the\n   [123]status table in the [124]create-element documentation for possible\n   values.\n\n   Style\n\n   Returns the name of the base [125]style used by stream.\n\n   Tb\n\n   Only available in Xtra applications\n\n   Returns the top border of the current page.\n\n   Title\n\n   Retrieves the title used for the stream.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The handle parameter can not be combined with the name, application, bb,\n   bin-in, colour, copies, duplex, formular, lb, new-page, ob, orientation\n   and tb parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Either the handle or name parameter must be specified.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_inquire_session__.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_listview.htm\n   4. b"   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          LISTVIEW()                                     side\n\n   The listview function is used to change the contents of a listview form.\n   The [4]listview form chapter contains more information and examples on how\n   to use the function.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   listview(\xc2\xa0[5]name(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[8]handle(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[11]command(\xc2\xa0DELETE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0LOOKUP\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0SYNCHRONIZE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0UPDATE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]check(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]exec-table-functions(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]image(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]item(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]result(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]selection(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]show(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]signal-events(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]sort(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]sorting\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]status(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]table(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]tableName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]values(\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]fieldName\xc2\xa0{,[48]?[49]fieldName\xc2\xa0}]\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0[50]?[51]textExpression\xc2\xa0{[52]?[53]textExpression}\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Command\n\n   Defines the operation to carry out.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command     Action\n               Delete one or more items in the listview. If the item\n   DELETE      parameter is not specified it is used to delete all items in\n               the listview.\n   LOOKUP      Retrieve values from a listview item.\n   SYNCHRONIZE Insert or update items in a listview\n               Update column header text, alignment and column sizes. Use the\n   UPDATE      [54]change-element function to change the elements in the\n               listview form and then the UPDATE command to apply the changes\n               to the listview.\n\n   Check\n\n   When used with the SYNCHRONIZE command, it sets the checked status for the\n   corresponding item in a listview with the [55]buttons attribute set. If\n   set to 'ON', the item is checked, if set to 'OFF', the item is unchecked\n   and if blank or left out, the current check status is retained.\n\n   When used with the LOOKUP command, it is used as a selection criteria. If\n   set to 'ON', the LOOKUP command only returns checked items, if 'OFF', it\n   returns only unchecked items, if blank or left out, the check status is\n   ignored.\n\n   Exec-table-functions\n\n   Available only in connection with the [56]table parameter. When set to\n   'ON' the functions on the table are executed for each row in the table.\n   The [57]select function can be used on the table to exclude rows from the\n   listview operation, a failing select will just ignore the current record\n   and move on to the next one. The [58]error function can be used to stop an\n   ongoing listview operation (returns status $UE_CANCEL).\n\n   'OFF' is the default value.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify the listview. The result of the text expression must be an\n   integer value that has been obtained using the result parameter of the\n   [59]inquire-form function. Using the handle parameter makes it possible to\n   change and inquire listviews in other applications than the one that is\n   currently active.\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines icon images for the item. A listview item requires two icons, a\n   large icon shown in the LARGE view, and a small icon shown in any of the\n   other views. Two separate icon files or icon resources can be specified\n   using the following notation:\n\n   image('<LargeIcon>;<SmallIcon>')\n\n   If a single file or resource is specified it is assumed that it contains\n   both the large and the small icon, if not, the lacking icon is\n   automatically scaled by the system. Please note that the first icons\n   inserted in the listview become default icons and will be used for any\n   following items that do not have an image specified.\n\n   Item\n\n   The item parameter is an integer value that uniquely identifies an item in\n   the listview. When used with the SYNCHRONIZE, command the item parameter\n   is used to decide whether the command is the insertion of a new item or\n   the modification of an existing item. When used with the DELETE and LOOKUP\n   commands, it identifies the item in the listview. If the item parameter is\n   left out in a DELETE command, all items are deleted (the listview is\n   cleared).\n\n   Name\n\n   Uniquely identifies the [60]listview form in the application.\n\n   Result\n\n   Available only for the LOOKUP command. When using the listview function\n   with the LOOKUP command the result parameter returns the item ID of the\n   next item in the listview that fulfills the selection criteria\n   ([61]selection and [62]check parameter values) of the function. If the\n   item parameter is left out or evaluates to -1, the result parameter\n   returns the ID of the first item in the listview that fulfills the\n   selection criteria.\n\n   Selection\n\n   When used with the SYNCHRONIZE command, it specifies whether the listview\n   item should be selected or not. If set to 'ON' the item is selected, if\n   set to 'OFF' the item is deselected and if blank or left out the current\n   selection status is retained.\n\n   When used with the LOOKUP command, it is used as a selection criteria. If\n   set to 'ON' the LOOKUP command only returns selected items, if 'OFF' it\n   returns only unselected items, if blank or left out the selection status\n   is ignored.\n\n   Show\n\n   Available only for the SYNCHRONIZE and DELETE commands. If set to 'ON' and\n   the listview function processes multiple listview items (when using the\n   [63]table parameter) the listview is refreshed after each item processed.\n   If set to 'OFF' the listview is refreshed once at the end of the\n   operation.\n\n   The default value is 'OFF'.\n\n   Signal-Events\n\n   Available only for the SYNCHRONIZE and DELETE commands. If set to 'ON' the\n   [64]@CHANGE event will also be triggered on the listview's control field\n   when items are checked, selected or deleted programmatically. If set to\n   'OFF' (the default value), the event is only triggered as a result of a\n   user action.\n\n   Sort\n\n   Available only for the SYNCHRONIZE command. When set to ASCENDING or\n   DESCENDING, the items in the listview are sorted accordingly, based on the\n   alphanumeric value of the first column in the listview. When set to NONE,\n   items are always inserted at the end of the listview.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. The value is $OK if successful.\n   Possible error values are (see [65]Macro Values for the numeric values of\n   these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_APPLICATION   No dialog in current application.\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND     No listview with the given name exists in the\n                     application or item not found for the LOOKUP command.\n   $UE_TYPE          The name or handle parameter does not identify a\n                     listview element.\n   $UE_SHOW          Illegal parameter value for the show parameter.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_VALUE Illegal parameter value for the exec-table-functions\n                     parameter.\n   $UE_CANCEL        See the [66]exec-table-functions section.\n   Database statuses Errors when accessing the table specified by the table\n                     parameter.\n\n   Table\n\n   Available only for the SYNCHRONIZE and DELETE commands. Specifies the name\n   of a table in the application that contains items to be inserted, modified\n   or deleted. The listview function will scroll through the table and carry\n   out the requested operation for all qualifying rows in the table (see also\n   [67]exec-table-functions).\n\n   Values\n\n   When used with the SYNCHRONIZE command, the parameter value is a comma\n   separated list of text expressions for the values of the corresponding\n   columns in the listview.\n\n   When used with the LOOKUP command, the parameter value is a comma\n   separated list of fields names. The fields will be filled with the values\n   of the corresponding columns in the listview item.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Please note that the table is only used while the listview function is\n   executed, it is not connected to the listview.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Only Icon images can be used for the image parameter. This is a\n   limitation imposed by the underlying implementation.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [68][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inquirestream.htm\n   2. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       SYSTEM-ELEMENT()                                  side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function can be used to add, remove and change additional system\n   information fields on the right hand side of the status line on the bottom\n   of the Concept main window. System-elements belongs to a single thread,\n   use the thread-handle parameter to add, delete or update system-elements\n   in other threads.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   system-element(\xc2\xa0[5]command(\xc2\xa0{\xc2\xa0[6]INSERT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[7]DELETE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[8]UPDATE\xc2\xa0}\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]alignment(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]background(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]colour(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]font(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]handle(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]image(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]result(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]status(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[33]text(\xc2\xa0[34]?[35]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[36]thread-handle(\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]width(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Alignment\n\n   Text expression specifying the [42]alignment to use when inserting or\n   updating system elements.\n\n   Background\n\n   Text expression specifying the [43]background to use when inserting or\n   updating system elements.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Text expression specifying the text [44]colour to use when inserting or\n   updating system elements.\n\n   Command\n\n   One of the following commands:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command Description\n   INSERT  Inserts a new system element between the [45]main system element\n           and the most recent system element.\n   DELETE  Deletes the most recently inserted system element.\n   UPDATE  Updates the system element identified by the [46]handle parameter.\n\n   Font\n\n   Text expression specifying the [47]font to use when inserting or updating\n   system elements.\n\n   Handle\n\n   Text expression that must evaluate to the [48]handle of a previously\n   inserted system element.\n\n   Image\n\n   Text expression specifying the [49]image to use when inserting or updating\n   system elements.\n\n   Result\n\n   Returns the [50]handle of the new element when inserting system elements.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. The following values may be returned\n   (see [51]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                    Description\n   $UE_FAILED                Insert [52]command failed or illegal [53]handle\n                             specified\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_VALUE         Invalid [54]width specified\n   $UE_COLOUR                Invalid [55]colour specified\n   $UE_BACKGROUND            Invalid [56]background specified\n   $UE_FONT                  Invalid [57]font specified\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND             Delete [58]command failed\n   $UE_DUPLICATE             Insert [59]command failed\n                             The function cannot be executed because system\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_NOW           elements are not available yet (i.e. very early\n                             in the startup phase of Concept)\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_THREAD_HANDLE Illegal value specified for the thread-handle\n                             parameter.\n\n   Text\n\n   Text expression specifying the [60]text to show when inserting or updating\n   system elements.\n\n   Thread-handle\n\n   The thread-handle parameter identifies the thread of the system-element.\n   When the thread-handle parameter is not specified, the current thread is\n   assumed.\n\n   Width\n\n   Text expression specifying the [61]width (in element units) of the system\n   element to be inserted.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using the INSERT [62]command, the [63]width and [64]result\n   parameters are mandatory.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using the DELETE command, only the [65]status parameter may be used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using the UPDATE command, the [66]handle parameter is mandatory and\n   the [67]width and [68]result parameters may not be used.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Function execution will be aborted if an error occurs and the [69]status\n   parameter has been omitted.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [70][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > User Interface    side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Components\xc2\xa0>                                                  til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          TREEVIEW()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The treeview() function is used in co-operation with a [5]treeview\n   element. It performs actions like clearing the contents of this element,\n   and so on.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   treeview(\xc2\xa0[6]name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[9]handle(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[12]command(\xc2\xa0[[13]CLEAR\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[14]SYNCHRONIZE]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]exec-table-functions(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]onOff\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]show(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]table(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]tableName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]status(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Name\n\n   The name of the treeview element.\n\n   Command\n\n   The command to be done:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command     Description\n   SYNCHRONIZE Synchronize the treeview with the contents of the table given\n               in the table-parameter\n   CLEAR       Clear the contents of treeview\n\n   Exec-table-functions\n\n   Available only in connection with the [27]table parameter. When set to\n   \'ON\' the functions on the table are executed for each row in the table.\n   The [28]select function can be used on the table to exclude rows from the\n   treeview operation, a failing select will just ignore the current record\n   and move on to the next one. The [29]error function can be used to stop an\n   ongoing treeview operation (returns status $UE_CANCEL).\n\n   \'OFF\' is the default value.\n\n   Handle\n\n   The handle parameter can be used instead of the name parameter to uniquely\n   identify the treeview. The result of the expression must be an integer\n   value that has been obtained using the result parameter of the\n   [30]inquire-form function. Using the handle parameter makes it possible to\n   change and inquire treeviews in other applications than the one that is\n   currently active.\n\n   Show\n\n   If the expression evaluates to \'ON\' or 1 (the default value), the treeview\n   element is refreshed during SYNCHRONIZE commands, otherwise it is not\n   refreshed before the command is finished.\n\n   Table\n\n   The name of a table in the application that contains the contents of the\n   treeview. See the [31]Treeview element chapter for more details.\n\n   This parameter is only used when the command is set to SYNCHRONIZE.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. The value is $OK if successful.\n   Possible error values are (see [32]Macro Values for the numeric values of\n   these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR   The table used for synchronizing do not contain the\n                     required columns.\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED The treeview function is only supported on 32 bit\n                     platforms.\n   $UE_APPLICATION   No dialog in current application.\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND     No element with the given name exists in the\n                     application.\n   $UE_TYPE          The requested element is not a treeview element.\n   $UE_CANCEL        See the [33]exec-table-functions section.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_CMD   Illegal command\n   Database statuses Errors when accessing the table, either for read or\n                     update.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The table used for synchronizing must at least contain the following\n   columns: ID and LABEL.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the access on the table includes UPDATE access and the STATE column is\n   present, the treeview function (with command(SYNCHRONIZE)) will\n   automatically clear the STATE column and update the database.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Although it is recommended (for performance reasons) that the table used\n   for synchronization is a [34]temporary table, any table belonging to any\n   supported DBMS might be used (as long as it contains the necessary\n   columns). If the table used belongs to an SQL database, the performance of\n   the synchronization can be improved by using [35]sql-where on the table to\n   ensure that only records with a recognizable value in STATE is returned.\n   (e.g. sql-where(\'@CONDITION(STATE in("I","M","D")\').\n\n   \xc2\xb7Please note that the table is only used while the treeview function\n   executes, there is no further connection to the treeview.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [36][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_to_vertical_eu.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. If neither + or -\n   is used, the commands listed will be the list of legal commands. + and -\n   may be mixed in the same definition.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Commands may be selected from the drop-down menu or from the keyboard.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Unlike the legal-commands declaration in the application declaration\n   which only allows you to define accessible commands at compile time,\n   available-commands are executed at run time. This means that it is\n   possible, for example, to make the available commands dependent on the\n   user name.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [10][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_treeview.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_available_commands.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_sign.htm#idh_la_pop_sign\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_functionkey.htm#idh_la_pop_functionkey\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_sign.htm#idh_la_pop_sign\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_functionkey.htm#idh_la_pop_functionkey\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_availablecommands.htm\n'
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Event Handling\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            DRAG()                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The drag function initializes a drag operation.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   drag(\xc2\xa0[5]values(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]cursor(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]cursorId;[11]cursorId;[12]cursorId\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]mode(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]status(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]type(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Cursor\n\n   A semicolon separated list that defines the cursors to be used in the drag\n   operation. The first list entry defines the cursor to be used on areas\n   that does not accept a drop, the second defines the COPY cursor and the\n   third defines the MOVE cursor. An empty entry defines that the standard\n   drag and drop cursor for the state should be used. If this parameter is\n   undefined the standard drag and drop cursor are used.\n\n   Mode\n\n   The mode parameter must evaluate to one of the following values :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Mode Description\n   COPY Allow only COPY operations\n   MOVE Allow only MOVE operations\n   BOTH Allow both COPY and MOVE operations. This is the default.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please note that the mode parameter is only used when giving feedback to\n   the user through the shape of the CURSOR, it is the programmer's\n   responsibility to actually fulfill the operation by e.g. removing the\n   dragged data in the case of a MOVE operation. See the status parameter for\n   details.\n\n   Concept prioritizes COPY operations, that is if mode(BOTH) is used the\n   user must press the SHIFT button in order to initiate a MOVE operation.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible values are (see [22]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_APPLICATION   The drag function is not executed in the application\n                     that received the DRAG event. The operation is aborted.\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR   The value or the type parameter is empty. The operation\n                     is aborted.\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED Drag and drop is not supported on this platform. The\n                     operation is aborted.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_NOW   Dragging is not allowed from this application window.\n                     The operation is aborted.\n   $UE_MEMORY        There is not enough memory to fulfill the operation. The\n                     operation is aborted.\n   $UE_FAILED        The drag operation failed.\n   $UE_CANCEL        The drag operation was canceled by the user.\n                     The dragged object was successfully dropped. The user\n   $UE_DRAG_COPY     expects the drop to be a COPY operation. This status is\n                     not returned if mode is set to MOVE.\n                     The dragged object was successfully dropped. The user\n   $UE_DRAG_MOVE     expects the drop to be a MOVE operation.. This status is\n                     not returned if mode is set to COPY.\n   $UE_DRAG_NONE     The dragged object was dropped in an illegal area.\n   $UE_OK            The dragged object was successfully dropped, but no\n                     indication of the drop state was returned.\n\n   Type\n\n   The type parameter must evaluate to one or more (as a comma separated\n   list) of the following values :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Type Description\n   TEXT The DRAG value is a text. This is the default\n   FILE The DRAG value is a filename\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The type parameter is used by candidates for a drop to decide whether it\n   can accept the drop or not. For elements in a Concept application the type\n   parameter conforms to the [23]drop-types declaration on an element.\n\n   Values\n\n   The value that is to be dragged. Use the internal field [24]@DRAG_VALUE to\n   get the marked/selected value(s).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The drag function may only be used inside the event handler for the DRAG\n   key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7It is the programmers responsibility to complete the drag operation by\n   implementing code to resolve the status returned from the drag function.\n   E.g. If the drag mode includes MOVE and the drag function returns\n   $UE_DRAG_MOVE the programmer must take the necessary actions to remove the\n   dragged value.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_availablecommands.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_drag_and_drop_functions.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm#idh_ma_drag_values\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm#idh_ma_drag_cursor\n   9. file:///dev/html_lexical__cursor.htm#idh_la_pop_cursorid\n  10. file:///dev/html_lexical__cursor.htm\n  11. file:///dev/html_lexical__cursor.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_lexical__cursor.htm\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm#idh_ma_drag_mode\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm#idh_ma_drag_status\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm#idh_ma_drag_type\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_macro_values.htm\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_drop_types\n  24. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_intdrag_value\n"

The drop position is interpreted as:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Element type        Value\n   INPUT, OUTPUT and\n                       The character position closest to the drop point.\n   DROP-DOWN-COMBO-BOX\n                       The index of the list box item at the drop point, or\n   LISTBOX             -1 if dropped below the last element in the list.\n                       (Indexes starts at 1).\n   TREEVIEW            The ID of the treeview node at the drop point. or -1\n                       if dropped below the last element in the treeview.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible values are (see [17]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status          Description\n   $UE_APPLICATION The drop function is not executed in the application that\n                   received the DROP event. The operation is aborted.\n   $UE_EMPTY       No value or type found.\n   $UE_OK          Success.\n\n   Type\n\n   Returns the type of the dropped object. Possible values are :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Type Description\n   TEXT The value is a text.\n   FILE The value is a filename\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The value of the type parameter is limited to the settings defined by the\n   [18]drop-types declaration on the element that received the drop. If the\n   drop-types declaration includes both TEXT and FILE and the dragged object\n   supports both formats, FILE is prioritized.\n\n   Values\n\n   Receives the dropped value.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The drop function may only be used inside the event handler for the DROP\n   key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The drop function can only be called once for each drop operation. On two\n   successive calls the latter will return status $UE_EMPTY.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drag.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_performevent.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_drag_and_drop_functions.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_position\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_position\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_status\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_status\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_type\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_type\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_values\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm#idh_ma_drop_values\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_macro_values.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_element.htm#idh_ma_element_drop_types\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Event Handling\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       PERFORM-EVENT()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The perform-event function is used to execute the standard functionality\n   of an event. In Concept there are some events that do not have\n   corresponding 4GL commands (like displaying standard help on a field), but\n   are only available through keyboard input. The function\n   perform-event(event=HELPFIELD) will make the system act as if the user\n   pressed the HELPFIELD key. Only the events listed under the [5]event-name\n   parameter can be triggered by the perform-event function.\n\n   Syntax 1\n\n   perform-event(\xc2\xa0[6]event-name(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]performableEvent\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]parameters(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]return-code(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]status(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Syntax 2\n\n   perform-event(\xc2\xa0[18]parameters(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]return-code(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]status(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Event-name\n\n   A predefined constant. The following table shows legal event names. Please\n   note that the parameter value can only contain the event name. Additional\n   parameters have to be supplied in the [27]parameters parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command               Default action\n                         Start the [28]open file dialogue.\n   APPLICATION\n   [<Application>]       Everything after the command will be treated as\n                         application name.\n   BLOWUP                Opens a drop-down list-box or combo-box\n                         [29]Call an application.\n\n                         The first word after the command will be treated as\n                         application name. To specify application names that\n                         include spaces, enclose the name in quotes. If not\n                         application name is specified, the [30]open file\n   CALL [<Application>[  dialogue will be shown for the user to pick an\n   <Parameters>]]        application.\n\n                         Optional parameters, separated by blanks, can be\n                         specified and will be exported to the application\n                         called. A corresponding import list must exist in\n                         the called application. Parameters containing blanks\n                         must be enclosed in quotes.\n   CANCEL                Abort pending updates and clear all fields\n   CLEARREGION           Clear all fields in the current region (table level)\n   DELREC                Deletes the current row\n   FIRSTREC              Creates a new region on the current table and\n                         displays the first row(s).\n   HELPAPPL              Displays help on application level\n   HELPFIELD             Displays help on field level\n   LASTREC               Creates a new region on the current table and\n                         displays the last row(s).\n   NEXTREC               Displays the next row(s) in the current region\n   PREVREC               Displays the previous row(s) in the current region\n                         Dumps the current window to file, printer or\n                         clipboard.\n\n                         <What> normally is a number between -3 and 3 and is\n                         used to specify what to dump. 1 dumps the whole\n                         screen, 2 the Concept window and 3 the current\n                         application window. Negative values or 0 can be used\n                         to prompt for this parameter (with the given content\n                         preselected).\n\n                         The <What> value can be specified in the extended\n                         syntax <Depth><What> (please note that the is no\n                         space between the values). The <Depth> value\n                         specifies the colour depth and compression algorithm\n                         to be used for the image and supports the following\n                         values:\n\n                         0 - Default (same as 24)\n\n                         1 - 1 bit (2 colours)\n\n   PRINTSCREEN [<What>   2 - 4 bits (16 colours) RLE\n   [<Where>]]\n                         4 - 4 bits (16 colours)\n\n                         6 - 8 bits (256 colours) RLE\n\n                         8 - 8 bits (256 colours)\n\n                         16 - 16 bits (65 thousand colours)\n\n                         24 - 24 bits (16 million colours)\n\n                         32 - 32 bits (4 billion colours)\n\n                         <Where> is the name of an output file. This can be\n                         any legal file name (as in the file-name parameter\n                         on streams), with the exception that it is not\n                         possible to dump to an external server. The special\n                         file name "@CLIPBOARD" can be used to dump to the\n                         windows clipboard. It is possible to prefix the file\n                         name with a question mark ("?"), to use a single\n                         question mark or to leave this parameter empty to\n                         prompt for a file name.\n                         Prints the contents of the table connected to the\n                         current grid-form. The output will contain all\n                         columns visible in the grid-form.\n\n                         <What> specifies the amount of data to be printed. A\n                         value of 0 means that all records found in the table\n                         (according to the applications key and range\n                         definitions) will be printed. Because this can be\n                         quite a lot of data, the amount of data printed can\n                         be limited by specifying the number of records to be\n                         printed using a positive integer for <What>. In this\n                         case the printout starts with the first record\n                         currently shown in the grid-form.\n   PRINTRECORDS [<What>\n   [<Where>]]            <Where> is the name of an output file. This can be\n                         any legal file name (as in the file-name parameter\n                         on streams). It is possible to prefix the file name\n                         with a question mark ("?"), to use a single question\n                         mark or to leave this parameter empty to prompt for\n                         a file name.\n\n                         When no parameters are specified at all, the user\n                         will be asked for the amount of data to print and\n                         the output device.\n\n                         Concept uses a standard system application for the\n                         printout. This application can be replaced by a\n                         system specific report ([31]@UQUGridRep).\n   QUERYMODE             Enters query mode\n   RUN [<Application>[   [32]Run an application.\n   <Parameters>]]\n                         See [33]CALL for an explanation of the parameters.\n   START [<Application>[ [34]Start an application.\n   <Parameters>]]\n                         See [35]CALL for an explanation of the parameters.\n                         [36]Start the given module in Concept. <Name> is one\n                         of:\n   STARTTOOL <Name>\n                         QUICK, XTRA, START, SECURITY, EDIT, COMPILE, DEBUG,\n                         SHELL, RT, SERVER, CM, HORIZON.\n                         [37]Call the given module in Concept. <Name> is one\n                         of:\n   TOOL <Name>\n                         QUICK, XTRA, START, SECURITY, EDIT, COMPILE, DEBUG,\n                         SHELL, RT, SERVER, CM, HORIZON.\n\n   Parameters\n\n   An optional value specifying a parameter value required by the actual\n   event. See under [38]on for information on which commands support\n   parameters.\n\n   Return-Code\n\n   The parameter identifies a field receives the return code of the\n   application called. Possible return codes are (see [39]Macro Values for\n   the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status              Description\n   $URC_NORMAL         The application terminated normally.\n   $URC_EXIT_REQUESTED The application terminated because an EXIT was\n                       requested.\n   $URC_ABORTED        The application was aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   When performing the events \'APPLICATION\' or \'CALL\', the same return-codes\n   as for the [40]call function may be returned.\n\n   Using the return-code parameter affects the behaviour of Concept when\n   receiving [41]EXIT events. The programmer may have execute the [42]exit\n   function when receiving a $URC_EXIT_REQUESTED return code.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK if the operation is successful. Possible error\n   values: $UE_ILLEGAL_EVENT (see [43]Macro Values for the numeric values of\n   these constants).\n\n   When performing the events \'APPLICATION\' or \'CALL\', the same status codes\n   as for the [44]call function may be returned.\n\n   Note that if status is not defined and an error occurs, the equivalent of\n   an error function will be performed.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Perform-event will not activate on functions for the given event.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The default actions (if any) for the given event will be executed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A dynamic version (syntax 2) of perform-event is possible. Omit the\n   event-name parameter and include the event-name as the first word of\n   parameters. Use this version when you need to build the event name at run\n   time.\n\n   \xc2\xa0Example: perform-event(parameters=\'APPLICATION MYAPPL\')\n\n   \xc2\xb7Note that events may also be activated from menus. In this case the on\n   functions will be executed (see [45]define-menu).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [46][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_drop.htm\n   2. This is the default.\n\n   Status\n\n   This parameter returns the status of the operation. See [13]on declarations for legal\n   event names.\n\n   Note that the event name is not a text expression.\n\n   Mode\n\n   If this parameter is set to UNIQUE, there can only be one thread\n   registered for the event. Trying to register an event with mode(UNIQUE)\n   will fail with $UE_DUPLICATE if the thread has allready registered the\n   event and with status $UE_EXCLUSIVE if another thread has registered the\n   event. AMBIGUOUS is the default.\n\n   Status\n\n   The status parameter returns the status of operation. Possible values\n   include:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status        Description\n   $OK           Ok\n                 The event is already registered for this thread. Please note\n                 that the event will still be triggered (registration is per\n   $UE_DUPLICATE thread), but you should not unregister the event in the\n                 current application as the correct unregister point is down\n                 the call hierarchy.\n                 If mode(UNIQUE):\n\n                 The event is already registered by another thread.\n   $UE_EXCLUSIVE\n                 If mode(AMBIGUOUS):\n\n                 The event is already registered with mode(UNIQUE) by another\n                 thread.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   See [14]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the thread exits, all registered events for the thread will be\n   removed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Registered events are only triggered if it is not handled by the thread\n   where it arises.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Events that have a standard default action like NEXTREC and PREVREC may\n   also be registered. But if they are, the default action will not be\n   executed in the thread where they arise.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The internal field [15]@EVENT_THREAD can be used in the event handler to\n   identify the thread where the event arose.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_read_message__.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_send_event__.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_events.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_eventname\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_performableevent.htm#idh_la_pop_performableevent\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_eventname\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_mode\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_mode\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_status\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_registerevent.htm#idh_ma_regevent_status\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_on.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_macro_values.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_internalfields.htm#idh_de_inteventthread\n'

defined.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the thread-handle parameter is used, the internal field\n   [30]@EVENT_THREAD can be used in the event handler to identify the thread\n   from which it was sendt.\n\n b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Event Handling\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           TIMER()                                       side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A timer is an event that is triggered after a specified time interval. If\n   the timer is triggered, the execution of a 4GL application is interrupted,\n   and the event handler for the timer is called. After the timer event\n   handler is finished, execution continues in the 4GL application at the\n   point it was interrupted. The timer() function is used to create, delete\n   and re-insert a timer event.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   timer([5]name(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[8]command(\xc2\xa0[\xc2\xa0[9]INSERT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[10]DELETE\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[11]QUEUE\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]interval(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]status(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Name\n\n   A text expression containing a name defined in the application that\n   uniquely identifies the timer.\n\n   Command\n\n   Defines the operation that should be performed on the timer:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command        Description\n   INSERT \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 Insert a new timer in the internal Concept timer queue,\n   DELETE \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 Delete timer defined by name.\n   QUEUE \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0  Queue this timer event again.\n\n   Interval\n\n   Specifies the time-out value in tenths of a seconds. Ignored for commands\n   other than INSERT.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the requested operation. Possible values are (see\n   [18]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status        Description\n   $OK           No error occurred.\n   $UE_DUPLICATE A timer with the given name already exists (command=INSERT)\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND No timer found with the given name (command=DELETE | QUEUE )\n   $UE_FAILED    Failed to create the timer (command=INSERT).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The Interval parameter has to be a numeric value between 1 and 32767.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Implementation of the timer function is based upon the TIMER\n   functionality in the Windows API. The functionality in Windows is based\n   upon messages which have low priority and which must be polled from the\n   message queue. This makes the TIMER functionality inaccurate.\n\n   \xc2\xb7After inserting a new timer the [19]@TIMER event is triggered after a\n   period of time given by interval parameter. The [20]@EVENT_PARAM field\n   will contain the name of the timer (WORD 1) and the number of\n   queued/delayed timer events in the next word (WORD 2).\n\n   \xc2\xb7If an application does not handle a particular timer it should use the\n   QUEUE command to queue the TIMER for other applications.
