Each name\n   is separated by a semicolon ';'. The result field is well suited as a\n   value list to a list-box field, or as input to the [35]string function.\n\n   Bind-Table\n\n   The name of a table to receive the list of requested file names and the\n   file attributes (see [36]file-info for a description of the attributes\n   returned). The table must contain at least one of the following columns:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Name     Description\n   PATH     File path or drive name\n   NAME     File name (including extension unless the [37]extension parameter\n            is set to OFF)\n   EXT      File extension\n   ATTRIB   File attributes\n   OWNER    File owner\n   SIZE     File size or available space on drive (in bytes)\n   WRITTEN  Date and time when the file was last written (modified; 0 for\n            drives)\n   READ     Date and time when the file was last read (accessed; 0 for\n            drives)\n   CREATED  Date and time when the file was created (for drives)\n   FORMAT   File format\n   TYPE     File type ('F' for files, 'D' for directories and 'H' for drives)\n   PROPERTY Different properties for image files (see the [38]properties\n            parameter of the [39]file-info function for details).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the FORMAT or PROPERTY column is specified the performance will be\n   reduced since each file has to be opened for determining the file format\n   and/or properties.\n\n   FORMAT and PROPERTY is always returned as blank if the path parameter\n   denotes a UCA file.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   Retrieves a descriptive text in the case of an IO error. For none IO\n   errors (like $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED) the text is blank.\n\n   Extension\n\n   ON - include .extension in result (default)\n\n   OFF - exclude .extension in result\n\n   Found\n\n   Returning the number of files found.\n\n   Mask\n\n   A text containing wild card characters to define a selection of files to\n   be included in the list. The wild card characters supported are '*' and\n   '?'. Several selections may be given separated by the character defined in\n   Separator.\n\n   Path\n\n   Name of directory to be read. Default is the users current directory.\n\n   Selection\n\n   A text containing a list of one or more commands. The following commands\n   are supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command Description\n   F       List files (default)\n   D       List directories\n   I       List drives\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The following modifiers are supported\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Modifier Description\n   H        List hidden files only\n   S        List system files only\n   W        List writable files only\n   R        List read-only files only\n\n   Separator\n\n   A character that defines the separator between several selections in the\n   mask parameter.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returning the status code of the operation. Possible values are (see\n   [40]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED Parameter value not supported\n   $UE_TRUNCATED     Result is truncated\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The returned names are not case converted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The returned names do not include the path name, only the file name and,\n   optionally, the file extension.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [41]@INSERT event will be triggered before for record inserted when\n   using the bind-table parameter.\n\n   Portability considerations\n\n   \xc2\xb7The path and mask parameters are case sensitive on UNIX\n\n   \xc2\xb7UNIX style names will work on all platforms\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [42][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. If the special value '@TEMP[<.extension>]'\n   is used when opening a file for WRITE or APPEND, a file with a unique\n   random name will be created on the scratch-path. If '@TEMP' is prefixed\n   with the name of a directory, the temporary file will be created in that\n   directory.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   Retrieves a descriptive text in the case of an IO error. For none IO\n   errors (like $UE_MISSING_PAR) the text is blank.\n\n   File-format\n\n   The [24]file format of the file to be opened. The default value is\n   'BINARY'.\n\n   Full-file-name\n\n   Returns the complete name of the file opened, including drive, path, name\n   and extension.\n\n   Handle\n\n   Returns a unique identifier (handle) for the opened file. The handle is\n   used as an input parameter to file-close, file-read,file-write, file-seek\n   and file-tell as well as to the handle declaration on streams. The field\n   that receives the handle must be able to hold an integer2 value.\n\n   Mode\n\n   The file open mode.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Mode   Description\n   READ   Opens the file for reading. If the file does not exist or cannot be\n          found the function fails.\n   WRITE  Opens an empty file for writing If the given file exists, its\n          contents are destroyed, if not it is created.\n   APPEND Opens the file for writing at the end of the file (appending). If\n          the file does not exist it is created.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If +TEMPORARY is added to the open mode it tells Concept to delete the\n   file when the Concept session terminates.\n\n   If +TAB is added, TAB characters are not converted to spaces when reading\n   files.\n\n   If +EXCLUSIVE is added to the open mode it tells Concept to open the file\n   exclusively which means that other threads or processes will not be able\n   to access the file until the file is closed.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returning the status code of the operation. Possible values are (see\n   [25]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status          Description\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR A required parameter is missing (E.g. filename is empty)\n   $UE_FORMAT      An illegal file-format was given\n   $UE_IO          File could not be opened.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status parameter is omitted and an error occurs, [26]function\n   execution is aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The name returned by the full-file-name parameter is not case converted.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   See the [27]File function topic for more information b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > File Handling\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         FILE-READ()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Reads from a file opened by the [5]file-open function\n\n   Syntax\n\n   file-read(\xc2\xa0[6]handle([7]?[8]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[9]field(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]error-text(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]length(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]result(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]status([22]?[23]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Handle\n\n   A unique identifier (handle) returned by the [24]file-open function, that\n   identifies the file to be read.\n\n   Field\n\n   The field that should receive the data read from the file. If the field\n   identified is a BLOB column, the data read from the file will be stored in\n   the database . If the field is not a BLOB column and the file is opened\n   with file-format PLAIN/<character set>, Concept will automatically convert\n   from the given character set to the Unique Character Set.\n\n   When reading BINARY files, the field will not be cleared before the read\n   operation. Be sure to use the [25]result parameter to find out how many\n   bytes have actually been read.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   Retrieves a descriptive text in the case of an IO error. For none IO\n   errors (like $UE_MISSING_PAR) the text is blank.\n\n   Length\n\n   Number of bytes that should be read from the file into the field. A value\n   of 0 is default.\n\n   Special values of length :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value Description\n         If the file is opened as BINARY: Read the number of bytes that can\n         be held by the storage code of the field. E.g if the storage code is\n         integer2, 2 bytes are read.\n   0\n         If the file is not opened as BINARY: Read the number of bytes that\n         complies with the display code of the field. E.g if the display code\n         is ZZZZ9, 5 bytes are read.\n   -1    If the file is not opened as BINARY : Read a line of text from the\n         file.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please note that if the field is a BLOB column both 0 and -1 will mean\n   read to end of file.\n\n   Result\n\n   Number of bytes that have been read from the file.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returning the status code of the operation. Possible values are (see\n   [26]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND     The value of the handle is illegal.\n   $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED A length less than zero was specified for a BINARY file.\n                     A length larger than or equal to zero was specified for\n   $UE_FORMAT        a file opened with a format that was neither BINARY or\n                     PLAIN.\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR   The field parameter did not identify a legal field.\n   $UE_EOF           End of file has been reached.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the field parameter identifies a BLOB the status parameter may contain\n   database status values, among those are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status               Description\n   $NOT_FOUND           There is not a current record on the table that holds\n                        the BLOB column.\n   $MULTI_USER_CONFLICT The BLOB column could not be reserved for writing.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status parameter is omitted and an error occurs, [27]function\n   execution is aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   See the [28]File function topic for more information and examples.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileopen.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_fileseek.htm\n   4. To flush the contents of the write buffer to the file\n   immediately, execute the file-write function using only the handle\n   parameter.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   file-write(\xc2\xa0[6]handle([7]?[8]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]error-text(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]field(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0,[15]text(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]length(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]result([22]?[23]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]status([25]?[26]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Handle\n\n   A unique identifier (handle) returned by the [27]file-open function.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   Retrieves a descriptive text in the case of an IO error. different from\n                 BINARY/ASCII or PLAIN.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the field parameter identifies a BLOB the status parameter may contain\n   database status values, among those are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status     Description\n   $NOT_FOUND There is not a current record on the table that holds the BLOB\n              column.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status parameter is omitted b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > File Handling\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                    INITIALISATION-FILE()                                side\n\n   The function is used to read and write values in [4]Initialisation Files\n   or the Windows Registry Database.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   1.\n\n   initialisation-file(\xc2\xa0[5]file(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0{,[8]import(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0[,[11]default(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0,[14]export(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0)}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]access(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]item(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]section(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]type(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]status(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   2.\n\n   initialisation-file(\xc2\xa0[32]file(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   File\n\n   Name of the initialisation file to be queried or updated. If the file name\n   does not contain a directory specification, the Windows directory is used.\n\n   The special file names '@REGISTRY', '@REGISTRY32' '@REGISTRY64' and \xc2\xa0can\n   be used to access the Windows Registry Database instead of an Ini File.\n   '@REGISTRY32' and '@REGISTRY64' is used to access bit specific registry\n   keys on 64bit Windows platforms. See also the macros [35]$MainRegistry and\n   [36]$AltRegistry.\n\n   Export\n\n   An expression defining a new value for the given item in the given\n   section. If either the item or the section do not already exist, they will\n   be created. If the file does not exist, it will be created.\n\n   If the [37]item parameter is omitted and the operation is performed on an\n   Ini file, the section and all items are removed. In this case the export\n   value should be empty.\n\n   If the item parameter is omitted and the operation is performed on the\n   Registry, the action depends on the value of the [38]export parameter. If\n   the export value is empty, the section will be deleted. Otherwise a new\n   sub section (key) with the name stated in the export value will be\n   created. Please note that it is not possible to delete sections which\n   contain sub sections. The error status $UE_OWNER will be returned when\n   attempting to delete such a section.\n\n   Import\n\n   A character field to receive the item value. If the item does not exist in\n   the file and the [39]default parameter has not be specified, an empty\n   string is returned. When reading values from the Registry, the Registry\n   [40]datatype will be converted according to the [41]storage code of the\n   receiving field. MULTI_STRING values will be returned as semicolon\n   separated lists.\n\n   If the item parameter is omitted, the field will receive a list of all\n   items in the section specified by the [42]section parameter. When reading\n   the Registry and the section parameter ends with a backslash (\\), the list\n   will contain all sub sections (keys) defined. Please note that the list or\n   Registry items does not contain the default item.\n\n   The field must be large enough to receive the maximum number of items,\n   otherwise the item list will be truncated. The items are separated by a\n   semicolon (;).\n\n   Default\n\n   An expression defining the value that should be returned when importing\n   from the file and the item addressed does not exist. The standard default\n   value is an empty string.\n\n   Access\n\n   This parameter is only supported when reading Ini files and defines the\n   way Concept accesses the file. The two possible parameter values are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value  Description\n          When using this access method, Concept uses Windows API calls to\n          access the file. On Windows 3.1x and Windows 95/98 this imposes a\n   DIRECT maximum size on the files accessed. The file cannot be larger than\n          64K. The status parameter can be used to trap error situations.\n          This is the default access method.\n          Using this access method makes it possible to access any\n   UNIQUE initialisation file regardless of it's size. Concept will perform\n          all I/O operations on this file itself. This access method is much\n          slower than direct access, esp. when writing large files.\n\n   Item\n\n   Defines an item whose associated value is to be retrieved or updated. If\n   this value is omitted, the [43]import or [44]export parameters will affect\n   all items in the given section. The default values of Registry keys can be\n   accessed using the special item name '@DEFAULT'.\n\n   Section\n\n   The section name identifies a section of items that are grouped.\n\n   In Ini files, the section name is enclosed in square brackets ([, ]), but\n   these cannot be part of the section name.\n\n   In the Registry, sections are path names separated by backslashes (\\)\n   which begin with the name of one of the following key groups:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Group              Description\n   HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT  Entries in this group contain document types used by\n                      shell and OLE applications.\n   HKEY_CURRENT_USER  Entries in this group contain preferences of the\n                      current user.\n   HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE Entries in this group define the physical state of the\n                      computer.\n   HKEY_USERS         Entries in this group define default configurations for\n                      new users and the configuration of the current user.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note:\n\n   Previous versions of Concept used the parameter name topic instead of\n   section. The old notation is supported for compatibility reasons.\n\n   Type\n\n   This parameter can only be used when writing values to the Registry and\n   defines the datatype of the item value. Possible values are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Type          Description\n   STRING        Alphanumeric value.\n                 Alphanumeric value. Environment variables referenced in the\n   EXPAND_STRING value (text enclosed in % characters; e.g. %SystemRoot%) are\n                 expanded when reading such a value.\n   MULTI_STRING  Alphanumeric value. Semicolon separated lists of texts are\n                 stored as arrays of strings in the Registry.\n   DWORD         32-bit numeric value.\n   BINARY        Binary value.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please note that the datatype of existing items is changed when using this\n   parameter.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field to receive the status of the operation. The value 0 ($OK)\n   is returned when the operation was successful, all other values signal an\n   error (see [45]Macro Values for the numeric values of predefined status\n   codes).\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Concept uses the file CONCEPT.INI to store user information. This file\n   may also be used by applications if the section names do not conflict with\n   the topics used by Concept. Using an underscore as prefix (or another\n   suitable text) will avoid conflicts.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using syntax 2 assures that the initialisation file is written to disk.\n   Since Windows 3.1, Windows 95 and Windows NT cache the initialisation\n   file, it might be necessary to flush this cache if the initialisation file\n   is accessed in any way other than through the initialisation-file function\n   from within Concept or the equivalent functions in the Windows API.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [46]file parameter allows the use of the special value @UQSYSTEM to\n   retrieve settings from the uqsystem.ini files. Note that the values\n   returned are a merge from the system specific uqsystem.ini and the global\n   uqsystem.ini. Please note that the value @UQSYSTEM is not handled upon\n   writing to a initialisation file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Using file name @REGISTRY32 or @REGISTRY64 when deleting registry\n   sections on 64 bit Windows XP might fail with status $UE_NOT_SUPPORTED.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When using the @UQSYSTEM file on a Windows platform, one can use the\n   special value @WINFONTS for section (do not specify item) to return a list\n   of all installed windows fonts.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [47]file parameter allows the use of the @WINRESOURCES macro to\n   retrieve a list of resources of a certain type contained in a file\n   (normally an executable file or dynamic link library). The @WINRESOURCES\n   macro uses the following syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0\n   \xc2\xa0@WINRESOURCES(<ResourceFileName>,<ResourceType>[,<ResourceNamePrefix>])\n\n   The ResourceFileName is the name of the file to read resources from. The\n   file will be found in the executable path if no directory name is\n   specified. The ResourceType can be one of the following values: BITMAP,\n   ICON, CURSOR, ANIICON, ANICURSOR, HDP_ICON or HDP_CURSOR (ANI = Animated,\n   HDP = Hardware dependant). The ResourceNamePrefix may be used to retrieve\n   only those resource names starting with this prefix.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [48][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. It can only be used in [6]XTRA applications.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   order-by(\xc2\xa0[7]source(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]orderByTarget\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]destination(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]orderByTarget\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]collate(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]?[17][<\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0>]\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]Field\xc2\xa0{,\xc2\xa0[20]?[21][<\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0>]\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]Field\xc2\xa0}]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Source\n\n   Defines the source stream containing the rows to be sorted. The stream\n   must be a stream defined in the application or an internal, temporary\n   stream. Internal streams are referred to as "@STREAM-<n>" where <n> is a\n   numeric constant from 1 to 8 or a letter between A and Z. An internal\n   stream can only be created by the [24]scroll function using the internal\n   stream as destination and a table as source. When using internal streams\n   for sorting, it is not necessary to define a separate stream to hold the\n   data set. See the example.\n\n   If a user defined stream is used, the formatting declared on the stream\n   must be either ASCII-DATA or BINARY. The include-fields declaration is\n   mandatory for such streams. The stream can either be mapped to existing\n   files or created by the scroll function.\n\n   Destination\n\n   Defines the stream to which the sorted rows are to be written. It can\n   later be used as a source stream in [25]scroll. If this parameter is\n   omitted, the rows will be written to the same stream they were read from\n   (source).\n\n   Collate\n\n   Any legal Concept 4GL [26]expression that results in a text being the name\n   of a collating sequence file (USO file). If no path is given the file is\n   expected to be found at the Concept setup directory. If no extension is\n   given the extension ".uso" is added.\n\n   The collating sequence file determines the sort sequence used by the\n   order-by function. For more information on collating sequence files,\n   please refer to the operation guide.\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of the field you want to sort. If you want to sort on several fields,\n   list them. Concept sorts from left to right.\n\n   Use of > or <:\n\n   If you want the rows to be sorted in descending order, put "<" in front of\n   the field name. If you want ascending order put ">" in front of the field\n   name. Default is ">".\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Sorting only applies within a table, so the owner and member tables have\n   to be sorted independently, i.e. two order-by statements are needed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7@STREAM-<n> are files controlled by Concept. They are given random names\n   and saved to the directory specified by SCRATCH-PATH in the configuration\n   file. The files will be deleted when the program terminates.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [27][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_initfile.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_saxget.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_order_by.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_stream.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xtra.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_source\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_orderbytarget.htm#idh_la_pop_orderbytarget\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_source\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_destination\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_orderbytarget.htm#idh_la_pop_orderbytarget\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_destination\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_collate\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_collate\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_la_sortdirection.htm#idh_la_pop_sortdirection\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_field\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_field\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_la_sortdirection.htm#idh_la_pop_sortdirection\n  21. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_field\n  22. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n  23. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_orderby.htm#idh_ma_orderby_field\n  24. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  25. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  26. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_expressions.htm\n  27. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_orderby.htm\n'

The function\n   will only return a value when this parameter is used in the\n   [36]@SAX-ELEMENT-START event hander.\n\n   Please note that namespace attributes (xmlns) are not returned.\n\n   File\n\n   Returns the name of a file containing the [37]value of the current node.\n   The file is generated on the scratch-path and is automatically removed\n   when the Concept session terminates.\n\n   Mode\n\n   When this parameter is set to TEXT, the [38]values parameter will return a\n   value trimmed for leading and trailing whitespaces. Whitespaces are all\n   control characters (ASCII value less than 32) and the space character.\n   When set to RAW, all characters from the XML file are returned. The\n   default is TEXT.\n\n   Name\n\n   This parameter is used to retrieve the value of a specific attribute of\n   the node. The [39]result parameter receives the value. Attribute names are\n   case sensitive and must include the namespace if one is present. The\n   function will only return a value when this parameter is used in the\n   [40]@SAX-ELEMENT-START event hander.\n\n   Name-Prefix\n\n   Returns the namespace definition for the current node.\n\n   Owner\n\n   Returns the node hierarchy for the current node. Each node in the\n   hierarchy is separated by a '/' character.\n\n   Result\n\n   Receives the value of the node attribute identified by the [41]name\n   parameter. The function will only return a value when this parameter is\n   used in the [42]@SAX-ELEMENT-START event hander.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returning the status code of the operation. Possible values are (see\n   [43]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status              Description\n   $UE_COMPONENT_ERROR An error occurred in the XML parser.\n   $UE_FAILED          Error when retrieving attribute information.\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND       The [44]name parameter specified a attribute name that\n                       was not found on the current node.\n   $UE_IO              Failed to create a temporary file for use with the\n                       [45]file parameter.\n                       The function was not executed inside the\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_NOW     [46]@SAX-ELEMENT-START, [47]@SAX-ELEMENT-VALUE or\n                       [48]@SAX-ELEMENT-END event handlers.\n\n   Tag\n\n   Returns the name of the current node. If the [49]name-prefix parameter for\n   the sax-read function is set to ON, the name will include the namespace\n   prefix.\n\n   Values\n\n   Returns the text content of the current node. If the [50]mode parameter is\n   set to TEXT, leading and trailing blanks are removed from the text.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status parameter is omitted and an error occurs, function\n b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > File Handling\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          SAX-READ()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Reads an XML file sequentially and is therefore extremely efficient when\n   processing large XML files.\n\n   The function will trigger the following events while parsing the XML file:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xb7[5]@SAX-ELEMENT-START\n\n   \xc2\xb7[6]@SAX-ELEMENT-VALUE\n\n   \xc2\xb7[7]@SAX-ELEMENT-END\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The function does not return until the file is completely read, an error\n   is encountered or the error function is executed in one of the event\n   handlers.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   sax-read(\xc2\xa0[8]file(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]check(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]error(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]error-text(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]mode(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]name-prefix(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]schema[27](\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]status(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Check\n\n   When this parameter is set to ON, the SAX parser will perform run-time\n   validation on the opened XML document using the currently loaded document\n   type definition (DTD), schema, or schema collection (see the [33]schema\n   parameter). Legal values are ON or OFF - default is ON.\n\n   Error\n\n   Returns the error code returned from the SAX parser itself when status\n   returned is $UE_COMPONENT_ERROR or $UE_FAILED.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   An error text returned by the SAX parser itself. The text will be on the\n   format:\n\n   [<reason of failure>][/,(<line>,<position on line>):<error text>]\n\n   File\n\n   The URL to the XML document to be opened. If no URL is specified, the\n   server defaults to the Windows Media Services (WMS) File Data Source\n   plug-in. For example, to specify a file on a FAT, NTFS, or any CIFS file\n   system, use c:\\wmroot\\movie.xml or file://c:\\wmroot\\movie.xml. ("file://"\n   identifies the URL scheme for the WMS File Data Source plug-in.).\n\n   Mode\n\n   When this parameter is set to TEXT, the XML parser will suppress control\n   characters (ASCII value less than 32) from the XML file, causing fewer\n   [34]@SAX-ELEMENT-VALUE events. When set to RAW, all characters from the\n   XML file are handled. The default is TEXT.\n\n   Please note that the mode parameter for [35]sax-get can be used to trim\n   the values independently of the mode setting for sax-read.\n\n   Name-Prefix\n\n   When this parameter is set to OFF, the names returned by the tag parameter\n   of the sax-get function are stripped for namespace information. Possible values are (see\n   [49]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status              Description\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_HANDLE  The handle parameter was not a legal XML handle.\n   $UE_COMPONENT_ERROR An error occurred in the XML parser, check the error\n                       and error-text parameter.\n   $UE_FAILED          There is no current node for the requested XML\n                       document. xml-get must be placed inside [50]xml-scroll\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND       The name parameter specified a attribute name that was\n                       not found on the current node.\n\n   Tag\n\n   Returns the node name, which varies depending on the node type.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Node type             Node name\n   cdatasection          #cdata-section\n   comment               #comment\n   documenttype          Contains the name of the document type; for example,\n                         xxx in <!DOCTYPE xxx ...>.\n   entity                Contains the name of the entity\n                         Contains the name of the entity referenced. Note\n   entityreference       that the name does not include the leading ampersand\n                         or the trailing semicolon. The name includes the\n                         namespace if one is present.\n   element               Contains the name of the XML tag, with any namespace\n                         prefix included if present.\n   notation              Contains the name of the notation.\n   processinginstruction Contains the target; the first token following the\n                         <? characters.\n   text                  #text\n\n   Text\n\n   Contains the text associated with the node.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Node type             Node name\n   cdatasection          Contains a string representing the text stored in\n                         the CDATA section.\n   comment               Contains the content of the comment, exclusive of\n                         the comment\'s start and end sequence.\n   documenttype          (Empty)\n   element               (Empty)\n   entity                (Empty)\n   entityreference       (Empty)\n   notation              (Empty)\n                         Contains the content of the processing instruction,\n   processinginstruction excluding the target. (The target appears in the tag\n                         parameter.)\n   text                  Contains a string representing the text stored in\n                         the text node.\n\n   Type\n\n   The type of the current node in the XML document. Possible values include\n   :\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value                 Description\n                         The node represents a CDATA section in the XML\n   cdatasection          source. CDATA sections are used to escape blocks of\n                         text that would otherwise be recognized as markup. A\n                         CDATA section node cannot have any child nodes.\n   comment               The node represents a comment in the XML document. A\n                         comment node cannot have any child nodes.\n                         The node represents the document type declaration,\n   documenttype          indicated by the <!DOCTYPE > tag. A document type\n                         node can have the following child node types:\n                         Notation and Entity.\n                         The node represents an expanded entity. An entity\n   entity                node can have child nodes that represent the\n                         expanded entity (for example, text and\n                         entityreference nodes).\n                         The node represents a reference to an entity in the\n                         XML document. This applies to all entities,\n   entityreference       including character entity references. An entity\n                         reference node can have the following child node\n                         types: element, processinginstruction, comment,\n                         text, cdatasection, and entityreference.\n                         The node represents an element. An element node can\n   element               have the following child node types: element, text,\n                         comment, processinginstruction, cdatasection, and\n                         entityreference.\n                         A node represents a notation in the document type\n   notation              declaration. A notation node cannot have any child\n                         nodes.\n                         The node represents a processing instruction from\n   processinginstruction the XML document. A processing instruction node\n                         cannot have any child nodes.\n   text                  The node represents the text content of a tag. A\n                         text node cannot have any child nodes.\n\n   Values\n\n   Returns the text content of the node or the concatenated text representing\n   the node and its descendants. Leading and trailing blanks are removed from\n   the concatenated text.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Node type             Description\n   cdatasection          Returns the text contained in the node, which is the\n                         same as the text parameter.\n   comment               Returns the text contained in the node, which is the\n                         same as the text parameter.\n   documenttype          (Empty)\n                         Returns a string representing the value of the node.\n   entity                This is the concatenated text of all sub nodes with\n                         entities expanded.\n   entityreference       Returns the string representation of the entity\n                         reference.\n                         Contains a string that represents the element\n                         content. This will also include the text content\n                         from all child elements, concatenated in document\n                         order. For example, consider the following XML.\n\n                         <count>\n\n                         <item>one</item>\n\n   element               <item>two</item>\n\n                         <item>three</item>\n\n                         <item>four</item>\n\n                         </count>\n\n                         The values parameter for the <count> element\n                         contains the value "one two three four".\n   notation              (Empty)\n   processinginstruction Returns the text contained in the node, which is the\n                         same as the text parameter.\n   text                  Returns the text contained in the node, which is the\n                         same as the text parameter.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status parameter is omitted and an error occurs, [51]function\n   execution is aborted.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The name and result parameter must always be specified together.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The values retrieved by the text, values and result parameters are always\n   considered to be text.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xml_scroll.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Input\xc2\xa0>                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                            ASK()                                        side\n\n   This function is used to prompt the user for input.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   ask(\xc2\xa0[4]?[5]<Destination\xc2\xa0field>\xc2\xa0[,\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]<Question\xc2\xa0text>]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Destination field\n\n   The answer to the question is stored in the <Destination field>. The field\n   name may be post fixed.\n\n   Question text\n\n   This is the question text displayed on the screen, prompting the user for\n   an answer. If this parameter is omitted, ask() can be used to check for a\n   key hit on the keyboard.\n\n   When <Question text> is non blank the function act as a simple interface\n   for the dialogue-box function using the following rules:\n\n   \xc2\xb7The first word of <Question text> is used also as [8]title.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the <Question text> contains at least one unescaped \'/,\' character\n   sequence, the text before the last \'/,\' is used as [9]text, and the rest\n   as [10]prompt. Otherwise the complete text is used as [11]prompt.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The [12]image parameter is assigned $IconQuestion.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The functions defined on the <Destination field> will be executed after a\n   value is entered. To avoid execution of the functions, the following\n   construction may be used:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\xc2\xa0field="TRIGGER"\xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0ask("TEMP",\'Give\xc2\xa0X\xc2\xa0a\xc2\xa0value\')\n\n   \xc2\xa0(field="TEMP") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0local\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0storage("DEST")\n\n   \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0assign("DEST"="TEMP")\n\n   \xc2\xa0(field="DEST") \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0if(....\n\n   \xc2\xb7The input rules will conform to the declarations which are specified on\n   the <Destination field>. (E.g. [13]storage, [14]display, letter-type,\n   automatic-return etc.).\n\n   \xc2\xb7If an error occurs while the functions on the <Destination field> is\n   executed, the ask function is repeated automatically.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The user may abort the input by hitting the CANCEL or EXIT key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7By omitting the <Question text> parameter, the function can be used to\n   check whether a key has been pressed. If this is the case, the value of\n   the key will be inserted into <Destination field>. The program will not\n   stop execution to prompt the user. The contents of <Destination field> can\n   then be tested. If any input has been given or any key has been pressed,\n   the <Destination field> will contain a positive number corresponding to a\n   numeric value of the character given. Otherwise it will be set to zero.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   UNIX note: Polling the keyboard may increase execution time. See function\n   [15]scroll for details.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [16][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_xml_properties.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ask.htm#idh_ma_ask_destfield\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_applicationfield.htm#idh_la_pop_applicationfield\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ask.htm#idh_ma_ask_questiontext\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm#idh_ma_dialogbox_title\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm#idh_ma_dialogbox_text\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm#idh_ma_dialogbox_prompt\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm#idh_ma_dialogbox_prompt\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dialogbox.htm#idh_ma_dialogbox_image\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_storage.htm\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_displaycodes.htm\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_scroll.htm\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_ask.htm\n'
b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Input\xc2\xa0>                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        DIALOGUE-BOX()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This function is used to give information and ask questions using a\n   dialogue window (dialogue box).\n\n   Syntax\n\n   dialogue-box(\xc2\xa0[[5]buttons(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]background(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]colour(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]default(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]image(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]modal(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]position(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[28]prompt(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]result(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[34]size(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]numberExpression,\xc2\xa0[37]?[38]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[39]status(\xc2\xa0[40]?[41]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[42]text(\xc2\xa0[43]?[44]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[45]title(\xc2\xa0[46]?[47]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Background\n\n   Defines the appearance of the background of the dialogue box. See the\n   style definition for [48]background for a description of the syntax of\n   this parameter.\n\n   Buttons\n\n   Any legal Concept 4GL [49]expression that returns a text string. Several\n   buttons can be specified consecutively by placing a slash ('/') between\n   them. The user is given the option of selecting one of the buttons which\n   appear from left to right at the bottom of the dialogue box in the order\n   which they were specified. The user may navigate between buttons using the\n   right and left arrow keys. If this parameter is left out, the user is\n   asked to enter a value directly into the field.\n\n   If the parameter buttons is used, the result=<Field> parameter must be\n   specified to contain the value of the button chosen. If the result field\n   is numeric and the left-most button is chosen, the result field will\n   contain 1. If the second button is chosen, 2 is returned and so on. If the\n   result field is alphanumeric, the text relating to the button selected\n   will be stored in the result field. If no button is selected, the result\n   field will contain 0 or blank depending on its data type.\n\n   Colour\n\n   Defines the [50]colour of the display area in the dialogue box.\n\n   Default\n\n   Defines which button is to be used as default button (1 for the first\n   button, 2 for the second and so on).\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines an icon image to be displayed in the top left corner of the\n   dialogue window. Any [51]image definition may be used, but the image will\n   be scaled to the icon size defined in the Windows Display properties\n   (typically 32x32 pixels).\n\n   The following image definitions may be used to show standard Windows icons\n   (see [52]Macro Values for the textual values of these constants).:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Description Image Macro\n   Error       '$IconError'\n   Question    '$IconQuestion'\n   Warning     '$IconWarning'\n   Information '$IconInformation'\n\n   Modal\n\n   Defines the [53]modality of the dialogue-box. Dialogue-boxes are modal by\n   default (same as using the parameter value 'ON').\n\n   Position\n\n   Specifies the line (first number expression) and the column (second number\n   expression) where you want the upper left corner of the dialogue box to\n   appear. If left out, Concept will put the dialogue box in the middle of\n   the screen.\n\n   Prompt\n\n   May be any legal 4GL expression that results in a text string. The prompt\n   will appear in the lower part of the window, in front of the input field.\n\n   Result\n\n   Must be a field specified within the application. Result has to be defined\n   when prompt or button are specified, to store the answer. The storage type\n   and colour of the field is used in the input dialogue. If the storage type\n   of the field is BIT, a check-box will be displayed instead of an input\n   element.\n\n   It is not legal to use an internal variable as parameter to result.\n\n   Size\n\n   Declares the size of the dialogue-box i.e. how much space it requires when\n   displayed on the screen. If left out a minimum required value will be\n   used.\n\n   Status\n\n   Status of the operation. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error codes\n   (see [54]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   1                 The dialogue-box was interrupted\n   $UE_UNKNOWN_FIELD An illegal field was specified by the result parameter.\n\n   Text\n\n   A text to be displayed in the upper part of the window, possibly over\n   several lines.\n\n   The text may contain formatting options controlling the layout of the\n   text. A formatting option has the syntax:\n\n   <option lead-in><option>\n\n   The default option lead-in is the forward slash (/) character. Legal\n   options are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Option Description\n   ,      Indicates that a new line is to be started.\n   n      No justification.\n   l      Left justification.\n   r      Right justification.\n   c      Center justification.\n   x      Disable option processing.\n   =X     Change the option lead-in to X (X may be any character)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the text is to contain the current option lead-in character (and option\n   processing is not disabled with the x option), the option lead-in\n   character must be written twice. Thus, if the text to be written is\n   runtime dependent and may contain the current lead-in character, either\n   disable option processing using the x option, or change the lead-in\n   character using the =X option to a character known not to be present in\n   the text.\n\n   Title\n\n   May be any legal 4GL expression that results in a text string. This text\n   will appear in the caption of the window.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The user may abort the input by pressing the ABORT or RETURN key.\n\n   \xc2\xb7On completed input, the functions of the result field will be executed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The dialogue box will use the same default-style-prefix as the\n   application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [55][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. Default is 'PLAIN/UCS'.\n\n   Status\n\n   Field receiving the number of texts converted.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The result file of the operation always has the extension '.ldt',\n   independent of the setting in the uqsystem.ini file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Any file existing will be overwritten.\n\n   \xc2\xb7All lines in the source file starting with a positive integer number\n   followed by an equal sign will be written to the LDT file. All other lines\n   will be ignored.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [20][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_progress_dialogue.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_ldt_load.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_ldtfileid\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_ldtfileid\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_file\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_file\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_language\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_language\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_fileformat\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_fileformat\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_status\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm#idh_ma_ldtload_status\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_ldtload.htm\n"

Default is 'PLAIN/UCS'.\n\n   Status\n\n   Field receiving the number of texts converted.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The source file can either be an LDT format file or an initialization\n   file.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The result file will be in initialization file format with a section\n   header as expected by the LDT system.\n\n   \xc2\xb7When the result file has the extension '.txt', a plain text file without\n   text numbers will be written. Empty lines will be written for each text\n   number not containing any text definition. In such a file a line number\n   can be considered as a text number.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Any file existing will be overwritten.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [20][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtload.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_license.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_ldt_unload.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_ldtfileid\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_ldtfileid\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_file\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_file\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_language\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_language\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_fileformat\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_fileformat\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_status\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_ldtunload.htm#idh_ma_ldtunload_status\n  20. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_ldtunload.htm\n"

The license name is the same as the\n   name of the license section defined in the uqconfig configuration file.\n\n   Status\n\n   A numeric field set to $OK (0) if the operation is successful. Possible\n   error values (see [52]Macro Values for the numeric values of these\n   constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                   Description\n   $UE_LIC_NO_ACCESS_DB     SECURITY not active\n   $UE_LIC_NO_SUCH_NAME     No such license name\n   $UE_LIC_DATE_EXPIRED     License date expired\n   $UE_LIC_TOO_MANY_USERS   Too many users\n   $UE_LIC_NO_NAME_GIVEN    Missing license name\n   $UE_LIC_INVALID_PASSWORD Invalid password\n   $UE_LIC_INVALID_NAME     Invalid license name\n   $UE_LIC_NO_RESERVE       No corresponding reserve of the license was\n                            found. Already released?\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The following parameters are only valid for the generate-license function:\n\n   Expire-date\n\n   Numeric expression defining the expire date of the license. The date is\n   defined as YYYYMMDD. Value 0 defines a license with no expire date.\n\n   Max-users\n\n   Numeric expression defining the maximum numbers of users that may use the\n   licensed product. A valid password is required to generate\n   a license string.\n\n   Result\n\n   Alphanumeric field to receive the license string. The field must be at\n   least 32 characters wide.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7SECURITY must be active.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The license string consist of lowercase letters in the range from \xef\xbf\xbda\xef\xbf\xbd to\n   \xef\xbf\xbdp\xef\xbf\xbd.\n\n   \xc2\xb7A password must be supplied by Visma Unique.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [53][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. The address book called is the one belonging to the mail\n   client. Each recipient name is preceded with a prefix indicating the role\n   of the recipient as has been selected in the address book. The 3 possible\n   prefixes are: to: (recipient to which a mail is to be sent), cc:\n   (recipient to which a carbon-copy of the mail is to be sent), and bcc:\n   (recipient to which a blind carbon-copy of the mail is to be sent).\n\n   If the field upon calling the addressbook-mail() function contains a\n   value, it is tried to pass this on to the address book. If the contents of\n   the field do not represent valid recipient names, the contents are\n   ignored.\n\n   Interface\n\n   Defines the interface to use for the command. Possible values are 'CMC'\n   and 'SMAPI'. If the parameter is not specified, the default mail interface\n   (as defined in the uqconfig file) is used. The internal field\n   [20]@MAIL_INTERFACE can be used to retrieve the default interface.\n\n   Count\n\n   Returns the number of recipients contained in the result parameter.\n\n   Mail-status\n\n   Return code from the mail client itself. This will provide you with more\n   detailed [21]error information.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [22]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status               Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY    The specified mail interface is not available on your\n                        computer.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL         Failed to load the Windows DLL for mail facilities.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLLSERVICES Failed to load services from the mail DLL.\n   $UE_MAIL_NOCON       No connection with the mail service provider\n                        available.\n   $UE_MAIL_ADDRBOOK    Failed calling the address book.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The address book is part of the mail client installed on your workstation\n   and is not a Concept application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [23][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Mail Functions\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        CONNECT-MAIL()                                   side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The connect-mail() function connects you to a mail service provider.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   connect-mail(\xc2\xa0[,[5]interface(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]service(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]profile(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]password(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]interactive(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]mail-status(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]status(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Interface\n\n   Defines the interface to use for the command. Possible values are 'CMC'\n   and 'SMAPI'. If the parameter is not specified, the default mail interface\n   (as defined in the uqconfig file) is used. The internal field\n   [26]@MAIL_INTERFACE can be used to retrieve the default interface.\n\n   Service\n\n   A string indicating the location of the underlying messaging service, for\n   example, the path to a message store or a remote server node name.\n\n   Profile\n\n   This is the name identifying the mail client application. Several user\n   profiles may have been set up in the mail client that define how the\n   client is set up for a particular user (definition of mail boxes, address\n   books and information services). If this parameter is omitted, it depends\n   on the mail client configuration what the result of connect-mail() will\n   be: if there has been defined a default profile, this profile will be used\n   - otherwise a dialogue box is shown by the mail client from which a\n   profile name can be selected. This last action can be suppressed by\n   specifying OFF for the interactive() parameter.\n\n   Password\n\n   A string containing the password required for access to the mail service.\n\n   Interactive\n\n   Default: ON. If this value is ON, the mail implementation itself may use\n   dialogues to ask the user for missing connect information (service name,\n   profile name or password). If the value is OFF, the status parameter will\n   contain an error code. If the connect succeeded with the help of mail\n   dialogues, the returned status will be $OK.\n\n   Mail-status\n\n   Return code from the mail client itself. This will provide you with more\n   detailed [27]error information.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [28]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status               Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY    The specified mail interface is not available on your\n                        computer.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL         Failed to load the Windows DLL for mail facilities.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLLSERVICES Failed to load services from the mail DLL.\n   $UE_MAIL_LOGGEDON    Already logged on to the service provider.\n   $UE_MAIL_LOGON       Could not log on to the mail service provider.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7What happens during a connect depends on the setup of the mail service\n   provider and (if available) on the setup of the mail client on your\n   computer:\n\n   Not connected to a network\n\n   If you are not connected to a network (i.e. there is no connection to the\n   mail server), the connect-mail() will succeed, but will only act on the\n   mail files locally on the computer. If you have \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0stored a personal\n   address book locally, this will be available. Of course, no mail can be\n   sent or received.\n\n   Connected to a network\n\n   If you have established a connection to a network, the mail server might\n   be available to a mail client application. The connection information\n   needed is stored in a user profile that can be \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0setup the first time\n   you run the mail client. If you already have a mail client available on\n   your computer, the connect-mail() will be connected using the same profile\n   as is used by this client.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n DLL.\n   $UE_MAIL_NOCON       No connection with the mail service provider\n                        available.\n   $UE_MAIL_LIST        Downloading the list of mail messages failed.\n\n   Rules\n\n b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Mail Functions\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          POP-MAIL()                                     side\n\n   The pop-mail() function is used to count, query, read and delete email\n   messages stored on a POP3 server.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   pop-mail(\xc2\xa0[4]command(\xc2\xa0CONNECT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0DISCONNECT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0COUNT\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0QUERY\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0READ\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0DELETE\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[5]attachments(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]error-text(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]file(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]handle(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]header(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]item(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]mail-status(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]mode(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]password(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[32]release-resources(\xc2\xa0[33]?[34]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[35]result(\xc2\xa0[36]?[37]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[38]separator(\xc2\xa0[39]?[40]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[41]server(\xc2\xa0[42]?[43]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[44]size(\xc2\xa0[45]?[46]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[47]status(\xc2\xa0[48]?[49]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[50]user(\xc2\xa0[51]?[52]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Attachments\n\n   Specifies the directory where any MIME attachments for the given email\n   message are to be saved. The directory must exist. Use '.' to specify the\n   current directory. Note that an older file of the same name will be\n   overwritten by the newer file.\n\n   Command\n\n   The following table lists required and optional parameters for each\n   command:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command    Required Parameters     Optional Parameters\n   CONNECT    server, user, password  error-text, mail-status, status\n   DISCONNECT \xc2\xa0                       release-resources, error-text,\n                                      mail-status, status\n   COUNT      \xc2\xa0                       result, error-text, mail-status, status\n   QUERY      item                    handle, header, size, error-text,\n                                      mail-status, status\n   READ       item, file, attachments result, error-text, mail-status, mode,\n                                      status\n   DELETE     item                    error-text, mail-status, status\n\n   Error-Text\n\n   A textual error message returned from the POP3 client.\n\n   File\n\n   Specifies the name and path for the file where the email message content\n   is to be saved.\n\n   Handle\n\n   Returns a unique message identifier for the email message. The handle is\n   always the same for a particular email message, regardless of the email\n   message number. Most POP3 servers provides such a handle. Please note that\n   the syntax of the handle is different among POP3 servers and that the\n   actual unique identifier needs to be extracted from the value returned.\n\n   Header\n\n   Returns the header part of the identified email message. See a POP3\n   specification on how to extract information from the header.\n\n   Item\n\n   A message number between 1 and the number of email messages returned by\n   the COUNT command. Note that message numbers are unique only in the\n   current session (between CONNECT and DISCONNECT).\n\n   Mail-Status\n\n   Return code from the POP3 mail client itself. This will provide you with\n   more detailed [53]error information.\n\n   Mode\n\n   Defines the way messages are read from the server. If the expression\n   evaluates to 'RAW', the message is retrieved without further processing.\n   Otherwise some less important information is stripped from the message\n   (this is the default).\n\n   Password\n\n   Password for the user account on the POP3 server.\n\n   Release-Resources\n\n   When set to ON, the POP3 mail client is unloaded from memory when the POP\n   session is disconnected. The default is OFF.\n\n   Result\n\n   For the COUNT command it returns the number of email messages found on the\n   POP3 server.\n\n   For the READ command it returns a semicolon separated list of attachment\n   file names (without path).\n\n   Separator\n\n   Specifies the separator character used in the [54]attachments file list.\n   The default value is ';'.\n\n   Server\n\n   The name of the POP3 server to use. The notation <server name>:<port\n   number> can be used if the POP3 server uses a non-standard port number for\n   the POP3 service (110 is the default port).\n\n   The POP3 server name can also be specified in dotted decimal notation (e.g\n   10.23.231.1).\n\n   Size\n\n   Returns the size of the entire email message, including any attachments.\n   Note that attachments will be encoded (MIME, UUENCODE, etc.), and thus\n   take up more room than after they are decoded.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [55]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status            Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY The U4GSEE.dll is corrupted\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL      The U4GSEE.dll was not found\n   $UE_MAIL_LOGON    Unable to logon to the given POP3 server.\n   $UE_MAIL_LOGGEDON Already logged on to a POP3 server. Only one POP3 server\n                     might be open at a time.\n   $UE_MAIL_NOCON    Not connected to a POP3 server.\n   $UE_IO            The path or attachment parameter of the READ command\n                     identifies a non existent or write protected directory.\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR   The file parameter was missing or empty for the READ\n                     command.\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND     Message numbers must be larger than 0.\n   $UE_MAIL_READ     Failed to read the email message header. See mail-status\n                     or error-text for more details.\n   $UE_MAIL_ID       Failed to retrieve the email message handle. See\n                     mail-status or error-text for more details.\n   $UE_SIZE          Failed to retrieve the email message size. See\n                     mail-status or error-text for more details.\n   $UE_FAILED        Operation failed. See mail-status or error-text for more\n                     details.\n\n   User\n\n   User name on the POP3 server.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The POP3 functionality is implemented on top of the SMTP/POP3 Email\n   Engine (SEE) from MarshallSoft Computing Inc.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_listmail.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Mail Functions\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         READ-MAIL()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Using the mail handle retrieved from the [5]list-mail() function, each\n   message can be downloaded separately with the read-mail() function.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   read-mail(\xc2\xa0[6]handle(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[9]interface(\xc2\xa0[10]?[11]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[12]mail-recipients(\xc2\xa0[13]?[14]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[15]result(\xc2\xa0[16]?[17]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[18]file(\xc2\xa0[19]?[20]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[21]attachments(\xc2\xa0[22]?[23]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[24]mark-as-read(\xc2\xa0[25]?[26]onOff\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[27]mail-status(\xc2\xa0[28]?[29]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[30]status(\xc2\xa0[31]?[32]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Handle\n\n   This is the unique identification of the message to be read. This\n   identification number is obtained from the [33]list-mail() function.\n   Please note that the datatype of the handle depends on the mail\n   [34]interface used.\n\n   Interface\n\n   Defines the interface to use for the command. Possible values are 'CMC'\n   and 'SMAPI'. If the parameter is not specified, the default mail interface\n   (as defined in the uqconfig file) is used. The internal field\n   [35]@MAIL_INTERFACE can be used to retrieve the default interface.\n\n   Mail-recipients\n\n   The alphanumeric field used in the mail-recipients parameter will contain\n   a semicolon separated list of recipients who have received the same mail.\n   The names are preceded according to the description found in\n   [36]send-mail() (see there).\n\n   Result\n\n   The alphanumeric field used here will contain the text of the mail\n   identified by the Handle. As the field length in Concept is limited, it is\n   also possible to store the mail text in a file directly. To accomplish\n   this, set the File-parameter to 'ON' and set the value of the Result field\n   to the name and location of the file you want the read-mail() function to\n   store the mail text in.\n\n   File\n\n   Set this parameter to 'ON' if you want to save the text of the mail in a\n   file. The file name used has to be provided in the Result parameter. By\n   default, the File parameter is 'OFF', meaning that the text of the mail is\n   stored in the field indicated by the Result parameter.\n\n   Attachments\n\n   Here, the attachments (if any) are stored as a semicolon separated list of\n   file names. These attachments can be opened by e.g. the 4GL [37]editor()\n   function.\n\n   Mark-as-read\n\n   Default: ON. When this parameter is set to ON, the mail message will be\n   marked as 'read' at the mail service provider. Setting the parameter to\n   OFF will not influence this setting.\n\n   Mail-status\n\n   Return code from the mail client itself. This will provide you with more\n   detailed [38]error information.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [39]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status               Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY    The specified mail interface is not available on your\n                        computer.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL         Failed to load the Windows DLL for mail facilities.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLLSERVICES Failed to load services from the mail DLL.\n   $UE_MAIL_NOCON       No connection with the mail service provider\n                        available.\n   $UE_MAIL_READ        Reading the specified mail was not successful.\n\n b"                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Mail Functions\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         SEND-MAIL()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The send-mail() function will send the specified mail to the addressees\n   listed in the recipients parameter.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   send-mail(\xc2\xa0[5]mail-recipients(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[8]automatic-connect(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[11]title(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]text(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]attachments(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]interactive(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]interface(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]mail-status(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]status(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Automatic-Connect\n\n   When this parameter is set to ON (default is OFF), the send-mail()\n   function will act as a function for sending a mail in-one-go. It takes\n   care of connecting, sending and disconnecting. If the send-mail() function\n   fails to connect to a mail service provider itself, it will present a\n   dialog box requesting the user to connect. If the mail-recipients\n   parameter is an empty string, your mail client will bring up an\n   application in which you can specify mail recipients and other mail\n   parameters. In most cases (dependent on your mail client), this\n   application will be a full worthy mail composer, so that by just\n   specifying send-mail(automatic-connect(ON)) you already have accomplished\n   an integration with your mail package.\n\n   With this parameter set to ON, this is the simplest way to send a mail\n   message from Concept.\n\n   Mail-Recipients\n\n   This parameter contains a list of names to which the mail is to be sent.\n   The names are separated by a semicolon and optionally preceded with a\n   prefix (to:, cc: or bcc: - use lowercase!). If a name has no prefix, the\n   prefix to: is assumed. If the send-mail() function is used in combination\n   with the [32]addressbook-mail() function, the value of the field used in\n   the result parameter of addressbook-mail() can directly be used in the\n   recipients parameter here. The name is resolved to a mail address using\n   the configuration in the address book.\n\n   It is also possible to use an Internet mail address in the list of\n   recipients. Example: mail-recipients('cc:Suzie@company.com').\n\n   When the recipient list is prefixed with a question mark ('?') and the\n   [33]interactive parameter is 'ON', the mail client program will show a\n   window in which you can modify the recipient list and other parameters.\n\n   Title\n\n   The title of the mail as it will appear in the mail listing of the\n   recipient(s).\n\n   Text\n\n   The contents of the mail. The length of the mail is limited by the maximum\n   storage code of an alphanumeric field. If more text should be sent with\n   the mail, use an attachment.\n\n   Attachments\n\n   A semicolon separated list of file names that have to be sent with the\n   mail. If one or more of the attachments cannot be localized, the\n   send-mail() function will fail.\n\n   Interactive\n\n   Default: ON. If this value is ON, the mail implementation itself may use\n   dialogues to ask the user for missing connect information (service name,\n   profile name or password). If the value is OFF and the automatic-connect()\n   parameter is set to ON, the mail implementation will not present user\n   dialogues when connect- or recipient-information is missing in the\n   send-mail() function. In this case, the send-mail() function will fail and\n   the status parameter(s) will contain an error code.\n\n   Interface\n\n   Defines the interface to use for the command. Possible values are 'CMC'\n   and 'SMAPI'. If the parameter is not specified, the default mail interface\n   (as defined in the uqconfig file) is used. The internal field\n   [34]@MAIL_INTERFACE can be used to retrieve the default interface.\n\n   Mail-status\n\n   Return code from the mail client itself. This will provide you with more\n   detailed [35]error information.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [36]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY     The specified mail interface is not available on\n                         your computer.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL          Failed to load the Windows DLL for mail facilities.\n   $UE_MAIL_DLLSERVICES  Failed to load services from the mail DLL.\n   $UE_MAIL_NOCON        No connection with the mail service provider\n                         available.\n   $UE_MAIL_NORECIPIENTS No recipients specified for the send-mail function\n   $UE_MAIL_RESOLVE      Could not resolve the given name to a valid mail\n                         recipient\n   $UE_MAIL_SEND         Sending the mail message failed.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the result code for this function is $OK, it means that the send\n   operation has succeeded - not that the mail has reached all recipients\n   successfully.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n
