b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Mail Functions\xc2\xa0>       til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                       SMTP-SEND-MAIL()                                  side\n\n   The smtp-send-mail() function will send the specified mail to the\n   addressees listed in the recipients parameter.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   smtp-send-mail(\xc2\xa0[4]mail-recipients(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]attachments(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]error-text(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]formatting(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]from(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]header(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[22]mail-status(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[25]password(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[28]reply(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]separator(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[34]server(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[37]status(\xc2\xa0[38]?[39]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[40]text(\xc2\xa0[41]?[42]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[43]title(\xc2\xa0[44]?[45]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[46]user(\xc2\xa0[47]?[48]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Mail-recipients\n\n   This parameter contains a list of valid e-mail addresses to which the mail\n   is to be sent. The names are separated by a semicolon and optionally\n   preceded with a prefix (to:, cc: or bcc: - use lowercase!). If a name has\n   no prefix, the prefix to: is assumed.\n\n   Attachments\n\n   A semicolon separated list of file names that have to be sent with the\n   mail. If one or more of the attachments cannot be localized, the\n   smtp-send-mail() function will fail. The file name can be specified using\n   the format "<File>|<Name>". In this case <Name> will be used instead of\n   the full file name (<File>) to name the attachment.\n\n   Error-text\n\n   A textual error message returned from the SMTP client.\n\n   Formatting\n\n   Controls whether the message is or is not encoded as quoted-printable. Use\n   \'OFF\' to disable quoting, \'PLAIN\' to enable normal quoting, \'HTML\' to\n   enable quoting of embedded HTML text, \'RICH\' or \'DEFAULT\' to enable rich\n   text quoting and \'ISO8859\' to enable ISO 8859 character quoting. Any other\n   value is handled as a user defined quoting and passed on to the SMTP\n   client.\n\n   Default is \'RICH\'.\n\n   From\n\n   A valid e-mail address identifying the sender of the mail. This is a\n   required parameter and must either be specified using this parameter or in\n   the smtp-server uqconfig file parameter. The internal field [49]@SMTP_FROM\n   contains the default value for this parameter.\n\n   Header\n\n   A list of additional header lines to be sent with the message. Header\n   lines must be in the format "<FieldName>: <FieldBody>" (see RFC #822) and\n   must be separated by the character specified in the [50]separator\n   parameter.\n\n   Mail-status\n\n   Return code from the SMTP mail client itself. This will provide you with\n   more detailed [51]error information.\n\n   Password\n\n   The password to use in connection with the user parameter.\n\n   Reply\n\n   A valid e-mail address identifying a reply-to address for the mail. If not\n   specified the reply address defaults to the address of the sender of the\n   mail. If neither the from or reply parameters are specified, the reply\n   address will default to the reply address defined by the smtp-server\n   uqconfig file parameter. The internal field [52]@SMTP_REPLY contains the\n   default value for this parameter.\n\n   Separator\n\n   The separator used in the [53]header list. Default: semicolon (;).\n\n   Server\n\n   The name of the SMTP server to use. The notation <server name>:<port\n   number> can be used if the SMTP server uses a non-standard port number for\n   the SMTP service (25 is the default port).\n\n   The SMTP server name can also be specified in dotted decimal notation if\n   wanted (e.g 10.23.231.1).\n\n   If not specified the server will default to the server specified by the\n   smtp-server uqconfig file parameter. The internal field [54]@SMTP_SERVER\n   contains the default value.\n\n   Status\n\n   Return code from this function. $OK if no error occurred. Possible error\n   codes (see [55]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                Description\n   $UE_MAIL_FACILITY     The U4GSEE.dll is corrupted\n   $UE_MAIL_DLL          The U4GSEE.dll was not found\n   $UE_MAIL_NORECIPIENTS No recipients specified for the smtp-send-mail\n                         function\n   $UE_MAIL_RESOLVE      Invalid syntax for a mail address in the\n                         mail-recipient parameter.\n   $UE_FAILED            Sending the mail message failed. See mail-status or\n                         error-text for more details.\n\n   Text\n\n   The contents of the mail. If the first character is a \xef\xbf\xbd@\xef\xbf\xbd then the value\n   is considered to be a file name which contains the message to be sent.\n\n   Title\n\n   The title (subject) of the mail.\n\n   User\n\n   The name of the user to log on to the server. The password parameter can\n   be used to specify a password.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the status code for this function is $OK, it means that the send\n   operation has succeeded - not that the mail has reached all recipients.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Email addresses used by SMTP must be bracketed, such as\n   \xef\xbf\xbd<on@mycompany.com>\' or \xef\xbf\xbdOla Nordmann <on@mycompany.com>\'. The\n   smtp-send-mail function will automatically add brackets around email\n   addresses if no \xef\xbf\xbd<\xef\xbf\xbd bracket is found inside the address.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The SMTP functionality is implemented on top of the SMTP/POP3 Email\n   Engine (SEE) from MarshallSoft Computing Inc.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_sendmail.htm\n   2. If set to RIGHT it\n   will right-justify the item on the menu/toolbar. Default is LEFT. If the\n   expression is empty the justification is left unchanged.\n\n   Command\n\n   An expression defining an event or action to be taken when the item is\n   activated (see [38]define-menu() for more details).\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines the [39]images used to represent the four states of a toolbar\n   button or menu item:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Image number Meaning in toolbar   Meaning in menu\n   1            button up            unchecked\n   2            button down          checked\n   3            button up with focus \xc2\xa0\n   4            button up and locked \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the menu item can be toggled and the image parameter is omitted, the\n   Windows standard menu marks are used: a check mark for boolean values and\n   a large dot for radio groups.\n\n   Information\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining the information text to be displayed\n   when navigating into the menu item. The text is displayed in the status\n   line.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Expression resulting in either \'ON\' or 1 to lock the menu item, or \'OFF\'\n   or 0 to open the entry.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Use \'&&\' to get the \'&\' character as a part\n   of the text. The access character must be unique within the level (top\n   level or sub menu). Access characters may not be used in the tool-bar.\n\n   Toolbar menus of type \'COOL\' can show button images as well as text\n   (normal toolbar menus only use images). Whether text is to be shown and\n   where it is to be shown is a user dependent option that can be set in the\n   Workspace Options dialogue. Text specified using the text parameter is not\n   shown when the Toolbar option is set to "Show selective text on right". In\n   this case the [41]selective-text parameter can be used to specify a text\n   to be shown on selected items.\n\n   The text and the selective-text parameters are mutually exclusive.\n\n   Selective-Text\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining a text to be used in coolbar menus\n   (see [42]use-menu) when the Workspace toolbar option "Show selective text\n   on right" is active.\n\n   The [43]text and the selective-text parameters are mutually exclusive.\n\n   Width\n\n   The width of the menu/toolbar item in pixels. Default is 0, which allows\n   the menu/toolbar system to set the appropriate width. The intended use for\n   this parameter is menu/toolbar items using the\n   STARTAPPLICATION/CALLAPPLICATION command.\n\n   [44][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. If set to RIGHT it\n   will right-justify the item on the menu/toolbar. Default is LEFT.\n\n   Command\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining event or action to be taken when the\n   item is selected. The following commands are available:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   EVENT <Event name>  [<Event parameter>]\n\n   Generates the event identified by <Event name> with the optional event\n   parameter <Event parameter>. See [41]perform-event and [42]on for a\n   complete list of events and their possible parameters. The event may be\n   trapped by the current application or generate the standard functionality\n   for the event.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   MENU\n\n   Defines the entry to be a sub menu. When selected the sub menu will pop\n   up.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   SEPARATOR\n\n   A \'dummy\' command defining the item to show up in the menu as a horizontal\n   separator used to group items. In tool-bars, additional space will be\n   inserted between the buttons.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   TOGGLE <Field name>\n\n   Toggles the field contents identified by <field name>. If the item is\n   activated, the field value is altered before the field functions are\n   executed. If the field belongs to a radio group and the item is already\n   checked, nothing happens.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the field is not defined in the current sub-application, the menu item\n   is disabled. The check-marks are set after the @START event.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   EXECUTE <Field name>\n\n   Executes the functions of the field identified by <field name>.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the field is not defined in the current sub-application, the menu item\n   is disabled.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   STARTAPPLICATION/CALLAPPLICATION <Interface Application>\n\n   Starts or Calls the application defined by <Interface Application>. See\n   the page on [43]STARTAPPLICATION/CALLAPPLICATION for details.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Image\n\n   Defines the [44]images used to represent the toolbar button or menu item.\n   The following table shows which state the different images represent:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Index Toolbar              Menu, Popup\n   1     Button Up            Not Checked\n   2     Button Down          Checked\n   3     Button Up with Focus \xc2\xa0\n   4     Button Up and Locked \xc2\xa0\n   5     Button Hot           \xc2\xa0\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Toolbar button images for normal toolbars should include the frame as\n   Concept does not draw a frame around buttons in this case. The image\n   prefix \'@@\' can be used to make Concept draw the frame. Alternatively the\n   menu can be defined with the type \'COOL\' (see [45]create-menu). In this\n   case Concept draws a thin frame when the mouse cursor hovers over a\n   button.\n\n   If both the text and the image parameter are used when defining items that\n   are to be used in toolbar menus (see [46]use-menu), the text is not shown\n   unless the menu is defined as type \'COOL\' (see also the notes for the\n   [47]text parameter).\n\n   If the menu item can be toggled and the image parameter is omitted, the\n   Windows standard menu marks are used: a check mark for boolean values and\n   a large dot for radio groups.\n\n   Information\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining the information text to be displayed\n   when navigating into the menu item. The text is displayed in the status\n   line.\n\n   Item\n\n   Expression defining the name of the item. The name must be unique within\n   the menu.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Expression resulting in either \'ON\' or 1 to the lock the menu item, or\n   \'OFF\' or 0 to open the entry.\n\n   Position\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining the position of the new item relative\n   to other items in the menu. If omitted, the default position is after the\n   last item defined on the top level.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A position specification takes the following format:\n\n   <item or offset> [. [<offset>]]...\n\n   <item or offset> is either the name of an existing item, or a number\n   identifying an existing item on top level where the first (leftmost) item\n   is item number 1. A period (.) indicates a sub level, and may only be used\n   if the item \'above\' is defined as a sub menu. <offset> is a number\n   identifying an item where the first item on the sub level is number 1.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible values are (see [48]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                    Description\n   $OK                       Success\n   $UE_MENU_UNKNOWN          Unknown menu name\n   $UE_MENUITEM_EXIST        Menu item name already exists\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ITEM_POSITION Illegal position definition\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_EVENT         Illegal event/command\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_ONOFF         Illegal parameter value supplied to lock\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note that if status is not defined and error occurs, the equivalent of an\n   error function will be performed.\n\n   Text\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining the text to be displayed in the menu.\n   If the item text contains the character \'&\', the next character will be\n   used as the access character. Use \'&&\' to get the \'&\' character as a part\n   of the text. The access character must be unique within the level (top\n   level or sub menu). Access characters may not be used in the tool-bar.\n\n   Toolbar menus of type \'COOL\' can show button images as well as text\n   (normal toolbar menus only use images). Whether text is to be shown and\n   where it is to be shown is a user dependent option that can be set in the\n   Workspace Options dialogue. Text specified using the text parameter is not\n   shown when the Toolbar option is set to "Show selective text on right". In\n   this case the [49]selective-text parameter can be used to specify a text\n   to be shown on selected items.\n\n   The text and the selective-text parameters are mutually exclusive.\n\n   Selective-Text\n\n   An alphanumeric expression defining a text to be used in coolbar menus\n   (see [50]use-menu) when the Workspace toolbar option "Show selective text\n   on right" is active.\n\n   The [51]text and the selective-text parameters are mutually exclusive.\n\n   Width\n\n   The width of the menu/toolbar item in pixels. Default is 0, which allows\n   the menu/toolbar system to set the appropriate width. The intended use for\n   this parameter is menu/toolbar items using the\n   STARTAPPLICATION/CALLAPPLICATION command.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [52][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. In the second\n   format, the field will receive a list of names of all the items in the sub\n   menu defined by the item parameter. For other items the format\n   <item>.<offset> is used.\n\n   Lock, Text, Selective-Text, Information, Command,Alignment,Width\n\n   These fields receive the current value of the corresponding parameter as\n   defined in define-menu and change-menu. Please note that width only return\n   a value (other than 0) if width has been set by [50]define-menu or\n   [51]change-menu.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation.  Unknown menu name\n   $UE_MENUITEM_UNKNOWN Unknown item name\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note that if status is not defined and an error occurs, the equivalent of\n   an error function will be performed.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [53][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_dropmenu.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Menu Handling\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                          USE-MENU()                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   The use-menu() function will replace the current menu in the main Concept\n   window with another menu definition. Both the drop-down menu-bar and the\n   toolbar can be replaced.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   use-menu(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]Menu\xc2\xa0name\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]current(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]status(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]usage(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]menuType\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Menu name\n\n   Expression defining the name of the menu. The menu must have been created\n   earlier using the [16]create-menu() function.\n\n   Current\n\n   Defines an alphanumeric field to receive the name of the current menu.\n   This value can be used later to restore the previous menu.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible values are (see [17]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status           Description\n   $OK              Success\n   $UE_MENU_UNKNOWN Unknown menu name\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Note that if status is not defined and an error occurs, an error function\n   will be performed.\n\n   Usage\n\n   Defines how the menu is to be used. DROP-DOWN is the drop down system menu\n   and TOOL-BAR is an optional window containing push buttons. Normally, the\n   toolbar contains the most used entries from the menubar to allow fast\n   access.\n\n   Toolbar menus can be shown in two different types. The type is defined\n   when creating the menu (see [18]create-menu) and influences the way images\n   and texts are shown in toolbar menus.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Menus to be used in the toolbar can not include sub menus.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [19][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inquiremenu.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_help.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_use_menu.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_menuname\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_current\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_current\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_status\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_status\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_usage\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_menutype.htm#idh_la_pop_menutype\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_usemenu.htm#idh_ma_usemenu_usage\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_createmenu.htm\n  17. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_macro_values.htm\n  18. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_createmenu.htm#idh_ma_createmenu_type\n  19. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_usemenu.htm\n'

                side\n\n   Invoke a help system and display help for a given topic.\n\n   WinHelp Syntax\n\n   This syntax is valid when using WinHelp files.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n \xc2\xa0[,[43]status(\xc2\xa0[44]?[45]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Element-Name\n\n   Valid for HtmlHelp only.\n\n   The name of an element of type WINDOW in the current application which\n   will be used to display the HtmlHelp viewer. If the file name does\n   not contain a path specification, Concept tries to find the file in the\n   help-path specified in the uqconfig file.\n\n   When working with HtmlHelp files, you may specify a complex file name\n   (including topic and window type) as described in the HTML Help\n   documentation (see the Microsoft web pages on HTML Help). In this case the\n   file name should include the path.\n\n   When working with WebHelp, filename should specify the main page for your\n   documentation (E.g \'refman\\html\\index.html\').\n\n   Find\n\n   The find parameter identifies a keyword to search on. If the keyword\n   identifies more than one topic, the first topic is selected. If the\n   keyword can not be found, the index will be shown.\n\n   When working with HtmlHelp files, the index pane will be displayed and the\n   keyword found will be selected - the topic found will not be displayed\n   automatically. This does not necessarily mean that the operation\n   $UE_FAILED      failed, but the Windows API does not handle such cases\n                   properly.\n\n                   Returned from WebHelp if executing the "WebHelp" reader\n                   (normally your internet browser) fails.\n   $UE_MISSING_PAR An invalid combination of parameter values has been\n                   specified.\n   $UE_APPLICATION WebHelp. No application was found to open the filename\n                   specified.\n\n   Topic\n\n   The topic name identifies a context to give help on. This may be a number\n   defined in the [MAP] section of the help project file or a context string\n   as defined in the help file. You must have access to the source of the\n   help file to find these values.\n\n   When using HtmlHelp files, the topic name must be the name of an HTML file\n   compiled into the HtmlHelp file. Depending on the structure of the help\n   project, the topic file name may have to include a path.\n\n   Text\n\n   Valid for HtmlHelp only.\n\n   Specifies a text to show in a popup window. If the [51]file parameter is\n   used and the text expression evaluates to a numeric value, or the\n   expression contains an exclamation mark (!) followed by a numeric value,\n   the text will be read from a text file compiled into the help file. The\n   numeric value must then refer to a text with the corresponding ID in the\n   text file referenced. If it is not installed on your machine, an installation\n   package can be downloaded from Microsoft\'s web pages.\n\n   \xc2\xb7As the HTML Help viewer uses Internet Explorer components to display help\n   files, it can also be used to display web pages. Using the topic parameter\n   to specify web addresses and showing the "help file" in a WINDOW element,\n   it is possible to embed a web browser in 4GL applications.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n See the chapter on [6]locking for more\n   details.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   lock(\xc2\xa0[7]?[8]Field,[9]?[10]lockType\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Field\n\n   Name of field to lock/unlock.\n\n   LockType\n\n   This parameter can either have the value ON or OFF, where ON locks the\n   field and OFF unlocks it.\n\n   If this parameter is preceded with the keyword PERMANENT, then the lock is\n   permanent - i.e. the initial lock value will not be reset for example when\n   the row is cleared.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The field declaration lock sets the initial lock state on a field.\n\n   \xc2\xb7lock(<field>,ON|OFF) is equivalent to writing :\n   [11]change(field(<field>),lock('ON|OFF'))\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [12][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_inspect.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_regular_expression.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_change.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_changeelement.htm\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_locking.htm\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_lock.htm#idh_ma_lock_field\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_la_locktype.htm#idh_la_pop_locktype\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_lock.htm#idh_ma_lock_locktype\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_change.htm\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_lock.htm\n"
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Miscellaneous\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                     REGULAR-EXPRESSION()                                side\n\n   Finds strings in texts using regular expressions. The function uses the\n   PCRE (Perl Compatible Regular Expressions) library (www.pcre.org).\n\n   Syntax\n\n   regular-expression(\xc2\xa0{[4]find(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0|\xc2\xa0[7]handle(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]numericExpression\xc2\xa0)}\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]error-code(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[13]error-text(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[16]from(\xc2\xa0[17]?[18]numericExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[19]length(\xc2\xa0[20]?[21]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[22]match(\xc2\xa0[23]?[24]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[25]multi-line(\xc2\xa0[26]?[27]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[28]position(\xc2\xa0[29]?[30]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[31]result(\xc2\xa0[32]?[33]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[34]status(\xc2\xa0[35]?[36]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[37]text(\xc2\xa0[38]?[39]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Error-Code\n\n   Returns the PCRE error code if the function fails.\n\n   Error-Text\n\n   Returns the PCRE error text if the function fails.\n\n   Find\n\n   Specifies the search pattern. The pattern may contain the following\n   meta-characters:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Meta character    Description\n   .                 Matches exactly one character, regardless of what the\n                     character is.\n                     The question mark indicates that the character\n   ?                 immediately to its left should be matched either zero\n                     times or one time\n   *                 Indicates that the character immediately to its left may\n                     be repeated any number of times, including zero.\n   +                 Indicates that the character immediately to its left may\n                     be repeated one or more times.\n   \\                 Indicate that the character immediately to its right is\n                     to be taken literally\n   \\d                Matches exactly one digit\n   \\D                Matches exactly one non-digit character\n   \\w                Matches exactly one letter, one number, or the\n                     underscore character (_).\n   \\W                Matches any one character except a letter, a number or\n                     the underscore\n                     Matches exactly one character of whitespace. (Whitespace\n   \\s                is defined as spaces, tabs, newlines, or any character\n                     which would not use ink if printed on a printer.)\n   \\S                Matches exactly one character that is not a whitespace.\n                     Matches the boundaries of words; that is, it matches\n   \\b                whitespace, punctuation and the very beginning and end\n                     of the text.\n   \\B                Searches for a character that is not a word boundary.\n                     Where "n" is a number from zero to seven. This is used\n   \\nnn              for specifying control characters that have no typed\n                     equivalent.\n                     Works like the star metacharacter (*), except the length\n   {min,max} \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 of the string it matches must be within the minimum and\n                     maximum length specified in the braces.\n   |                 It indicates an either/or behavior by separating two or\n                     more possible choices.\n                     Matches one occurrence of any character inside the\n                     brackets. A dash can be used to indicate a range. If you\n   []                wish to include a dash as one of the characters to\n                     match, put the dash immediately before the right\n                     bracket. The ^ character inverts the search for the\n                     characters inside a bracket.\n   ^                 Beginning of String\n   $                 End of string\n   \\t                Matches the TAB character\n   \\n                Matches newline\n   \\r                Matches return (CR)\n   \\xhh              Matches character with hex code hh\n   ()                Sub expressions\n   \\Q\xef\xbf\xbd\\E             Removes the special meaning of any character in between\n                     \\Q and \\E\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Please refer to the PCRE documentation (www.pcre.org) for a detailed\n   description of the expression syntax.\n\n   From\n\n   Specifies the start position in the text from where to start the search.\n   The default is 1.\n\n   Handle\n\n   Specifies the handle of a precompiled search pattern. To speed up searches\n   use the find parameter along with the result parameter. The result\n   parameter will return a handle to a compiled version of the search pattern\n   specified by the find parameter. This handle can be used for all following\n   searches.\n\n   Length\n\n   Returns the length of the matched result.\n\n   Match\n\n   Must evaluate to either CASE-INSENSITIVE or CASE-SENSITIVE and decides\n   whether the search should be performed case-sensitive. The default is\n   CASE-INSENSITIVE.\n\n   Multi-Line\n\n   Specifies whether the text should be treated as one line, or as multi-line\n   text..\n\n   Position\n\n   Returns the position in the text where a match was done.\n\n   Result\n\n   Returns the handle of a compiled version of the search pattern specified\n   when used with the find parameter.\n\n   Status\n\n   Returns the status of the operation. Possible error codes (see [40]Macro\n   Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status                      Description\n   $OK \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 Success. A match was found or a find\n                               expression was successfully compiled.\n   $UE_NOT_FOUND \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0       There was no match.\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_HANDLE          The specified handle was not found.\n   $UE_FAILED \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0 \xc2\xa0  The operation failed\n\n   Text\n\n   The text to search in.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The result, match and multi-line parameters can only be used along with\n   the find parameter.\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the handle parameter is specified without the text parameter, the\n   search pattern specified by the handle is released.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [41][IMG]\n\n   Acknowledgements\n\n   This function uses the PCRE library which is distributed under the\n   following licence:\n\n   PCRE LICENCE\n\n   ------------\n\n   PCRE is a library of functions to support regular expressions whose syntax\n\n   and semantics are as close as possible to those of the Perl 5 language.\n\n   Release 7 of PCRE is distributed under the terms of the "BSD" licence, as\n\n   specified below. Smartcard\n   authentication means the user must have a valid smartcard in a smartcard\n   reader connected to the PC in order to use the application. This is\n   implemented by only accepting user input while valid smartcard is present.\n   If not, a dialogue is presented giving the user the option to either\n   reinsert the valid smartcard or terminate the session.\n\n   Please consult the Operations Guide to learn how to configure the\n   smartcard authentication functionality.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   request-smartcard-authentication(\xc2\xa0[4]mode(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]rsaMode\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]status(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]fieldName\xc2\xa0)])\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Mode\n\n   TEMPORARY\n\n   Means that smartcard authentication is activated for the application in\n   which the function call is done. (Hint: Call the function from the\n   applications @START event.)\n\n   PERMANENT\n\n   Means that smartcard authentication is required for the application in\n   which the function call is done and all subsequent application.\n   (Requesting permanent smartcard authentication from the initial\n   application is equivalent to using the uqconfig system command\n   smartcard-authentication=on.)\n\n   Status\n\n   Status value $OK is returned if a valid smartcard is given. If the status\n   parameter is not used an a valid smartcard is not given, the function\n   execution stops and an error is raised.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The first valid smartcard inserted becomes the only smartcard accepted in\n   the session. b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Miscellaneous\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           TOKEN()                                       side\n\n   This function breaks up a string into tokens. In a source program, a token\n   is the basic element recognised by the compiler. Keywords, identifiers,\n   constants and operators are examples of tokens.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   token(\xc2\xa0[4]source(\xc2\xa0[5]?[6]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[7]token-separator(\xc2\xa0[8]?[9]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[10]separator(\xc2\xa0[11]?[12]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[13]result(\xc2\xa0[14]?[15]fieldName\xc2\xa0)\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Source\n\n   The name of the alphanumeric field that contains the string to be parsed\n   into tokens.\n\n   Token-separator\n\n   Separator for the source-parameter iindicated with this parameter. Default\n   separator is colon (,).\n\n   Separator\n\n   Each token in the result-parameter is separated by the character indicated\n   with this parameter. Default separator is semi-colon (;).\n\n   Result\n\n   The tokens found in the source parameter are stored in the alphanumeric\n   field referenced by the result-parameter.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7Each token in the resulting field is prefixed with one character\n   describing the token type:\n\n   \xc2\xa0S : single token, like AAA and \xef\xbf\xbdBBB\xef\xbf\xbd\n\n   \xc2\xa0C : composite token, like AAA(BBB,CCC) and XXX=YYY\n\n   \xc2\xa0K : the keyword of a decomposed composite token\n\n   \xc2\xb7If the source-parameter contains one composite token and no single\n   tokens, the composite token is decomposed into a keyword and its\n   parameters.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Composite tokens using the equal sign separator (\xef\xbf\xbd=\xef\xbf\xbd) take only a single\n   parameter token.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [16][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_set.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_trace.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_source\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_source\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_token_separator\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_separator\n  10. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_separator\n  11. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n  12. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_separator\n  13. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_result\n  14. file:///dev/html_idh_la_fieldname.htm#idh_la_pop_fieldname\n  15. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm#idh_ma_token_result\n  16. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_token.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Miscellaneous\xc2\xa0>        til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                           TRACE()                                       side\n\n   The function is executed if any debug trace option is enabled, or debug\n   output is set to a file. It writes a text to the current trace output\n   (debug window or file).\n\n   Syntax\n\n   trace(\xc2\xa0[4]?[5]Text\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Text\n\n   Any legal 4GL expression that results in a text variable. The value will\n   be displayed in a debug window or written to the trace file.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7The <alpha expression> is evaluated and written to the debug window or\n   trace file if any debug option is enabled, or debug output is set to a\n   file. Thus. in normal operation, the function is ignored and has a\n   negligible performance cost.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The trace function is evaluated and written to the current trace output\n   even if the application is protected.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [6][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_token.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_multimedia.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_trace.htm#idh_ma_trace_text\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_trace.htm\n'
b'                                                                   [1]Forrige\n   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components   side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > Output\xc2\xa0>               til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                        MULTI-MEDIA()                                    side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Executes commands on the following multimedia devices: wave audio, MIDI\n   sequencer, CD audio and movie (avi).\n\n   Syntax\n\n   multi-media(\xc2\xa0[5]type(\xc2\xa0[6]?[7]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[8]command(\xc2\xa0[9]?[10]textExpression\xc2\xa0)\n\n   \xc2\xa0,[11]device-id(\xc2\xa0[12]?[13]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[14]element-name(\xc2\xa0[15]?[16]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[17]file(\xc2\xa0[18]?[19]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[20]hold(\xc2\xa0[21]?[22]textExpression\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[23]result(\xc2\xa0[24]?[25]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[26]status(\xc2\xa0[27]?[28]fieldName\xc2\xa0)]\n\n   \xc2\xa0[,[29]track(\xc2\xa0[30]?[31]numberExpression\xc2\xa0)]\xc2\xa0)\n\n   Parameters\n\n   Type\n\n   Identifies the multimedia device to address. Possible values for the type\n   parameter are: \xef\xbf\xbdWAVE\xef\xbf\xbd, \xef\xbf\xbdMIDI\xef\xbf\xbd, \xef\xbf\xbdCD\xef\xbf\xbd and \xef\xbf\xbdMOVIE\xef\xbf\xbd.\n\n   Command\n\n   Defines the command to execute on the device specified in the\n   type-parameter. Possible values are here:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Command  Description\n   \xef\xbf\xbdPLAY\xef\xbf\xbd   Start the device playing the file or track specified\n   \xef\xbf\xbdLOOP\xef\xbf\xbd   Same as \xc2\xb4PLAY\xc2\xb4, repeatedly playing the file until stopped. Only\n            supported for device type \xc2\xb4MOVIE\xc2\xb4.\n   \xef\xbf\xbdPAUSE\xef\xbf\xbd  Stop the device playing a file or track, but maintain the current\n            position within the file or track played.\n   \xef\xbf\xbdRESUME\xef\xbf\xbd Has to be issued after a \xef\xbf\xbdPAUSE\xef\xbf\xbd when the remaining of the file\n            or track has to be played.\n            Stop the device playing a file or track, and reset the position\n   \xef\xbf\xbdSTOP\xef\xbf\xbd   to the beginning of the file, or the beginning of the first\n            track.\n   \xef\xbf\xbdLENGTH\xef\xbf\xbd Return the length of the track specified in the track-parameter.\n   \xef\xbf\xbdTRACKS\xef\xbf\xbd Return the number of the tracks on the media (file or CD).\n\n   Device-id\n\n   A unique identifier is returned when the PLAY command is issued. It\n   identifies the device used to play the item specified. The device-id is\n   required when issuing the PAUSE, RESUME and STOP command. This parameter\n   is ignored for the LENGTH and TRACKS commands.\n\n   Element-name\n\n   This parameter is used only in the PLAY command for MOVIE devices. It is\n   the name of the element where the movie is shown in. The element must be\n   declared in the current application and be of type WINDOW. Note that this\n   WINDOW element cannot be resized when your application is run, so you have\n   to make sure at design time that your video fits the size of the window\n   (the movie is not resized, but clipped inside the window).\n\n   File\n\n   Is a complete file specification of the file to be played by the WAVE,\n   MIDI and MOVIE device. The WAVE device accepts wave-files with the .wav\n   extension, MIDI accepts MIDI files with the .mid or .rmi extension, and\n   MOVIE accepts movie-files with the .avi extension. This parameter is\n   required for the PLAY command on WAVE, MIDI and MOVIE, and is ignored in\n   all other cases.\n\n   Hold\n\n   Two values are accepted here: ON and OFF. If the value is ON, the\n   multi-media() function will not return until the command is completely\n   executed (a CD track played completely, for example). If OFF, the function\n   execution in the program will continue. In this case, the event [32]@MM is\n   triggered when the command is finished. For the PAUSE, STOP, LENGTH and\n   TRACKS command, the default value is fixed to ON (and the value of the\n   hold-parameter is ignored), for PLAY and RESUME the default is OFF.\n\n   Result\n\n   A field reference in this parameter will be given the following results:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Value  Description\n   PLAY   (not used)\n   LOOP   (not used)\n   PAUSE  (not used)\n   RESUME (not used)\n   STOP   (not used)\n          length of the WAVE, MIDI or MOVIE file in seconds\n   LENGTH\n          length of the CD track specified (or if tracks=0, the whole CD) in\n          seconds\n          1 for WAVE, MIDI or MOVIE\n   TRACKS\n          actual number of audio tracks for a CD\n\n   Status\n\n   If the command is completed successfully, a field specified in the status\n   parameter will receive the value $OK. Possible error codes are (see\n   [33]Macro Values for the numeric values of these constants):\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Status             Description\n   $UE_TYPE           Invalid value for the type parameter\n   $UE_ILLEGAL_CMD    Invalid value for the command-parameter\n   $UE_MM_DEVICEID    Invalid value for the device-id parameter (or: not\n                      specified)\n   $UE_MM_FILE        The file-parameter needs to be specified (or: file was\n                      not found)\n   $UE_MM_ELEMENTNAME An element name of a WINDOW element is required to show\n                      the video in\n   $UE_MM_TRACK       Value of the track parameter is out of range\n   $UE_MM_HOLD        Illegal value for the hold-parameter\n   $UE_MM_NOMEDIA     No media is found in the device\n   $UE_MM_NOTREADY    The device is not ready to execute the command\n   $UE_MM_ERROR       An error occurred when executing the multi-media()\n                      function\n\n   Track\n\n   Defines the track to play or to request the length from. For WAVE, MIDI\n   and MOVIE, the only valid value is 1. For CD, the value must in between 0\n   and the total number of audio tracks found on the CD, where 0 has the\n   special meaning \xef\xbf\xbdwhole CD\xef\xbf\xbd. For the commands other than PLAY and LENGTH,\n   this parameter is ignored. Default for CD is 0, and 1 for the other device\n   types.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [34][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_trace.htm\n   2. After this function has been\n   executed, the fields that have been changed by the last user input are\n   highlighted. The message taken as argument by the error function is\n   displayed in a dialogue box and the user has the choice of:\n\n   \xc2\xb7inputting new data, where all functions will be re-executed after the new\n   input.\n\n   \xc2\xb7rolling back, where the old values in the changed fields will be restored\n   and no changes registered in the database. This is the\n   error message that will be written in the error dialogue box. If the\n   result is a blank text, the dialogue box will not appear.\n\n   The error text may contain formatting options controlling the layout of\n   the text. A formatting option has the syntax:\n\n   <option lead-in><option>\n\n   The default option lead-in is the forward slash (/) character. Legal\n   options are:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Option Description\n   ,      Indicates that a new line is to be started.\n   n      No justification.\n   l      Left justification.\n   r      Right justification.\n   c      Center justification.\n   x      Disable option processing.\n   =X     Change the option lead-in to X (X may be any character)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   If the text is to contain the current option lead-in character (and option\n   processing is not disabled with the x option), the option lead-in\n   character must be written twice. Thus, if the text to be written is\n   runtime dependent and may contain the current lead-in character, either\n   disable option processing using the x option, or change the lead-in\n   character using the =X option to a character known not to be present in\n   the text.\n\n   Rules\n\n   \xc2\xb7After having executed the error function, the processing of functions are\n   aborted. Functions defined after the error function will not be executed.\n\n   \xc2\xb7The error function will normally only have meaning when defined within an\n   if-endif structure. The if test is used to define the error condition.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [7][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_bell.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_message.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_error.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_error.htm#idh_ma_error_errortext\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_error.htm\n'

The user\n   may only select files from one of the given paths, unless the list starts\n   with a semicolon. In this case, the path list acts as a list of predefined\n   paths.\n\n   When this field is empty, the user will get access to the whole file\n   system.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   InitialMask (storage(A(256))))\n\n   This field contains a mask for the files to show in the application\n   initially. The user may change this mask by entering a mask in the file\n   name field or by selecting a mask from the available file types list.\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will use the mask that was used\n   when the file pick has been used the last time (see also ModuleName).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   InitialPath (storage(A(256)))\n\n   This field contains a path initially to be searched for files with the\n   given mask. When LegalPaths is set, this path must be a path from this\n   list. Otherwise it may be any path existing in the file system.\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will use the path that was used\n   when the file pick has been used the last time (see also ModuleName).\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FileTypes (storage(A(256)))\n\n   This field contains a semicolon separated list of file types to pick file\n   selection masks from. The list may either consist of masks only, or it may\n   use a special syntax to include short descriptions for the file types\n   together with the file masks. In the second case the file mask has to be\n   included in the description enclosed in round brackets (see the example at\n   the end of this section).\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will use a default list\n   containing file types most commonly used with Concept.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ModuleName (storage(A(20)))\n\n   This field contains a string identifying the module or application using\n   the file pick application. This string is used when remembering the last\n   used file name, path and search mask. This can be used to keep this\n   information local to a certain module or application. As this information\n   is stored in the concept.ini file, it is maintained when leaving Concept\n   and starting it again.\n\n   When this field is empty, the information will be stored without a\n   reference to the module that used it, thus making it possible to share\n   this information between modules.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   MultiSelect (storage(BIT))\n\n   If this parameter is set to 1, it is possible to select multiple files\n   from the list. In this case the return parameter FullFileName contains the\n   directory from which the files were picked, and FileNames contains a\n   semicolon separated list of file names.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   WindowTitle (storage(a(100)))\n\n   This field contains the title for the stream (window). If no value given,\n   the default title apply.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FullFileName (storage(A(512)))\n\n   This field contains the full name (including the path) of the file chosen\n   by the user. It will be empty when the selection has been canceled. If the\n   MultiSelect parameter is set to 1, the field contains the directory from\n   which the files were picked.\n\n   As it is not possible to select a file that is not existing, the result is\n   always a valid file name.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FileNames (storage(A(10240)))\n\n   This field is only used when the MultiSelect parameter is set to 1. In\n   this case the field contains a semicolon separated list of file names. The\n   return parameter FullFileName contains the directory from which the files\n   were picked.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [7][IMG]\n\n   @UQUSAVEAS\n\n   This application shows files in the given directory with the specified\n   extension. The user can then pick a file from this list, enter the name\n   manually or show different selections.\n\n   The application can be used to let the user pick a file to save to.\n   Therefore a warning message will be displayed when the user selects a file\n   that already exists.\n\n   The actual saving of the file has to be done in the calling application.\n\n   Syntax\n\n   call(\'@UQUSAVEAS\',\n\n   \xc2\xa0export(FullFileName,\xc2\xa0FileFormat,\xc2\xa0FileTypes,\xc2\xa0FileFormats,\xc2\xa0ModuleName,LegalPaths,InitialPath),\n\n   \xc2\xa0import(ChosenFullFileName,\xc2\xa0ChosenFileFormat))\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Parameters\n\n   FullFileName (storage(A(512)))\n\n   This field contains the full name (including the path) of a file that is\n   proposed as the file to save in when the application starts. The user may\n   change this file name afterwards.\n\n   When the file name does not contain any path information, the last used\n   path (see also ModuleName) will be used.\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will not propose any file name\n   and show the files available according to the last used path and file\n   mask.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FileFormat (storage(A(16)))\n\n   This field contains a file format that is proposed to the user as the file\n   format to store the file in. The user may change this format unless the\n   FileFormats list contains only this format. In this case, it will not be\n   possible to choose a file format in the application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FileTypes (storage(A(256)))\n\n   This field contains a semicolon separated list of file types to pick file\n   selection masks from. The list may either consist of masks only, or it may\n   use a special syntax to include short descriptions for the file types\n   together with the file masks. In the second case the file mask has to be\n   included in the description enclosed in round brackets (see the example at\n   the end of this section).\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will use a default list\n   containing file types most commonly used with Concept.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   FileFormats (storage(A(10240)))\n\n   This field contains a semicolon separated list of file formats.\n\n   When this field is empty, the application will use a default list\n   consisting of all file formats supported by Concept.\n\n   Note: To disable the display of the file format list box in the\n   application, use the same value for FileFormat and FileFormats when\n   calling @UQUSAVEAS. As a default list will be used when FileFormats is\n   empty, this value has to be non-blank. Always use this technique when you\n   don\'t use the file format in the calling application.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ModuleName (storage(A(20)))\n\n   This field contains a string identifying the module or application using\n   the file pick application. This string is used when remembering the last\n   used file name, path and search mask. This can be used to keep this\n   information local to a certain module or application. As this information\n   is stored in the concept.ini file, it is maintained when leaving Concept\n   and starting it again.\n\n   When this field is empty, the information will be stored without a\n   reference to the module that used it, thus making it possible to share\n   this information between modules.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ChosenFullFileName (storage(A(512)))\n\n   This field contains the full name (including the path) of the file chosen\n   by the user. It will be empty when the selection has been canceled.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   ChosenFileFormat (storage(A(16)))\n\n   This field contains the file format chosen by the user.\n\n   When the field has not been changed by the user, the same value as\n   supplied in the input parameter will be returned to the calling\n   application. Please see the note on the input parameter FileFormats on\n   ignoring the file format.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   LegalPaths (storage(A(10000)))\n\n   This field contains a semicolon separated list of legal paths. The user\n   may only store files in one of the given paths, unless the list starts\n   with a semicolon. In this case, the path list acts as a list of predefined\n   paths.\n\n   When this field is empty, the user will get access to the whole file\n   system.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   InitialPath (storage(A(256)))\n\n   This field contains a path initially to be shown if the FullFileName is\n   empty. When LegalPaths is set, this path must be a path from this list.\n   Otherwise it may be any path existing in the file system.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [8][IMG]\n\n   Common Include File\n\n   To make the usage of the file pick applications as easy as possible, you\n   can find the contents of a common include file in the following example.\n\n   This include file contains all the fields needed for calling the file pick\n   applications and two more fields for calling them by just executing them\n   or computing a filename into them.\n\n   You can supply default values to the parameter fields by defining\n   constants with the same name as the corresponding parameter field (e.g.\n   $UFPInitialMask) before including the file. Doing so, you don\'t have to\n   set the values on startup of your application or by assigning them before\n   the file pick is called. The constant must be defined as a valid\n   alphanumeric expression, as it is used in an initial-value declaration.\n\n   When using this include, you can easily call @UQUFP01 and @UQUSAVEAS by\n   computing a file name to be proposed in the file pick to either\n   "UFPGetFileName" (calling @UQUFP01) or "UFPSaveFileAs" (calling\n   @UQUSAVEAS). In both cases the results will be in the fields described in\n   the previous sections.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [9][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_write.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_idh_uq_uqfilepick.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_idh_uq_uqfilepick.htm#idh_uq_uqufp01\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_uq_uqfilepick.htm#idh_uq_uqusaveas\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_uq_uqfilepick.htm#idh_uq_commoninclude\n   7. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_uqufp01.htm\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_uqusaveas.htm\n   9. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_commoninclude.htm\n'

b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > System            side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Applications\xc2\xa0>                                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         @UQUGRIDREP                                     side\n\n   [4]See also\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This report is used when a user chooses to print the contents of a\n   grid-form (see [5]perform-event(event(PRINTRECORDS))). Concept will then\n   produce two files, one initialization file containing a description of the\n   layout of the grid-form, and a CSV file containing the data of the\n   connected table. After this report is called, the necessary forms and\n   elements to print the data are created (based on the information found in\n   the initialization file) and the CSV file is scrolled to print the data.\n\n   This general mechanism makes it possible to replace the default report in\n   Concept by a system specific one that can be tailored to meet specific\n   needs. See the section "System specific report" for a detailed description\n   how to write such a report.\n\n   The default report in Concept uses a set of styles to produce a standard\n   layout when printing the contents of a grid-form:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Name                       Used for\n   XT-PAGEHEADER-BACKGROUND   Page heading form\n   XT-PAGEHEADER-TITLE        Page heading elements (Table name)\n   XT-TABLEHEADING-BACKGROUND Table heading form\n   XT-TABLEHEADING-TEXT       Table heading elements (Hdr.<n>)\n   XT-TABLEDATA-BACKGROUND    Table detail form\n   XT-TABLEDATA-TEXT          Table detail elements (Elm.<n>)\n   XT-PAGEFOOTER-BACKGROUND   Page tail form\n   XT-PAGEFOOTER-TEXT         Page tail elements (Date, Time, Page)\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   A different prefix for these styles can be defined in the System Database\n   (uqsystem.ini). You can specify this prefix in the [SETTINGS] section in\n   the item "XtraDefaultStylePrefix".\n\n   If specific style components (Background, Colour, Frame, Font) as defined\n   in the grid-form should be used, then this can be accomplished by a\n   definition in the [SETTINGS] section of the System Database. In this case,\n   the item "PrintRecordsMode" must contain the name(s) of the style\n   component(s) (separated by \'+\'). If you e.g. want to use the same colours\n   in the report, you define the PrintRecordsMode as "Background+Colour".\n\n   System specific report\n\n   The report has to be registered in the [APPLICATION] section of the System\n   Database (uqsystem.ini) in the item "PrintRecords". When Concept finds an\n   application registered in the System Database, it will call the first sub\n   application of this application after the two data files have been\n   produced. It also contains the name\n   of the CSV file that contains the data to be printed. See the next section\n   for a detailed description of this file.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   OutFileName\n\n   This field (A(512)) contains the name of the output device for the\n   printout.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Initialization File\n\n   This file contains the following sections describing the contents and\n   layout of the grid-form to be printed:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [Settings]\n\n   DataFile=<Name\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0CSV\xc2\xa0file>\n\n   TableName=<Name\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0connected\xc2\xa0table>\n\n   Formular=<Formular\xc2\xa0used\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0online\xc2\xa0application>\n\n   HdrHeight=<Height\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0header\xc2\xa0elements\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0element\xc2\xa0units>\n\n   FormHeight=<Height\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0line\xc2\xa0elements\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0element\xc2\xa0units>\n\n   NumberOfElements=<Number\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0columns\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0grid-form>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [Hdr.<n>]\n\n   ;\xc2\xa0with\xc2\xa0<n>\xc2\xa0being\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0number\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0a\xc2\xa0column\xc2\xa0(<=\xc2\xa0NumberOfElements)\n\n   Type=<Type>\n\n   Bck=<Background>\n\n   Col=<Colour>\n\n   Frame=<Frame>\n\n   Font=<Font>\n\n   Align=<Alignment>\n\n   Y=<Line>\n\n   X=<Position>\n\n   H=<Height>\n\n   W=<Width>\n\n   Connect=[Y|N]\n\n   Text=<Name\xc2\xa0of\xc2\xa0connected\xc2\xa0field\xc2\xa0(Connect=Y)\xc2\xa0or\xc2\xa0text>\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [Elm.<n>]\n\n   ;\xc2\xa0same\xc2\xa0entries\xc2\xa0as\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0Hdr\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   This\xc2\xa0information\xc2\xa0can\xc2\xa0be\xc2\xa0used\xc2\xa0to\xc2\xa0generate\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0same\xc2\xa0layout\xc2\xa0that\xc2\xa0is\xc2\xa0used\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0online\xc2\xa0application\xc2\xa0in\xc2\xa0the\xc2\xa0xtra\xc2\xa0report.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   CSV File\n\n   The CSV file contains the data found in the grid-form as alphanumeric\n   values using the standard CSV separators. b'   Navigasjon:\xc2\xa0 Concept 4GL Reference Manual > Components          [1]Forrige\n   and Definitions > Function Reference > System            side[2]G\xef\xbf\xbd tilbake\n   Applications\xc2\xa0>                                                til kapittel\n                                                             oversikt[3]Neste\n                         @UQUPROGRES                                     side\n\n   This system application is used if a [4]Progress Dialogue is initiated by\n   the [5]progress-dialogue function and the [6]application parameter was not\n   specified. The application implements three different types of Progress\n   Dialogues. The type and behaviour of the dialogue depends on the\n   parameters passed on in the [7]text supplied when initiating it. The\n   parameter string must be defined using the following syntax:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   <Title>,<AllowAbort>,<Type>,<Lock>,<Delay>\n\n   Title\n\n   Title to be used in the dialogue. If the title contains spaces it must be\n   enclosed in quotes.\n\n   AllowAbort\n\n   Specifies whether it should be possible for the user to abort (cancel) the\n   Progress Dialogue. Possible values: 0 and 1.\n\n   Type\n\n   Specifies the type of the dialogue. Currently the following types are\n   supported:\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   Type   Description\n          Simple dialogue displaying the text sent when updating the\n   0, 100 dialogue. Type 100 will also ensure that the progress-dialogue is\n          the focus thread at each UPDATE.\n          Dialogue displaying a progress bar and the text sent when updating\n   1, 101 the dialogue. The progress bar will be changed during each update.\n          Type 101 will also ensure that the progress-dialogue is the focus\n          thread at each UPDATE.\n          Dialogue displaying a progress bar which shows the progress in\n          percent and the text sent when updating the dialogue. For this type\n          the text parameter must be supplied in the following format:\n\n   2, 102 <Text>,<Percentage>\n\n          where <Text> is the text to be displayed and <Percentage> is the\n          progress of the operation in percent. Both values should be quoted.\n          Type 102 will also ensure that the progress-dialogue is the focus\n          thread at each UPDATE.\n\n   Lock\n\n   Specifies whether the thread controlling the Progress Dialogue (executing\n   the progress-dialogue function) should be locked or not (see\n   [8]change-session on locking threads).\n\n   Delay\n\n   Specifies a delay (in seconds) during which the progress dialogue will be\n   hidden after startup. The dialogue will be shown after this delay, unless\n   it is terminated before.\n\n   Examples\n\n   Display a loop counter in the standard Progress Dialogue; do not allow to\n   abort the dialogue; Also be aware of the fact that the different DBMS\xef\xbf\xbds implements\n   transactions differently, for example with respect to table or record\n   locking. Thus, after a call to rollback-trans, any database\n   function depending on this database context may fail. (The database\n   context dependent functions are next, previous, scroll, group-by, delete\n   and update.) The context must be re established for this functions to work\n   properly again. Note that this applies for all currently active\n   applications and not only the application executing the rollback-trans\n   function.\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_committrans.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_enter_critical_section__.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_see_also_rollback_transaction.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_begintrans.htm\n'

This means that any other thread trying to enter\n   the same critical section, will block until the owning thread leaves the\n   critical section.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Critical sections may be nested. Be aware of the danger of deadlock\n   situations when nesting different critical sections.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Trying to leave a critical section without having entered it first will\n   be ignored.\n\n   \xc2\xb7Critical sections held by a thread are automatically released when the\n   thread is terminated.\n\n   \xc2\xa0\n\n   [8][IMG]\n\nReferences\n\n   Visible links\n   1. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_rolltrans.htm\n   2. file:///dev/html_idh_ma_accumulate.htm\n   3. file:///dev/html_leave_critical_section__.htm\n   4. file:///dev/html_leave_critical_section__.htm\n   5. file:///dev/html_enter_critical_section__.htm#idh_ma_entercritical_text\n   6. file:///dev/html_idh_la_textexpression.htm#idh_la_pop_textexpression\n   7. file:///dev/html_enter_critical_section__.htm#idh_ma_entercritical_text\n   8. file:///dev/html_idh_ex_critical_section.htm\n'
